text: What a place! Coming from NY I have seen grand restaurants, however, this one takes the cake. A wonderful atmosphere and an almost formal setting. When I first walked in I felt under dressed, but realized that so was everyone else. This place gets packed quick, and after having the meal we had, we understood why. The kitchen was very busy and the meals took some time but well worth the wait. The wait staff were very friendly and on their game. We had the Calamari Fritte and an Artichoke dip that was amazing (if you like Artichoke dip) We ordered 2 salads both were very tasty. The Four Cheese Ravioli and Gnocchi, Tomato Vodka Sauce were some of the best past dishes that I've had (and I married an Italian). The Main courses were out of this world, the Chicken Saltimbocca and the Veal Parmesan (old faithful). As for deserts (yes we had desert too) . We had Apple Crostada, Caramel Sauce and Maggiano's Signature Spumoni. I have to say the desert , just like the meal were fantastic. If you enjoy Spumoni, then you are going to love this desert. They actually make it better then any other place I have had it. But to what really makes Maggiano's one amazing place it there is an "endless supply" of food. Our waitress said "there's plenty more where that came from" and believe me .... there was. Happy Eating!
label: POS

text: I love this place! They have delicious tofu hoagies at a reasonable price. They also started carrying coconut-ice cream for us vegans. The guy who works the counter is always in a great mood with a cheerful hello every time you come in. My only complaint are the prices, which are way higher than even Whole Foods, but considering I only have to walk a couple of blocks to get there, I would guess I'm paying for the convenience! (I mean it IS a convenience store).
label: POS

text: It's been 3 long years since I've been to the Country Club. They just recently renovated the place with new showers, a new in-ground hottub that seats like... 15 people... and a brand new outdoor bar that was still dryinig from the lacquer. My god. If I still lived in NOLA, I'd be here at least once a week! This place was beauiful before the storm but the renovation now makes it even better. I love that they stay open late so you can come here for a late night naked swim after you've been eating, drinking and dancing elsewhere. Or... you can do all that here too. Which reminds me of the fact that my boyfriend's father managed to get my 20 something roommate to go swimming naked with him at the Country Club. Must've been the booze. ;)

text: A sort of different fast food Mexican place. This place advertises itself with it's huge a la carte burritos, but what really makes it special is the authentic ingredients used, and simple, grilled preparation of everything. I especially like the Super Nachos-lots of warm Queso--just decadent. The bilingual staff are very nice and efficient. Next time you want this kind of fare, pass by the Bell and go here instead.

text: I cannot, for my life, why this is considered the best dim sum place in Chinatown. Somebody please explain that to me. The dim sum here is very typical and they don't offer any specialties, such as shao long bao or Shanghai shumai (not the Cantonese kind). Tastewise, the food is decent enough but I have a qualm about the service and the generally abysmally inept staff. Honestly, Ithink that I need to be standing on a table in a bull-fighter costume imported from Andulacia and holding a red cape to get the attention of a server. When I'm here with my parents' friends, all is well because they know the owners. When I'm here with my friends without them, all goes to the Inferno. I once ordered in Chinese and the lady said "You Chinese? No! You no look Chinese." Gee thanks. Anyhow, rant aside, there are better places to get dim sum, namely at Joy Tsin Lau right across the street. They have great service, more variety, and don't insult your lineage.

text: A lot of people really love this place. and with good reason. The Beer selection is the best in town of all the brew houses in Reno and Sparks. I don't make it out here enough I guess because it's probably one of the only reasons I have to go to sparks. I heard they plan to open a Reno location and I'm looking forward to that.

From the time we ordered our food until we actually got it was about 40 mins (there were literally 3 other tables). I ordered salmon and upon receiving it, I noticed it was raw. I showed the server who kinda hmmm and haaa over it. Their resolution to my problem was to offer us dessert. I feel ripped off because we had to pay for a meal that was inedible. I will never go back there. I am completely mortified that a restaurant would run like that.

Overall, though, the meal was satisfying and the service was pretty good.

text: I will definitely visit the Napoleon House again the next time I'm in NOLA. I took the advice of other reviewers and tried the Pimms Cup...loved it. So light and refreshing on a warm day. We sat in the garden area which was lovely. Be sure to arrive early as it fills up fast. I had the Shrimp Remoulade Stuffed Avocado. Very yummy! My husband had the Italian Muffuletta. Great! If you like olives and fresh bread, you'll love the Muffuletta.

text: "The Green Tea Cupcake. THE GREEN TEA CUPCAKE!!" Haters will say cupcakes have jumped the shark. The real issue is that the national cupcake wave never produced a single acceptable specimen. Until now. Delicious and unexpected, Cups & Chairs green tea cupcake is an anthem of yum. Moist, subtle, wonderfully fragrant, and never cloying, with a light application of the most tantalizing lemony green tea frosting. You know how most cupcakes try to fake you into thinking they're moist by lobbing on an equally giant blob of icing? Not these, my child. Not these. The other cupcakes are equally riveting: carrot, red velvet, and pumpkin (with a cute candy treat atop them). I also highly recommend their latest addition to the menu, banana blueberry muffins: thunderously moist, nicely dense, and thoroughly satisfying. Haven't tried the iced coffee? The ginger peach tea, iced? The brown egg sandwich? The chicken salad? These are all rockstar knock-em-out-of-the-park items. Also loving the amazing Kylie and crew. Nicest people ever. Cheers!
label: POS

text: Umm, did I go to the same place as the other reviewers? I understand that thrift/vintage stores can be hit or miss. On the day I went to visit, it was a complete miss. Problem one: no parking. The lot across the street has signs saying that it's only for such and such business. The lot right next door to Pre to Post has signs saying it's only for this and this business. Frustrated, I went into the other store and politely asked the guy behind the counter if he knew where else I could park and he graciously said it would be ok for me to park in his lot. He added that he appreciated me asking. Second problem, as soon as I opened the door it smelled. I don't like it when thrift stores smell because it's hard to tell if the clothing is going to smell. Not that there was any clothing worth buying. I didn't even have a "Oh, that's too bad it's not in my size" moment. The store is pretty small, so it didn't take more than ten minutes to browse the whole place. I went last Friday, during the day, and there were a couple of teenagers browsing plus me. It wasn't busy. The girl behind the counter didn't say a word to me until I was halfway out the door and then she gave a weak "thank you." I am giving it two stars instead of one though due only to the furniture. I don't live in Nashville, so I wasn't shopping for furniture, but from what I glanced at, they did have some neat pieces. (I didn't look at the prices, so I can't speak to that.) If you are coming to Nashville from out of town, this place is too small to make it worth your valuable vacation time.
label: NEG

text: Um, is there a NO star option here??? I wouldn't check in my dog at this dump... if I had one. I stayed at this hotel overnight (thank God that was all it was!) with a friend to attend a conference. When we got to our room, we were overwhelmed by the ashtray stench that whooshed out of our alleged non-smoking room. I immediately returned to the front desk to request a room change and they granted one to us without incident (to their credit). Thinking our troubles were behind us, we go to the second room only to walk in and look at each other with somewhat incredulous looks and ask, "Was this room even cleaned???" Well, upon further inspection, it became rather obvious that no, it had not. There was trash on the floor, the Kleenex box was taken out of the holder in the bathroom, smashed, and left on the floor of the "bar area", dirt and who-knows-what-else on the floor of the bathroom under the sink, absolutely NO soap available for the sink or shower, hair in the tub, and the piece d' resistance, a wad of TOILET PAPER shoved under the covers of one of the beds!!! But doggone it, they left mints on the bed which they did bother to make although we're not all that confident the sheets had been changed from the prior guest! As they say... Don't go there.

text: This is the first book store that I ever set foot into in Philadelphia. and it certainly gave me an interesting perspective of what to expect from the others. I had a friend who used to volunteer there and she showed me all the cool Wicca books and button selection that they had. Anarchy can be fun, and they have an abundance of it. but it's definitely not all they have. As Nicole R. says you can definitely find a lot of quirky hardcore albums here. and the T Shirts are pretty damn cool. You can also imagine all of the interesting fliers that they have for events, and the informational pamphlets that they get.

Though the chai came highly recommended, I hit up some 4th St. Breakfast and was not disappointed. Tried my friend's chai and was pleasantly surprised - not too sweet, a little smoky. Well priced, too! Becky was very accommodating and has a puppy that looks like my Rosie's twin, so I was sold on the Random. Too bad I live 20 blocks west.

Even after I speak to the manger on duty. You say your open past one and then when I call and drive all the way there you say, "oh just appetizers?" Are you freaking serious? I've been here a series of times before and because of this our order of ten just went to the U. Your welcome!

text: Okay, I finally tried the sushi yesterday with a friend. We had the crazy roll ( tamago, cucumber, crab, salmon, and tobiko) and the spicy scallop roll, along with a radish and shitake mushroom salad appetizer. The salad wasn't something that was, at least to me, amazing, and I wished that they had mixed the dressing in, but it was an interesting course and my friend really enjoyed it, which was what counted. I was extremely happy with the spicy scallop and crazy rolls; the spicy sauce was creamy but not overwhelming and complemented the fresh scallops perfectly. The crazy roll had just the right amount of rice and I was able to fully taste the seafood, which was quite fresh and didn't have that fishy taste characteristic of lower quality fish. We also split the braised tofu and seafood with vegetables entree, which was heaven. Seriously, the two of us were not that hungry but we managed to finish the entire dish. The tofu was mixed with minced shrimp, gently fried, and braised with a light garlic white wine sauce along with spinach, king crabmeat, and winter squash. Soooooo good. I think that I might have a new staple here now.
label: POS

text: I think the weather brings out odd cravings. First hamburgers, now hot dogs. After a horrible bout with internship, I hurried out of that building for a hot dog, plus tea -- reviewing tea spot right after this. She screwed up the egg order (served regular scrambled eggs), and brought out extra turkey bacon. Still, I have not received my food. She takes the eggs back inside and the bacon and comes back out and asks the people at my end of the table "what did you order again?", I told her what I was waiting for and she stated "your food is coming out". text: Ott's has been hanging in the back of my mind of odd places places I've been wanting to check out for years, when this last weekend I suddenly found myself right upon it without trying. With Terrain at Styer's as my baseline for how much potential a nursery/garden center can have, I was pleasantly surprised. It was truly weird and whimsical and thoroughly plant-focused, without any of the extraneous artifice. Taken aback at first by the enormous onion-shaped mothership of a greenhouse, I was then re-floored by the giant mountain just behind it that was covered painstakingly with mums for fall in quirky-perfect fashion. Every part of the place I ended up in I felt like I had wandered into a forgotten back room of some palatial mansion...an ancient secret garden gone wild that time had forgotten. The jungle rooms, the succulent rooms, the fern rooms, the koi ponds - it feels more like a destination garden to view, rather than somewhere to shop. And as someone who is not much of a plant person, that was exactly what I craved.

text: It amazes me the number of different "scenes" that one can experience in this cool historic space depending on when you go. I will confess up front that this old lady almost always finds it too loud at night, but I have had raucous good times when I was in the mood for them. They keep a nice rotation of draft beers including local micro-brew favorites and some more exotic choices, as well as solid, basic beers (e.g. Yeungling, Sam Adams, etc.). I have had some good mixed drinks as well, but the bartenders and waitstaff can get a little overwhelmed when it's packed, making beer seem like the easier and kinder choice. My favorite National Mechanics experience has to be brunch. It is quieter, more mellow, and the diffuse sunlight streaming through the antique stained glass windows really highlights the grand space. The rough-hewn wood tables and little touches like carnivorous plants under glass bells on the window sills stand out. All of the breakfast and lunch dishes I have tried (turkey sandwich, Breakfast!, monte cristo, and a couple of salads and omelettes among them) have been quite good, and a HUGE amount of food for the price. They also do a spectacular bloody mary bar even though I am generally not into these. The times that I am out seeking therapeutic early-day food with liquor are usually the times I most want someone else to do all of the work. However, the generous pours of customizable vodka (or tequila), and absurd variety of hot sauces and extras really make it worth the effort and the money.

The atmosphere is old school steakhouse; wood, wood, and more wood; bow ties, and black vests. If I was there just for booze and atmosphere, five star treatment all around. Here's where it gets a little ugly. Drinks + food + tip=$92 for one person. I came expecting to drop a lot, but I was expecting Dickie to do me a solid and blow me the fuck away. It didn't happen. What I got was an OK salad. It was supposedly a chop salad with kalamata olives, feta cheese, and a balsamic/cane vinagrette. I guess that's what it was, but the feta was a bland, non-stinky variety. text: I had to go to the ER this morning, only the third time ever in my life, thank you very much. What can I say, I'm a klutz! The hard and icy snow piled up so high along the streets and parking is pretty crappy, so when you do park along the side and bring your utility vehicle up onto the hard packed snow, do not underestimate your first step out of the truck like I did. Little did I know that under several feet or so of snow was a drain, if I had parked a little further back or forward I would have been fine. Expecting to step onto the hard packed snow, I stepped right out and my left foot and leg went slamming down to the drain grid. At that I then lost my balance and went sideways. I see you laughing, but ouch! It was painful yesterday and last night I could barely sleep it hurt so bad, when I awoke this am. the pain was twice as bad as I tried to apply pressure to the foot. Being the stubborn fool that I am I waited for hubby to leave for work, called my own work and then drove myself to the ER using one foot. Am I your hero? The ER waiting area was empty and I thought joy, joy. Checking in was as quick as a wink and I only waited about ten minutes before being taken back. Yikes why did I come here today? I saw how busy they were and it wasn't even 7:00am, so I said no to a bed that was offered to me and said I was fine in a chair after hearing all beds were full in both the hospital and the ER. During my time there I watched ambulance's bring in patients who were registered right there in the hallways from the stretchers they were brought in on. Some of these patients stayed right there, because there were no rooms left. Maybe they would have moved me along a little faster so they could have had my room, if I had agreed to one. Two hours I waited for a simple foot Xray, it did not even require the ER's time, it was a matter of calling an Xray tech to come and get me. After seeing someone brought in who fell on the ice and get attention right away, I started to get angry, but I started to cry too. I finally said to a Doctor passing by that it has been two hours and no one has seen me and I would like to leave and go elsewhere, since they were so busy. Dr. Jack did not catch his last name, grabbed my wheelchair with fury, swung me around and down corridors in a very rude and malicious way! He was so ignorant in the way he talked to me and handled my wheelchair. Two techs were standing there talking, doing nothing else, had no patients and I was seen right away. They were very nice. Turned out I have torn ligaments and tendons, no broken bones and I'm in a show boot and on crutches for the first time in my life and hopefully the last. They prescribed me heavy duty narcotics, but I'll pass on those. This is the closest hospital to my home, I tend to drive three times as far to go to another hospital, for the couple of times I have had to go. I have heard nothing but horror stories of St. Mary's, but hubby has been admitted here several times and I thought it was okay, not as good as others, but okay. I wonder how they will open up beds in the hospital for the heart attack patients just arriving. Do they go by who could have been released two days a go and their insurance is just being milked? Do they weigh the insurance of the new patients arriving or do they really care about who needs the most care? The way they handled the patients coming in and out was unbelievable. Most were pacing like hello, what is going on here with my care. Instead of standing around for a good half hour talking in huge groups when the shift changes, keep on moving to take the few minutes of care you need to for the many fall victims who came in and the burn victim. Get us in and out to free up your space and time for the seriously ill. I lost two dear friends in this hospital, one was a diabetic who had fallen and was in for injuries and treatment, he ended up with pneumonia and died, another was in after a stroke, he was to be released and go into therapy in two days, he got pneumonia and never did leave. I am not a fan of this hospital. I give kudos to Michelle who fitted me with this awesome blue boot (not) and crutches and taught me how to use the damn things. She was awesome.

text: It's a shame it has to be this way, but I absolutely HATE (with a fire-y passion) false advertisement....ESPECIALLY if it causes me to loose a quarter tank of gas and ruins my day off from work. This "farm" advertises "pick-your-own pumpkins" like there is no tomorrow. I Googled the crap out of this place yesterday, hoping to find an alternative to Eckert's this year. (Honestly, I should trust my gut instincts more often.) This "farm" IS NOT a "pick-your-own" destination, in any way, shape, or form. I grew up physically twisting the pumpkin from the vine after scouring the fields for the perfect pumpkin, every single year. For the past three years, I have missed out on this simple joy by living in a part of the country that can not offer these delights. This year, I was excited to be home and I was even more excited at the prospect of picking my very own pumpkin, just like old times. The dilemma involved Eckert's being in Illinois and Illinois cops having a very inconvenient distaste for California license plates (a whole other story for another time). In loving fashion, my fiance spent some time yesterday researching Missouri options. Stuckmeyer's was at the top of the list, boldly advertising the very thing we wanted: "pick your own." Imagine my dismay when we take the trip out of the city and drive for over thirty minutes in bad traffic, only to find nothing more than a clever pumpkin patch. Thinking this surely couldn't be the right "field," we went inside. A nice older lady gave us directions to the pumpkin picking. We followed her directions and found ourself in an area about half the size of a soccer field, WITH PRE-PICKED PUMPKINS sitting on TOP of old vines. Every single pumpkin was pre-picked and strategically placed to "look appealing" to those that had been scammed into coming there. Yes, there was a huge selection and they were crammed together, but every pumpkin stood upright - proof this was a sham. We walked to one end, thinking perhaps we were still in the wrong area and needed to walk further. No luck. Not one pumpkin was actually a "PICK YOUR OWN." This place is no different than going to nursery in the city and picking UP a pumpkin. We went back inside and found a different employee. I asked her if THAT was their pick-your-own pumpkin patch. She said it was. I told her that was not a "pick your own" patch and promptly left the store for my car. I guess Eckert's wins again for authenticity. At least they actually let you pull the pumpkin from the vine. I feel bad for people who come to this fake farm and get excited thinking that THIS is the real deal. Educate yourselves a bit, people. As for the "extras," I saw a lame mini-playground and a corn maze the size of my living room. I also saw a deflated bounce house. The farm is in a weird spot RIGHT off the highway, so it's not really "out there." Their prices aren't worth it, either. The pumpkins inside were marked with prices. Expect to be out nearly fifteen bucks for a normal-sized one. Totally lame. (Obviously, I'm angry. I REALLY hate being lied to.)

If you want to show off how much money you have and how much cooler you are than everyone else, I admit.. Tonic is your place (be aware of long lines, Vegas cover charges, and bartenders that don't give a damn). You won't enjoy sharkeez. If you enjoy having a great time and not worrying what others think, cheap drinks, cheap and good food, and great bartenders who actually give you the time of day... Sharkeez is your place. It is hands down the only place worth watching sports at in SB. They have all the fights and games you can imagine in HD and I've even seen the manager take out a laptop so a customer could watch an un-televised sports game. The staff truly does care. Just a tip. If you plan on going to watch a fight with a group call ahead and book a table. They will even hook you up with drink specials and free appetizers if you call ahead for a group. They are really cool about having groups, not just for fights. This food is actually very good for the prices. Large proportions and free chips & salsa are a plus! I'm not a huge Mexican fan, so I usually got the Barbecue Bacon Burger, which was awesome! Breakfast is awesome and very in-expensive. Like I said, if your looking for a fancy bar where you can go to show off how cool you are. Sharkeez is not that place... but I'm from Philly, and where I come from.. we go to bar's to get wasted, meet girls (I met my beautiful girlfriend of 3 years there), watch sports, and have a blast with friends. The kids would run amok everywhere, and I had to tell staff a number of times to monitor small children who would try and use the weight machines. The parents were a total mess. Complete assholes. Fairmount Athletic has an identity crisis: Is it a squash club, a fitness club, or a karate dojo? Unfortunately, it doesn't do much of it well. Avoid it, unless you have a lot of money to spare. text: Haven't had the desserts or baked goods, but they look as good and fresh as any Mexican bakery in the area, and smell delightful. The lunch/dinner items here are the basis for my review. Not sure if you can get combo plates, it all looks like a la carte stuff. Nine items to choose from, plus the specials. But with about 8-10 varieties of meat to choose from, that's a lot of possible combinations. Also, they have not-so-easy-to-find items, like pupusas, menudo, and duros. What the hell is a duro? I know it means "hard" so I'm picturing something with a hard shell, like a tostada or a huarache perhaps? I'm intrigued and will try one on the next visit. Today I got a breakfast burrito and a torta for later. $11 was the total bill, $5-6 for either item would be a steal. Huge full-meal portions in each case. You can get chorizo or ham in the breakfast burrito--I went for the chorizo option. They did a great job of blending the chorizo in nicely with the eggs. Eggs tasted fresh, not reconstituted. And amazingly, it wasn't all that greasy--with chorizo that's an accomplishment. Or maybe the eggs soaked it up, either way it was bomb. The kicker though, were the potatoes. You might want to specify potatoes in the breakfast burrito...they asked me so it might not come with automatically. We're talking fresh home fries that still had all the skin intact, not overcooked into a mush. A very slight crunch to them...if you're insistent on potato items being well-done, again you might want to try to specify...for me it brought out the potato flavor a little more and made the freshness aspect stand out, so double thumbs up!! Use caution if they ask you if you want the "hot" sauce on the side. I happen to like the eye-tearing stuff myself, so I thought it was an excellent topping for the burrito. This stuff was so packed with red peppery goodness (serrano peppers I believe) that it was more similar to a Vietnamese pepper sauce than a salsa. HOT!!! They threw in a couple green sauces too, but I don't typically care for green sauce (salsa verde type) unless it's an avocado salsa, or maybe on chicken enchiladas once in awhile. As top tier as my burrito was, it didn't prepare me for the quality of the torta. I'd had one there a couple times before, and again it didn't disappoint. I guess that's to be expected at a bakery (freshly baked, soft torta rolls = BIG WIN). I had it with al pastor. The meat was a little on the dry side, but that didn't matter much with the tomatoes, salsa, lettuce and most importantly LOADS of fresh avocado moistening the sammich. Portion wise, quality wise, and price wise, I'm gonna have to call this my favorite Reno taqueria @ this point in time. Perfect blending of ingredients takes it up to the full five stars. Their tacos are a good way to sample the meats and choose your favorite--the carne asada is good and fresh-tasting, as well as the lengua (tongue). If you're a stickler for atmosphere, there's not much--maybe four small tables and a TV, that's it. But hey, it's a panaderia first and a taqueria second I guess. I don't care about atmosphere at all (other than cleanliness issues, which I didn't see any problem with here). I got it to go today, but I've been perfectly fine at one of those tables. They also have the La Michoacana popsicles/ice creams (available at many small convenience stores locally) which are only about $1.50 and are pretty good for the most part. An array of Mexican and American sodas rounds out the menu, along with a couple of Mexican beers. I look forward to returning and trying the baked goods, as well as one of those mysterious "duros." Viva Las Palomas!

text: Besides airports and government buildings, places with metal detectors make me nervous. Why? Because metal detectors imply knives and guns; two things that will put a halt to me having fun, oh, and living. I don't know about you but I tend to enjoy places more when I don't feel like I may be the victim of some random violent crime. I'm not the president. I didn't sign up for that. Another thing I look out for and use to gauge the 'will-I-ever-come-back' ness of a place is their security staff. For example, a security staffer at the zoo may be pushing sixty years and suffering from Alzheimer's. This is because zoos tend to be safe and fun and don't really need someone capable of providing security. That's why when I have to get rubbed, sorry, pat downed by another man who clearly abuses steroids, I get a little leery. It's an indicator that on a GOOD night, they'll be there to stop me from getting hit with a beer bottle for the fifth or sixth time. Now if you're strumming your finger tips together like you just stole Christmas wondering if a place like this exist, then you must find serial killer documentaries relaxing. Zee Bar is in fact this place but I assure you that if you are of a sane mind you do not want to go here... ...because Zee Bar is like a low security prison. PRISON. Hey, if being locked up is your thing then go high-five a cop in the face. Or you can stumble in here at one AM and go all sorts of aggressive-animal-behind-bars crazy. This place is perfect for that. They have plenty of guards, um, bouncers there waiting for you to act up. Look around and you'll see them stationed everywhere, like a prison yard. All this place is missing is a watchtower. The inmates, (damn) patrons are all very cool people. Cool as in, 'look how much money I can spend' or 'laughter is for dummies'. The last thing you would want to do at the wee hours of the morning is to have a good time, right? You should be in bed by now, so you can act like you are while in a public place. And you can do it here while scowling. Even though I paid the $20 entrance fee and became a "member" entitling me to pay $10 on subsequent visits, I can assure you I will NEVER go back here. At least not under it's current operation. The only redeeming thing about here that I can think of is that they didn't handcuff or shackled me to anything. You know, they could of done it as a security measure. Save yourself some trouble and grief and go to bed. Or break into your neighbors apartment and party there. Whatever. Sadly, Yelp won't let me give a rating of negative anything, so I'll be plenty generous and give this place one star.

text: In doing business with this company, keep your eyes wide open, This was a flat rate move, less than 10,000 pounds, out of state. The bid was not the cheapest, yet not the most expensive (Bekins). All very nice people, yet we "misunderstood" the sales contract. When the sales person was at the house, the quote for packing was estimated as 40 boxes, and she indicated that if they didn't pack the amount of boxes, we wouldn't have to pay for them. A competing sales person (Bekins) pointed out that we would need to hire a shuttle: load the goods into a small truck and then have it moved to a larger van, since the street was too narrow for a large van. When we went to the office to finalize the paperwork, right before the move (too late to secure the 2nd bidder), we were informed that the quote was "binding", that we would be paying for 40, whether they packed them or not. They packed far less than 40 boxes. Oh, & yes, we would need to pay for a shuttle, something the sales person knew when she visited the house. The excuse was that she didn't know if a smaller van and its drivers would be available on the day of the move. On the day of the move, the sales person called us, regarding the "binding" quote & kept saying "but you have the best movers", instead of addressing our "misunderstanding". Yes, that was true, the movers were the best. The bad taste was that we were misled by the company itself, not once, but twice. Moving is stressful, and you do start to worry about the other "misunderstandings" that may happen. Also, if you're getting 2 separate bids, be advised that Sierra Moving Systems, a Mayflower franchise & Puliz Moving, United Van Lines, are owned by the same company, with employees doing work at both buildings. Not exactly something you'd pick up off of their web sites.

I can only think of 2 other restaurants where there wasn't anything on the menu I wouldn't have ordered. Gemelli's menu makes for number 3. I have not been able to find a good steak tartar since moving to the US so once I saw it as an appetizer, I had to have it and it was heavenly. (I know it's not for everyone so anyone needing to hurl, please do so now and come back and finish reading my review which references fully cooked food from here on). My entree was a healthy serving of scallops on a bed of butternut squash risotto: skillfully cooked and beautifully presented. Deirdre was a friendly and attentive server. The price point is exactly where it should be and the ambience is extremely inviting. I think I'll be making a New Year's resolution to eat my way through Gemelli's menu. text: 2.5 stars (I didn't want to round up) It was really cold this last Saturday and the idea of a fresh quality beef followed by a warm bowl of udon sounded like a great dinner solution (plus, CPK had a 30 min wait). We were greeted by a really nice waitress who sat us down at the shabu shabu bar. The menu listed two portions sizes; small and large. I usually go for the large so that's exactly what I ordered. The type of meat wasn't listed on the menu nor did I ask, but there were two signs posted on the mirrored wall in front of me that said the beef was "Kobe" beef. I thought, wow, this must be a real steal (Large was $18.95). The plate of vegetables came out, which was a fresh assortment of the usual; napa cabbage, spinach, tofu, carrots, green onions, long stem mushrooms, and udon. The amount of udon was very small and it didn't look as fresh as it could have been. While I waited for the meat, I prepared my dipping sauces with the finely mashed garlic and the sliced green onions. They didn't offer any spice drops but the peanut sauce did have a slight kick already (or it could be from the spoons of garlic). The meat came out shortly after and I wasn't too thrilled. The meat looked a little pink like it was frozen and didn't have that rich red texture that I usually expect from really fresh meat. Also, the meat wasn't lean, but had lots of marbling. I mean, lots! Now, with steaks I like this meat because it will be very juicy. But when cooking it in a pot of boiling water, I don't want to see the floating fat. And the fat doesn't add anything to the flavor of the meat when you boil it. And sure, the Kobe and Prime choices of meat will have some marbling, but when there seemed to be more fat that meat within each slice, I started to wonder of I was actually eating "Kobe" beef or not. The meat was still tender and it was beef so I still ate all the beef with the bowl of white rice (yes, no brown rice here). And as I got closer to finishing the beef, I overheard another patron sitting three people down asking for the miso base for his udon. The waiter replied with, "huh, what do you want? Oh, no, we don't do that here". Huh, no miso base? The last two establishments that I went to provided a miso base. I didn't want to believe so I asked the waitress the same question and got a similar response, "oh, sorry, we don't have that here". No miso base for my udon and no new clean bowl to eat my udon. So, I cooked the udon, placed it in my bowl that had a few grains of rice and poured the remaining of my peanut dipping sauce and had it "Gene chop suey style". Not the best bowl of udon soup, but edible. The bill for two orders of large beef with ice tea and hot tea: $45.45. Oh, we also got an order of Spicy Tuna Cut Roll and Avocado Cut Roll, both which was okay. The rice of both rolls seemed very mushy, like a paste. And the spicy tuna wasn't as spicy as I've normally had it. Plus, the amount of tuna was on the conservative side. Add the two orders of cut rolls and the bill was now about: $60.00 for a so so experience. Sorry Kai, but when you get patrons that had had better quality meat, dipping sauces, and more meat choices (as well as better sushi cut rolls) at other Japanese restaurants 100 miles South of Santa Barbara, it's a hard sell. And with this being the third experience in the last two months for me, this was the least favorite of the shabu shabu restaurants. I didn't check, but maybe being the only shabu shabu in town that's on the major tourist strip of town has gotten Kai Sushi a bit too comfortable with what they serve.

text: We went to Moritomo for Valentine's Day dinner. It was a bad experience that just kept getting worse. The description below gives all of the details. We did send this letter to Moritomo's on Feb 20, 2008 and have yet to hear back from them. "The script at the Japanese Steakhouse started pretty much the same. Dinner customarily starts with a bowl of clear soup. In this case, it was a beefy broth spiced with dried minced onions - you know, the kind that come in gallon jugs. Sadly, the flakes had not completely rehydrated, rendering them an odd mix of crunchy, soft and simply hard. This rather lackluster starter was followed by an equally uninspired salad. The all iceberg lettuce concoction was washed, evidenced from the pool of water collecting on the bottom of the bowl. The top was drowned in half a cup of thick, somewhat sweet, slightly ginger spiced dressing. After scraping most of the dressing off and mixing it with the lettuce, the dressing promptly slid off and settled on the bottom of the dish with the water. Our chef arrived and began his routine. As hokey as this can be, my family enjoys the procession- the whirling knives, the clanking spatula and the spinning egg. In this case, the flying spatula banging off the side of the grill and onto the floor (he thought a moment, considering still using it, before putting the spatula back on the cart and picking up a fresh one). The eggs broke open, one, two, three, and immediately started to burn. The poor man tried in vain to slice and dice the eggs, but they were well past brown in a matter of seconds. Great globs of butter were thrown on, turning the mass into a soupy mess. Slowly the fried rice began to take shape as the ingredients were added. I say it took shape only figuratively, for in fact the rice flew in all directions. Each time our chef scooped and flipped rice went flying. Soon, a third of the rice lay scattered across the grill, popping as it cooked. He served the portions one by one, spilling copious amounts back onto the grill. (I wondered idly where the chef came from. My guess was the kitchen. In desperation after the defection of their scheduled master hibachi guy, the dishwasher had been promoted.) The burning of food continued. As the beef was set down, it immediately hissed and gouts of steam rolled into the air. Apparently, the establishment failed to purchase the fans on the hibachi grills, as evidenced by the continuous cloud of steam that bathed my poor wife for the rest of the cooking demonstration. ( I did try to get her to change seats with me.) As food continued to burn, our chef scraped it off into an ever growing pile of vile, black goo on the side of the grill. During all of this, our chef tried to re-enact the time honored traditions of the American Japanese Steakhouse hibachi chef. If you have visited such an establishment, you know of what I speak. There is of course the classic inverted stack of onions, filled with some sort of flammable liquid and then set on fire to form a "volcano", followed by steam and a "train". Only, in our case, a fourth of the grill was inundated with the flammable liquid, so that the inverted onion tower became ground zero of a flaming inferno. The hapless onion slices drooped and caved in. Our chef also chopped sliced Zucchini into little cubes, all the better for tossing into people's mouths. Here is a hint for all you would-be hibachi wizards: four year olds are not good at catching small cubes of flying vegetables flung at their face. Once it bounces off their nose or forehead three or four times, it's best to move on to another victim. The circus finally came to an end, and our master chef set about cleaning his grill. Now, in every restaurant of this nature I've been in, the chef scrapes off the grill, wipes it down with a few quick, skilled passes and moves on to applause and fame. Not so for our culinary hero. The hapless dishwasher dumped water onto the grill (my wife promptly disappeared for about thirty seconds as a cumulus cloud formation spread across the room) and began sloshing around with a wire pad. I did not know this at the time, but apparently he managed to slosh his slop onto my wife and her food. Chevalier that I am, I would have risen to my wife's defense and demanded to see the manager at once. Cloaked in the cloud of steam as she was, I failed to see such gross inadequacy and continued eating my mediocre fare. In the end, the experience was so bad it was funny. My son was rather oblivious to the laundry list of faux pa, and was quite pleased when he left. We did walk away with a pair of miniature origami birds, which he thought were pretty nifty. I can't say I'll be going back to Morimoto's, but they certainly did give us a meal we will not soon forget."

text: This dining experience was a spectacular event to end a spectacular day in Santa Barbara. Like Lawrence C. said, we were in the private dining room known as the "Cork Room" which seats between 10-20 people. There's a nice, large impressionist painting in the back, which I stared at for a large part of the night. The table is so big, it felt like being a knight as part of King Arthur's roundtable. The menu is referred to as a "streamlined version" of the dinner menu, and it was legend-wait for it. The entire table starts off with an amuse-bouche, which I remember as being a chocolate-centered pastry. I had trouble dissecting it with my fork and knife, so i just ate it whole. The appetizer chosen was the duck rillettes on grilled sourdough. Think of it as pate made of duck confit. It was a great way to get me buttered up for the actual main course. However, ordering the main course was one of the most difficult decisions of my life. The options were: pan-roasted salmon, chicken duxelles, blood orange & mint-marinated rack of lamb, bourbon & maple-glazed california duck breast, and grilled kobe new york steak. Asking me to choose between the last three is like asking me which of my future sons I would love more. Ultimately, I came to the decision of ordering the rack of lamb (and I will likely love my eldest son most). There was an initial concern that I might have ordered wrong, but when all the food came out, I realized I made the right choice. The waitress didn't even ask me how I wanted it cooked; it was rare and it was perfect. The best lamb I've had to date. The blood orange glaze and mint toned down the gaminess of the lamb. But even better than having the best lamb ever, I got to sample some of the other entrees that my wonderful friends ordered. The duck confit was just delicious. The recipe on the website says it uses 1/4 pound of duck fat per duck leg. Doesn't that just sound like one of the menu items in heaven? Luckily, I got to sit next to my friend who only ate half of her duck (thanks for being small). Also had a bite of the Kobe steak, which was cooked rare, with beautiful grill marks and a blood orange glaze. For dessert, I thoroughly enjoyed the blueberry upside-down cake served with lemon zest ice cream. The sweet from the cake was a great compliment to the sour of the ice cream. As for the texture, it must have been cooked by terrorists cause it was DA bomb. All of the plating was beautiful for every dish. I think the service deserves 5.5 stars. It's not easy to serve our party of 18 people in a timely manner, but we all got our plates at approximately the same time. I probably will never understand the rigors of preparing 4-5 duck confits and racks of lambs and kobe steaks simultaneously, but it was done. Moreover, our head waitress was extremely personal and professional. She let us play with the private music settings (selecting various pandora stations), promptly addressed any of our concerns, and gave me the recommendation for the exquisite lamb. She listened to some of our reminiscent moments and joked with us, all while also taking orders and filling up water and wine glasses. But she was a psychology major in college... so maybe she was messing with our minds somehow and forced us into liking her. At the end of the night, the owner of the restaurant told us the story of his wedding. It was a story that paralleled the same journey two of our amazing friends had just officially begun earlier that day. Oh yeah, I forgot. This place would be an ideal engagement dinner location as well. Can't really beat an experience that captures great company, great food, and great service. -ary

text: I first went to PF Chang's in Las Vegas, and was downright thrilled when I learned that we were getting one of our very own in Reno, too. If you question the authenticity of a Chinese restaurant in the middle of the vice-filled desert, well, that's kind of missing the point. Sure, it's a big chain and all the restaurants look very similar, but so what? The dark wood paneling on the walls, the recessed shelves with pseudo-antique-Oriental vases and sculptures, the warm light from the elegant little sconces hanging from the ceiling - it's stylish but not fussy (and, living in Reno, you learn to appreciate any place that doesn't use neon or flashing lights). The restaurant is justifiably famous for its "soothing" chicken lettuce wraps, which have now become a common sight in other eateries. The Shanghai cucumbers, though, also make a good appetizer for one or two - crisp, fresh chunks of cucumber in a salty-sweet vinegar dressing. The pan-fried shrimp dumplings are good as well. PF Chang's offers all of the dishes you normally find in a Chinese restaurant, and I've never disliked anything I've ordered there. My favorite is the general's chicken, but I've also enjoyed the crispy honey shrimp, Cantonese scallops, and shrimp lo mein. Rice comes with your entree, and you can request brown rice if you actually like the stuff. The prices are pretty reasonable - most of the entrees are about $12, and (with the rice) it's more than enough for dinner and leftovers. On weekends, there's often a short wait for a table, but the service is usually friendly and competent, and I've never gotten a bad server there. Great for a girls' night out, a family gathering, or a casual date, PF Chang's is a fun and low-key place for when you want Chinese food, but don't want to eat off a divided Styrofoam plate.

The menu was small-ish but held a variety of foods - although there were surprisingly few beef and pork options for a restaurant named "Cochon" and having a butcher upstairs. The entrees were good although somewhat unimpressive; however, the appetizers were very good and held many unique plates. Several different people I ran into during this trip raved about Cochon as a place they'd had one of their finest meals, but I was disappointed having come in with that expectation, particularly after all the other wonderful meals I'd already had in New Orleans. For my main course, I had the grilled filet of beef tenderloin (cooked medium-rare) with whipped potatoes and green beans. Let me say it was excellent. I don't know how they prepare their medallions, but I wished I'd had seconds. But I have to single out the potatoes. I spent the rest of the day thinking about them, and my only conclusion was that they must be made using whipping cream instead of milk and butter. I had to skip the dessert, but it, too, looked great. In fact ,I noticed one of our client using their cell-phone to take a picture of the plating. text: Camping in Santa Barbara for a week, and the starter motor on my 1955 Buick stopped functioning. More than a hundred miles from home, and on vacation, I had no resources on this area, but found positive Yelp reviews for a different repair shop. They were honest and told me that I should go directly to AGS. I called Matt, the owner of AGS, early the next morning and had my car towed in a couple of hours later. In Los Angeles, companies that rebuild components like these usually require that you bring in the motor itself -- they rarely let you bring the entire car, and offer removal and installation. After Matt told me he could do this, I was sold. When the tow truck guy arrived, and asked me where I was going his exact words were "That's the best shop. Quality work." It reinforced everything I had heard. I learned that AGS stands for Alternator, Generator, Starter, and Matt himself was very personable, knowledgeable and his rapid diagnosis matched mine: starter motor. A couple of hours later, before the close of day, I received a phone call from him. He had pulled everything apart, diagnosed the problem and estimated project completion by about noon the next day. I was even more impressed. This was a semi-major component (not as major as an engine or transmission, but close) and to have complete service and repair in fewer than 24 hours, on a car that is 55 years old, is pretty impressive. As I drove away, I began to experience a carburetor problem, which I incorrectly thought might be related to the starter. Matt went through the system, and examined and tested things. We found out that it wasn't anything related to the starter motor -- the problem was in a completely different part of the engine -- but he still fixed it in. And he did it in about 10 minutes. Wow. Thank God I broke down in Santa Barbara. Any other town and I would have been royally out of luck. Possible scenarios would have been leaving the car somewhere in town, having it towed hundreds of miles or waiting a week for a mechanic only familiar with modern cars to figure out older technology.
label: POS

text: By the time we ate at Tommy's I was sick and tired of eating out in New Orleans. I just wanted to be home. Combine that with the fact that the acoustics were terrible. There were a gazillion Opthalmologists under one roof all trying to be the loudest one at their table. Conside these things when you read this review. Tommy's started out great (mostly because the service at nearby Emeril's sucked so badly that we acutally left and came here instead). The service was lovely. But, the dining room we were in was beyond loud. The wine was good but the kitchen was back-logged and painfully slow. We tried 3 different types of baked oysters (Tommy's, Bienville & Rockefeller) and they were all only okay. The dressings were really salty and overpowered the flavor of the oysters. I think I just prefer them raw. I got the duck salad and I laughed out loud when I saw it. It was a huge portion of sliced duck breast with a tiny bit of of undressed spinach in the middle of the plate. Imagine the size of one scoop of ice cream. Yes, that was the portion size of the greens in my "entree" salad. All duck - no salad. You might be thinking, "What's wrong with that?" Well, I would say "nothing" if I had ordered the duck entree and not the duck SALAD. I don't like smoked foods and I think I either missed the "smoked" mention on the menu or it wasn't there. But, let's just say, my duck tasted like bacon. To me, everything smoked tastes like bacon. And, I don't like bacon. The only thing funnier than my salad was....my fiance's salad! His green salad with crabmeat was actually a scoop of shredded lettuce and crab meat mixed together and doused in mayo. Of course, the menu made NO mention of the mayo. (I tried to warn him having lived in New Orleans that I had never seen crab that wasn't was fried or doused in mayo or some sort of cream or cheese sauce, but he didn't believe me). Imagine getting scoop of tuna salad with some lettuce mixed in with it (and getting really soggy) and nothing else. Now, replace the tuna with crab meat. I know I sound bitter but Tommy's really put me over the edge. It's not even really Tommy's fault. But, I was so happy to get back on the plane and come back to Boston where greens are green, crunchy and plentiful and not everything tastes like bacon.

The BBQ ones were super, super sweet and tasted like the cheap brand of store bought sauce from a discount store. Sugar, ketchup, um...that's about it. I know some people love the stuff, but I'm just not a fan of BBQ you can eat as dessert. I also ordered the fried green tomatoes with fried oysters and their special sauce. I think somehow it was forgotten because I finally asked about it after the wings and the waitress looked confused at first. She came back and said they had to do a new batch and it would be ready in less than 5 minutes. It was (as I said, I liked the waitress). The sauce was...almost not there. I saw some discolorations on the tomatoes but there was no sauce anywhere that we could find. Still, even with the tomatoes not really cooked all the way, it was the best part of the meal to me. They have their spiced down for both the fried oysters and the tomatoes. I think if it hadn't been forgotten about, it would have been brilliant cooked correctly. My dinner companion ordered the portabella pizza with pesto sauce. As stated by another reviewer, the crust was blackened in places and the texture was dried out. Almost like they made the crust and froze it for a few days, then cooked it from frozen at a HIGH temp. Black and bubbly but hard and cracker-like. There were a total of 6 small pieces of mushroom on her pizza and for the money, there should have been a lot more than that (Plus, it WAS in the name of the pizza). She was disappointed but said it "wasn't that bad. I've had frozen pizzas that were worse". I thought that was the whole point of going to a pizza place..better than average pizza. Conclusion: I think they DO have promise but cost cutting this early on will turn away potential repeat local business, which, despite what so many places think, IS important here in NOLA. Cutting their prices by about 10% across the board or making a more quality product will go a long way toward return customers and they will make much more money in volume than in higher costs for lesser foods. I do wish them luck but I doubt I would ever eat there again.

text: I've been to the Phoenix Salon and Spa 5 times in the past month. My friend bought me a Smart Circle card that gave me 5 treatments for a total of $50 plus tips (there's a mandatory minimum 20% gratuity with each treatment). I was very satisfied with every one of them. Massage - Upgraded my 30 min massage to a full 50 minutes, and I'm glad I did. Ike was my therapist. I have some serious trapezius muscle spasm, and he's the only massage therapist that's ever been able to work it out completely. Big thumbs up here. Also, he used a great massage cream that didn't leave me feeling greasy and dying for a shower as soon as I got out, like most other massage places I've been to. Facial - 30 minute "Get Up and Glow" facial with Stacy. She was really pleasant to talk to and tailored the facial to meet my skin's specific needs. I looked and felt radiant when I got out. She also suggested specific treatments to help with hyperpigmentation and dryness. Nails - just your basic filing, cuticle treatment, and polish with Winnie, who was also great to talk with. Manicure lasted a lot longer than they usually do on me (I'm active and work with my hands a lot). Waxing - also with Winnie. Eyebrows, lips, and chin were included, but since I don't have any chin hairs, we just did the first 2. I've only had my eyebrows done twice before, but she gave me a really nice arch that was better than I've seen with prior eyebrow waxes, and didn't rip my skin off. I guess that's really all you can say about a wax. Hair - cut and styled by Nicole. She gave me a great cut that works well with my hair texture and oiliness. She used a great volumizing shampoo and mousse. The place has a great relaxing atmosphere, especially given its busy Center City location. Their receptionist, Mark, was very nice every time as well. I can only compare this to one other spa in town, Rescue Rittenhouse. The Phoenix was WAY better for me. Better massage, and the facial didn't make me break out like the one at Rescue did. Would be happy to go back once a month or more if it weren't for the cost. Sadly, their regular prices are way beyond my reach, which is why it gets 4 stars instead of 5 from me. Bring the prices down a bit and this place would be perfect.

text: 5 stars considering the intel I got on this dive: It's the oldest public house in Philadelphia, which means this is where Ben Franklin used to drink. I could only wish they had a regular who dresses up period costume ... or something to mask the smell. What's with me and alleyway entrances? I guarantee the smell was not from the alley; it emanated from within. CRAZY that we still went inside the dark, yet lively place for a Friday night. Good thing a sign was lit indicating the second floor bar was open. There should be a Monopoly card that reads, 'Go directly upstairs, and collect your sense of smell'. A sense that is worth far more than $200. A few TV screens broadcasted NCAA games and a pro NBA match-up. Villanova has been on fire this year! Music was of the vintage college variety: Dave Matthews, Journey ... even Michael Jackson. I've never seen people start dancing to 'Man in the Mirror'. My friends have always found it an introspective song. Still I prefer that title to 'Ben & Me'. Though the actual bar was crowded, a friendly guy on the end made space for us to order: Jameson on the rocks in honor of the record number of Irish bars I've seen in one city. Does the count rival Boston? Only one way to find out; another trip! Not sure what Manoj ordered, but he said it was a house specialty like a Guinness knockoff. We weren't here long since Mitchell called and we went to meet up. This was a fun place aside from the first smell. BTW I was told this place has karaoke 3x a week; that's quite frequent programming unless you own a system at home! I really like the old timey neon sign

text: Once when I was fifteen and very stubborn with my palette I accompanied some friends to Mama's only to abstain from eating anything. Five years later I returned with a friend ready to complete another phase in my quest to try every Philly falafel gem. They serve up large, mouth-watering, and wholesome falafel. I haven't been to the Falafel King or Magic Carpet yet but this is tied with (if not slightly tastier than) Alyans in my book. It's a healthy and heartier alternative to fast food. Mama's packs your pita with falafel balls, a shredded lettuce mix, cucumbers, tomatoes, humus, tahini, and so forth. Upon ordering they also offer a spicy option that is some additional sauce, it's very good and allows me some sort of variation upon visiting. Their signature combo consists of a large falafel, a generous serving of fries, and a soda or water for $8.50. I've always taken left overs home so it's definitely worth the price. I'm a sucker for combos but they also serve individual (and smaller sized) falafel, platters, and soups. The only inconveniencing facet of Mama's is their schedule. As other yelpers have pointed out, they close on Jewish holidays. However in my experience whenever a fast food or hole in the wall has a challenging schedule that often inconveniences the customer (i.e. mostly every cheesesteak spot which I love ever) it often means that the food is very good! Plus if you're unfamiliar with Jewish holidays that is nothing that a quick Google search can't remedy. I highly encourage anyone to make the pilgrimage to Mama's. This falafel possess the power to cure hunger, poverty, blindness, the recession, the gender gap, etc. I'm just playin but it is a healthy decision for your next meal!

text: One of my favorite things we saw in New Orleans -- St. Roch's cemetery, home of The National Shrine of Saint Roch, patron saint of miraculous cures, where they have an altar room filled with marble thank-you tiles and plaster casts of feet and polio braces and eyeballs and big spiders and cockroach parts. Lots of gorgeous mosaics and statues of saints all around the cemeteries, too. For more info, see http://strochproject.com/neighborhood.html "People came to the shrine in large numbers to ask St. Roch for help in cases of affliction, disease and deformities. A small room on the side of the chapel holds a number of offerings left by visitors to the chapel. The tradition was to leave accoutrements of the illness or disability (including, in the past, eyeballs, crutches, and false limbs!) in gratitude for recovery." NOTE: No joke about closing time, they actually locked us in a few minutes before the posted time. text: Don't let the setting of a strip mall discourage you. This place was quite lovely. I went here for lunch on a Saturday. I hope this place is more busy during dinner service, because it was dead inside. The good thing about it being so slow was that I got to check out the whole place. Upon entering, there is a small bar of about 5 stools that overlooks the open kitchen area. I wasn't sitting there, but I do think it may be fun to watch them preparing their lovely food, and the guys working in the back were nice eye-candy too. There was upbeat jazz music playing at a decent level, white table cloths, comfy yet elegant seating, and helpful waitstaff. Now to the good part, the food. It was a unusually chilly summer day when I visited to the carrot ginger soup of the day sounded wonderful. It was quite flavorful and yummy. I'm not normally a person that gets excited about soups, but it was so good, I had difficulty waiting for it to cool and not burn my tongue as I was eating it. I also had an urge to lick the bowl, but was able to hold myself back. I also had the salmon tart. It came with a small spinach salad nicely plated with the tart. The salad dressing was tart, but perfect. The tart was flaky and the salmon artichoke and spinach on top of it was great. The combo of the soup and tart was also pretty reasonably priced at about $15. I'm not a drinker, but they had an extensive wine list. I'm glad I discovered this place while I'm staying in Indy for work. I highly recommend it.

text: I'm not completely sure what all the fuss is about this place. Fiancé and I joined some friends here for a late dinner and drinks recently and were rather underwhelmed. For a Thursday evening, the place was hopping, so maybe I'm just missing something. First, the good. The ambience is great. The building is billed as a Tucson historical landmark, and it certainly feels that way. Several dining areas are adorned with large, ornate wooden furniture that feels ripped out of a Mexican hacienda. The lights are kept at an acceptably low level - dim enough to lend a romantic feel to one's dinner, but not so low that one feels as though the manager is trying to hide something. The outdoor patio is nicely landscaped and feels like a refreshing desert oasis. Finally, the manager(owner?) seems like a friendly, stand-up guy. When his waitstaff seemed to be put-upon and out to lunch, he was kind, solicitous and made some good wine pairing suggestions. Unfortunately, the menu doesn't really match the overall experience. Food is awfully expensive for what you get. While some of the more adventurous entrees have clearly had some care put in to them, a number of the meals and appetizers have a decidedly store-bought feel to them, and the salads seem to contain an abundance of iceberg lettuce to conceal the fact that they don't have much else going on. The wine list is anemic, and, at least on the night we were there, the first four wines I tried to order were either out of stock or had been removed from the menu. When I finally settled on a glass of port for dessert, the price was marked up considerably over what the same glass goes for at Rumrunner's bistro. Our friends thought the place was the second coming of Christ, but for us, Cushing Street fell short. I mean, it was ok, and if I had to go there for a work function, I wouldn't put up a stink, but, in the end, I felt like the upscale tone the place sets for itself didn't really live up to it's actual dining experience.

text: I was a little nervous about this place after reading it was a franchise out in California, since I've never heard anything good about bbq in California. Still I wanted to keep an open mind and I do like good bbq, so I went here for lunch. I was seated right away, but it did take some time for my server to get to me, since it was a little crowded and they appeared to be short staffed on the waitress/waiter end. Once my waitress came over, she took my drink and food orders very fast and efficiently. Like the Yelper Kalina I, I too had what tasted like a watered down drink. In my case it was a Sprite. Though on second though, I wonder if someone didn't set the mix/mixer right. Usually those are prepackaged though, unless technology has changed. I ordered the Carolina style pulled pork sandwich with fries and coleslaw. When it comes to bbq there are 4 things you need to do well: Meat, meat, meat, and sides. The meat was tender, but had absolutely no taste. Now if its a Carolina style meat, it should definitely have some taste ie a rub or vinegar/sourness to it. The fries were a mix of sweet potato and regular fries. They were ok, but nothing noteworthy. The guy who brought my order over said "Try this apple cider vinegar with peppers in it on your fries. It's delicious". I did so on a small portion of my fries, and well it tasted like vinegary fries. No real apple or pepper taste. So unless my tastebuds are completely shot that was a waste. The coleslaw tasted like it had been made fairly recently, since it had some crunch to it. However there was no zip to it(needed pepper or something else) and it wasn't creamy enough. It also irritated me that they served the coleslaw on TOP of my meat on the sandwich. I'm not sure if that was intentional or just a plating error. It's possible I missed the description of the sandwich, but thats the first time I ever had coleslaw dumped on top of a barbecue sandwich. And I've eaten my fair share of bbq sandwiches at this point, especially after living down South for graduate school. Service was good. Kalina was right about the servers. If I was 10-15 years younger and single I'd be back almost every day just for them. The space was nice but there is one flaw. The bathrooms are located downstairs with the kitchen/prep area. This wouldn't be a big deal except there is a narrow staircase. So you have to play chicken/who goes first in order to get back up. I did actually see some burnt ribs that could have been Kalina's. I"m glad she sent them back because they looked scorched. I might go back and try something else at some point. The ribs actually looked and smelled good that were upstairs.

text: Based on the reviews I wasn't expecting too much, but I have to say I was pleasantly surprised. Yes, it is on the expensive side, but I disagree with the pretentious label. The old church setting and stained glass windows juxtaposed a very violent, gory "lion hunt" painting on the wall. It was all very interesting. I did find the vaulted ceilings made for a loud room. The bar was big and very nice. On to it now... the food. Most of us stuck with the New Orleans fare. For starters, we had the Slab of Bacon (more like a fatty ham, but good) and gumbo (very good and spicy). Entrees: I had the Jambalaya and it was great. Spicy with plenty of shrimp and sausage. I also tried the Eggplant Ophelia and would highly recommend that (eggplant, shrimp, crabmeat casserole). Yum! Another person ordered the NY Strip which was good. Nothing earth-shattering though. Sides included sweet potato casserole which tasted as sweet as a dessert, green beans, garlic mashed potatoes, and cream spinach. Drinks were good and strong. I would definitely go back!

All delicious and all huge! Often, we'll get a sandwich, eat (maybe) half of it on the spot and save the rest for later. This especially applies to the Skyscraper Club, which is a monster. Any wrap or sandwich I have ever had from here has been great. I also happen to love their Broccoli and Cheddar soup. It's really really thick but creamy and cheesy and delicious. And their Greek salad is, of course, ginormous, but truly amazing with the option of having the potato salad right on top, which is a treat. The knishes were okay. text: Pi's pizza is good. Really, really, really good. If you like deep dish pizza, you gotta give this place a shot. The crust they use has corn meal in it, so it has a little extra bite to it than traditional crusts. This also gives the crust a little more rigidity, lightness, and less of the doughiness that a lot of other deep dishes have. Not saying it's good or bad, just different. And different is good here. This place is in the East Loop across from The Pageant, so that means good luck getting a table here on a show night. In fact, good luck getting a table here in peak hours period. Once it became known that this is Obama's favorite pizza joint (and it is, no joke...the owner flew to the White House to make him pizza), it's not unusual to wait 1-2 hours for a table. It's worth it to try it once...whether it's worth it a 2nd or 3rd time is up to you. I took my parents here, who are not down with the hip culture of the area, and they didn't think it was all that great. All they noticed was the cooler-than-thou vibe and weird music coming out of the speakers. So I suppose this solidly counts as a yuppie hang-out, and I'm ok with that. Just know that going in. This isn't a mom-and-pop place with candles and all that. It's a noisy place to see and be seen, and there's a good chance that the people at the next table have better taste than you (or at least think they do). So in summary: pizza = good, atmosphere = ok (depends on your perspective), value = ok. I find it's a tad overrated by people, but judging on the merits of the pizza itself, it's very good. Give it a shot.

text: AVOID BUSY BEE and if your agent suggests them, reconsider how with-it your agent is. Busy Bee was one of the earlier staging companies in the city, but is certainly one of the lower quality. They basically seem to have a large stock of ikea furniture and a lot of not-very-attractive accessories with Marshal's stickers still on them which they throw randomly into whatever project they get. I have seen some decent jobs done by busy bee early one-- nothing ground-breaking, but decent. It seems like the original core crew knew what they were doing, but lost touch as they expanded. Lately, though, their brand has become something of a derogatory short-form for really sloppy 'design.' I have known several sellers who actually moved the furniture out of their new construction units in order to improve the salability of their property. When I personally tried to call the management to resolve issues with my own property professionally, the owner started screaming at me and calling me and rambling on how 'karma will get me.' (Seems she confuses Buddhism with Voodoo). This without having any prior interaction and because I simply asked to have the vomit-stained rugs and broken, taped-together lamps they brought in replaced. When I had such a difficult experience with the business, I initially assumed it to be out-of-line employees. However, the problem is clearly at the top. Here is a message the owner sent to me via yelp, which I think serves to illustrate the 'professionalism' one would expect in dealing with this company. Mind you, I have no idea whom this Katherine woman is, but I think it only serves to illustrate that the ownership is absolutely unwilling to accept responsibility for their own actions. "Anna P. has sent you a message on Yelp: Your Review "wanna keep posting katharine? all evidence of your lunacy, all evidence that will come in front of the judge. get ready cause kharma is a bitch. you are one insane person. are you so desperate for business? your copycat company with your fake pictures and copycat ideas isn't working out for you? do you realize how pathetic your reviews are and how everyone sees through them? oh yeah, busybee was great when you worked for me since you are a nationally published designer! you are a joke. your company is a joke. your posts are a joke. and you are playing with the wrong person. keep sending posts, the more the better it will be for me when all is exposed and your subpeoned into court. get a lawyer darling cause you will need one, the papers are coming and we're going to trial:)" SO... that only further reiterates my experience. Being unskilled is bad enough, but this is another level of inappropriate. As for other staging companies, I have no experience with the Voila people the owners of Busy Bee want to trash, but friends have had great experience with Matthew Izzo and many furniture stores are willing to offer reduced prices and free design services if you order a fair bit at once. My friend paused long enough in front of the window for me to suggest actually going inside - I had been there previously and had walked away with two BEAUTIFUL vintage gold earrings and the most kick ass glitzy octopus ring I have ever seen. I'm obsessed with it. But my friend hadn't seen their selection so I took her in, knowing she would like a lot of their stuff. And she did. We ended up in front of the glass cabinet that contains these awesome, intricate rings they design in various animal shapes. My friend almost got one of their simpler designs (they can get very complex, and LARGE), but it wasn't in a metal she liked so now she's thinking of getting one custom made in burnished silver. And considering the amount of detail and workmanship that goes into the rings, they are rather reasonably priced. text: For my parent's 50th Wedding anniversary, we were looking for a place that would be a great 'multi-generational' vacation destination, since we were planning a 3-generation gathering. After extensive research, we ended up going to the FVC (as it's affectionately called) 5 years ago. Well, Grandparents, parents and grand kids had SO much fun, we've made it an annual tradition! Everyone looks forward to our week at the FVC. The grandkids have 'camp' each day so get lots of playtime together and truly love the fun activities they get to do. The parents get to go biking, hiking, surfing, play tennis or just hang out, while the grandparents go on nature walks, museum tours, and outings. We all get together for meals (great food and no one has to cook - can't beat that) and other activities during the day. It really is an ideal vacation for a family of any size. Oh, did I mention it's located right on the beach, just north of Santa Barbara? The accomodations are like condos -- one big sitting area, and either 2 to 4 bedrooms around it. It's a great blend of privacy and camaraderie. We're all looking forward to Year 5 this summer!
label: POS

text: My tour of mediocre Philly nail salons continues. My most recent stop: Allure Nails. First impression was terrible. I walk in and a woman in the middle of a pedicure glares at me. "Hi, do you do pink and whites?" Her: "No!" She then goes back to the pedicure. Yep, that was it. I look at the menu. "Well it says you do on your menu!" Her: She flat out ignores me at this point. Another woman comes over and says no pink and whites today (basically they didn't feel like it?). Ok fine, ladies, I'll just take a plain manicure. I sit down and wait about 10 minutes. The second lady finally has time for the manicure and does a half assed job. My entire nail bed wasn't even painted on some nails. I went home and added my own topcoat of seche vite because I was confident this manicure wouldn't even last a day. I've had the WORST luck with inexpensive nail salons in Philly. I may be going to Rescue Rittenhouse all of the time (tres pricey), because there are just no decent options in CC . Allure, learn some customer service!!

text: This place was a colossal disappointment. I am, as a rule, a fan of anything flamboyant. Especially when said theatrics are entirely unnecessary. Therefore, I am a fan of Japanese barbeques, which are typically home to over-the-top flourishes, juggled utensils, food flicked around, and eggs opened in midair. But not at this location. The guy got up and cooked our food. It was entirely pointless that we got to watch him. I've seen people mixing ingredients before, and do not consider it high entertainment (at least not high enough to justify $15 an entrée). What's more is that the food was strictly mediocre. Better than take-out, sure, but not by a whole lot. To compound this, the guy made me the wrong meal: he added teriyaki to my chicken. When confronted on the issue, he offered me some steak, about ten pieces, and considered us settled up. Plus, I never got a refill on my Diet Coke. I hate to say it, but avoid this place. It's overpriced, uninteresting, the service is terrible, and the food disappointing. It didn't have dirt on the floors or anything though. That's worth something, I guess.
label: NEG

text: Just want to update because although this review was written a long time ago, I want to reiterate how awesome Culpepper's is. My co-workers and I liken Culpepper's to Cheers as "sometimes you want to go where everybody knows your name..." Okay, well they don't know our names, but they do know our orders, always get our food out quickly, and always do so with a smile. It always makes you wonder if you go out to lunch too much when the serving staff knows you well enough to give you little updates about their life...and you actually care enough to know these details! (ie: our server today, who is always sweet and wonderful, is graduating this weekend!) I've been to several different locations, and the Central West End one is by far the best. I pass at least 4 different locations to get to this one, but it's still the location we go to when we want to share a local favorite with out-of-town guests. Right now I'm stuck on the Buffalo Chicken Wrap - but lots of stuff there is amazing. I've never been disappointed with any of the food selections I've made. Keep rockin', Culpepper's - CWE. We'll be back.
