text: I feel like I should have something witty to say about this place, but I'm just going to lay it out there. They make some damn good food. And. They are nice. On the couple of trips my other half and I have made to Nora's so far (soon to be many, many more trips), I've had the portabella sandwich, the potato party soup, the potato salad, and the hemp salad. It was all sooo fantastic, and I think this place could win some amazing soup awards. The party potato soup is rich and creamy- please don't tell me the calorie count. What I don't know can't hurt me, right? I had the wheat bread on my portabella sandwich- it was so fresh and tasted the way bread should taste. My meat-loving boyfriend even adored the help salad and I wouldn't be surprised if one day he orders it on his own. It's huge, so lucky for him I had enough left to share. The potato salad is just about perfect- no extra nonsense that you don't need. Just good old potatoes, mayo and mustard. MMMMMMMMM. Serious comfort food. He's had the Hangover and the Pete's Sake sandwiches on wheat. Needless to say, Nora's is now his favorite sandwich place of all time and he's vowed to try everything on the menu. A bowl of the chicken tortilla soup stole his heart and now he's considering asking the owner if he can move in. I might have to beg for the recipe! Nora, we'll be back tomorrow. text: This is hands down the best liquor store in the county, and in my opinion the best wine selection in town. I love the atmosphere at this place. However, the atmosphere here is worth mentioning. The place is massive, clean and bright. Wine is kept in beautiful wood boxes, I just love the way this place feels. Also, they have a massive wine selection. The wines are organized by country and state. The Missouri section is pretty amazing and so far is the only place that I have been able to find Adam Puchta wines...(my boyfriend and mother are both huge fans and were ecstatic I found it so close). Also, the staff is really helpful. If you are looking for something specific and don't feel like making the drive to see if they have it, just call them. They will check the store, and if they have only one bottle left, they will hold it for you until you can get there. Also, they sell pocket shots. If you aren't in the know, these are one shot sized plastic baggies of liquor...perfect for hiding in your pockets (hence, pocket shots) for concerts or sporting events if you are trying to save a few bucks. I just love this place....Five stars for sure.

text: Stayed here 3 days with family/kids in April 2010. The place itself if pretty nice, and the staffers made a good effort at accommodating their guests. Suite I had was pretty nice too -- good condition (not great), but spacious and fair price for what I got. The Spa (my wife used) was also pretty good. However.... Safety Harbor has to decide what it wants to be - there's higher end /paying clients at the spa and who are trying to enjoy the place, but they're juxtaposed with a bevy of low-life folks hanging by the pool getting drunk. There's also all kinds of smoking at the pool area -- nowhere to get away from it. Worst-- a belligerent and drunk man was stumbling about the premises on a Saturday night, yelling and falling down drunk, with his primped girlfriend clacking about in her high heels, and all the staff tip-toeing around them. Most bizarre scene I've beheld at a resort. I asked one staffer where security was to take the yelling man out of there and was told, "that would be the owner, sir..." So, you are the company you keep. This place could be really nice, but the owners need to think about this: is this their private playground or is it a Spa and Resort, catering to a high-end client. Right now, it sure seems the former. Again, the staff themselves were great. The restaurant, surrounding town, the spa itself , and nearby scenery are fantastic. But the management here is poor and seems to be encouraging a certain class of tattooed, binge-drinking, chain-smoking, walk-ins to take over the pool, which just brings the place down, at the expense of other guests' experience. Clean up your act, fellas - your staff and guests deserve better. For $400/night, your guests expect a lot more.

text: Sometimes when I'm feeling antsy, and need to take a break from my normal salon (Salon Royal Court), I head on over to Victor at Oggi. My mom has been a devoted client of his for years, and her hair always looks gorgeous. I have very pin-straight, unfussy hair, and I've become quite spoiled in that I don't like to really spend tons of time messing with it and styling it. One would think it's pretty hard to mess up straight hair, but oh has it been done! But at Oggi, I've always left with a wonderful cut. I love that Victor listens to exactly what I want and uses his expertise to give me a gorgeous, flowing, shapely cut that I can even let air dry without compromising its style. It falls beautifully in all the right ways and gives my Peppermint Patty-esque hair life! I usually grow my hair out very long to donate it to Locks of Love, and everytime I have them cut off a ponytail to donate, it is done meticulously and the actual haircut after never suffers! He creates wonderful bangs as well, which is definitely an art form in itself. Getting bangs can be a terrifying experience, and only the slightest snip can ruin the entire look for months. Not here! The staff is also pretty friendly which is nice. Last visit I had a severely broken foot and was on crutches, and they made arrangements for me to have my hair washed downstairs rather than climbing to the third floor, even though I insisted I could've made it! Wonderful customer service, and all without making a big deal or having me feel silly or embarrassed about my injury (and the toddle that accompanied it!). The front desk can sometimes leave a little to be desired, but all in all, for all the great looks I've gotten from here, I will definitely return.

text: Several months back I was driving all over Reno to every drug store pharmacy type place I could think of.... I needed an (apparently) very obscure hair product that was probably much more popular in the 80's (that crazy spray on temporary hair color stuff - a great addition to any costume or themed party!). So now I'm somewhat of an expert on CVS stores and Walgreens. This CVS was a creeper.... even at 3 in the afternoon. Its in a bad neighborhood, and the parking lot is awkwardly huge, so it makes the neighborhood look even worse because there is a ton of asphalt with this square CVS building in the middle. There were kids loitering with their ADORABLE white bulldog who I wanted to pet (but I was scared of the kids lol) - They were getting eyed by the employees the whole time. I got the feeling like theft and general criminal acts might be a common fear of the employees. Everyone seemed a little on edge. The store is much bigger than the others, but half of it is devoted to beer and liquor so it doesn't make the selection any better than the other locations. That being said, they didn't have what I needed :/ So I walked out.... the wrong way.... I ended up in the entrance turn around thing that I wasn't supposed to be in - so the layout out is a bit strange. A while later I was in the neighborhood and needed some Tylenol and figured it would be MUCH cheaper at CVS than the Raleys across the street (it was like 10pm this time, and MUCH creepier). I asked to use their bathroom and they said No, only for paying customers. So I grabbed my Tylenol and asked again at the checkout stand (since I was a paying customer). They kinda looked at me, and looked at each other, and said, no we locked it cause we are closing in 30 minutes. Oh darn :( Honestly its totally understandable since I bet they have bums trying to use their bathrooms all the time - to take showers in the sink and stuff - but just so others know, if you have a potty emergency don't pull into CVS, drive on down to the McDonald's maybe :) All in all, it is a CVS almost like any other - but I say keep on driving to the next nearest pharmacy (I like the one on California/Mayberry).

text: Urban Outfitters. I'm going to hand them two stars for a couple of reasons. Their staff, for some reason, screws up a lot when I buy from there. I think flirting with each other and acting cool distracts the staff, but I'm okay with that because it's always in my favor. And time to time you can find something worth buying here. Not so much lately, but it's usually a pair of shoes or a dress. For example, a few years ago I found a second pair of the perfect soft, kind of floppy black combat boots here for $15. The first pair I got for almost the same price, as a result of a $25 store credit I received when it took two weeks to receive something I paid for two day shipping on. And I found the perfect opaque black tights on sale on their website for $2.99. Okay, two-stars. But for the most part, they're extremely over-priced and low-quality. Their selection of clothes becomes more and more boring every season and rather than selling unique pieces or novelties, they tailor their selection to what hipsters are doing NOW. They sell custom fixed-gear bikes on their website now - this is obviously a Philadelphia company. I used to love this store. My impression of Urban Outfitters in 2009 is that they are trying to emulate the hipster experience for lazy hipsters with money to waste. Everyone has been teasing Abercrombie & Fitch for years about their fake vintage $70 paper thin t-shirts and Urban Outfitters is basically the exact same. I agree with one of the previous reviews. Save your money and go next door to buy quality products from American Apparel and make your own style and break in your own t-shirts.
label: NEG

text: As of this writing, Le Viet is not "officially open." Their grand opening is April 11, 2010. I guess they wanted to do a soft open and we happened catch them during this period. First, this place is brand new. Atmosphere is really modern - sharp lines, fancy lighting, walnut tables, pretty trendy design. Wait, this is on Washington Ave? It's like a Banana Republic fell on flea market - a huge departure from the rest of the Asian Washington Ave offerings. How does it compare to Nam Phoung and Viet Huong? (1/2 a block away?) Based on the pho and the charbroiled pork plate we got, I'd say it's on par. The crabmeat and white asparagus soup was pretty good - kind of like Chinese fish maw soap. I don't know how to rate this place. It's certainly not bad. But the food we had wasn't better than our usual Nam Phoung and Viet Huong. At the end of the day, are you will to pay a 25% price premium for the fancy atmosphere and the marginally better service? Le Viet is betting you will.
label: POS

My choice of indulgence today was their beer-battered pickles with a horseradish dip; great bar food and for all my jew friends, they're kosher! Other previous choices have included a hefeweisen hummus, which was sent from the gods. Also their leek mac-n-cheese, tasty, but a little heavy as a lone entree. They do a great job of tying their bar into the menu with selections that incorporate beers into the menu items. Great food, even better beer, and best of all, you can bring your dog into the bar area!

Choosing just one dessert when your here is never an easy task. text: I don't usually like to write so-so to bad reviews because my mother always taught me "if you don't have something nice to say, don't say anything at all." Luckily, I'm being reimbursed by my company for my stay because otherwise, I'd be livid. The room literally stunk. I thought it might have just been my room, so I requested another one. Nope, that one smelled too. So I called my boss who was also staying there to ask her if her room smelled. Apparently, it did. She said she couldn't take it so she opened 2 packs of coffee spread it around the room and used the door as a fan to try to circulate the "aroma." Well, I don't like coffee, nor do I want to smell like it, so I was SOL. Marriott honestly needs to either do some renovations and change out all the carpets, fix the apparent mold problem, invest in Febreze, or better yet, do ALL! Also, for it to be DE, I thought the price of the room was kinda high. Maybe I'm underestimating our "first state," but for $140 on a Monday night, I expect a normal smelling room, a flat panel TV and HBO or some other movie channel. Instead, I got a musty smelling room as my boss put it, a tube TV and no movies. The only reason I'm giving this review 2 stars as opposed to 0 is because this isn't actually coming out of my pocket plus Mia at the front desk was a true sweetheart. I can tell she was honestly apologetic and surprised about the smell of the room. Clearly, she stays in the lobby and goes nowhere near the rooms...lol! I think Customer Service has a lot of value and it showed here. I'll stop for now. I feel a bit bad for this post, but I'm just being honest!

text: Breakfast at Mother's defines what southern style breakfast should be. While visiting New Orleans, my favorite and only taxi driver from day one to last day, Ms. Creole, recommended me to come to Mother's for breakfast, lunch and dinner. It is located close to downtown area and 5 short blocks from French Quarter. Lucky us, it was close to the hotel my dad and I stayed. I chose to eat breakfast here twice because of their best grit, THE BEST house made Blackened Ham, yum yum yum Andouille sausage, biscuit and scrambled egg. Breakfast here is hearty and the line convinced my dad to stop thinking about a diet and fruity breakfast. If you look for lean, Special K with milk, Granola and fruit....sorry mama Mother's doesn't serve low fat or low carb breakfast. Side butter is equal two stick of butter!! Everything is tasty, greasy, buttery and homey. It is a N.O. food landmark and a place N.O. people know well. Go hungry, leave there hungry for more and more visit. Line is ridiculously long but worth a trip. Lucky me, I went there earlier than 7am. I have never seen any place having a line starting this early.

text: This is the tour we should have taken on our first day in New Orleans. Jeff is a credit not only to the tour guide profession but to the city of New Orleans as well. If you take only one guided tour of N.O., take this one. It's a three-hour easy bike ride through parts of the French Quarter you won't see if you're just walking from Bourbon Street, and adjoining neighborhoods. You'll see the architecture, people and changing face of the city, and with Jeff's deep knowledge, you'll get an instant history lesson. Everything from New Orleans' founding to Creole culture to the mechanics of a funeral parade. Great trivia, like the origin of the name of the game of chance we now call craps; how the Po Boy sandwich originated; why a road median is called neutral ground in the city. He'll also dispense great advice on where to the get the best food, drink and music in New Orleans. Jeff's full of energy and knows his stuff, and he can weave tales while seamlessly leading you through the streets without getting run down by traffic.
label: POS

text: For the person that thinks there is a better minor league field in the world...get real. Anyway, the prices are dirt cheap, cheap enough that you don't really have to plan ahead to go to a game, you can just decide you want to go, and tickets are $8 and the never really sell out, because let face it, no amount of cool ball park-age can save a bad minor league team. The beer is cheaper than any majo league park and they have a dollar night, one dollar dogs and other snacks, which is almost a reason to go on its own. My mother had the Signature salad which was also delicious, the chicken was prepared the same way as it was on my caesar and the steak came out perfectly cooked (nice and rare) without her even asking for it that way. text: Just today I tried to get my prescription refilled and the automated system told me it was too soon. When I finally got through to a real person, she was nice and helpful and I told her that I noticed on the bottle they had crossed out the "60" and put in "30" (For the amount of pills dispensed). On the bottle, it clearly says I'm to take 1 pill twice a day. So I should have had 60 pills. She said she would do some research and see if they owed me any pills and maybe that was what had happened. I waited for a while, and then a guy comes on the phone and was not very kind or understanding from the start. Of course I had to tell him the whole story again like I had told the previous person. He said what had happened was they had to mix and match my pills (using different brands) and they put them into two separate bottles. I told him I didn't have two bottles. I told him I knew they had to mix and match them because they told me that, but that when I opened the ONE bottle that they were all mixed in together. He said it was strange that they were all mixed in the bottle together but that for whatever reason it happened that way. I told him I wasn't trying to be rude but since they were all mixed in one bottle and shouldn't have been I asked if it was possible that they forgot my second bottle, because I sure didn't remember it. He was short and rude with me and said "Impossible! We triple check those things!" Obviously his employees aren't human and are above making mistakes. I find it funny that he thought it was strange that the pills were mixed together in one bottle when he said they normally aren't, but he was positive that they gave me a second bottle. I only found out he was the manager by asking. He didn't introduce himself on the phone, he wasn't nice at all. He was cold, short, and rude with me. He made me feel like I was trying to get extra pills, or like I was a crazy pill-popping idiot. The medicine I'm on is for anxiety, and I can tell you that dealing with a rude pharmacy manager doesn't help my issue. I'll be switching pharmacies!

text: I tried my first European-style hot drinking chocolate here! And thank goodness that they offer petite sizes - boy, was it dense. text: Valentine's Day 2009 will forever be on the Worst Dinner Ever List, thanks to Lorenzo's. I booked a reservation for Saturday, Feb. 14 several weeks in advance. Having worked in the service industry, both my boyfriend and I knew that it was going to be a crazy night (Valentine's day AND a Saturday night on The Hill? Yowsers!) and were expecting to wait. No biggie. When we arrived at 7:15 for our 7:30 reservation, the lobby was a crowded mess! Turns out that they had double-booked all of their reservations and were running an hour behind. Waiting at the bar was even unpleasant because the one bartender was super stressed and couldn't handle the large amount of drink requests. Oh and he wasn't allowed to run tabs for people, so he was forced to run cards for every round of drinks. While waiting for our table, there was no manager present to help the overworked bartender or the poor young girls working the front desk, who had to face the wrath from a hungy customer every few mintues. No apologies, no free drinks, just a crazy mess. When we finally got to our table at around 8:45, we weren't even hungry! Just annoyed and a little tipsy from the 3 glasses of wine each we had while waiting at the bar. Our server was OK and the food was alright, but not worth the hour and a half wait. We want our $100+ night back! Next year, we'll call ahead and reserve a table at White Castle. At least we know the cheese fries are worth the wait :)

text: Wow, I was sorely disappointed at this restaurant considering the reviews it has here. First off, it was a warm evening, no cool wind, and the restaurant was uncomfortably warm. No A/C that I could feel blowing to make it feel better. I don't know how people could eat with the lighting at night...just a little too dark for me to enjoy my dinner. On to the food. In a word, bland. The only good thing about the meal was the appetizer, which consisted of the hot combination platter. The beer boiled shrimp, garlic clams, Oysters Rockefeller were all delicious. I decided to try the clam chowder just to compare to ones I've had before, and it was the first of many disappointments. Just way too bland, and I could barely taste the clam broth or whatever clam flavor needed to be in there. I decided on the blackened cajun tilapia for an entree, and again, surprisingly bland. Besides the appetizer, the other upside to the experience is the service. Prompt and friendly. Otherwise, this was a complete letdown.

text: Short review - Hell on earth. Not as short review - A Walmart is what it is: a poorly lit warehouse where one goes to obtain toiletries and 5 pound bags of rice on the cheap. You don't go to find last year's styles or even something that was fashionable 5 years ago. The stereotypical clientele has been documented on tumblr blogs aplenty, but one doesn't really pay much attention to them as you dash in and out in hasty fashion. The South Philly Walmart takes every terrible impression you have about this chain and multiplies the pain you feel by how many items you have to purchase during your shopping excursion. There's never a cart to be found at the entrance because they're littered about the store. The ones you do find has three rickety wheels and a screeching that would force a sane man to puncture his ear drums to cease the misery. The shoppers are oblivious to anything outside of their headspace, plowing you over to get the last jar of peanut butter you intended to buy. The layout of the store isn't intuitive, as the last item you have to pick up is never in the spot where it would be in any other big box store. And, if you require assistance, the best bet is to just hit up a person on a register because there's no chance you'll find someone on the floor. That's what I learned as a customer butted in while I was checking out in the express lane. Oh, did the cashier ask him to wait? Of course not. She departed her station to help the guy not find the razor blades he sought out. If I want to lose faith in humanity, this Walmart is a wonderful place to start. If a place has me ponder "wait a second, the South Philly Target is a wonderful store!", you know they're doing something very, very wrong.

text: The Breeze, formerly Greek Islands, was yet another installment on my still unsuccessful quest for a good falafel in Nashville. I was excited at first because they had spanakopita on the menu. It's one of my very favorite Greek dishes, but a hard to find one. This one might as well not have been found. The filo on top was thick and mushy instead of delicate and flaky. I didn't taste any of the feta or onions supposedly inside, just a thin layer of spinach. It was served with some sort of sweet dried fruit stuff, the addition of which remains a mystery. When my falafel platter arrived I was glad to see it lived up to its platter name; the servings were generous. Unfortunately, the falafels were the small, hard type and not too flavorful. The highlight of the meal was the salad. It actually had taste to it and they were generous with the toppings. I started taking bites of it with every other item on my plate and it took the meal from disappointing to acceptable. The waitress was also a highlight. She was sweet and efficient. She offered me an extra glass of diet coke with to go with my box which is something a lot of places on grudgingly oblige. She was working alone, but seemed to have a perfect handle of the lunch crowd. The price is what pushed my rating down from a 2 star to 1. The whole meal (appetizer, entree, soda) plus her 20% cost me a whopping $23. I have enough left over for a full meal later, but that still seems like an exorbitant amount for the quality of the food.

text: It was almost 2pm on a Saturday when we decided to get sushi for lunch. The Thai/Japanese combo was a little peculiar but we were starving so we gave it a shot. There were only 2 other tables occupied and our server arrived with a big smile. We ordered the "Love Shrimp" which was 6 grilled shrimp on skewers with a Thai spicy (really spicy) dipping sauce. The shrimp were fresh and tasty. We love the spicy but maybe not when you're going to eat something as delicate as sushi/sashimi afterwards since your taste buds need a minute to get back to normal in between bites. Also, the Thai chili spicy and the Japanese wasabi spicy get you at different spicy levels so that's also something to think about. Then I got the Sushi Combo which was 7 orders of sushi (chef's choice, I like that) plus a choice of Cal or spicy tuna roll. I got the latter. The chef's choice for the day was, yellowtail, tuna, seared tuna, albacore, salmon, mackerel and...can't remember one more. I loved 5 out of the 7 and the spicy tuna was good, not great. What I loved about the sushi was how small the rice was. My pet peeve is sushi with big roll of rice. The sashimi slices were really thick (borderline too thick) and big but 5 out of 7 were so tasty, even when my little ball of rice was already gone. It was like I had the sashimi plate. The salmon was also exceptional. My husband had an order of his favorite, salmon sushi, as well as the shrimp and asparagus tempura roll. He liked them both and ate most of my spicy tuna roll. So the sashimi quality was great. I'm not sure why they decided to combine Thai and Japanese...the decor was a bit mismatched and confusing. I'm not sure if I'd go here if I wanted Thai food. They should really start a lunch special bento box or a lunch-sized sushi combo to feed the lunch crowd. They only have one menu for lunch/dinner but it's basically a dinner menu so the prices are a bit high for lunch and so are the portions. I would definitely like to see them do a busier lunch with a lunch menu.

When in chicago, there are many nights when I long for the comfort of the the Yardley Inn bar, the flowing cocktails, and the unbeatable food. I almost always order off the bar menu, for lighter, more upscale pub grub, but I absolutely LOVE the ungreedy option of a smaller plate vs. the hungry man's plate you'll find on the dinner menu. In the summertime, the chef makes a MEAN lobster roll, I think you'd have to travel on up to the Mystic to find the next best one. The Yardley Burger is a greasy monster of a gourmet burger, the filets are usually cooked perfectly, and the crispy sesame crakery type things they give you to munch on are hard to quit eating. Oh... also, Y.I. tweets great deals every now and again that only the tech savvy are in the know on, so make sure you follow them on Twitter!

text: I've been neglecting the West End for quite some time. Blackstone is the perfect place to get my toe wet again. I probably go there once every two months. Guests? Let's hit the Blackstone! The fish and chips are the best I have had in Nashville. I miss Edinburgh Castle's (ok really Old Chelsea's) fish and chips. The Blackstone has been a good enough replacement. The only thing that is missing is the newspaper. As for the decor the Blackstone is like the Winchester Mansion, surprises whichever way you turn. The bar is centralized, off to the left is the patio, then moving clockwise you have a fire place, couches and oriental rugs, then you have the dining room and beyond that I think there is a special events area. I'm pretty sure last time we were there someone was having a rehearsal dinner. The beer is definitely the highlight. We bought one of the high alcohol beers and the guy had to walk us out to hand over the bottle. The pretzels are also a highlight. Hands down I like Village Pubs beer cheese dip but if I were to forgo the cheese I would definitely venture out to the B-Stone. Overall a solid West End eatery and brewhouse. text: "It was a cold and rainy day in March. I went to Kristoff's where I usually get my hair done. But Kristoff wasn't there. He had mysteriously disappeared. In his place was a stranger named... Rinaldo. I'll never forget him. His eyes were steely gray. His hands were like ICE. He said 'I'll streak your hair and I'll give you a body wave.' He worked very fast and then, as he turned my chair around to face the mirror... I saw it... HE PERMED ME!" I'm sure many of you remember this story from the oh-so-campy eighties movie, Troop Beverly Hills. Well, it was the exact scene that came to mind after a recent hair misfortune. My story goes a little something like this: It was a hot and sticky day in July. I was in Boca Raton, where I never get my hair done. Luckily, I had my Paul Mitchell products, the hotel hair dryer, and my straightener named... Chi. I'll never forget it. The cord was long and black. The hot plates had always made my hair look nice. I plugged the bad boy in and then got to work with the dryer. Then, with a lion's mane of fully-dried, poofy hair, I picked up the Chi. That's when I noticed... MY STRAIGHTENER HAD DIED ON ME! AHHHHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!!!! (blood curdling screams) ______________________________________________________ You don't even want to know what my hair looked like that day! Luckily, I flew home that night and set my alarm for the following morning, a Sunday, so that I could go to Bed, Bath and Beyond first thing and replace my most valuable hair tool. At five til 10, I stood outside the BBB like a crazed animal waiting for a feeding. Finally, the manager unlocked the doors and I stalked to the beauty section, a woman possessed. A nice (scared?) employee unlocked the case containing the pricier beauty appliances and retrieved my Chi. Moments later, the manager graciously approved a price match, based on a picture from Ulta's website that I conjured up on my iPhone, as I could not produce a hard-copy flier since Ulta was not yet open for the day. Even better, the good people at the register accepted my 20% off coupon. 96 dollars later, I raced back home with my wonderful new replacement, purchased significantly lower than the suggested retail price.

text: My wife and I started going to Salsa's when it opened a few years ago, and it was good, basic Tex Mex at reasonable prices in a friendly atmosphere before or after shopping at Montgomery Mall. Then, a year or so ago, the food started to suffer and we stopped going. The guacamole wasn't very good any more, the seafood enchalada dishes were mediocre. Not even a cold, 22 oz mug of Dos Equis can make up for bad food. Other people must have felt the same way, because every time we walked past on our way into or out of the mall, the crowds seemed to get smaller and smaller. We figured it was just a matter of time before they went out of business. But this past weekend, we walked by and saw a big Saturday evening crowd. So we thought, maybe they've gotten it together again, and decided to give it another try. Big mistake. Huge. From the moment we sat down, our server exhibited a negative attitude toward us, and there was nothing we said or did to encourage this. My wife ordered cheese nachos and asked for some pico de gallo on top -- rather than beef or beans. When the dish arrived, it was puny -- just a small handful of warm chips with a little melted white cheese -- and no pico de gallo. I tried to get the server's attention, but he ignored us. Finally, I managed to get him to stop at our table and, rather than do battle with him, asked to see the manager. The manager came over, was very polite, listened to my wife's complaint about her dish, and promptly put the order in again. This time, it came out exactly as she had requested. My dish, a chicken enchalada platter, was pretty good, nothing spectacular, but no complaints except that it wasn't quite as hot as it might have been. Our server didn't bother to ask if everything was okay after that. In fact, he didn't stop by even once to see if we needed anything. He simply dropped off the bill when it was obvious we were finished -- without saying a word to us. And to add insult to injury, he added an order of guacamole to our bill that we never asked for -- thus causing another trip to see the manager to have the item removed. The last time I stiffed a server on a tip was 35 years ago, and I really hate to take that kind of action because I feel that servers routinely take a lot of crap from many customers who treat them badly, and I never want to be counted among them. But this time I felt it necessary to stiff our server out of the few bucks tip he would have earned had he treated us a little better. So, is it too much to ask that, when a server makes a mistake on an order, he or she tries to make sure the customer is satisfied that the error has been rectified? Is it too much to ask that a restaurant train its staff to treat people with a minimum level of respect? I know these are rhetorical questions, and I don't expect a place like Salsa's to get it. But it helps to vent, and if a single restaurant can learn from these kinds of situations, my rant will have been worth the effort. Needless to say, we won't be going back to Salsa's any time soon, and probably never. Adios!
label: NEG

The recipe was different from what I'm used to, being from Maine (it involved green peppers), but it was quite good; I was surprised, however, that the cakes themselves were squishy and not crispy on the outside. Really don't know if this is specific to the locale, or the restaurant. They weren't bad, but I definitely prefer them more... cooked. text: 6 of us went for a friday night Restuarant week dinner. My first mistake was forgetting to read Yelp before making a last minute reservation. Luckily that was not done to our friends because if so, we would probably all had to get up and leave...or maybe it should've.... Our waitress was OK. She didn't give us any bread. She came once in a while. She didn't ask everyone how the food was. We had another waiter that guided us to our upstairs table, poured our wine for us. I think he took offense at my husband's comment or story. After he gave my husband the testing of the wine (half price all night on fridays), my husband mentioned to the table about how he knows some other guy that makes a big deal out of it. Well the waiter decided to join our conversation, which is normally fine, but his tone was rather sarcastic. We were supposed to laugh at his jokes but it was more like he is making fun of customers, which were us. Food: our food came slowly and 3 trips at a time. Therefore, everyone would have to wait extra long to eat. Some of us ordered the restuarant week menu. The appetizers were not very good looking to me. But we were so hungry we all finished it. The chill platter came with 2 slices of "rare" tuna, a bite of cocktail shrimp and 2 oysters. The color of the tuna was TOO red. It looked almost fake. I will see if my husband goes to the bathroom a lot tonight. No one talked about the oysters so I am assuming it was edible only. I had the seafood corn chowder which came luke warm and had 1 baby shrimp. We waited forever after the appetizers. So when the wine guy came back I asked for some bread. He replied with a very sarcastic Yes sure. The 2 chunks of bread were not enough for 6 people and it was cold. Like sitting in the fridge cold. Once again, I was still hungry so I ate it. Our entrees were luke warm and arrived in 3 batches again. The halibut was tasteless. It was breaded and served with huge couscous. My mahi mahi was dry and previously frozen. It actually looked very amateur. Like something someone tried to make at home. It came with sweet potato crab hash with bbq sauce. All I tasted was BBq sauce, dry fish and I saw some bits of crab meat at the end. And yes, I ate that too because I was still hungry and also the thought of how much I was spending bugged me. My husband ordered the chocolate cup with mouse for dessert. That was eh OK. I am glad I didnt pay extra $5 for dessert. Our friend didnt finish hers at all. She didnt finish her entree either. Our bill for 2 of us came to almost $100. We should've gone to ur favorite Shinju sushi instead. This is very disappointing because we have been to other McCormicks before and they are always excellent. Atlanta, Austin etc. This location is a shame for the whole chain. I do not recommend coming to this place, esp if there is an advertised good deal. I know they have cheap happy hours but I would not waste that money. text: Which is worse: a restaurant with terrible food and great service, or one with great food and terrible service? The former won't stay in business, so it's pretty harmless. The latter, however, will stick around for years to infuriate countless patrons. Why won't it close? People who have heard the promise of the cuisine will continue to seek out this establishment, assuming that the stories of poor service are overstated, or perhaps imagining that it's charming in a "Soup Nazi" sort of way. It will stay in business because nobody can quite comprehend how bad the service will be. Until they experience it. Again and again. And by the time they realize just how wretched and demoralizing each meal is, they've already contributed to the circle of life that keeps this restaurant afloat. This brings me to Siam in Lambertville. I will concede that it has some of the best Thai food around. However the service leaves more than a little to be desired. I will sum up my feelings about Siam with a couple examples of my experiences there over the years: 1. The Crying Vegetarian. Before I met my wife, I had a vegetarian girlfriend. She wasn't vegan, but she was veggie in a pretty serious way -- such that she would read all the product ingredients at the supermarket to make sure there wasn't a hint of anything meat-like (e.g. the picoliter of anchovy in a bottle of worcestershire sauce). We stopped into Siam on a sunny afternoon, and she was delighted to find one of the specials listed as "vegetarian". Halfway through eating it (nay, devouring it), she gave me a sour look that I knew couldn't be good news. She called over the waiter to inquire about the "vegetarian" status of her entree. Yes, of course it has fish sauce, explained the waiter rather matter-of-factly. But it's called a vegetarian dish! A vegetarian dish can't be made with fish sauce! So did this get an apology, perhaps an offer of at least a replacement meal, if not a free one? No, because it was HER fault, he explained: she didn't *explicitly* state that she wanted the vegetarian entree prepared without fish sauce. Cut to tearful girlfriend freaking out. Cut to my look of disbelief at what had just transpired. Cut to miserable, silent drive home from Lambertville. 2. Count the shrimp. Before we married, my wife and I went to Lambertville fairly often to visit friends who live there. On one such visit, somebody suggested that we hit Siam for dinner. Having put "the crying vegetarian" behind me, I went along with this plan. As luck would have it, three out of the four of us had Thai Basil Shrimp on the brain that evening. After the appetizers, out came the entrees... OK, out came two of the entrees. One Thai Basil Shrimp and one "other". Hmmm, that's funny, we ordered three Thai Basil Shrimp, not one. That IS three Thai Basil Shrimp, we were told -- all together on one plate. Now I'm all OK with family-style dining. But this was really ONE order of shrimp, maybe TWO if you stretch it, but no way was this THREE orders worth of shrimp. Of course our server insisted that it was, showing more than a little irritation with our gall to suggest otherwise. So the three of us began playing "count the shrimp" to make sure that we all got equally screwed by this miserly portion of food. Was it good? Of course it was, which makes it even more infuriating to watch the entire meal disappear in a matter of seconds. From the tab we split that night, you'd have thought we'd dined in style. But from the fact that both couples ended up ordering pizza later that night (no joke), I can't help but remember this as The Last Time I Will Ever Eat At Freakin' Siam!

text: Phonoluxe is the black sheep of the Nashville record store family. You've got the Ernest Tubb Record Shop downtown (and the tourist hole annex at Opry Mills) which is recognized, because of its tourist appeal, as the patriarch of the whole family. Then there's the Great Escape, the matriarch of the family, with its flourishing and oft-times overbearing store down on Broadway and all its children spread out across the Southeast living their own lives but never straying too far from home. She means well, but sometimes she can really get up your ass. Grimey's is the cool aunt. Ya know, the one who comes to family functions wearing a leather jacket and proceeds to drink too much wine, then steals you and a few of your cooler cousins away to tell you stories about how she used to hang out with the Ramones and Patti Smith in NYC. But Phonoluxe, well, the family tries not to mention him. He's the uncle that time forgot, the weird one, that one that you weren't really allowed to hang out with when you were a kid. But then you got a little older, out from under the protection of mom's skirts, and you found out that Uncle Phonoluxe was, well, he was kind of awesome. So you'd sneak over there with a little money and a few beers that you managed to steal from your dad's fridge, you know, back in the early days of your Kerouac stage, and you'd just sit and listen to Uncle Phonoluxe for hours. He'd tell you stories of big legged women who were loose with their charms and who would whisper the secrets of the universe to you as you drifted off to sleep in their arms. Or stories of keen eyed road warriors whose world was built of leather and chrome and rock and roll. Or maybe he'd let you in on the world of the juke joints, with their ribald men and women, howling like a pack of wild, hungry dogs into the great gaping night of the world, wanting like nothing else to be heard above the roar of evil and despair and ignorance. Uncle Phonoluxe was shabby and wild-eyed, and it wasn't always easy to be around him when things got rough, but the things he taught you were the things that would save your life on all those dark, wicked nights that you would encounter throughout your nomadic twenties. Dad may have provided for the family, mom may have shepherded you through the days of your childhood, and cool aunt Grimey may be the family member you speak to the most, but there's not a day goes by that you don't think about Uncle Phonoluxe, and everything he showed you.

The Shrimp bisque was infused with such aromatics that it tantalized the sense. The texture of the bisque was silky but not overly creamy very nice balance. The pork slider flavors were like and explosion in my mouth. Perfectly juicy and the spice tang was spot on. The sliders came with the skinny sesame fries and aioli sauce was perfectly crisp with a soft center. Yum!! Now the the crispy tuna tacos was quite a nice twist on the regular taco fare. The tuna is served sashimi style and oh so buttery melt in your mouth taste. The "taco" is made to look like regular taco but which I suspect is egg roll wrapping. The service was attentive but not to the point of exaggeration. Overall, the experienced can be summed up to being sublime. We cant wait to try dinner as it is a totally different menu!

text: We stayed here for a week. This is our second time staying in a Hotel Indigo - last year we stayed for a week in the West End location. I very very (very very, very very) very much prefer the downtown location (NOT West End) - we were on the 12th floor here and had no complaints about water pressure. The W.E. location had poor pressure, lukewarm water, toilets that refused to flush, sinks that drained slowly/not at all.. We had none of those issues here. The room was beautiful, modern and clean, our floor was quiet. The hotel restaurant was OK. I had a yogurt "parfait" which consisted of about a quarter cup of yogurt with two small pieces of pineapple topping .... .... .... and how much did we pay for it? argh! ..... But the drinks in the bar were tasty and they have nice desserts. The bar hosts writer's rounds nightly, which is a great Nashville touch. The staff is super friendly, attentive and quick. I did wish that we had a fridge/microwave in room, especially since we stayed for a longer period of time. No bathtub either, but I don't mind that so much. The bed was very comfortable (firm, not cushy, which is what I like) and the linens were very clean and fresh. This is a very insignificant thing to complain about, but is a pet peeve of mine: the in-room coffee came with powdered creamer. Not that the in-room coffee was that great to begin with, but powdered creamer just makes my eyeball twitch. A minor complaint, but it makes a difference to have the good liquid stuff, even if the good stuff is still fake chemical-ly milk. TV was fine, lots of channels. The parking blows, 22 bucks a day for valet or 20 for self-park. There is no street parking. They comped us on valet parking, maybe since we were staying with them for a decent length of time, but I'm not sure if that's the official policy or not. Our room was on Union Street, and traffic rarely was noisy enough to be distracting, although there were a couple of ambulances/fire trucks that would scream down the street. We had a nice view of the pretty new City Hall building. The hotel adjoins a somewhat mediocre Starbucks, but there are some decent dining options within walking distance - Varallo's and Provence are reasonably closeby, and then you have some tasties on 2nd avenue (nachos at Buffalo Billiards are my favorite on earth. Also, try the wings at Piranha's or the cozy Beer Sellar.. if you venture down to B'way, there's the BBQ at Jack's.. text: This place bills itself as "The Cupcakery Boutique". I had to stare into the window for a few seconds before figuring out that, yes, it was actually cupcakes they were selling in there, because it looked like some combination of a jewelry store, a clothing boutique, and my grandmother's living room with a baker hoarding supplies in the back. "Be still my heart!" said my heart as I walked through the door and laid eyes upon the glass-windowed cabinets filled with a veritable bombardment of baked extravagances. I was greeted with a good deal of enthusiasm and directed to a menu. There is quite a good selection, with all the obligatory classics. My opinion, though, as always, is that if you're going to get one cupcake right, it had better be the red velvet, so red velvet it was. The man at the counter packaged the adorably Christmasy-decorated cupcake with its shiny red foil wrapper into an inverted cup with pop-on lid and gave me the cupcake to go. I wanted to eat this cupcake on the spot, but I wanted even more for this cupcake to be as perfect as possible, so I waited until I got home and put it in the microwave for a few seconds (which I highly recommend). "Please, cupcake," I whispered, as he stared up at me from the counter. "Please don't let me down." He obliged. Holy cow, did they get the red velvet right. This was probably the moistest cake I've ever tasted in a cupcake, but the cake also had a sorta-crunchy outside layer which was both pleasant and useful in holding the cupcake in one piece. The cream cheese icing was perfect (I think the microwaving set it off). It was normal sized, but slightly small for the $3 price-tag; however, it was more than worth it. Welcome to the city, Philly Cupcake. Welcome to the city and welcome to my life.

On a recent weeknight, my dining companion and I were the only ones there. Our waiter, while very nice, was over-attentive (perhaps out of sheer boredom), asking us frequently if everything was "ok." Fried calamari were heavily fried and greasy, but tasty. Steak "medallions" tasted like a Lean Cuisine I could microwave. Lukewarm and lacking sophistication. They came with an avalanche of mashed potatoes. Way too big a portion, and the potatoes were too hard. Vegetables were decent. My dining companion seemed to enjoy the lamb, which came with the same side dishes. Bread pudding was "interesting," but I can't tell if that was a good thing or not. Rarely have I ordered bread pudding that was an actual "piece of bread." The reviews in the paper said it was good. It consisted of a large piece of challah bread, warm and soft, drowned in what seemed like a pool of butter. It tasted more like french toast than dessert. I asked the waiter what the sauce was made of, and he sheepishly said something about a rum "reduction," but I'm not even sure he knows. The prices here are fairly steep for such mediocre food, but there is potential for better. The one bathroom I saw was "iffy" and you had to pass by an open kitchen to get there. Once done, our waiter asked for our names and seemed genuinely thankful that someone had come by to eat. He said business had been "good" since a move from Germantown. He said the owner was sitting at the bar downstairs and would be sure to thank us on the way out. We never saw him. Either way, the food was forgettable and I probably wouldn't return, though I'm told the brunch is good. Roxborough desperately needs some good restaurants. text: My boyfriend took me here recently for my birthday dinner, and it was truly a wonderful experience. After going there, I can definitely understand how popular it is regardless of what time of the day. The interior is wonderful - dark wood floors and furniture highlighted with creamy linens. It can feel a bit crowded when its full, but not uncomfortably so. The kitchen is also partially open to the dining area, with a bar right there (ideal eating location in my opinion), and the bar itself is on the side, partitioned off from diners. The food is delicious; it was very hard to choose only a few, especially since they offer so many traditional spanish tapas. The full entrees seem unnecessary compared to the tapas since we weren't even interested in them. We had: Escalivada: Roasted Peppers & Eggplant, Cippolini Onions & Confit Tomatoes (really good, but would skip next time) Morels Salteados: Morel Mushrooms, Thyme & White Asparagus (exquisite - its small, but very memorable) Grilled Baby Squid (simple but cooked to perfection, they were amazingly tender) Arroz de Langosta: Lobster Bomba Rice with Clams, Lemon Zest & Golden Pea Shoots (MmmMmm gooooood) Pimientos de Padron: Fried Peppers, Sea Salt & Salbitxada (delicately spicy - a must) Piquillos Rellenos: Crab-Stuffed Peppers (If you get one dish, this is the one. Amazingly good) Olas de Chocolate: Godiva Liqueur Cake, Chocolate Mousse, Milk Chocolate Ice Cream (definitely for the chocolate lover, and surprisingly large compared to the tapas) Banana Torrijas: Crispy Spanish Bread, Carmelized Bananas, Maple Syrup Ice Cream, Banana Anglaise (TO. DIE. FOR. If you like bananas, that is) We also each had a glass of sangria; I had the tinto, which was incredible and lived up to the ones I've had in Spain, while my boyfriend had their seasonal bianco with mint and mango, which he loved but was too sweet for my taste (weird, because I'm the one with the sweet tooth). The portions are smaller than some might expect, especially with some dishes, but for the two of us those 6 plates, two desserts, and sangria was perfect - however, it does leave a substantial bill at the end of the evening. However, we both agreed (especially me since I didn't pay ;D ) that it was completely worth it. And the service was spectacular, we had a very attentive, informed waiter. This is truly one of Philly's top restaurants.

When we pulled up outside the place, I was kind of surprised to see that there were meters outside. Hey, I'm a Jersey girl! I haven't spent a lot of time in Germantown, so I thought meters were just a downtown thing, for the most part. LOL When we walked in, to our surprise, there was no host to greet us. One of the cooks in the kitchen told us we could either eat upstairs or downstairs. That was a relief to hear, because "downstairs" consisted of 3 already filled tables. We went upstairs, selected our table,and decided we were feeling Urban Cafe's vibe already. What a unique mix of people. Everyone from church-goers, to college kids, to families, artsy, geeky, white, black, old and young. It was modestly furnished, but comfortable, and it was warm and cozy on this 12 degree day. We decided we loved the menu choices... your typical breakfast choices, but you could also get fish, or turkey bacon or sausage, something my bf and I took note of immediately because we aren't pork eaters and very rarely eat beef. We both ordered the Rittenhouse Scramble: eggs, crabmeat, spinach, tomato and cheese. (Although OURS was MYSTERIOUSLY missing TOMATO! LOL) It came with your choice of two sides, so I got turkey sausage and potatos, and my bf got turkey sausage and grits. Our food was DELICIOUS!!!!! Best of all, we got REAL portions, not those mini-samplers you get at MOST of the popular brunch spots!! My bf also ordered a delicious hot apple cider, served with frothy whipped cream on top. I ordered a milk chai tea, which was good, but not half as EXCITING as my bf's cider. LOL When our drinks were delivered, I was immediately sorry I didn't get what he got!! Our waitress was cool. Bubbly personality, and right there with whatever we needed. I enjoyed Urban Cafe. I would suggest they play the music a little louder, as I'm NOT a fan of other people's conversations AT ALL!!!! LOL Go..... you'll be happy you did!

text: Named for the stream that once flowed where 43rd St. is today and is now contained in a giant sewer pipe, the Millcreek Tavern has a swampy, fetid quality much like its namesake. There's no reason to go here unless: 1. You have a friend in a band that's playing here. 2. You live within two blocks. So for those of us who find ourselves still supporting our aspiring rock star friends, or for those who live in this lovely little corner of West Philly and are too lazy to hike a few extra blocks to get drunk (alas! how I miss my old apartment), here's a brief survival guide to the Millcreek. First, you should know that Millcreek has managed to duck the smoking ban, perhaps because it meets the criteria or perhaps because it's owned by an ex-cop. Be prepared to be hit with a wall of USA GOLD smoke. You should also know that it's really two connected bars. The east side (entrance on 42 and Chester) is newer and superficially less dingy. This is where your friend's band is playing, on a shitty little stage way in the back corner. The sound will be both ear-splitting and incomprehensible at the same time. The sightlines and acoustics are dreadful, so you might want to show up early to get a better seat. Don't order the food. You'll save money and get your food quicker if you pick up something a door down Chester at the Five-Star Deli. That said, if it's late (the Five-Star closes at 11), the chicken fingers will suffice. The western side (entrance on Chester) is an older bar once known as the Track and Turf. (That's why USP kids in the know call it "The Track.") This side has more character. Character is a euphemism for wood paneling, dart boards, and a colorful cast of neighborhood alcoholics. You'll also find Larry on this side. Larry is a Southwest-Philly-born-and-raised bartender with a thick Philly accent. Larry can smoke a whole Winston without once removing it from his lips. Larry will encourage you to get the pitcher. Larry may not notice that something is floating in your beer. Larry likes you more if you have breasts. I like Larry. A few other tips. The jukebox will eat your money. Larry may or may not offer a refund. The Millcreek no longer serves actual Yuengling Lager. Instead, they carry a generic lager with a phony, cheesy tap that says "Millcreek Lager." I think they pump it up directly from the 43rd St. sewer pipe.

text: Oh, Oceano - I really wanted to like you. I wanted to like you so much, that I was willing to overlook my, "only eat seafood in states that border oceans" rule. I had been waiting for the right time to visit, and when I recently found a $40 for $18 offer on a local foodie website, I happily pulled the trigger. Wow, was I disappointed. For starters, my girlfriend and I shared our dinner with several fruit flies. It wasn't just our table either. I noticed another table swatting flies as well. I was willing to overlook this, because minus the flies, the atmosphere in Oceano really is quite nice. Let's move on to the drinks. Our server took our drink order professionally enough. My girlfriend ordered a cranberry and Absolut. When the drink arrived it was mostly Absolut. The server knew the drink didn't look right, because when she set it down she said she could add more cranberry if it were too strong. It definitely needed it. Rather than take the drink back and try again, the server brought a second glass with cranberry juice in it. So now, we have to play bartender and mix our own drink at the table. We began our meal with two appetizers - oysters on the half shell, and marinated tomatoes and halloumi. The oysters were fine. Not much control a restaurant has over raw shellfish, just buy good quality and put it on the tray with some ice. I had no complaints. The other appetizer was an interesting dish. In addition to the halloumi and tomatoes, it contained grilled watermelon, arugala, and some aged balsamic. The dish had a lot going on. I couldn't understand why the tomatoes got top billing, when there were two giant pieces of grilled watermelon on the plate. Anyway, if there are any would be BBQ chefs out there - don't grill watermelon, it doesn't taste good. For dinner, I ordered the Sauteed Herb Crusted Sea Bass. No complaints about the emulsion or risotto, it was quite good, but the fish is where things started to go wrong. If the name of your establishment contains the word Ocean, the fish had better be stellar. Sea Bass should be a touch on the firm side - this was not. The fish was almost soggy. The flavor was OK, but the texture was way off. My sea bass was also missing its Herb Crusted jacket. My girlfriend ordered the Rainbow Trout. First, the fish was bland. Second, it was lightly pan fried. Nowhere in the menu or in the server's description of the dish was it mentioned that the trout would be pan fried. Had she known, she would have ordered something different. The flavor of the fried batter overwhelmed the already bland fish. Given our experience with the meal, we decided to skip dessert. Our server brought the bill, and this is where things really went downhill. My coupon clearly stated that it could not be combined with other coupons or offers. I understand, and it makes perfect sense. The coupon, however, didn't say anything about method of payment. I chose to pay with a gift certificate. The server came over and said that it was not allowed. I asked to see the manager, who came over and explained that a "gift certificate" is technically an "offer" and that it was the rules of the coupon - his hands were tied. I felt like I was arguing the definition of "is" with Ken Starr. When it became obvious that the manager was not going to accept the gift certificate (something which Oceano had already collected the money on when it was purchased, mind you), we paid and left. If it had just been one of the previously mentioned grievances, I could have justified a second visit. But, after mediocre service, poorly prepared food, and an argument with management, I am content letting Oceano be the big fish that got away.

text: Sugar Mom's is only a so-so establishment, especially compared to the other bars in the Olde City area. Upon arriving, my friends and I descended into a sweaty, smelly basement of a bar, which, at the time, was full of cigarette smoke (thank goodness the smoking ban went into effect pretty soon thereafter). Despite the fact that the bar is basically in a factory cellar, it is charming, with places to sit, low-hanging brick ceilings and brick columns, juke boxes, and games like pinball and pool. After fighting our way to the bar, my friends and I did manage to get some pretty cheap (although not the best quality) beer and mixed drinks, and we had a good time enjoying the juke box music and meeting new people. I do admit, this place is packed with 20-somethings on weekend nights, so it's a good place to go with your friends. However, it was a bit of a meat market, so be forewarned if you don't like skeezy guys trying to cop a feel as you work your way through the crowd on your way to the bathroom. Also, at 25, I felt like I was a bit too old for the rest of the crowd. In all, however, I had fun and returned with my friends on a Thursday night, and my experience was much less positive. It took us less time to find the place this time around, but we still had to search a bit. Then, the smoking ban had been in place in Philly for some time, but some scary looking older lady (who looked like the sun-baked old lady from "Something About Mary" - only worse!) was parked at the bar and puffing away at her Marlboro Reds. Despite complaints from the other patrons, the lady continued to smoke inside, and the bartenders did nothing to get her to stop. As someone with asthma, I didn't appreciate the flagrant disregard for the smoking ban or the fact that I left smelling like an ash tray. Despite ye olde chimney up at the bar, my friends and I got some seats in the back, as far away as possible from the smoke, and ordered $1 cans of Pabst Blue Ribbon (a good deal if you like cheap beer) and some way overcooked cheeseburgers and fries. It wasn't all that fun, and we left as soon as we finished eating to go somewhere better in Olde City. Overall, I'd recommend this place for people who want to go on the weekend and who don't mind a meatmarket and/or illegal smoking. This place, however, is really not for me.

text: The reviews for this place confuse me. In fact, I'd go so far as to say that the other reviews for this place are making me doubt myself. Could I be wrong? Is it possible that the food is actually bad? If I'm wrong, does that mean no one will pay attention to my reviews? Will people just click their tongues at me, roll their eyes and say, "Oh don't listen to him, he liked the food at the Irish Pub"? So for all of you people who are making me doubt myself... You make me sad. And a sad Jeff is a Jeff who does a lot of emotional eating. Now I want more Irish Pub; I hope you're happy. Seriously though, their burger was yum. Their parmesan chicken sandwich was yum (albeit greasy as all get-out). Their buffalo chicken sandwich was yum. Their grilled chicken sandwich was... well, like a grilled chicken sandwich from anywhere else, but that doesn't make it bad. Even their coleslaw was good (albeit minuscule), and I hate coleslaw. Is the food original? Neh, but it's still tasty. You'll leave full (assuming you're not a fat*ss), and because of all the attractive waitresses/hostesses, you'll leave fairly happy. Games are on all the TV's around the bar, and the patrons all seem chill. I've never had any experience here that could be categorized as out of the ordinary. Give the place a try, and if you don't like it, let me know so that I can subsequently find solace in a plate of french fries.
label: POS

text: Ohh Magerks, I had so much hope for you. I kept driving by as you remodeled the old Bent Elbow, looking at the "Coming Soon" sign, reading the reviews for your locations in Maryland and waiting for you to open. The first time I walked in and saw the great job you did completely renovating the inside, I thought I was going to be adding a new restaurant/bar to my local haunts. Unfortunately the experience went down hill from there. The waitress was friendly, but slow in getting to us and inattentive throughout the meal. The food is OK, but the portions are smaller and more expensive than your rivals. The beer selection is good, but again the prices are higher. In conclusion, there's really nothing terribly wrong with Magerks, they just missed the competitive mark. If you're thinking of stopping at Magerks for food don't bother, you're better off continuing up Bethlehem Pike to Halligans or to Fatty's in Wyndmoor. Both Fatty's and Halligans have food that is as good or better, larger portions, and cheaper prices. Magerks is a good place for happy hour or drinks on Friday or Saturday night as the crowd is younger than Halligans and there is more space than Fatty's.
label: NEG

text: The magazines are never up to date, it usually takes two weeks for a recent issue to be there. I also find their selection of books slimmer than most Borders. The staff are very nice, but that doesn't make up for what the place is for.

text: Do you have a favorite park in St. Louis? I do. Tower Grove. It is much smaller than Forest Park and I think that is one of the many reasons I love it. I love the quirky gazebos that decorate the park. I love the ginkgo trees, especially in the fall when the leaves turn a vibrant yellow, and the wind hits them just right and the leaves rain down, there are few things as beautiful. I love SCOSAG. My kids have taken classes there and have gone to camp and they always have a fabulous time. I love the Palm House. Some of the best weddings I have been to in St. Louis have been there. I love just sitting with someone I love, having a picnic beneath the many trees throughout the park. I love the festivals. The park has some of my favorite festivals, including Festival of Nations and Pridefest. I love the location. Smack dab in South City, it provides character to the neighborhood. I actually think Tower Grove Park ,is one of the reasons the neighborhoods surrounding it ,have been able to come back to life as strongly as they have over the last 15 years. Tower Grove Park is a St. Louis gem.
label: POS

text: Holy crap I feel stuffed just thinking about eating here. DISCLAIMER: The only reason I go to Reno is to get to the airport on my way either to or from Tahoe. Ok, got that out of the way. How dare they make the most delicious hand rolls 4 at a time? How dare they constantly ask me if I need anything? And how on earth do they get away with charging me so little? Don't they know that all the bay area sushi places don't work like this? Where is the constant checking to make sure I am eating the rice? Where is the rude guy yelling "DON'T SHARE!!?" text: Have been to Farmacia for brunch and dinner and both times the restaurant did not disappoint overall. Great shabby-chic feel to the place. Brunch was great. Service was slightly slow in having drinks brought to the table, but the crab and apple salad with avocado dressing made up for it. Second visit was a recent dinner with a group of twelve - and the restaurant was able to accommodate a last minute reservation request. The server had his work cut out for him with this group :D, but managed to successfully keep everyone happy-no small feat. My family became fans of the burger, salmon and cannelonni. Believe Metropolitan Bakery provides bread (the brown bread was delcicious) and some desserts. Ice-cream was amazing (I had the eggnog)...the cookies were too dry for my taste. Oh...although the have a full-bar, they offer BYOB without corkege fees on the first two bottles of wine, small service charge on each additional. Check out Farmacia, it's a great place in the area.

text: "Eek. Methinks not" (aka: one star), if my opinion was to be solicited, should be reserved for the dregs of the restaurant world. Slyfox in Rofo is not horrific or blood curdlingly bad. Though...I will say the beer saves me from dropping a one star on the place. I am a big fan of brew pubs, so my heart does ache to like Slyfox more than I do. I've been there four times over the last few years. The beer has been pretty consistent, not my favorite, but I really like their O'Reilly stout even though they did not have any the last time I was there. Now onto the food. The menu is standard American fair and sandwiches, and they do have various entrees you would expect to be on the menu. The sandwiches, and worse yet the fries, were not good last two times we went. My wife's cheesteak was soggy and gross, my burger was equally bad. I also find restaurants that cannot serve up good fries are not doing something right in the kitchen. I may end of going to Slyfox again. I would find it hard to pick Slyfox over Iron Hill or if time permits driving out to the Victory Brewery restaurant. text: They're nice enough, but I would just be very careful relying on advice from the physical therapists here and stick to what your actual doctor (MD) says about physical activity. I can honestly say that didn't give enough consideration to the non-surgical option of treating my injury because they treated me like an invalid whose leg would fall apart if I engaged in even the simplest physical activity instead of a healthy early-20 something. They really drilled in to my head that I would really need the continual physical therapy and I think were happy at the idea of having a client post-surgery (which I won't be anyway since I had the surgery in a different city.) The trainers are generally nice and personable, and that's why I'm giving them more than the barest minimum. The head trainer (not the physical therapist) has an extremely awkward sense of "humor" and "jokingly" harassed me about being late for weeks. I get it -- it was appropriate and within the bounds of politeness the first time, but when you make "jokes" about how late I was the rest of the time I went for physical therapy there (a couple of weeks), it's just not funny. You addressed me about it once, I acknowledged the message and stopped being tardy, now stop it. I would probably go back to these people for the simple fact that this is the closest physical therapy place to my house and when you're mobility impaired, that's freaking important. Just be careful and buyer beware. Like I said -- they're good at being personable, but never forget that all you represent to the company are dollar signs. My prescription from my doctor was only meant to be six weeks of physical therapy and yet they called me for weeks after the prescription expired and I stopped going to see if I planned to return. For what? I'm not sure.
label: NEG

text: I had OCD with regards to my iPhone's data connection speed. Who would have thought that Santa Barbara would have a much, much faster download (and upload) speed compared to the much larger city of LA? I can tell you that it blew my mind. Fresco was conveniently located off the 101 and situated in my ideal just-started-on-the-road-and-now-I'm-hungry location. We pulled off and ordered some food, lunch for me and breakfast for the boy. My sandwich was just ok. I had a half caprese: basil, tomato, mozzarella cheese on ciabatta. The bread was the highlight, as it should have been considering this is a bakery, but the sandwich was not that good. The basil was concentrated on one side of the sandwich, so for the first part of my sandwich I was wondering if they had forgotten about the basil and the latter portion I had to open up the sandwich and disperse the green specks. The cheese was stringy but the tomatoes were fresh. The breakfast burrito was also ordered. This was supposed to have jalepenos and jack cheese mixed into scrambled eggs and wrapped in a burrito. I could not taste any of these spicier flavors, just bland eggs wrapped in a bland tortilla. Salsa came on the side, but this was very mild. The desserts looked tempting so we ordered a fruit tart, which usually consists of fruit covered in glaze on top of custard in a sweet pastry crust. They substitute custard for whipped cream here. The whipped cream was home made, but I'm not a fan of whipped cream and do not enjoy paying 5 dollars for it. The layout could use more signs. There are three doors and it is still unclear to me which one you are meant to enter through. After getting in, you are supposed to walk up to the counter and place your order/pay and then go sit down. But right next to one of the "entrance" doors is what looks like a hostess table and a basket of menu's. To their credit, there is a tiny light blue sign with yellow writing directing you to place your order. This sign is unconspicuous. Other than the physicality of bringing the food to the table, everything here is self service. They don't even clear your table between the meal and the dessert. Water is provided both inside and outside (again, self serve).
label: NEG

text: Honestly, I've been here once, but it was sooooooo good.... I was in Santa Barbara for a wedding, and Jake's is "Just Around the Corner!" from their apartment. A handful of us went there on Saturday morning, around 10:30, and the place wasn't crazy crowded. There were 6 of us, and we got seated right away. We just had to wait 2 minutes for them to shove two tables together. They've got a couple TVs, and the one closest to us had the Wiggles on, but since the other one had News, we caught a story we wanted to watch, and requested a channel change. Rather than sticking us with whatever channel they chose, we simply got handed the remote, which was nice. The place only serves Breakfast & Lunch, but I can see why they stick to their specialties. Before we had ordered, we got a plate of muffins that we honestly some of the best I've ever had. They were a cranberry muffin, but the inside was soft and moist, and the outside was crispy, just we way a muffin should be. I knew then that breakfast would be yummy. I ordered something called "The Charleston". It comes with 2 or 3 eggs (your choice based on your appetite), canadian bacon, grits (which I substituted for Hash Browns, because I hate grits), and tomato slices. I have a thing with eggs. I always order them over-easy because I hate runny egg whites. The problem with this is that 95% of the time, the yolks are harder too. I like my yolks runny. This is the first time in I don't know how long that my eggs, when ordered Over-Easy, actually came out over-easy. The hash browns were perfect, nice and crispy, but still soft in the interior parts. The tomato was on the slightly not quite ripe side, but nothing to complain about. other people at my table were raving about their breakfasts as well, and I think we all ate more than we really should have. I know I would have been loosening my belt, had I been wearing a belt to loosen.
label: POS

text: i don't understand what the big hype is about this place. it's overpriced and the food is just mediocre. for how much it costs, i could get 2-3 good meals elsewhere. i had the sashimi plate last week when i was here and the fish was not very fresh at all. the portion size was so small, i was still hungry afterwards despite having already thrown away $25 on dinner. i suggest sticking with the cooked entrees if you really must come here, because my friends' sea bass and lamb chops at least looked decent. i understand that sometimes you go to a more "classy" restaurant and it's pricier because you pay for the presentation of the meal too. and the food IS very aesthetically pleasing when it's served here. but no matter how good the food looks, it doesn't make up for the fact that it tastes like crap. i like the design of the restaurant and the changing color concept inside the booths, though i think it's weird that the restaurant is located a little below ground level, so you can see people walking past the restaurant above eye level from the restaurant windows. the service here is just alright. for how much they're charging for items on the menu, i expect better. they come around a lot to ask if you need anything and how the food tastes etc. but their attitude is one of exasperation and impatience, two things i don't like to see when i'm trying to enjoy dinner with some friends. i say if you have money to waste, better to go somewhere else in center city that actually serves decent food for $25-35 a plate.

text: I love mom and pop restaurants. I support them frequently. But my experience at this place shows what happens when people don't know how to run a service business. When I arrived for lunch there were 2 other couples in the dining room. I was greeted, I sat down, and ordered right away. I ordered a Philly Cheesesteak because it was featured in Indianapolis Monthly magazine. I heard and saw nothing for 47 minutes. Seriously, 47 minutes. The sandwich arrived with no "sorry for the wait". I took a bite, and the LAVA hot sandwich literally burn not only the inside of my mouth, but my FACE. It literally burnt my face. The cheese sauce was waaaay to hot. I waited for it to cool down another 10 min and it was still too hot. My waiter stopped by to check on me and I told him that I wasn't too happy. I've never sent an item back to the kitchen in my life, so I felt justified in looking for a solution here. I told him that I didn't want the sandwich and I didn't want to pay for a terrible experience. He said, "can't do that". I asked for the manager. She came out and rudely asked "what's your problem?" I explained, and she said that they had a big catering order and that sandwiches are supposed to be hot. At this point my lip is swelling, and I just go to the counter so I can pay for the Philly Lava Steak and leave. I told the server again that my experience was unacceptable, he didn't care, and said that it wasn't his problem. I have gotten better customer service from a cop pulling me over and writing me a speeding ticket. It was ridiculous. Pass on this place until they figure out how to be human.
