That being said, I hated the taste of the flavors. They need to change up their mixes... - Toppings: Semi-good variety. I expected more (at least coming from where I'm from...) like the mangoes, more choclates (Twix/kit-kat). They had your normals and a bit more (i.e. Oreo's, capn' crunch, a nice caramel filled chocolate one and etc.), but it really didn't impress me. Price: It's 40 cents an ounce, which I find is normal (back home, there's a place that took a monopoly by pricing it like 20 cents an ounce). So it got sort of expensive with ~$4 a cup with all my 'heavy' toppings. Bottom Line: Since I didn't like the food and disliked the young, loud crowd even more... I'm not coming here anymore. text: Short story: Friendly, caring, professional staff. They apologized when they had to charge me $3 for a tool that would help me give medicine to my cat. Only gave 4 stars because it could use a good vacuuming. Long story: I was really impressed with the level of care and extra work that they did for my kitty here. My roommates and I adopted him after seeing him hanging around our block for a couple weeks and looking fairly under nourished. When we would offer him food, he would be ravenous, and when we would open our door, he would walk right in as if he owned the place, giving us the feeling that he belonged here. Since we weren't sure about his history, we wanted to make sure that he was neutered and disease-free. After reading about the Cat Vet on yelp, we thought it would be our best bet. The place definitely has the atmosphere of loving kitties. They have a store front window in which they have well-cared-for kittens up for adoption, and a pair of gorgeous Siamese that walk around freely. The staff was well-trained and highly attentive. We told them our kitty's story, and said that we weren't sure if he still had an owner who might have been looking for him (I know, we should have posted something on Petfinder, but we just couldn't bear it.), so they checked to see if he had a microchip. After they found that he did have one, the assistant went out of her way to call the microchip company and track down the former owner. Thanks to Vashti's help, we were able to learn that our little guy did have a former owner, that he had traveled a great distance across the city since living with them, and that his owner no longer had a locatable phone number or address. On top of everything, they provided us with super affordable care and a nice place in the neighborhood that we know we can trust. Though I have accompanied my former roommate to the Cat Doctor in the Art Museum area, and found them equally as friendly, it's nice to now have a place within walking distance and that is not quite as costly.

text: There are tourist traps and then there are tourist traps. This tourist trap happens to be one because it's in the FQ. However, the food is great. Fresh, well seasoned and cooked to perfection. The service is efficient, but grizzled from over-exposure to drunk tourists, I'm sure. The boo fries (which I was against ordering) were amazing, the oysters are fresh, the beans and rice tasty, and the po boys delicious. Their fried seafood is not greasy and cooked tender. Expect to stand in line for up to 20 minutes before you get in. It's probably a nightmare to get in during normal lunch or dinner times... we were there at 2:30pm on a cold and rainy day and still had to wait.
label: POS

text: It was great! We went for lunch, which started with delectable chimichurri sauce with tasty baguette (la brea bakery? maybe? so good). We had the empanadas (perfect crisp pretty pastry with beef), the beef milanese (i didn't try it but it looked exquisite!) and the puerkito chileno sandwich. This was the best sandwich I have ever had in my entire life. They describe it as pork cooked in beer and something, which led me to think it'd be pulled pork, but it's actually tender thin-ish slices of it, on a really nice focaccia-like bread with mayo, tomato, onion, lettuce, avocado and SAUERKRAUT. It came with a butternut squash soup. I am normally pretty averse to butternut squash soup, as it's become bloody ubiquitous around here and it's usually a sicky sweet fat-bomb, but this was just smooth and straightforward. A starter, hot tea, a sanwich with soup and some meat 'n potatoes, all for $36, and we still have some full leftovers boxes. The dessert menu looked really cool too, but we were full. That's a lie, I went to Renaud's after and ate 6 macaroons and 2 caramels, but still.

text: My printer quit on me today so I had to head to Staples to do some printing. Let's just say, I will never make that mistake again. The girl that was working at the printing/copy desk ignored me so I had to figure out how to use their system on my own. When I went up to the desk to get my printed papers (they all print behind the desk so you can't just print and run), she looked at me, annoyed, and told me to do my printing at the computer on my own. I let her know that I already had done that and I needed to get the stuff that I had already printed. She grabbed the pages, threw them on the counter and walked away. I was under the impression that I was supposed to pay for them there but since she threw them down and left, I assumed I could take them to the front counter. I started towards the front counter and she yelled at me, telling me that I had to pay her. This trip was a customer service nightmare, to say the least. Also, they charge 49 cents per page to print in black in white and $1.99 per color page. Are you kidding me? I've done printing at Café Dabar and their printing was only 24 cents. And Café Dabar is an independent café, they don't get discounted products or free products! To sum up my experience at Staples today - epically bad doesn't quite capture it. If you need to get some printing done, don't go to Staples. Save yourself the rudeness and the overpricing.

The meat was ok, and the peppers and onions were a little lackluster but that roll was just bad, and I don't mean stale but spongy and not very pleasant tasting and since there was so much of it, it really ruined the whole meal. text: My review is only for the formal dress department. I went to Dillard's in the Mall at Green Hills to find a fancy dress for a formal wedding in San Franciso. I already have a black, simple dress for the rehearsal dinner, and wanted something with a different shape and color for the Big Day itself. I'd stopped at Panagea and Posh and a few other Nashville boutiques before hitting the mall, and was getting a little worried I wouldn't find anything. Luckily, I stumbled into Dillards, because they have a really great selection of formal and cocktail dresses in one department, even if most of them are a bit matronly and come in larger sizes; there was one dress i wanted that did not come smaller than a 6. What? Anyway, there were a few gems amidst the bunch, which I tried on in a spacious, well-lit dressing room. The sales associate is really why this place gets 5 stars. She was ultra helpful in getting new sizes for me while I changed. I opened the door to take a garment from her while wearing a red halter number and she gasped. "Oh my goodness, that looks stunning on you," she said, holding her hand to her chest. Now, I'm not one to fall for sales girl swooning, but my friend was right. I did look stunning. I tried on other dresses, a few of which she saw, and she kept saying that the red was best, despite it being 40 dollars cheaper than the others. She was genuine, and I really appreciated it. So, I bought the red dress. I can't wait to wear it in front of my man. Thanks, lady at Dillard's! Your sending me away with a "you'll look like a fox!" really made my whole day. You rule.

text: I went here with my in-laws for Father's day (our treat). It's obviously a dress up occasion and has a warm, dim, nice interior. My only thing would be that it was actually quite noisy when we were there and there weren't that many tables full. The salad was delicious. I had a wedge salad that was crisp and refreshing. Now I'm craving one, great! My husband had corn chowder soup that was delicious and creamy. They give you amazing rosemary bread with two types of butter. I believe one was a rosemary one and the other a cheese one. They were both very good. One was just a bit creamier than the other so I favored it! The sides come family style. They do warn you about that when you order, but I was the only one who hadn't been there, so the rest of the party knew that already. We ordered Flemings potatoes...which are amazingly delicious au gratin type potatoes. They were so good I had to stop myself from inhaling them. We also got the chipotle mac and cheese. It was creamy and delicious (I'm using that word too much, I know), with a slight kick. My mother-in-law ordered a plain baked potato for my sister-in-law (she's only 4) and the thing was a monster! They don't have a kids menu, but they will tell you that they have some things that are kid friendly, like chicken strips. They also brought out a small plate of cheese and apples for my sister-in-law to eat while we were eating our salads. As a born and raised Kansas City girl, I ordered a steak. It was a 6 oz sirloin and I ordered it medium. It came out perfectly cooked and juicy and delicious. We were all already starting to fill up entirely too much, but they had experienced, and I knew about, Flemings' molten lava cake. You have to order it while you are eating because it takes awhile, and we most definitely ordered one for each of us. Let me tell you...go there for this cake ALONE! Holy cow, it was heaven in my mouth. It comes out with powdered sugar dusted on the top and a few raspberries hanging out on top as well. Two scoops of delicious ice cream sitting on some sort of high end fortune cookie like boat creation...I know, great description, right? But seriously...delicious. i couldn't stop eating. So bottom like, the food is amazing...you'll walk out feeling like crude from the massive amount of delicious food you ate, but for special occasions you can handle it! :P

He brought us something in a small bowl that looked like bright red oatmeal. I gave it a taste and nearly gagged. I couldn't even finish the meal I ordered. Injera was a little gluey - something you will know isn't exactly good if you're used to eating Ethiopian food. The meat entree we tried was nearly burnt, and the vegetable entrees were overcooked. The bigger problem is cleanliness. We spotted no less than three roaches on both the walls and tables. Raw vegetables were stacked up on the floor near the bathroom. text: "Rawwwwwwwwwr Grogggggggg!" Not only grog, but a house of grog! So the crazy Royal Navy created grog by mixing rum with weak beer. This is not happening here. A real old fashioned delight in this burgeoning city.

text: Being from California, I spend a lot of time criticizing Latin American food as I travel and move across the country. It is ingrained in me, I can't help it. So when I find a place that achieves a good balance of authenticity, price, and taste, I celebrate. And such is Agave. On Gulf Blvd this small place sits at a corner, fairly obscure. Venturing inside, there are only a few tables, which necessitates waiting times for large parties during a dinner rush (no reservations accepted). It's worth it. The menu is stacked, with a selection of appetizers, enciladas, tortas, burritos, and platos especiales. We went twice. The first time I had gorditas, which is nothing like what you read about at TacoHell. These were hand-made corn shells, stuffed with pork in green sauce, shredded beef, or chicken and tomatoes and lettuce. Dense, and delicious. Second time out I had a burrito, with a shredded chicken filling with a corn, roasted pepper, and cream sauce. You can get chips, with fresh pico de gallo, and 3 smaller dishes of salsas: one a tomatillo-green chile, a second a habanero, and the third was unidentified by us. Add a side of guacamole! The place had a good drink selection. Their sangria was fresh, with a citrus punch to it. Margaritas were served large and strong, and the horchata was super-cinnamony. Just the way I like it. Overall, a good family establishment, with great food and a nice evening. Definitely on the to-see list.

Sides were allright, but not great. The crabcakes were so fishy, they were almost inedible, very fishy, and not in a good way. One of our entrees was accompanied by what were obviously frozen french fries. We were told in advance this entree came with pomme frits, well we knew this was french fries, but we thought in a place with these prices and reputation they would at least be fresh food, especially since they make a big deal about using fresh and organic vegetables. These were not even a better grade frozen fry, but about the cheapest kind you can buy in any grocery store. Two in our party had seafood, one as an entree, one as an appetizer. The seafood came with no condiments or side sauce. We asked for some tartar sauce for one of the dishes and were shocked when our final bill charged $3.95 for it. The wait staff is pleasant. I know a great steak should be able to stand alone without condiments or sauce, but even the garlic butter they were supposed to have was missing, and they were a little dry. Wine cellar is really impressive and the young man who gave us a tour was charming and bright. If wine is what you go for, this may be your place, otherwise mediocre at best.

text: Took my sister last night 9/18/2010 for her belated birthday dinner; she had never been to Melange. My sister enjoyed the special appetizer of the evening, grilled eggplant, basil, tomato and mozzarella with a balsamic drizzle. Very nice. I of course had the wonderful Fried Oyster. A little too much sauce for my liking, however, it's on the plate and not smothered over the Oyster so I could control it. Don't get me wrong the sauce was delicious, just a little too much of it for my particular liking. My sister had the BBQ Salmon, she couldn't stop raving about it. It was in fact cooked to perfection. I had the special Mediterranean fish bouillabaisse with fish, mussels, clams, scallops and two the largest shrimp I have seen in a while. Very nice. Perfect for eating so late at night. For dessert the Kahlua Pound Cake. Now I'm not a big sweets eater so I could not really be the judge of it, however, my sister is the Queen of Sweets and while she found it too sweet. There wasn't any reason to have butter cream icing on this cake which is served gently warm with vanilla ice cream. We should have stuck to the bread pudding, but our neighbors at the next table talked us into this dessert. We shall be back in December for my birthday dinner. The only this that was missed - I had requested that they put a birthday candle in my sister's dessert and they forgot to. Perhaps for my 50th in December, they'll remember. Overall, had a nice evening at reasonably priced comfortable restaurant. Thanks Joe Brown for a great dinner and thank you Laura for good service.

text: New Orleans Birthday Trip = Bourbon and Burlesque at the CAC Like Suzanne, I was here for the Bourbon and Burlesque show last back in June. Awesome, is all I have to say. Since she gave you the rundown of the show, I'm going to give you the specs of the center itself--I am an events manager, after all, it's what I do. Venue: I've been to a lot centers, and thrown a lot of events, but as far as venues go, CAC gets props for being one of the coolest spaces I've seen in a while. You enter via the atrium, and it's just a few steps up to the first floor. There are four separate small gallery areas, as well as the stage and cafe. During the show, the cafe was the VIP area, and three of the four galleries were set up as catering stations. Downstairs has standing room for about 150 to 200 depending how packed you want people, with just a bit over 6,000 square feet. The stage is in it's own enclosed room, with mildly sloped stadium seating--which is entirely rearrangeable. Seating maxes out at 200, and the stage is about 15 feet deep, vaguely U-shaped, and on the same level as when you enter. Seating goes higher and lower than the floor. I'm not sure about how good or bad tech is, but there is a separate sound booth up top. I have to admit, for once, I was having too much fun to scope out the tech--trust me, that's out of the ordinary. One of the largest pieces in the CAC is not an installment, but architecture. The large sloping, spiral--well, it's not a staircase, it's a walkway, and when you're drunk, trust me, it's a little hard to navigate. But it's still rather impressive. There is an elevator that will take you to the second floor, but the spiral, or "clamshell" as they call it, is more hysterical. Watching people stumble is great. It can be a rather long and dizzying walk, you have been warned. Upstairs is the largest gallery, a foyer and a separate enclosed room. This room was the cigar lounge at the Bourbon and Burlesque show, which was nice, as we sipped some Saz and smoke as the sun set. There is also a small balcony that overlooks the atrium. The foyer was set up with another food and beverage station, while the gallery had more food, drinks, a stripper pole (which is used shamelessly) and the picture/naming area. I didn't get a stripper name--sorry, Suzanne!--but if you saw the girl in the red dress spinning around, that would be me. Upstairs can accommodate another 250-300 people, possibly closer to 400 if you include the foyer and the cigar room. There is over 30,000 square feet total in the CAC--including the "New Warehouse" which we did not have access to at the show--and can accommodate over 1,000 people. What floors me about the CAC is how adaptable it is, it can do almost anything. Hell, there was an acrobatics act in the atrium which, because of the contemporary architecture, meant hooking up a pulley and harness system was easypeasy. The Bourbon & Burlesque Show probably gout about 500 people throughout the night, and we were VIPs which means we're now card-carrying members of the CAC. So put on some great things, NOLA, I want an excuse to go back! Food: While the convention center is just a few blocks away--with all that implies foodwise--the CAC was a great break from the typical downtown fare. Our event was catered by Deanie's Bourbon House, and it was downright delicious. Those blueberry pork sandwiches were to die for, and the bourbon shrimp made me smile like no tomorrow. Best drink of the night was the Blue Betty, although I had a mean Saz too. On a typical day, though, the CAC is still home to the French Market Cafe, which has a very modern feel. From what I saw, they do coffees pastries. A nice spot to stop by and cool down on a hot summer day.

text: The Jefferson National Expansion Memorial is located in St. Louis, Missouri, near the starting point of the Lewis and Clark Expedition. It was designated as a National Memorial by Executive Order 7523, on December 21, 1935, and is maintained by the National Park Service (NPS). The Gateway Arch is known as the "Gateway to the West". It was designed by Finnish-American architect Eero Saarinen and structural engineer Hannskarl Bandel in 1947 and built between 1963 and 1965. It stands 630 feet (192 m) tall and 630 feet (192 m) wide at its base. The legs are 54 feet (16.5 m) wide at the base, narrowing to 17 feet (5.2 m) at the arch. There is a unique tram system to carry passengers to the observation room at the top of the arch.

text: 5 stars. By far one of the 5 best places to frequent in St. Louis, particularly if you like to grill. Keep them cold and you won't regret it, whichever one you buy. I have to admit I'm from Boston so I don't take kindly to provel, which is in a number of their sandwiches (actually I f**kin hate it - it makes me sick and want to throw up when I'm around it - how does anyone eat that garbage?) So if you're from out of town be sure to replace provel with mozz or cheddar or your favorite. The great news is these guys will do anything for you, so don't let provel in the description keep you away. The main reason I go here all the time is for their meats - ribs, pork steaks and brats are my standards. There is no reason to try anything else because these are so freakin good. The pork steaks are usually extra lean, but they melt in your mouth like a filet mignon (if you cook it right). The ribs are excellent. And the brats are by far the best I've ever tasted. I get at least 2 every time I go here. I will soon probably start to branch out and try their chickens and steaks. I'm sure they'll be just as good as the standards. The LeGrand brothers are the nicest people behind a deli counter that I have ever met. Twice I've been given 2 free brats, and this was before I started frequenting the place. I forgot to mention their sides are amazing as well. The regular coleslaw is some of the best slaw I've ever tasted. You can also select from a decent variety of beer (for the size of the store) and get simple veggies, like peppers and onions, to throw on the grill. Awesome place, awesome meats, awesome experience, awesome service, awesome sandwiches, every time!

text: After an exhaustive search for hotel accommodations in the Santa Barbara area, I ended up booking a few nights at the Pacifica Suites. About 5 or so miles away from the hubbub of State Street, these suites are better suited to visitors of UCSB. Honestly, I didn't mind the distance from the hustle and bustle of downtown SB. The Pacifica Suites are located near the 101 freeway and Hollister Avenue. This secluded hotel is easy to miss as it seems to be hidden behind a dense, verdant overgrowth of foliage and trees. Once found, you'll be pleasantly surprised by the accommodations. At check-in, we found fresh fruit and baked cookies (Otis Spunkmeyer) awaiting us. We were also just in time for the Manager's Wine Reception (Mon-Thurs, 5:00-7:00 pm only). Complimentary breakfast vouchers were even added to our check-in packet. Nice touches! The amenities were above average, in my opinion. Our suite included two televisions, a dvd player, a mini-fridge, two complimentary bottles of water, a sofa-bed (in addition to our king-sized bed in the bedroom), and free WiFi. I was pretty happy with the level of service and courtesy from the hotel staff. We had a small problem with our room key/card (didn't work the first time). However, Kimberly (at the front desk) quickly remedied the situation and had a maintenance worker fix the problem the following morning. The WiFi is super spotty, though. I don't know if our room was too far from the router, but my connectivity was horrible - one minute I'd be connected, the next I was lost. I got so fed up with it that I just used my Blackberry for Yelp searches! Despite the WiFi mess, this place is quite nice. It's no Ritz-Carlton, but it doesn't claim to be. text: Cripes, this place is begging to be closed. I apologize in advance, for this is a long one, but man... I needed to vent. Upon moving to our new 'hood, the husband and I were looking forward to finding our new go-to Thai place. Luckily, there are a few within walking distance and while the majority of reviews for Thai Cafe are pretty 'meh', we thought we'd give it a go anyway. After all, there is ONE radiant review and we were being optimistic... Now, I've eaten in many restaurants and experienced service ranging from crappy to incredibly awesome, but I never, EVER experienced worse service than at Thai Cafe. Absolutely abysmal, atrocious, abhorrent... I've gotten better service at White Castle. Justin and I invited his family to visit our new neighborhood and thought we'd try this place out. We walked in at 7pm on a Saturday to see one occupied table of two, but not a single employee anywhere. We hovered around the hostess stand, admiring the interesting decor (that's where one star comes from). We waited and waited and considered just leaving (as we should have. One table on a Saturday and no one seating customers? Run for your life!!!). FINALLY a very unhappy-looking woman seated us, threw menus at us and stomped off in her flip flops. A million years later, she came back and asked, "What do you want to drink?" A valid question, of course, but it was said with such venom, we were taken aback. My father-in-law asked for his regular, Sapphire and tonic, to which she replied, "We don't got that." He asked for Tanqueray instead. "We don't got that." We could've played that game all night, as she wasn't offering what, in fact, they DID have. I mean, did she want our money or not? Finally, she told us they only had "the cheap stuff." He said he'd take it. Another million years later, she came to tell us they didn't have any tonic. Jeeeeesus, this place is awesome. So my father-in-law looked over the specialty drink menu and asked what was in the elusively-named drinks, when at this point he should have known that answering any of our questions was not anywhere close to this woman's priorities. She had to ask the people in back about the drink ingredients and then had to go back again to see if they actually had those ingredients. At this point, there was still only one other occupied table in the place, which was no longer a shock, especially since I was ready to leave. We finally placed an order for appetizers and our entrees, which took another bazillion years to appear. The appetizers were brought out by a delightfully friendly older woman whom I'd wished had served us the whole night, as I suspect it would've changed this review in its entirety. One of the apps went missing and was never received, the tempura veggies were batter-sodden and the accompanying sauce was an unidentified gelatinous mess, and the satay was so overcooked it was like shoe leather. Maybe it's a good thing the fish balls never appeared... The second star comes from the entrees, which, after the hideous service, drinks and appetizers, were shockingly good. They don't mess around with namby-pamby spice levels here. If you ask for medium spicy, be prepared for some zing. I liked my green curry, Justin enjoyed his duck curry and while I can't remember what everyone else had, the entree portion of our meal briefly settled our grumbling about unprofessional service, lack of water refills and the fact that they did, in fact, have Tanqueray in the bar (my sister-in-law went on a covert mission and peeked at the bottles). During this whole dinner ordeal, a few other parties came in hoping to have dinner, I presume. Two parties waited it out and were finally seated, while two other parties waited, waited, waited and finally just bailed. If you have the patience of a saint, bring your own water bottle to dinner and avoid the appetizers, you will likely enjoy yourself at Thai Cafe. If you have ever dined anywhere else in the world, EVER, you will likely realize that Thai Cafe is perilously close to running off all their business with their absolute lack of service and unremarkable food.

text: The just-opened Twenty Manning Grill is my favorite new restaurant in Center City. I could eat there 2 or 3 nights a week. In fact, since it opened a few weeks ago, I have already been to TMG about 5 times. I live in Center City and eat out a lot -- too much, probably -- and it is so great to find a friendly, happy place that is comfortable, warm and affordable (entrees are generally in the teens, topping out at about $22). The food is great, too. Even though it has only been open a few weeks, every dish I have eaten has been delicious. I highly recommend the caprese salad (so fresh and healthy), the roasted chicken and peas (served in a cast iron skillet) and the pork chop with roasted peaches. My favorite, though, I think is the flash-seared tuna, which I absolutely loved! For desserts, you can't go wrong with the half-baked chocolate chip cookie (served with vanilla ice cream). One final note: To a person, every bartender and server I have met at TMG has been really good, and super friendly. They all seem to genuinely enjoy working there, and their positive attitude helps define this happy little bistro! Oh, and one more final note: It's nice to see owner Audrey Claire walking around every night, greeting guests and attending to little details. Makes you feel like you are being welcomed into the home of a good friend.

text: If I could give them zero stars, I would. The people at 9th and Filbert are more reasonable to deal with as I have experienced. However, I cannot say the same for the residential parking permit office or ppa in general. I moved to Philly at the end of this summer, purchased a temporary parking permit because I had to switch my registration and title to Pennsylvania. It was for fifteen days, and at no time during the robotic spiel that the woman at ppa gave me did she tell me that I couldn't use that permit when I switched my plates. I got my new license and registration the following week and because I'm in graduate school, only had time to get my car inspected (for 80 dollars! but that's another story all together) at which time their offices are closed (although this is just an assumption given that their website doesn't give any hours and the phone number they provide goes to a full mailbox). So, I waited until my fifteen days were up. I had moved my car a few times during this period to go on errands and had miraculously found a space on the same block every time for whatever reason. I went in the morning of a day I had class because it was the day that the permit expired and I hadn't had time before that to go. I gave them all my information and was told that I had three outstanding tickets. I gawked at her and said I didn't have any on my car when I drove over here. So she gives me a print out that doesn't tell me anything about who gave me the ticket but that there were three for pretty much consecutive days at the same time, all of which never made it on my windshield. Had I not gone to get a permit I wouldn't have known and probably would have gotten booted or had to pay large fines as well. The woman I dealt with was a huge jerk and had no sympathy for me. I was told that I could go to the violations branch and dispute it and get a walk in appointment for that day. Unfortunately, when I got there, wasting about a half hour in line, I was told that they didn't do that anymore and that I would have to pay my tickets if I wanted a permit, so I paid $108 in tickets that I didn't know existed. I went back to the parking permit office and got my permit, and told them that they were wrong and the woman still disputed with me. And I've since gotten yet another ticket for a stupid violation that was not my fault, and the ticket was filled out incorrectly for two different amounts. But, I digress. I've read most of these posts and I have to comment on the people who think that PPA is reasonable. I understand that they're only doing their job, but parking wards exists for a reason, there are many, that outweigh the reasonable ones, employees who give tickets out for unexpired meters and who don't bother to look at permits or signs. They're lazy and they don't know their facts. When I asked to speak to a supervisor of the meter maids, she even told me she didn't think I should get a ticket for having a temporary parking permit on my car yet the people at the parking permit office said I should have. They can't get their stories straight and they are the biggest jerks in this city and the only reason why I have to feel fearful that my car might not be where I parked it when I go to use it, not the threat of someone stealing or breaking into it. Haha, so after I explained it, we finally formulated that the dish I was looking for was called Bo Xao To. A good friend of mine (and fellow Yelper) took me out tonight, and I had to get Bo Xao To again. If you're looking for a good Vietnamese place, service is great and the new restaurant atmosphere is very classy and nice.

text: Silver building Construction rebuilt the entire rear face of a 3-story apartment building for me. The work included a total re-build of the first floor sun porch. I am very happy with how the project turned out. Dominick made the right first impression when he came to examine the property. He was on time. He listened carefully to the scope of the problem as I understood it. We discussed potentially advanced decay and what my options might be. He did not arrive with a pre-formed solution, and he did not attempt to sell me on any one method of solving the problem. Dominick's bid was thoughtfully prepared, detailed, and competitive. Throughout the construction process, Dominick was accessible, and always returned my calls. The work area was left as neat as can be for such a large project, and Dominick checked with me to see if I was comfortable with where he proposed to store the tools. In addition, Dominick invited me out to inspect his progress several times, and he explained everything that he was doing in great detail. The cost of the project did grow, as the scope of the work expanded due to some advanced decay that was discovered when the siding was removed. Dominick did not surprise me with a larger bill, but he invited me out to see the damage for myself, and then he presented me with options. There was no pressure to choose one option over another, but I felt comfortable expanding the scope of the project. The cost did not exceed the estimate, once all the conditions were known. Dominick has a real love of buildings and in doing the job properly, unlike many in the business who will try to do whatever is easiest. I am very satisfied, and would not hesitate to hire him again.

text: Loved it! I dined with my husband and another couple this past weekend to celebrate friend's birthday. This was my first time dining at Morton's and I had been hyped up about it from my friend. They greeted us, took a picture for the birthday boy then immediately seated us in a comfortable grand booth! Our server was the WONDERFUL Christopher. My husband ordered the center cut iceberg salad with their house made thousand island dressing- I was impressed. The portion size was incredible. Him and I ended up sharing it because it was so large. Our companions enjoyed their caesar salad and lobster bisque. I ordered the Filet Oscar cooked medium, which had two small filets on top of a potato with asparagus and fresh lobster on top covered in a creamy sauce. Even though I was stuffed, I wanted more because it was so good. My husband ordered the double cut filet, medium rare and said it was the best steak he's had in a restaurant. We ordered the sauteed spinach & mushrooms and green beans for sides to share- both also very good and filling. We skipped dessert, but the waiter brought out a massive slice of New York style cheesecake for the birthday boy, which they said was awesome as well. Seemed to be the running theme for the night! text: I love how this is a 5 star standout for just about everybody who took the time to write a review on it. You know why? Because there is something for everyone. For those who have never been, rest assure it is not just jazz music on display. There is the Popeye's Blues tent, a gospel tent, big named rock acts, local world class musicians, reggae, soul, bluegrass, r&b, folk, gypsy jazz,,,,,etc. There are parades going on non-stop with marching bands, dancing native Indians, music for kids. Craft tents with very cool local art. And the food options are the stuff that dreams are made of. Also the scheduling is genius because it is the last week of April, first week of May, so there are no college kids which is kinda awesome. Make no mistake- people party HARD, but it isn't drunks puking on one another, it is a more mature group of people who have done it and don't act like it's their first time. In my opinion, it is the ultimate party. MUSIC - I've been twice now, once before and once after Katrina (you bitch!). I've seen Stevie Wonder, The Raconteurs, Derek Trucks Band, Santana, The Dirty Dozen Brass Band, Ivan Neville's Dumpstafunk (It's a good rule of thumb to go check something out if there is Neville involved, same goes for any of the original Meters, especially George Porter Jr. because yes: George Matters) Toots & The Maytals, The Roots, Papa Grows Funk, Galactic, Widespread Panic. It is impossible to see everyone you want because there are crazy options on simultaneously. Your best bet is taking a look at the schedule, circling that acts you really want to see and motivating to get there about 20 minutes before their set so you can get a good spot closer to the stage. That being said, it is also all about checking out new acts you never heard of. My rookie year at the fest I was running around trying to do it all, and it is just impossible. I was kinda spun out and just ducked into a tent and saw this french cat playing nylon string jazz guitar and it totally blew me away and was the highlight of the day. So def keep an open mind. Also, keep in mind there is incredible (some might say better) music going on all night once the fest wraps for the day in the early eve. Save some energy for late night. I never made it in for the night before 3am while in NOLA. At night, around town I've seen Gov't Mule, Les Claypool, Umphrey's McGee, Trey Anastasio, PBS, Garage a Trois, Soulive, Rebirth Brass Band, Trombone Shorty, etc. The best part of these night shows is the collaborations that take place. Think about it, you got some of the best musicians in the world all in one town, you know they're fans of one another. They're chillin and partyin, and before you know it you got this guy from that band jammin with this band, while some kid is sitting in and blowing your face off with a trumpet solo. Love it. Food: Heeeeey-zeus Christo. It doesn't get better then this. I'm going to keep it just about the fair grounds. They have everything you ever heard of and more you never even dreamed of. Watch your step cause there are crawfish shells everywhere. Gumbo, Jambalaya, Crawfish Monica (fusilli pasta with spicy cheesey creamy sauce and crawfish meat), Meat stuffed bread, jalapeno corn bread, the big winner is the Cochon du Lait which is this cajun marinated pit-roasted suckling pig sandwich with coleslaw and spices. The muffaletta is a winner too, basically a huge round sandwich with tons of Italian meats then doused in a chunky olive spread. Yeah, me talking about it does it no justice. I will say you have NEVER been to a music festival with so many delicious options at a fair and reasonable price. TIPS: Sunblock, hat, water Pace yourself - it is more marathon then sprint. I don't drink alcohol during the day there. There is no day time drinking when you're trying to catch a show that starts at 3am. Yes there are shows that start then and later! I'm not one for schlepping a chair all over, but it would be nice if you wanna deal. F the free transportation, go with a few friends and take a cab. Don't skimp too much on your hotel. There are cheap options but you don't want to go too cheap because it can get pretty shady and disgusting. (Yeah our motel was next to "tent city" last time, the smell of urine came into our place) On the other hand, you will only sleep and shower at your hotel, there is way too much other stuff going on every hour of the day. Do get tickets for night shows in advance. Nothing like being shut out of a small show of one your favorite acts because you snoozed on getting tickets. Bigger names will play smaller clubs like Tipitina's. You want to be there for that. Wilco played there with a horn section and I didn't see it, and that doesn't sit too well. Do plan on eating at least one or two nice meals around town while you are there, but if you are on Yelp, I'm sure that is on your agenda. So in summation, GO TO FUCKIN JAZZ FEST!!

text: The Joint is my favorite place in New Orleans for BBQ, far and away the best the city has to offer, IMO. I'd rank it much higher than Ugly Dog, Ms. Hysters, and VooDoo (yuck) in terms of both quality and atmosphere. Located at the edge of the Bywater neighborhood within sight of the Industrial Canal and in close proximity to the naval installation, the building looks like a small shack from the outside. After you enter you'll find that this book's cover was a good judge of its insides as well. This is an not upscale establishment and the focus is on the food, as it should be. Orders are served in plastic baskets lined with paper. The wonderful smell of smoked meats is immediately apparent as soon as you enter this tiny shack and will linger on your clothes for a few hours after you leave. The decorations include some Dr Bob artwork, a jukebox, a picture commemorating a visit from Diners Driveins and Dives, and a sign proclaiming The Joint as carnivorous cuisine, just in case you couldn't already tell. There's a small counter to your immediate left where you place your order and a few patio tables inside. Just to the side there's self serve sweet tea which is always the perfect accompaniment to BBQ, sugar rush be damned. The back yard contains the rhinoceros-sized smoker and a few picnic tables paired with some rusted out metal chairs for outdoors eating. If it is your first time eating here I'd recommend the W special, giving you a little brisket, a little pulled pork, and two ribs plus a side. In reality what they claim as a little is truly a full portion, so you'll have plenty of leftovers for later. I drown my pulled pork in the dark sauce and mop up the excess with my bread at the end, but the ribs are just fine without, their dry rub imparts plenty of flavor all on its own. I always opt for the beans as my side. They're cooked in pork fat and are MMM MMM GOOD. They also have chaurice (a type of sausage) and chicken, but chicken always tastes dry to me when it's been barbequed, no matter where I order it. Other sides include mac 'n cheese, potato salad, and cole slaw, which aren't as memorable as the baked beans. That said, if you're in New Orleans and in need of some BBQ, this is THE PLACE to go.

text: Italian food has a mandate. It must be more than merely present. It must be transformative. It must do more than fill the space between the hours. It must define them. I did not invent these rule. They are held inviolate by lowly Spaghettio slingers and homemade pasta people alike. They're understood by your favorite South Philly fatso with the marinara moustache. Even extras in advertisements for Olive Garden get it. No doubt you have your own examples. For all those who follow the rules, there will be others who break them. Enter Spasso. There was nothing terribly wrong with our meal tonight at Spasso. There just wasn't anything especially right. The Caesar salad was forgotten as it was being eaten. The dressing lacked complexity or brightness. It ached for anchovy and lemon. The added grape tomatoes had the flavor of dishwater. Involtone Di Manzo (beef tenderloin rolled with prosciutto, mozzarella & spinach in a mushroom sauce) seemed perfectly executed (textures and temperature were excellent; the sauce was nice...) and yet? The first bite did not beg the second. One would have been enough. My dining companion reported similar findings with his entree, the Shrimp Fradiavolo. The shrimp did not seem to have been cooked in the sauce (perhaps boiled separately, then plated with the sauce), so they lacked flavor. And the tomatoes tasted fresh. As in Superfresh. My Prosecco tasted almost medicinal. Now, I'll put almost anything in my mouth -- but with this, I took a pass. So it went unimbibed. Very pleased with the service. It made up for the snoozy food and was good enough to merit return visits. A final thought. Dinner was served with forgettable bread and a ratatouille-type chunky relish spread. I happen to loathe ratatouille with a white hot passion; however I did go ahead and taste it, because you never know. Like everything else, it was perfectly fine. Just something to pass the time.

text: I visited Bridge last week as part of a tweetup and for dinner with out-of-town guests. The location was perfect for our transit tweetup, as Bridge is just a few blocks from the 8th and Pine Metrolink station downtown and just near Left Bank Books (easy to reach everything in downtown, really). It's also just two blocks from my loft, so I'll likely be visiting regularly. The tweetup folks had secured Bridge's main level for finger foods and mingling. It was a little tight, as it's a narrow space, but it suited our group just fine. I love the wall-tall windows looking out to the street, and the bar is large and beautiful. Another super-awesome thing? Bridge is completely smoke-free! My friends and I needed something a bit more substantial for dinner than just cheese appetizers, though, so we moved upstairs to order entrees. As others have mentioned, Bridge's upper level is a little warmer than the lower level (heat rises, after all), but I didn't mind it, as it wasn't overly hot. Upstairs, tables are covered and candles are lit. It's inviting and cozy. More: there was a half-wall/ledge thing that was next to our table, so we had a place to put purses and laptop bags. Handy! Bridge is smart and leaves a carafe of water on the table so you don't have to flag down a server every 8 minutes -- being a fast water drinker, I love this. Bridge's menu is phenomenal. Our group shared an appetizer of peppered goat cheese, foccacia, olives, hazelnuts and roasted tomatoes. We all had have our weird food quirks, but among us, we devoured everything except a few olives. The bread was slightly crispy outside and spongy inside, and it went perfectly with the goat cheese. For my dinner, I ordered an "adult" grilled cheese sandwich -- different cheeses, onion and tomato on a roasted bun. I'm all about cheese, and this sandwich certainly hit the spot. I was starting to fill up after the great cheese board appetizer, so I only ate half of my sandwich. The other half held up well when I reheated it the next day. My sandwich came with potato chips from St. Louis' own Billy Goat Chip Company. SO crispy, seasoned and delicious! (There were options for other sides, but I don't remember what they were) I also had a side of a bean salad in a vinegar dressing. It was yummy. A friend had ordered a pot of mac and cheese. VERY cheesy, and the sauce had some finely chopped tomatoes in it. I stole a bite, and I'd totally order it next time. The only things I wasn't in love with at Bridge were the low lighting and the loudness. I found myself tilting the menu closer to the candle to get just a bit more light to read everything. And the sound from the tweetup on the lower level carried upstairs (the upstairs overlooks the downstairs instead of being a full, separate floor). I don't know if the sound issues were just from this event or if it's always like that. But it became increasingly difficult to chat at our table. I do wish Bridge would post menu items on its website as HTML instead of PDF, as that's annoying, particularly when browsing on a phone. My sandwich/chips entree was about $8 and the cheese board was about $12 -- fair prices for the deliciousness that was consumed. I'd go back to Bridge. There were plenty of enticing dishes that caught my eye. Bridge has enough vegetarian and meaty entrees and appetizers for everyone.

text: In about as many weeks, I had but two disappointing meals in NOLA. Sadly, Dante's was one of them. I really wanted to like this place, and we even took our one-day rented car to get there on a Friday night for a change of scenery from the quarter. I almost gave Dante's three stars, because for the most part, it seems to be a decent local slow-food joint, but they served me an entree for which there was NO excuse, which should never have left the line, and which I can only assume escaped from the kitchen on a night when no senior kitchen staff were on. Because no one who cares about this restaurant, and its reputation, its fresh-and-local image, could have served the eggplant napoleon I received, a dish so bad I shudder to think of it, and I just know I won't be able to order eggplant again for a long time. I totally didn't trek here to order eggplant, though -- I came for chicken-fried flank steak. CHICKEN-FRIED STEAK! It was on Dante's online menu, posted right alongside the date we went. When we arrived, however, the menu was a good deal different than the one I had seen. That's lame -- why post a daily menu if it's not accurate? I got teased with chicken-fried steak. There was instead a flank steak piri piri, and to the credit of the server, she tried to steer me that way ... but I really wasn't in the mood for just any steak, but for CHICKEN-FRIED steak. And after eating two weeks of creole cooking, by the time we ordered dinner at nearly 9 this night, I was just not hungry enough to settle for just steak. So I thought the egglant napoleon -- with smoked tomato sauce, heirloom tomatoes, fresh local basil, local mozzarella, and parmigiano reggiano would be a fresh, simple, layered dish with just a bit of creole kick. What arrived should have been immediately returned, but I did order it over the server's clear steering away, so I suffered in silence. First, this was no napoleon. The dish was not layered at all, but was instead a large blob of eggplant chunks, grey, lukewarm, and incredibly seedy. So seedy, every bite was crunchy. The smoked tomato sauce wasn't integrated, and the heirloom tomatoes were half-heartedly sauteed, bitter, and set among some flavorless, stiff onions. There were no more than two tablespoons of cheese -- about one of each type -- and these were just sort of embedded in the eggplant. There was zero presentation here, on a dish that everyone knows -- by its very nature -- is supposed to be layered. There was also no basil at all in the dish, as claimed on the menu. Fresh basil should have been featured prominently, considering the menu took the time to note its local origin, and to simply omit it insulted my intelligence. There were instead some fresh snipped chives -- hey, they're green, too! -- which had no business hanging around smoked tomato sauce. Had I made this dish at home, I would have discreetly slid it in the compost bin before anyone could notice my ineptitude. The molasses spoon bread -- a buttery, sweet corn bread -- was really nice, and my guy's chicken cooked under a brick was wonderful (although I thought the sauce was maybe a little too maple syrupy, he dug it despite having a generally French aversion to too much sweet with savory), and our appetizer of shrimp and grits was well-executed, with creamy, stone ground grits and four sweetly charred whole shrimp. As a former trade bartender (and current hobbyist bartender) I was interested in checking out Dante's homemade infusions, but the peach-infused old-fashioned was watery and unsweet, and the cucumber gin and juice lacked any sharpness to its citrus component to balance the cucumber. We had water with our entrees and got the hell out of Dante's Kitchen.

text: Technically, my rating is 4.5 stars, but Yelp doesn't let you give halves. Sometimes it's difficult being a vegetarian foodie, especially one with a mushroom allergy. At Bayona, it was pretty effortless, starting with making the reservation. Upon calling I had several questions and they were all met with a good, helpful attitude which set a really good tone for the evening. When we arrived the same helpful woman (I recognized her voice) greeted us and seated us in the parlor-type area for drinks while our table was prepared. She had a good knowledge of the wine list and her recommendation for a red (Tempranillo/Cabernet Sauvignon blend) was spot on! Once seated, we were greeted by our server's assistant, who was adorable and charming. He brought a small dish of olives and curried and pickled veggies, which were super tasty. Our main server greeted us next. He has an extremely cheerful demeanor and seemed to genuinely love his job and the food he serves. Right off the bat he gave us a great explanation of the menu (including when something was made with chicken stock WITHOUT ME ASKING!). I let him know that I was a vegetarian with a mushroom allergy and he immediately suggested some ways to modify or combine existing menu items. He also took my dietary restrictions to the Chef de Cuisine and let him come up with some dishes that he would want to make based on what he had in the pantry. I know sometimes chefs can get snippy about modifying their dishes (each component has a purpose, I know!), so I was excited to see what he would come up with. Before I go into what my mom and I ordered, I want to say three words: SWEET POTATO BRIOCHE! Moving on. My mom settled started with the Bayona salad. The portion was unexpectedly large. It was well-dressed (don't you hate when restaurants drown your salad? I do!) and had a slight sweetness that paired well with the shaved parmigiano reggiano. My mom didn't finish her salad (saving room), so I gobbled it right up! For her entrée, she went with the pan-seared pancetta-wrapped halibut, broccoli flan, and shoestring potatoes. After the first bite of halibut the only thing she could say was "outstanding." The broccoli flan was amazing (mom was nice enough to share). Those aren't two words that I would have put together before my trip to Bayona, but it's now something that I am hoping to replicate at home. The only "bad" thing my mom had to say was "I would have been okay with more shoestring potatoes." I began with the Greek salad, which was on the daily specials menu. I was extremely pleased with the proportions of the ingredients in my salad as all too often someone gets carried away with the feta. Not here. You don't always see garbanzo beans on a Greek salad, but I enjoyed the addition. For my entrée, I chose to go with one of the chef's options: gnocchi, sautéed spinach and broccolini, and puréed tomato confit. This dish has converted me from feeling luke-warm about gnocchi into a HUGE FAN. And kudos on not overcooking the spinach. So many people do that I generally refuse to order it. Thanks, Bayona, for not making me regret taking those risks. So where's the reason for the half-star deduction in the rating? I had a pretty good conversation with the server about my mushroom allergy. He repeated it back to me several times and yet my entrée arrived topped with hen of the woods mushrooms. Everyone was extremely apologetic and it was quickly resolved. A new plate was fired up and delivered piping hot, but it's a big pet peeve when my plate is delivered with poison on it. The simply charming aesthetic of the interior and the courtyard charming is a perfect fit for the vibe of the food. I only wish I had been able to tummy-rub the restaurant's cat (I believe his name is Crusty). OH! I almost forgot!! My mom purchased Susan Spicer's cookbook, and we came back for it the following day as they had held it so it could be signed. Unfortunately Susan wasn't going to be in before our flight left so they graciously offered to ship the book to my mom at no charge. Way to go, Bayona staff!

I realize that the ushers are there on a volunteer basis. My mom did it for a season or two. They're not getting paid and they often have to sit through the same show several times before it finally moves on (and not all the shows they sit through are as entertaining as you might think...my mom sat through Phantom of the Opera FOUR times. I would have died.) HOWEVER. The ushers that were working the show on Sunday, June 27 (at 2:00 pm) probably should have paid me back for my tickets. Clearly stated in every program, on lots of signs throughout the theater, on your tickets, and as GENERAL THEATER ETIQUETTE, people should expect to have to wait for a pause in the action to be seated if they show up for the show after it's already started. Then WHY, are ushers seating people while this show has already started, blocking the views of those of us who DID bother to arrive on time, and shining flashlights (which are supposed to be pointed to the ground at all times anyway) in MY FACE?! It's when stuff like this happens, that I just freaking wish the ushers would use a little common sense and perhaps take that moment to educate people on a little theatre etiquette. Don't even get me started on the Muny (i.e. it is never okay to SING ALONG with the actors onstage). This time around at the Fox I wasn't sitting in the best of seats, so had I been paying a little more, I probably would have complained. But, attention to everyone - it is RUDE to show up late for a show. Just like baseball, you're to wait for a pause in the action before you make your way to your seat. It's also rude to talk during a live performance. Sure, in a place like the Fox, the actors can't hear you, but I paid money to hear them, NOT YOU. I adore the Fox, I swear I do. I'll be going there for years to come and hope to bring my children there some day (once they're old enough to follow the rules above). Look, if you are there, you are probably going to want to try it (after all, OPRAH recommended it and who am I to disagree with the big O when it comes to food) -- but, I have to be honest and say for the price, it was a big disappointment. And as far as flavor goes, it's good, but not even in my top 10. Maybe I got them on a bad day, or maybe they are just a bit overrated.
label: NEG

text: I was surprised by this place. The happy hour is one of the best in Tucson for good cheap apps. and drinks. The drinks are exotic, strong and good but better with upgraded liqour. Our bartender was great, he was friendly and full of good humor, can't remember his name though. I was shocked at how good the baby back ribs were. The meat fell right off the bone, it took no effort on my part, F-IN delicious I tell you. So the most shocking thing about this place are the prices. How goodcan it get, not to mention you feel like you are not in Tucson when you are at Kon Tiki.
label: POS

text: I have noticed this new addition to the Met-tropolis on many occasions as I bustled about on my oh-so-important business, so when my friend suggested we visit for a mid-week workday power lunch, I very importantly agreed. Like a typical deli primarily designed for lunching, Caffe Caffe had the ubiquitous salad/sandwich/wrap/soup/quiche menu, with just enough choices so as not to overwhelm. There was a gorgeous assortment of baked goods on display that looked so perfect I made a note not to (1) ever bring the children with me (easily another $15-20) or (2) come when I am depressed (easily adding a pound or two). I chose the Ants Marching Wednesday special - the cup of soup/ 1/2 sandwich combo. (If it had been Feisty Friday, I would have probably gone full monty with a whole sandwich and chips; and of course, on Mormon Monday, it would have been a dry garden salad, hold the fun.) We placed our orders, took a ticket to the end of the counter, paid at the register and were given numbers, and then let loose to fill our cups and find a table. It was busy with a nice mix of ladies who lunch and business types, which is much like the 1/2 sandwich combo on the menu-- too heavy on either side would have been too much. I approved of the goldilocks crowd and found a table that was also just right. The split pea soup was very good, but I had to add a lot of salt and pepper to suit it to my Tabasco-addled tongue. The whole grain croutons that accompanied the soup were PERFECT, and I will probably order soup alone next time just for those (most appropriate on a Penance Sunday). The 1/2 turkey club was adequate- again, not too dry, not too dressed, but just right. It was piled with shaved turkey meat, swiss cheese, crispy bacon crumbles, lettuce, tomato and mayo on toasted soudough. My friend got the rather colorful quiche (and cup of split pea), which she said was very good. I caught sight of a salad, but it didn't look like a Monday affair- it was piled high with avocado (and sin). I assume it was the Avacado Salad, which is described thus: "Romaine lettuce topped with sliced avocado, gorgonzola cheese & walnuts, garnished with orange slices & red onions, finished with our Mango Vinigrette"....mmmm....
label: POS

text: I came here just a few weeks ago when I was visiting from New England. I was craving some mexican food since I can never find any up north. We happened upon Los Mexicanos Mexican Restaurant on St.Pete Beach. The parking was terrible, the lot so small once you back up you face death on Gulf Blvd with the traffic flying by. Really hardly anywhere to park safely here. Inside the restaurant you could sense the corny atmosphere. There was a banner on one wall that said Happy Fiesta. Yeah...lovely. The waitress seemed like she was tired and bored, I don't blame her. I didn't order a margarita but I saw them on other tables around the restaurant, they didn't look very good. I ordered an enchilada and a taco. The enchilada was very bland with grey-brown meat and had no taste at all despite being drenched in some kind of stringy cheese. Where was the enchilada sauce? My dad was dining with me and he pushed his plate to the side after a few bites. The waitress didn't even ask why we hadn't finished our entire meal when she came to collect our plates. I assume she sees this a lot. Unfortunately I will not be dining here again.
label: NEG

text: Stayed here for 4 nights on a recent business trip. The location is right downtown, close to restaurants, the convention center, the new Colts stadium, the Capital building and more. Limo ride (shared) from the airport ran about $13 plus tip and took about 10-15 minutes. The room I stayed in was a nice size and very clean. King bed, work desk with lamp, tv (older tube type, not flat screen), chair with ottoman. The bathroom was nice sized and my faucet leaked on the cold water side whether on or off. I must have been in a basketball player's room because the tub was sunk about 6 inches in the floor and the shower head was on an extension rod and was about 6 inches above my head at 6-ft 1-in. I didn't eat at the restaurant, Hot Tuna. I did have a couple of drinks at the bar next to Hot Tuna and had breakfast daily at the 40 West coffee bar. Beware - it's pretty busy at 40 West with the breakfast rush between 8 and 9 AM. Our rate was $99/night.
label: POS

text: If I could change my last name to Cheesesteak, I would. That being said, I was expecting Geno's to be better. Maybe it's all that hype. Really raises your expectations. I like Geno's enough, though the super finely sliced steak wasn't quite so satisfying. I guess I like a more substantial steak. Not chunky or hearty, just something that doesn't disintegrate in my mouth under the weight of all that cheese, onions and bread. I'd have to say Steaks on South is my favorite.
label: POS

text: I am not sure why I keep giving Panda Express a chance. It may be that I keep thinking that maybe their food will be better than it was on my previous visit. Regardless, my latest visit is my last visit to Panda Express, if I can help it. I recently went to their newly opened restaurant on 96th St in the Meijer parking lot...I wasted my money, again. I ordered the spicy chicken pao, and broccoli beef. They both tasted like soap. Honestly, this is the worst chinese food I have ever tasted. I threw most of it away. You only get two entrees and rice for almost $7. I can go to another chinese restaurant and get that along with a side and drink for that price. In addition, I have determined that Panda Express tastes like plain, make-at-home chinese. In fact, I think I could do better than this. At least I have finally learned my lesson and know for sure that their food will never be improved. I am just really surprised that they get enough business to need to open another location.
label: NEG

They advertise as upscale but it was very down right ghetto. They do not inforce a dress code you can wear anything and anyone can go. Just a mess. Never again. Don't waste you time going.

text: Have I got a story for you. El Azteca seemed a great place for my friends from out of town and I to go to and enjoy a Martguerita or several and rehash old times. BYO and decent prices. So we get there early, just in case they would seat us, and were told that there was no room, even though we were looking at TWO clean, empty tables. Whatever. so we come back at 9. We were then told that in order to dine at this fine establishment that we would have to sign a VOMIT WAVER, whereby we would be charged $25 per person who vomited in our party. Furthermore, we would be given one warning for foul language, and the second time we were notified, we would be thrown out. Read that: we would be thrown out for foul language, but not for vomiting. Now, after all this, our expectations for the food were low (and not even met) but the food could have been world class and i would not have cared, because the restaurant was so filled with rowdy, pushing, noisy people that i could barely scream my order to the waiter. I have to vote no on this one.

The Bad: None of the beers are beers you've ever heard of before, and they don't have a sampler, plus the descriptions are extremely minimal, so you buy about four or five beers before you actually find one you like. Also, if anyone working at Local 44 reads these, please please please put better descriptions of your beer on your menus. If you're going to have random ass beers only, at least give me a good idea of what I'm getting into. Four words is not enough. Either that, or offer a standard choice or two.

text: I had no idea what to expect from Hot Kabobs, but I had driven by it a million times so I figured I should check it out. I ate there last week, and it was really tasty stuff. You might miss this tiny house that's now a restaurant so keep your eye out! I was the only person in the place when I went in, but the girl at the counter was happy to walk me through the menu and give me suggestions on what to have. I ended up with a sampler platter which had both chicken and beef kabobs. The meal came with some tomato and cucumber salad and great jasmine rice. As I was waiting for my carry-out order, several other dinners came in and took a seat. It definitely seemed like they were all repeat customers who really enjoyed this food. It's a pretty inexpensive meal that I know you'll enjoy. They are also open for lunch with daily specials so I know I'll be back to check those out.

text: As a huge proponent of the philosophy that everything is better with bacon, I found El Guero Canelo to be a soul mate of sorts for me. The sonoran style hotdog is probably the best regional hotdog treatment around. Bacon, beans, onions, tomatoes, mayo, mustard, jalapeno all crammed into a fluffy, sweet, over-sized bun.... sigh, a hot dogs wet dream. I really love the roasted peppers and green onions available on the expansive toppings bar as well as the speedy service. I was snapping photos of my dog between bites because I wanted to share the awesome with friends back home. The only thing I would change about this place is to have a location in DC, where they would surely rake in some serious cash.

text: Didn't try the cannoli but ogled one someone was buying. Guess I'll have to go back. Did try some kind of strawberry cake, mostly pink icing with white edges and pink swirls in the cake but no actual strawberries. That's fine, I don't like actual strawberries... just things that taste like them. The cake was good, dense but not in a moist way. (I know I just used the m-word but I think it should be allowed when discussing cake.) The frosting had a great consistency, not overwhelmingly sweet but real (sugary) frosting. I can't stand that whipped/non-dairy BS they use in grocery stores. $2 for a slice. Friend had a slice of the chocolate mousse cake but she and I both agreed the mousse had a kind of alcoholic taste.. I guess from a chocolate liqueur or something. It was still edible but I don't think I'd get it again.

The sushi and hibachi are very very good! And they also have a late night menu from 10pm - 4am (no drinks after 2am). After 10pm EVERY night they have half-price sushi, drinks, and appetizers. You cannot beat this! Go check it out and be impressed! It usually fills up from 8pm on. You can even call for reservations.

The discounted price was NOT worth the time wasted at Rizzeri. The student was friendly and engaging - the ONLY positive to my experience. They really deserve not stars, but Yelp won't allow that...

text: This place screams advancement of a sophisticated, but fun hangout. Whether this twist on frozen yogurt originated in the West or not I couldn't tell you... but I'm so happy that it finally exists here. Phileo Yogurt had a delightful scheme- the contemporary seats, pink and lime green backsplash, the interesting food facts with vivid fruit representations displayed on the wall and the bright lighting so you won't miss a thing- all the elements worked together to pleasure your senses. I also noticed that the frozen yogurt dispensors were VERY clean and was hard to believe considering that it was self-serve. There must have been an invisible cleaning fairy that wipes away everyone's mess because boy was this place spotless! They had several choices of yogurt which you can sample approximately a heaping tablespoon of anything you desire- chocolate, taro, cookies and cream, mango, green tea, butterscotch, cream and more. It was an array of different flavors, the common and the not so common, but they all were very good. There is also a plethora of toppings to accent your creation from cereal to fresh fruit and standard sweet morsels like white and milk chocolate. And don't worry about the pricing; it's not so bad considering that the place is new and is trying to fit in with the crowd. The price reflects the quality of the food and we all can't wait to come back to make new concoctions. Makes you wish this place hits a nerve and takes over Dairy Queens everywhere. It's a less than guilty expenditure and we need more fun places like this on the East coast!
label: POS

text: This had to be one of the worst places we "almost" stayed at--worse than any Motel 6 I've ever stayed at. We arrived into a room so cloying with mustiness, we just knew the odor would permeate our hair and clothes. We asked for another room and found it to be equally horrible in a dark and dank way. We were told that a credit could not be given as their was no manager on duty. Thankfully, prior to leaving for another hotel, we asked our host to write a note indicating her agreement with our assessment of the state of the rooms, for the next day, when we arrived back to ask for our credit, we were told we should have got one the evening before. If we had not produced the handwritten note from our prior night's host, I regret that we may not have been properly credited. While we ended up at a standard Omni up the street, our little petite suite there was clean, fresh, and wonderful.

The service wasn't all that great either, even by Philly food service standards. Don't get me wrong, it was an indulgence and kind of a tasty one at that but I don't think I could eat the food again knowing that the next day I'll feel sick.

text: Our attempt to eat here on May 29th after the US v Turkey match was a disaster. We don't have a Turkish restaurant here in Austin, TX so we always check out ones when we travel. We thought great - they have Efes, let's go! After the game we headed over, walked quite a bit, sat down, and had a server come up to us and basically tell us that we won't be served for a while and we should reconsider eating there because they were overwhelmed. Plus we were only two people so we were a "low priority" Efes? They were out. OK. So we figure, lets just have a beer and move on - we were tired and thirsty from the walk. We move to another table (after being kicked out of our previous one for a larger and higher priority party). Hubby goes to the bar and asks for and gets two relatively warm Efes beers. OK, so lets at least enjoy those as we never get any unless we are in Turkey. Then we notice a table behind us received their food - they had sat down after us. We thought - hey, why not wait it out. We got another two orders of Efes from the bar. We had servers walk by us repeatedly and tables come and go and NEVER once were we approached by any staff. NO Hos Geldiniz, nothing. After about 80 minutes and a rising level of disgust we ask for the guy in charge (he is in one of the pics on the homepage here) and he apologized and offered to serve us himself. But, by that time - no thanks. We were insulted. And, further, as our visits to Turkey are frequent, we know what genuinely can be expressed as "I'm sorry", this wasn't it. We left. Figured we would let people know how you can be treated here. They didn't even have a hostess taking names or telling people it will be a 90 minute wait and we will have a table for you. And, for the size of the restaurant they were not understaffed, they had about 10 servers. Funny thing is - we were warned about the attitude at this place by a friend who recently went. Just chalked it up to a bad day. Apparently not. Sad this is what it took to get me writing on Yelp. But at least now I can write a glowing review on Positano - THAT was yummy! I mean, it is not as if they should have been surprised there was a game that day and they might be busy.
label: NEG

text: I was recently in Reno, NV for business and consulted Yelp for a breakfast location. The favorable reviews pointed me towards Heidi's and I was very happy they did. Some folks around town that I met talked about the high price of breakfast at Heidi's, but in my opinion it was well worth it. The portions are large and really hit the spot. If you're in Reno and looking for a great breakfast, I don't think you'll be disappointed.

text: I've visited Einsteins 5 times within the last month. The store itself is clean, there's ample seating, but there is a distinct sense of chaos that is unmistakeable the instant you walk in the door during a busy time of day (which seems to be just my luck..) Orders are taken and you are sheparded down the line only to discover that what you ordered is "out of stock" only moments later. This has happened on at least 3 occasions when I've ordered simply plain bagels and challuh rolls (which I don't understand why these are even on the menu.. I think I've only gotten to get them once!).. Today I went through the drivethru (which is an accident waiting to happen - there was lots of paint scrapings on the side walls of the building) and ordered a plain bagel.. nothing more - just one plain bagel. I got it home and discovered I'd been given a poppyseed!.. I can appreciate a good bagel, and Einstein does in fact have them, its just the other incompetence that bothers me. Especially when it's not isolated to just one or two instances. The workers seem cheerful enough.. just wish they'd actually listen to what's being ordered instead of worrying about rushing to the next one in line.

text: Many people have that place where "everybody knows their name." For most, it's the local pub, a favorite restaurant or a store that gets the bulk of your paycheck. For me, it's Walgreens. But accidents happen, and the overworked pharmacists never make me feel like a loopy broad who takes a veritable variety pack of medications. I like to stay healthy. And thanks to Walgreens, I will be. Or, at least as healthy as I'm possible of being, with the help of modern medicine and all. Cue maniacal laughter...because "Carrie" and "healthy" are not usually two words you put together. Thanks Walgreens. You give me a reason to reach for a glass of water first thing in the morning and last thing at night.

text: I must say that i believe that I have been to almost all the coffee shops in town here, large and small. I had to meet someone in town and they suggested Bibo's. Never having heard of this place I was excited for new coffee place to try. The Sunday AM I went, (extremely early at 6am) I was floored by the sheer number of people in line!!! After a bit of a wait just for a drip coffee I finally was handed my hot beverage. I will say now that the wait was well worth it! For regular drip coffee I was amazed by great it was!! Not burnt not stale, almost perfect (darn near impossible to find "fresh" coffee anyplace) I sat there for at least 3 hours and the coffee just kept on pouring! Person after person after person, non stop for those 3 hours poured in the store and enjoyed the beverages they were made. The ambiance of the shop is very pleasant as well! Very comfortable sofas in the back and the regular tables were large enough for me to spread out and do some work on without having my papers drop off the side. I did hear that they also have oustide sitting but I didn't find that out until later. Over all I was very happy with my experience here and will be visiting as often as I can!!
label: POS

text: Yes, it's a chain, but oh how I love me some Penn Station. I'd marry the fries if it were legal. And, you know, not weird and stuff. No, seriously, I sometimes come to Penn Station just for the fries. I'll order two large buckets and nothing else, and I'll be perfectly happy. The fries are made from actual potatoes, and if you're curious, you can watch them spin-peel and slice the taters into fries. Add those to the oil, and bam! Real-fry heaven. Sometimes my body does yell at me to eat some veggies, though, so I either order the artichoke sandwich or make up my own. My weirdo dream sandwich includes artichokes, mushrooms, saurkraut, two types of cheese, lettuce, green peppers, tons of onions and some oil and vinegar. The folks at Penn Station never blink an eye when I order this, which I totally appreciate. For the record, I'm a skinny girl, but I can eat. When I do two buckets of fries, I'll only supplement that with a cookie. When I order a sandwich, it's either a small or medium, and I'll still order fries. My friends usually are filled by just a sandwich, but not me. In fact, I ate TWO large orders of fries AND a sandwich the other day. The Hampton Avenue Penn Station particularly is great. The workers there are friendly and quick, and they always manage to make my sandwiches really cheesy, even though I don't request it and even though I don't pay extra for it. "Cute girl favor" for me? Maybe. But seeing as how most of the sandwich makers here are girls and not boys, I wouldn't count on it. I think they've just finally realized that people like cheese on their sandwiches, especially vegetarian sandwiches. As others have mentioned, the lemonade at Penn Station is really, really good. I've found myself watering it down just a touch lately, though. Oh, and you'd probably guess this, but Penn Station is smoke free. Rock on. I give four stars instead of five for the following reasons: * The lemonade is behind the counter, and I feel really awkward waiting to ask someone to give me a refill. * They don't have to-go cups for water. I love the lemonade, but I only get it on rare occasions now; I generally drink water at all meals. More than half of my Penn Station orders are take-out, with me eating in the car on the way to wherever. However, the folks at most of the area Penn Stations look at you like you're crazy when you ask for a to-go cup for water. They usually hand you one of those tiny plastic cups, which are fine for dining in, but they don't fit into cup holders and lids don't fit them.
