text: Your typical "modestly upscale" Korean/Japanese Restaurant. That's the first tip off. Numerous non-Korean staff. Second tip off. Predominantly non-Korean diners. Third tip off. If you like restaurants that pretend to be hip by offering expensive "authentic" asian food in a sophisticated setting then this is for you. Yes, there are a lot of banchan(the small dishes), but they are awful. Eat the kimchi and you should be able to tell. Your korean friends know that they can judge a korean restaurant on that alone. Plus the lack of fishcake and beansprouts made me super sad. Soon dubu(soft tofu stew) was a wreck. I look for that certain viscosity thickness and overall unctiousness that is to be expected from good soon dubu. It was thin, one dimensional, and boring. My korean friends would be pissed...seriously. The rice which is basic was way too starchy. The rice must be sticky, not gummy. That pisses off everyone asian. It was tedious to eat. Bi bim bap. The gochujang(red sauce) was too thin and difficult to apply with the spoon. The bowl smelled of burnt chemicals probably b/c it hadn't been seasoned yet. But hey, it's Philly. There are literally 2 or 3 decent Korean restaurants and that's being generous. Some restaurants feed on culinary ignorance(wow! i've never had lebanese food before, this is so awesome! wow! chopsticks! Have you ever had sushi? I like chicken teriyaki!) this is one of them. Go to Jong Ka Jip for some seriously good and cheap soon dubu. There is a reason why everyone else eating is korean. Educate yourself with the real deal.
label: NEG

text: Meh indeed. First - we had a great rate, through Priceline I got our room for $28.00. The room itself was large and clean. End of the positive marks. The sheets were poly/cotton blend and the feel creeped me out, that and the holes in the sheets. Not, mind you, miniscule little wear spots - no. no, these were semi-huge. I got a toe stuck in one. The toiletries were awful. I usually donate my left-over hotel goodies to a shelter in SF but I wouldn't inflict these on anyone. The noise level was beyond belief. Our next door neighbors were alternately vocally amorous and throwing punches while screaming at the top of their lungs. I literally had to call security because of the fight one night. They put the guy out of the hotel. You know it's bad when you have to wear earplugs to get some shut-eye and you can STILL hear the folks and their "Oooh baby, mm hmm, yes yes you GOD" litany. The physical set-up of the place is a bit odd. There is no parking garage so all the parking stretches out horizontally. Major schlep from car to resort to room. Oh, and by the way, "Resort" is a serious misnomer, at least for the rooms allotted to the riff-raff (cheapo rooms) I'm sure the re-done "resort" rooms & suites are lovely. Howsomever, the standard rooms are not part of the resort - there is even a separate elevator to the hoi polloi sections. The food in the cafe was expensive and mediocre and the wait was long. We were there at the same time as the Tour de Nez, the beginning of the Reno Rodeo and a huge high school baseball tourney. Never again!

We told our server how much we enjoyed the fish and she gave us a much appreciated recommendation to go to Little Fish (that made up for her initial abruptness).

However, that probably just makes you appreciate your entree that much more. The dining room doesn't seat that many people, but that is a good thing. text: After a difficult morning at work, I decided to take myself out to lunch. I was on my way down Page Ave. with plans to eat at Gokul (one of my favorite lunch places) and saw that Haveli was open for business. I decided to change my plans and duck in. It was a good decision. I was warmly greeted at the entrance by Ms. Patel, the owner. She seated me and a server came over immediately, took my drink order and suggested I try the buffet. I found lots of great things on the buffet. Being American, I enjoy eating Indian cuisine even if some of it mystefies me. I know by this time I should know the names of the different dishes but I just can't quite get them down. Let's just say that everything i tried was yummy. The naan bread was piping hot and fresh and all the other hot casseroles on the buffet were great. Nothing was disappointing. Please note: I'm a vegetarian so i didn't try any of the dishes that had meat (though they looked good). If you're a vegetarian, you can always count on the Indian restaurants in the community to have something to eat that is not only vegetarian, but also tasty. Ms. Patel made it a point to come over to my table to be sure I was enjoying my meal and made me feel very welcome. I will be back again! You should give them a try!

text: BIG YAWN. I came here with my parents for dinner recently, as they live in the area and are always looking to try new places to eat. I wish I could have given this place a better review, but there was so much wrong here that I don't even know where to begin. Let's see... First of all, this is a CHAIN restaurant. Why do they have mandatory valet parking? Seriously? You're located next to a Crate & Barrel, right outside of a mall for God's sake - you're NOT Oystercatchers or Bern's! Secondly, a velvet rope by the entrance? I didn't realize I was going to eat dinner at a club in NYC's meat packing district! Again I must ask - seriously?! To top it off, they have this big gas fireplace blazing full force in the bar area...in the middle of the Summer...in Florida. Any place that is trying this hard to be over the top cool is obviously NOT. The food and service was decent. I had the pecan crusted mountain trout which was quite yummy. My Mom's dish, however, was less inspiring and mostly just a great disappointment. She ordered the Chilean sea bass (which mind you, was priced at $36). When our dishes arrived, the tiny piece of sad fish was obviously NOT Chilean sea bass, but regular sea bass. It was the smallest piece of fish I've ever seen for $36. It was literally served with maybe 4 carrots and NOTHING else. Now, I don't mind paying a pretty price for a top notch meal, but this was far from it. I've paid the same for dishes in much better restaurants and have gotten a much healthier piece of fish...that at least came with a potato or two! The most disappointing part of the meal? My Mom had clearly stated TWICE when we first arrived that she is gluten sensitive. Our waitress (who was over-the-top friendly in an almost phoney way) acknowledged she knew a great deal about gluten allergies as her roommate suffers from it. She assured us that she spoke with the chef and made sure that everything my Mom ordered would be prepared gluten free. Well, my Mom was up half the night, sick - having an attack after we got home from dinner, so I can assure you, her meal was NOT prepared gluten free! So diners with food allergies beware! Long story long - this place is super pretentious (as are many of it's clientele) and a bit on the tacky side. I felt like I was having dinner at some cheesy Vegas casino and paying WAY too much money for what I was getting.

text: Don't be fooled by the 4+ star rating. This place was an utter disappointment by all accounts. The building looks like it was flown in from Rocky Point. In this case I should have judged the book by its cover. I was so tempted to walk out and go to the place across the street that was highly recommended and looked much more pleasing to the eye. How much I regretted not doing that I can not describe. I ordered a carne asada torta and a fish taco. The wife ordered 2 chicken tacos and a carne asada taco. We also ordered a half side of guac, pico de gallo and chips, and drinks. The bill came out to 26 bucks with a tip. We found a seat in the back to hang out and wait. There were a few flies buzzing around which is always enjoyable to see when you have already ordered your food and need something to kill your hunger. A few minutes go by and they call our number. When going to get it I knew we had ordered too much. The guac was huge and they gave chips with both it and the pico. My wife described the chips as fried styrofoam. It seemed as though everything I tried was lacking any kind of flavor other than the main ingredient. The torta was also huge. The tacos looked very tasty as well. The bread on the torta was as big as I have seen. There was beans, carne asada with pickled onions, jalapenos, and carrots on the side. I piled it all on and added some guac and pico and began. The carne asada was not as fresh or hot as it should have been. Like it had been cooked well before I got there. The flavor was also lagging. The fish taco was great. It was fresh, hot, battered nicely, and had a good taste to it. The guac was basically chopped up avocado. Not much seasoning or any other flavor. Very disappointing. What was the worst was the pico de gallo. It consisted of chopped up tomato and a speckle of onions and jalapeno. I could see the green and white but all I could taste was tomato. The wife's tacos were on corn tortillas that looked amazing. I tried her carne asada taco and the corn tortillas tasted as fresh as they looked. However, her carne asada had the same unfresh and flavorless taste that mine had. As we ate we both agreed we should have went with our gut and went across the street. Then as we were walking out the wife the 100 dollar question. "How in the heck can you call yourself Taqueria Pico De Gallo and have the nerve to serve that chopped tomato crap and have any self respect?" This is not a knock on Tucson but if this is a 4.5 I'm afraid to know what you think a 2 is. From what I heard from relatives is it used to be good back in the day. That's understandable.

text: Alright, I know that Tucson isn't known for its stellar Chinese food, but I refuse to leave this experience stewing in the back of my mind. I have come to accept that, in general, when you don't have a huge community of ethnic people who will demand a certain "authenticity" to their home cuisine, you'll end up with a lot of Americanized versions of dishes. I actually don't mind it at all. What I DO mind is when the quality of those dishes are so incredibly piss-poor, it makes McDonald's beef patties seem more wholesome. So that was a long prelude to say - no matter how desperate you are for Chinese food, avoid this place until they fix a few things: 1) their "hot and sour soup" was pathetic - not hot nor spicy, absence of any kind of recognizable pork or seafood, and just plain bland. 2) their "lunch specials" are barely better than what you can get at Panda Express - why not charge $1-2 more and put some meat in your fried rice (as well as some vegetables), get rid of the neon-orange "sauce" on your slightly rancid and cold wontons (why are they there anyways?) and improve the quality of your meats in your main dishes. My husband got the General Tso's and the breading to meat ratio was about 5:1, and when you add in a bland and florescent "spicy sauce", it was nearly inedible. 3) we ordered the dumplings (6 for $8) and they were an insult. Again, the wrapping to meat ratio was totally off (3:1), and the filling had more cabbage in it than pork, and, to boot, it was bone dry on the inside. Really...I mean if you're going to overcharge for dumplings, then try to buy the premade ones that are a higher quality, please? Again, all I can say is that the problem with Golden Dragon wasn't necessarily the lack of spicy, authentic flavorings, but rather a consistent lack of quality is any of the ingredients they used in their dishes. I hope they read this website and improve their offerings.

There is a waiting area with windows so you can see the kitchen staff making the pizzas, complete with pizza tossing. The whole place has a loft-feeling to it - few walls that go to the ceiling, exposed brick, silver air ducts criss-cross the ceiling. Eat at the bar, in booths, or at tables. text: I must preface my review by first saying that I have not yet sampled the cuisine at Eastland Cafe. Eastland Cafe offers what the management refers to as "casually elegant" food, and what I've seen (brulee and roasted duck, for instance) seems to be about as upscale as it gets in our part of town. Eastland Cafe is cold hard proof that the East Side is becoming more and more gentrified by the month. Eastland claims to bring in a great and diverse blend of people from the neighborhood, but it's not much of a blend when all of the patrons are white, middle class 30-somethings who work in graphic design. Ok, that last bit wasn't necessarily fair. But that's kind of the vibe at Eastland. They offer really elegant cuisine, some delicious premium beers and fine wines, and that's what keeps the riffraff at bay. The servers and bartenders all seem quite nice, and if the food is as good as it looks and smells (and worth the cost), then I'm sure it's superb. It just seems a bit inauthentic for the neighborhood. If I was having a celebratory dinner because of a promotion or an engagement or something, this is probably the place I'd want to have it. Aside from that and popping in on occasion to try out some high alcohol content lagers, this place just isn't my scene.

text: When Citygarden first appeared last summer, I was a bit surprised and not sure what to make of it. I work nearby and walk around this area a lot and was pretty stunned to all of a sudden see children playing in fountains, a random head sculpture, and a lot of random people milling about in the middle of downtown. And it is just what downtown needed. A public green space, centrally located, where downtown visitors can just hang out. You can get a good view of the arch, the old courthouse, the civil courts building, and you are only a few blocks from Busch Stadium, Scottrade Center, and Washington Ave. Not to mention how amazing the landscaping and sculptures. For the uninformed, Citygarden is a part of St. Louis' gateway mall, which is a long mostly green corridor that extends from Kiener Plaza to Union Station. Eventually there will be even wider sidewalks, with an LED illuminated walkway all the way down. That's the plan, anyway. I highly recommend everyone check Citygarden out, and it should be on any downtown must-see list.

text: Meeting a friend obsessed with Greek cuisine for lunch, we naturally ran down the suggestions until he came to a restaurant I've never been to. So Ari's it was. The place DEFINITELY had some feng shui - and I immediately liked the cozy atmosphere. The waitresses were quick, accurate and attentive and I really appreciated how personable our waitress was- offering suggestions and making our eating experience that much more enjoyable. On to the food - never having eaten here I decided to try an appetizer along with my meal to get more data. Feeling apathy toward grape leaves, I decided I'd try the the Saganaki Flambe with the image of a platter of imported Greek cheese sticks in mind. The dish came out and on it were two small wedges, caked in what looked like panko batter. The waiter poured (what I assumed was) Ouzo on the wedges and set if aflame. Let me put this out there for everyone to see- FIRE IS ALWAYS FUN. The cheese wedges were, unfortunately, not as much fun. The flames DID mildly toast the breading and melted the outer edges of the cheese, but left the core intact - and apparently Saganaki is in the firmer family of cheeses. I also wasn't impressed by the small portion for $7 dollars. Fireworks be damned. I ordered the Gyro sandwich, which was advertised as being smaller and less expensive than the Gyro platter - but it's a pet peeve of mine when a 'sandwich' comes to the plate disassembled with not enough bread to go around (a rare exception to this philosophy exerts itself in my enjoyment of quesadillas - odd no?). I also took the option of adding 'Greek Potatoes' with 'special Greek seasoning' over french fries for a $1.00 up-charge. Try to look for that on the menu though - I sure couldn't find it. The Gyro was good - typical in my experience - and it was moderately sized. The meat was well prepared and seasoned and I always love the taste of tzatziki. And the proportions were appropriate for a hands on eating experience - even if I did feel the sandwich was smallish overall. And those Greek potatoes? They didn't seem to be more than potatoes cooked in oil long enough to soften. While not bad, there was definitely nothing 'special' about them. I'd have preferred fries. The experience added up to about $15 plus tip. I felt it was a little overpriced since my small appetizer was the same price as my small sandwich and I definitely felt as though I could have made better choices. I've had better, for cheaper at such places as Antonino's Taverna On the Hill. But the tastes and preparation were good, and I'd go back to try something else... when I can afford it. ^_~

text: Like Francesca K., I went into Career Girl Bridal because I was in the neighbourhood. text: I really feel the need to step in now; after reading reviews on a few restaurants on this site and being disappointed each time (even though the places all received high ratings). I counted 8 booths that could really only hold two people comfortably and then three tables cramped in between (one of which was filled with old newspapers). But it wasn't busy at all when I was there so I suppose I can't complain. Service: Again, it wasn't busy, so the service was immediate and fairly quick. No complaints. Food (sub-divided) Gyro: Pita Bread: Definitely store bought, I noticed it sitting in a retail plastic bag while ordering my food. Sauce: Their tzatziki sauce....well, they call it Cucumber sauce instead of tzatziki for a reason. It was sour cream, dill (LOTS) and huge chunks of cucumber, not a smooth sauce. Meat: The Meat was quite tasty; but without the accompaniments, it could not stand alone. Sandwich as a whole: This is the type of gyro place that puts the meat and toppings inside the pita bread, not between the two folded over halves of bread which makes for both sides to be extremely thin and prone to tearing/breaking. So ultimately I had a gyro that was overflowing with chunks of dill/cucumber that was falling completely apart by my second bite. I ended up eating it similar to a gyro dinner plate with a fork, luckily my greek salad came with a few chunks of the pita bread. I know what I typically expect out of a gyro sandwich includes lettuce, tomato, onion and fetta cheese, this sandwich did not have any of these; just Pita, Cucumber Sauce and Meat...That's it. Greek Salad: It's hard to mess up Lettuce, Fetta Cheese, a slice of Tomato and a slice of cucumber all topped with a vinegarette. Ultimately, and in short; I'm stuck continuing to search for a decent gyro in this town, and will not be heading back to Sam's any time soon.

text: The Chatillon-DeMenil Mansion is a pretty neat place to go if you are interested in Greek Revival architecture and history. The Chatillon-DeMenil mansion is an awesome sight to see. Build by one of St. Louis' earliest and one of the most prominent residents, the Chatillons and the DeMenils, the home was built to the grandeur that it is now. Inside you can see many of the old classic furniture that the family had from the 1800s. The Chatillon-DeMenil Mansion also houses one of the coolest things that I think this place has, the largest collection of artifacts from the 1904 World's Fair. You can see many of the things that would have been present at the World's Fair that people would have picket up while visiting it. There are things from crystal ware to sheet music and fan's that people would have used. The exhibit is very interesting. The Chatillon-DeMenil Mansion is very interesting and if you have an interest in St. Louis history then it is something that is defiantly worth checking out.

The waitress was pleasant and gave us plenty of time to decide, and there looks like a ton of great things on their menu. It's pretty hot & humid so I decided against the lobster corn dog w/mac & cheese, which was what really intrigued me. Instead, I got a sandwich - the Medusa: spinach & feta spread, muenster, mozzarella, white cheddar and roasted tomato on sourdough. Plus a side of frittes. My friend ordered Antoinette: strip steak, gruyere, onions & mushrooms. "Roasted tomatoes" says something to me other than "sliced romas," which is what was on the sandwich. It pretty much tasted like a grilled cheese & tomato. Which isn't bad, but I was thinking there'd be more green on it from the spinach spread. It was way too cheesy for my taste, though it was definitely a tasty grilled cheese sandwich. The fries were warm when they came out but cooled quickly; my beef with any restaurant that serves fries is that they should be served in a cone like Belgians do, so they stay hot. Not Lola's fault that we're not in Europe, I suppose, though a good idea should be cross-cultural. They were definitely homemade and had the slightly greasy consistency of really good homemade fries. Quite tasty. The bread was fresh and grilled just right - very tasty bread. Jay's sandwich was a big disappointment: The meat was tough and one piece of it was half gristle! No one wants to dismantle a sandwich to cut off the gristle & then reassemble. Blech. Why serve that? It wasn't that it was bad, but for the price & all the good reviews the place has gotten I just expected more. If someone suggests Lola in the future, I'll go and try something different - maybe a crepe, since that's why Jay loves the place and that's what he usually gets. text: Exceptional, wonderful clinic that offers low-cost acupuncture and herbs on a sliding scale based on your income. The clinic is a group setting: You have a private consultation with one of the two doctors, and they become your permanent doctor (unless you want to see the other one). The first visit is the longest one: you spend about forty five minutes discussing everything: your diet, your exercise levels, your health history, etc. Then you go in for treatment: The treatment room is warm, clean and very comfortable. You choose a reclining chair and the needles are administered. The doctors at Community Acupuncture are somewhat conservative in their approach; they only use needles where absolutely necessary. Each one is taken out of their brand-new, completely sterile paper pouch. They are immediately discarded after use. As with all acupuncture clinics they are NEVER re-used. I would recommend this clinic to anyone. Acupuncture is designed to be most effective when used frequently. The sliding scale fee at Community Acupuncture makes it possible for me to go every week; sometimes twice a week if I'm working through something. Community Acupuncture rocks!

text: I visited Bottleworks on a night that began with plans of going to the Tap Room, but ended up here instead. Bottleworks turned out to be a great choice. Bottleworks is located next to the Schlafly brewery where you can take a tour. Bottleworks offers an array of dishes, and many of their appetizers and entrees incorporate locally grown ingredients. Possibly the biggest bonus to this location, is since you are right next door to the brewery you have access to all of Schlafly's different varieties. I decided on the ahi tuna reuben. The tuna had been grilled and was a nice change from the salty fatty corn beef that you traditionally find on a reuben. It was also served opened face on what the menu called "black Russian bread" that stood up to the sandwich and didn't get soggy. I found it very easy to eat with a knife and fork, which I appreciated. My sandwich also came with a side salad of romaine lettuce served with a dressing that I couldn't figure out but really liked. Two of my friends that joined me got personal 10'' pizzas that I got a chance to try. I will be coming back to Bottleworks to get a pizza of my own. Not only were the toppings great, but the sauce had a great full flavor that reminded me of a Chicago style pizza, but it wasn't. I'm a big fan of Chicago style pizza so the sauce won me over alone. On the night I was there Bottleworks also had a live bluesy type band playing that I really liked. Also the service was great. I could see my waiter was very busy, but he was on top of things. I think Bottleworks is a great place for locals or out of town visitors. Locals can appreciate supporting local businesses with many of the dishes, and visitors can get a taste of Schlafly (try the beer sampler). I'm going to give it 4 stars for now, but I could see future visits bringing it to 5.

text: Yangming is much like the Main Line; pretentious, over-rated, uninspired, and a bit of a tired cliche. Which must explain why Yangming is normally busy with pretentious, uninspired and a bit tiresome Main Liners. Here on the Main Line, it doesn't have to be good, it just has to have the mythos of being good. But what a ancient myth it is in the case of Yangming (circa early 1990s to be exact). Yangming was one of the first restaurants in the Philly area offering Asian Fusion. At the time it was unique and notable. But with the growth of Asian Fusion cuisine, Yangming has been left behind. Yangming's fusion is stale and timid. Is the food bad? No. Yangming uses quality ingredients and what results is passable. But it is hardly what they promise, a great dining experience. Unfortunately Yangming is too much fusion to be a good Chinese restaurant, and too lackluster to be a great Asian Fusion choice. As for service, well, surly Asian waiters may be authentic, but not what I'd desire at a place where the tab for two could easily exceed $100. The decor is straight out of the early 90's and lacks any interest. Like the cuisine at Yangming, the ambience is tiredly refined.

text: In the past 6 years, Morimoto has always been a guilty indulgence-type restaurant for me & my friends. We have dined there several times before, to great satisfaction (except we discovered that their omakase menu never changes). These same friends drove up from Baltimore last night in the rainy, cold weather specifically so we could go eat at Morimoto. I made reservations for three people at the sushi bar at 9:15p. The hostess on the phone told me that there might be a "little" wait, but not more than 15-20min. Fine. Jump ahead to 8:45p - we arrive early, expecting to go up to the lounge for some drinks while we waited for our reservation. 9:15p comes, and we ask about our seats - we're told that it will be a little longer. Fine. Jump ahead to 10:00p - we ask a waitress to check on our table, as it's now been 45 min. since our reservation - she never comes back. We then ask a different server the same question - she comes back about 15 min. later to tell us that our seats still aren't available. At this point, one would think that the server/hostess would have the sense to at least offer us peanuts and the option maybe to sit at an actual table, if the sushi bar is over-crowded. Of the three hostesses hovering around the hostess stand, their combined brain cells could not come up with any alternative options or consolation items. We saw people in the lounge, who were seated well after us, being led to their tables/seats before us. After paying our $78 check (for 4 drinks) and being told several times that we would have to wait "a little longer," we finally decided to leave. The food is good at Morimoto, but there's no restaurant where the food is worth waiting over one hour, especially when you have a reservation. It was like a Seinfeld episode - what's the point of a reservation?! Word to the wise - if you want good sushi, there are better places than Morimoto; if you want good martinis/drinks, there are better places than Morimoto; if you want omakase, it's worth trying once at Morimoto, but you are a sucker if you get it again & again - the whole point of omakase is that the menu should be created on the day of w/ the freshest ingredients specific to that day - Morimoto's omakase is a cookie-cutter menu with slight variations (i.e.: maybe they give you hamachi instead of toro). On our way out, my friend complained one of the vapid, brainless hostesses, who did nothing but say "I'm sorry." Yes, you should be sorry - you just lost 3 customers!

The service is good, but its a casual place, not fine dining. The decor is modern, and it can get a little loud, because its always packed. text: My aunt and uncle regularly stay at this hotel on their monthly trips to the Quarter, so when my father and I were coming down to escape the Wisconsin cold they more or less insisted we stay here. I'm happy they were so insistent, because if left to our own devices we would have ended up someplace rather generic and likely not in the Quarter. Le Richelieu is an older hotel with what you'd call 'character' - it certainly reminded me of hotels in Paris or London. It was an interesting contrast for me, as just before leaving for vacation I'd gone up to the Twin Cities for an industry event. I'd ended up staying at a brand-spanking-new Courtyard by Marriott in Maple Grove, and by all outward appearances my room was excellent. The furniture and wardrobe were new, there was a flat-screen TV, and the mattress was new and soft with layered pillows and duvet. Despite the relative luxury of the room, I slept poorly on the mattress (too soft), couldn't get the WiFi to work, and the hot water was a bit touch and go for the shower. Le Richelieu, on the other hand, looked its age. The room was a bit spare, the furniture a touch dingy, and the mattress and bedding nothing to speak of. Yet our stay went perfectly in every way. My uncle had secured the reservations for us, and as a result neither my father nor I had actually looked up the location of the hotel aside from the address and number. My father had gotten quick Google directions from the rental car place to the hotel, but unfortunately Google forgot Jackson Square is pedestrian-only. No matter, it was easy enough to find our way around. Once we pulled up to the front of the hotel I ran in and received a parking pass from the clerk and instructions of how to get to the parking lot. After navigating down to Esplanade and back around to Barracks we quickly found a spot and unloaded our luggage. The hotel has a secure parking lot directly to the rear of the hotel, and it could not have been more convenient. Our first impressions of the lobby and staff were quite favorable, and we quickly checked in and dropped off our bags in the room. As previously mentioned, the room wasn't outwardly impressive but once I discovered the doors leading out to the balcony my opinion did a full 180. I'd been given the WiFi code as well at check-in, and my father logged in quickly to dash off a few emails as I soaked up the afternoon sun. We were in a thirsty mood so I didn't stay too long on the balcony. We dropped off the key at the front desk - another policy reminiscent of the Old Country - and made a quick jaunt down Gov. Nicholls to Decatur. The entire French Quarter was well within walking distance, and we ended up spending the entire night rambling about, returning a couple of times to change and later drop off the remnants of dinner. It was close enough to everything that we could easily go back and forth, but also located in a relatively quiet and peaceful part of the Quarter so we slept undisturbed. The next morning we were up with the sun, surprising given the night prior. The hotel has a small glassed-in cafe by the courtyard, and we came down for a quick breakfast. I was still relatively full from the night before, so I limited myself to a croissant and coffee. My father went big, ordering a full breakfast that I ended up tag-teaming on. The cafe was excellent, serving by far the best coffee I've ever had in a hotel excluding Paris. The croissants were light and flaky, and a bit surprisingly cut in two and lightly toasted. I'd never had a croissant done up in this manner. It was bright and sunny, and after enjoying a couple additional cups of coffee after breakfast we made it down to the French Market to see the vendors start to set out their wares. New Orleans isn't really a town suited for early risers, but it was especially enjoyable to walk around and see the city start to rise. The check-out time at the hotel wasn't until 1:00 PM, so we had plenty of time to continue our exploration. I now know why my aunt and uncle stay at this hotel every time they come to New Orleans, and I can say I'll do the same.

text: We were cranky by the time we got to Felix's. The temperature was set to "Hell" and "2nd Realm of Hell." We pushed aside our fears about the fact that the joint was near-empty and got our sustenance on. 1/2 dozen raw oysters and a shrimp po'boy later in an air-conditioned cafeteria-style restaurant, and I was a happy human again. Because of the Gulf oil spill, the oysters are being shipped from Texas. Slight bump up in price, but still worth it. They give you a bunch of condiments to concoct your own perfect cocktail sauce for the oysters and I liked that. Great service and great food -- and I'm certain it's cheaper than Acme's. text: For more than 75 years, Fleishman Fabrics & Supplies has loomed over the Fifth Street intersection where Passyunk Avenue vanishes into the tumult of South Street, selling fabric, trimmings, dry cleaning and tailoring supplies. All summer along, a wheeled rack has perched on the sidewalk in front of the store, as bright and incongruous as a bird-of-paradise in the concrete jungle. I paused to rummage the rainbow the other day and was delighted to discover it was full of dance costumes. As I surveyed the selection, Tricia Fleishman, who owns the business with her husband, Stanley, approached. "If you have time, I have a thousand more costumes on the third floor." Say what? How many? After climbing three flights of stairs through Fleishman's vertical fabric warehouse, Tricia led me to a series of jerry-rigged racks stuffed with enough spangled tulle and bedazzled Lycra to outfit an army of Rockettes. Leotards shining with sequins, a fully decked-out Vegas Elvis suit, tutus of all colors, harem pants and fringed rompers -- it was enough to make this former performer dance with glee. Prices start at $5 per piece, with discounts for those (like me) who purchase in multiples. My best friend and I walked out with 22 pieces, some destined for Halloween parties, others to start the best dress-up box ever for my 3-year-old cousin. The Fleishmans welcome dance companies, as well as anyone with a yen for sparkles, to peruse the racks for Halloween and beyond.

text: Das Marriott Philadelphia Downtown liegt im Herzen der Stadt in direkter Lauf nähe zur City Hall und zu den Sehenswürdigkeiten und Einkaufsmöglichkeiten. Der Hotelkomplex umfasst über 1300 Zimmer und Suiten in zwei Häusern. Somit hat man das Gefühl, man steht an einem Flughafen als in einem Hotel. Ca. 6 bis 8 Empfangsmitarbeiter checken ständig Hotelgäste ein und aus. Wenn man es mal geschafft hat, einen Zimmerschlüssel zu bekommen, geht die Suche nach dem richtigen Aufzug los. Man muss wirklich gut zuhören, ob man im Hauptgebäude oder im luxuriöseren Annex untergebracht ist. Die Zimmer allgemein sind sehr schön und teilweise neu renoviert. Der Stil ist mir persönlich einfach zu altbacken. Blümchentapete, Kronleuchter, schwere Vorhängeaber absolut in Ordnung. Im Hotel selber gibt es einige Restaurants. Das große Frühstücksrestaurant befindet sich im Lobby Level und bietet jeden Morgen ein großes Frühstücksbuffet für 19 US-Dollar an. Der Service war nett und das Speiseangebot absolut lecker und ausreichend. Von Kollegen habe ich gehört, dass es Abends leider wohl nicht so ist! Ebenfalls gibt es direkt daneben einen großen Starbucks um ein schnelles Frühstück einzunehmen. Zur Entspannung gibt es einen großen Pool und mehrere Fitness-Center im Hotel. Das Hotel ist perfekt für Geschäftsreisende sowie für einen privaten Aufenthalt. Durch die perfekte Innenstadtlage ist es ein prima Hotel. Lediglich die Größe ist wirklich manchmal stressig. So musste ich 40 Minuten warten, bis mir ein Modemkabel aufs Zimmer gebracht worden ist.

I wanted to go for a banana chocolate chip ice cream with some twix pieces "blasted" in. Unfortunately, they don't do that. The blasts are only for chocolate and vanilla soft serve. Maybe there's some explanation as to why they can't toss some twix into a blender with hand-dipped ice cream, but I'm sure it's lame. So I was left with the choice of banana chocolate chip ice cream or a twix blast. I chose the latter. Poor choice. Their soft serve kind of tastes like chalk. Actually it's more like that milk they serve in Philadelphia public school cafeterias. You know, the kind that comes in a juice box and doesn't have to be refrigerated? Gross. text: This is solely about the AYCE Dim Sum special. We came here Saturday night since I've been wanting to try out the 13.95 AYCE Dim Sum special. First off, the place was SLAMMED. We were in line for about 10 minutes waiting for a table, as the tables were completely full. After being seated, it took almost ten minutes to get our drinks, which were ordered as we were being seated. My first round of Dim Sum came out pretty quickly, about ten minutes or so, but was missing an order of spring rolls. Not a huge deal--I figured I'd order it again on the next round. Our server was busy to the point where I had to get up and got my own sauces, which, for the record, I was fine with. If you'd rather sit there waiting for the obviously swamped server to come back around to your table than to get up and get it yourself... well then I think you deserve to be sauceless, my friend. 100 percent without sauce. After I'd polished off the first round, I had to walk around the restaurant to try to track down the server in order to get another order sheet. Filled it out quickly and thrust it at him as he rushed by to another table. I suspect that had I not done that, it would have taken five or ten more minutes for him to get back and pick it up. The second (and as it turned out, final) round of dim sum came out quicker than the first round. Turns out it came out faster because it was undercooked a bit, as well as saturated with grease. It was as if the oil temperature was too low, so the oil just soaked the food rather than cooking it crisply. Within five minutes, the oil had leeched out of the pot-stickers and crab rangoon, pooling in the bottom of the tray the dim sum was sitting on. It was pretty rough going from there, and I only got through about half of the remaining food before I couldn't do anymore. Luckily this place isn't anything like Sushi Pier 2, where they watch over your shoulder and ring you up full price for each individual roll you don't finish entirely, so it wasn't an issue that I didn't finish everything on the tray. Out of everything I tried on the dim sum menu, only two items struck me as being noteworthy. First, the shrimp and pork siu mai was loaded with shrimp, which was cooked to perfection. And while I'm sure that all shrimp is magically cooked to perfection in the bay area (just like everything else is... I think the bay area fairies must fly around sprinkling 'perfect food' dust on everything there--at least according to a ton of fuck-tard bay area yelpers anyway)... finding shrimp cooked so well in Reno tends to be a rarity, so it's worth mentioning. Second, the crab rangoon had actual crab in it, and not "krab flavored juice" or whatever these other places in town try to get away with. I can say I probably won't be doing the dim sum again, but I'll be definitely back in here soon for some regular menu items.

text: It is quite enjoyable to try to eat and drink your way through a city. I must say that I have just begun to scratch the surface of this town. In a valiant effort to start at Penn's Landing and eat my way through to University City, I went to Morimoto. The decor reminds me of the sleek, mod vibe of Pod with the shape of the seating as well as the shapes on the walls. I started with the rock shrimp tempura and my friend had the edamame. Both appetizers were quite large. The shrimp tempura had a slightly sweet glaze on it, which contrasted quite nicely with the good saltiness of the edamame. Next came the entrees, I chose Duck,duck,duck and she chose the "surf & turf". My duck meal consisted of a madras roasted duck breast (yum!) and a confit risotto with a duck egg on top (double yum)! The breast was cooked perfectly, and the risotto was great with a hint of sweet and savory. The surf consisted of Hamachi on avocado and lightly tossed with something that I don't remember, but I do remember the taste. Her turf consisted of Kobe beef, sliced very thinly. I would estimate that it weighed about 2oz., but it was like eating butter! I can see the draw in eating Kobe beef. I saved room for a dessert (of course) and had the pot de creme. It was covered with a lovely whipped cream and the chocolate was the right density that I love. The only thing I did not enjoy was the carmelized banana that was served on the side. The texture was a little off for me. The wait staff was attentive, knowledgeable and efficient. It was a great experience and I will go back to have the sushi there. Maybe on that visit, I'll see Morimoto! ETA: *see* Morimoto (last sentence)
label: POS

text: My mom has Celiac disease, and I am allergic to yeast (and I am also suspected to have Celiac), so I eat a lot of gluten-free foods. A lot of people think that people who cannot eat wheat or gluten have nothing to eat. I've seen the pity in their eyes, but I am here to tell you that there is no more need for pity! Kinnikinnick has come to the rescue of Celiacs everywhere! This gluten-free bakery has some really amazing items. There are some ill-tasting gluten-free products out there, but most of Kinnikinnick's items are extremely tasty. The most delicious items are the chocolate cupcakes, carrot cakes, muffins, cookies, lemon tarts, and pizza buns. I actually can't even tell that these items are gluten-free--they are that good. The donuts are also quite good, but they are a bit heavy and brick-like. I don't personally like their pizza crusts--I have a much better recipe that I make at home. The gluten-free bread doesn't taste like real bread--it's not even close really, but I have gotten used to it, and I like it. It's best toasted. The English muffins, however, are very good. They are very light and spongy. I wouldn't bother going for the hamburger buns, because they seem to be the same recipe as the English muffins and are too small. I also don't enjoy the hot dog buns, because they are way too big, and it feels like I am eating my hot dog between to giant slices of sponge cake. The store is rather expensive, but for Celiacs it's worth it. There are other products on the shelves like pasta and flour mixes. Some of this stuff you are get elsewhere for cheaper, especially the brown rice pasta. The packaged gravies are really good and are worth every penny. Kinnikinnick does ship items all over the world. They also take orders, but if it's close to a holiday like Christmas, you need to order early; otherwise, you'll miss out.

text: This restaurant easily makes a new addition to my list of the worst restaurants in the United States. Located at the end of Stearn's wharf in Santa Barbara, CA, the restaurant is literally situated above the ocean. Their sign outside says "Fish and Chips" and clearly depicts a fish with fries superimposed on it. Their menu inside lists Fish and Chips for $10.95 and adds the words to the effect "You must try this". The message was clear enough to me. Their best dish is the fish and chips, and I should try it immediately lest I be made out to be a fool. Given the proximity to the ocean and the ease with which this comfort food can be prepared, this seemed like a sure bet. Sure enough though, this choice was a most regrettable one. What was presented to me was an unmitigated disaster. The several apparent errors were all equally egregious. First of note was that the chips were actually POTATO CHIPS and not fries as depicted on their very own sign. If you are going to re-define a well known dish, you should provide the appropriate caveat to the customer. Short of that, if you are going to make a major substitution, it should at least be for the better. Alas. These potato chips were unusually salty, and their flavor once adjusted for the high salt content, failed to add anything to the dish. There were also not many chips, so this clearly was a cheap gesture. Another cheap gesture was stacking the two filets on said chips on a tiny plastic salad plate and not offering trays. One really needed to use both hands to carry this plate to a table and make sure nothing fell along the way. I am sure someone looked at unit costs and determined that tiny disposable salad plates would be a money saver. Additionally, cocktail sauce was not on view, but was available upon request only. So far not so good, and we haven't even got to the fish yet. Dreadful -- in a word. I will allow that the color was nice and that it was not over fried. But seriously, how do you fry fish so that it has NO TASTE whatsoever?? I would insert a forkful in my mouth, jostle it around my tongue, consider it, search for some nuance of flavor, shake my head effectively giving up, and swallow. Repeating the process twenty times or so I ultimately finished this terrible meal. While I labored and, well, suffered through this meal, you don't have to. Please, just avoid this place. The majority of their business is unsuspecting tourists who won't return to the wharf anytime again soon. With all of their cost cutting measures, it is just easy money for them, and they have no incentive to change. Amazing seafood can be found in Santa Barbara at a spectrum of price points. There is really no reason to consume anything here. And if you think my critique of the fish and chips was harsh, I can only imagine what my review would have been like for their number two bestseller, the clam chowder in a bread bowl. The broth was brown -- yikes!Enough said.
label: NEG

The place is really recently opened; it used to be a hotel and before that, a printing press, so Jason explained that every room is really different in character because of it. Our space was really nice, spacious bathroom and all the normal amenities, including free wifi. The only downsides - you can tell (maybe because its a 3-star hotel) that the sheets were worn and thin, as were the pillows. The night time person was also somewhat unhelpful when we couldn't get our pay-per-view movie to work, but *shrug* it was okay. They also have a hang-on-the-door card that you mark to indicate your breakfast choices - its all packaged stuff (juice, blueberry muffin, piece of fruit, and yogurt or nature valley bar), but the gesture was nice nonetheless and Jason was the one who actually delivered it. Would definitely stay there again and highly recommended.

text: I wish there was a "zero" stars option. My husband our baby daughter and I went over to Reno for a quick getaway. We had only played at Peppermill but never stayed there so we gave it a try since we got a free room upgrade on hotels.com to a jacuzzi room. As for the room, the bed was so uncomfortable that I didn't get any sleep, they only provided two little teeny pillows for a huge bed, the shower was just a light stream of water in a big cold space, and the jacuzzi had this annoying spout that ran a big loud splashing stream of water in between me and my husband. We had originally planned to have dinner at the main Italian restaurant on the casino area but it was so smokey in the casino that I was afraid that the baby would get sick. So we ended up spending way more money than we had planned on at the new steakhouse on the second floor. At least the food was good, but the wine list was so big it took us 20 minutes just to pick something out. And they were charging 45 bucks for wine I buy at the store for 11.99. Later that night my husband and I took turns gambling while the other stays with the baby in the room. When it was my turn, I needed to cash a ticket he had given me to gamble with but the machine wasn't reading it. When i finally found the information booth (finding anything or even knowing where you are in that place is very difficult) I asked the lady where the cashier's desk was. She pointed me around the corner, but all I found was another machine. When I was going back to tell her that wasn't what I had asked, I tripped over one of the pole things that mark where the line is and knocked it over, almost falling down. Rather than making sure I was okay or helping me fix it, she just laughed at me! and loudly too! I went in tears to the front desk and told the shift manager what had happened. She was very nice and apologetic and assured me shed let her manager know. I was so embarrassed that rather than enjoying myself and gambling a little, I went back up to the room and cried to my husband. I'll never go back to the Peppermill, not for anything. Which is sad because my husband and I used to enjoy the island buffet and the fireside lounge when its just us two. I'll never spend another penny in that place, and if anyone is considering staying here, just don't. The Atlantis was our first choice, it is so much nicer, less smokey, less confusing, the staff is awesome and its even cheaper! Shop around!!!

text: Recently I went back to New Jersey and the restaurant businesses that had busted out all over the place gave me the creeps, set me wondering whether I was in the right place. It never seemed to change in all my eighteen years of angsty childhood and adolescence. Pei Wei now paves the way for excellent and efficient Asian cuisine in this part of stuffy suburban South Jersey. Faster than your typical take-out Chinese, Pei Wei offers a more trimmed down selection but from more parts of the continent. Our order for five on a Friday night included: Crab wontons, how they were not crab rangoon escapes me and doesn't even bother me. So delicious. Get the six count. Get two orders of the six count. We did. Spring rolls, nothing special but packed with plenty of springy stuff with just a little crunch. Chicken fried rice, not very special, fairly devoid of Stuff. Beef lo mein, absolutely amazing wonderful dish with well-spiced beef and delicious noodles that are not too greasy and just oh so good. Sweet n sour crispy chicken, which was yummy and crispy to just the right degree accompanied by pineapple and other stir fried goodness. Honey seared shrimp, again like the fried rice nothing special and actually a little heavy. Shrimp pad thai, this I did not actually taste. My mother was a big fan though. And at the end no one felt like a huge greaseball, just a bulging belly of satisfaction. Wouldn't reccomend going here to eat, as it is very fast and thus quite noisy. 15 minute wait for this entire order! Took us almost that long to drive here.

text: I visited STL over the weekend. Due to a bet that I won, one of my friends treated me to the infamous "Adam" Bomb. What is an "Adam" Bomb? It is a combo platter that is in honor of Adam Richman from Travel Channel's Man Vs. Food. It consists of a full slab of ribs, a beef brisket sandwich, a pulled pork sandwich, a 1/4 chicken, 4 sides, and a hot link frito pie. I think we lucked out because it seemed like we received a 1/2 chicken, not a 1/4 chicken. In addition to this monstrosity, my friend also ordered some additional hot links. Do you think this is a lot of food? What if i told you this was to feed myself (1 guy) and 2 petite girls? Unbelievable right? Well believe it. For sides, we got cole slaw, corn on the cob, sweet potato fries, and green beans. Okay fair enough, i will be the 1st to admit that we were no where close to finishing this monstrosity. We killed the ribs but picked at the chicken, ate very little of the beef brisket, and pulled pork. Ate probably 1/4 of the sides, and i tried one spoonful of the hot link frito pie. The portions are huge so come with a big party or a hearty appetite. The food was good though. The ribs were memphis style dry-rubbed ribs. Isn't that ironic? A STL bbq joint that serves Memphis style ribs...and it's GOOD! The hot links were amazing, they had a nice kick to them. The chicken was very moist. The beef brisket seemed too lean for my taste, but the pulled pork was good with the bbq sauce. The cole slaw was too liquidy but it was flavorful. The deep fried corn on the cob was chewy but tasty. Caveat, this place can get CROWDED. We did take out, but when we picked up the food there was a huge line there. It was insane. Either come early and beat the crowd or have your food to go. They wrap the food really well so you don't have to worry about things leaking out. I can't wait for Pappy's to show up to NYC for the Big Apple BBQ Block Party.

text: I've been to Dickey's a few time for lunch. Here's my two cents: Pro's: *The folks working the counter and the bussing are always very friendly. *The quality of meat is good. It won't win any awards for best BBQ, but it's still high on my list. *Free ice cream! *I love the take home cups. It's a great size for filling up at home when you don't want to keep refilling, but don't want a HUGE glass. Con's *This place gets a considerable amount of business at lunch. To ease the lines, they should put the menu up somewhere other than the front counter. Maybe I'm a tad slow, but the menu is hard to read/understand when you get up there. Perhaps placing a smaller version of it in the long entrance hallway would work. *In relation to the first con, this place is quite cramped at lunch. They could double the size and it would probably be just right. *Ease of Sauce. Unlike other BBQ joints where the sauce is on the table, Dickey's makes you get it from the "Sauce Bar". In order to get some sauce for your food, you have to use these awkward ladles and extremely tiny cups. text: What can I say? This Pat O's is one of my favorite places in the entire world. That pretty much says it all, and I shouldn't have to write another word, but I'm going to! I've had an awesome time every single time I've come here. The nighttime crowd is a bit older, but it's a nice break from the sweaty and often creepy joints along Bourbon, which are always packed with way too many grab-happy dudes. The lines to get into the piano bar are often long, but they move fast. The drinks are strong and the piano players are excellent (although I could do without the tray-tapping guy). It's the perfect place to tie one on and sing like an idiot. What else could you ask for? Well, you could ask for an amazing courtyard, and you'd get one here! The courtyard is one of my favorite stops during the day, and the flaming fountain is just magical at night. The courtyard can get hot during the summer, though they try to cool things down with fans and big shade umbrellas. Service in the courtyard is generally better than it is in the piano bar, but things get cramped and crazy in the piano bar and you can't really blame the servers for that. One thing that bothers me about Pat O's is that they charge you for the glass when you buy their specialty drinks, then if you don't want the glass you take it to the bar when you're done and they'll give you the $3 back. I just wish I didn't have to mess with that at all, but it's not enough of a nuisance to deduct any stars. I've had a five star experience at Pat O's every time, even on those nights when I have one hurricane too many...

text: Here's a rundown of Chifa's chef tasting menu from my birthday. Please keep in mind that this was my first ctm, so I'm a little biased and over excited. We had a great time! The restaurant was very dark and trendy with modernist Asian design. I recommend requesting a booth as the tables toward the front of the place are cramped quite close together. Our waitress was friendly, and really on the ball. We ate for 2 solid hours, but it felt like 20 minutes. First plate - Duck Ceviche: duck confit with foie gras, cherry puree on toasted brioche with corn nuts. Each serving was presented in a Asian style soup spoon which you ate in one bite. The ceviche was very smooth with a surprising crunch. Second plate - Snapper Ceviche: snapper sashimi with a wasabi and ? dressing and roe garnish. Served on a round glass tray. The snapper was perfectly seasoned, the taste of the wasabi was only a quick tang. I ate the entire dish, which went really well with the white wine I was drinking. Third plate - Pan: four small, slightly sweet buns with a reddish spread. I have no idea what the hell I was eating, but hot-damn it was good! The bread alone was delicious, but the spread had a tangy, sweet flavor. Fourth plate - Simple Green salad. A mix of tomato and feta cubes with string beans, edamame, and garlic dressing. The feta gave the salad a fantastic, creamy finish. Fifth plate - Oyster "leche de tigre" served on the half shell in a cream sauce. I wish there had been more then just the one. Sixth plate - Braised oxtail, layered on top of a potato-ish disk with a tiny little egg and a flake of bacon. This was my least favorite dish, but I've never been a big fan of oxtail. Seventh plate - Pork Belly Buns. Apparently this is Chifa's specialty and I can see why. Two fatty pork belly slices layered on small sticky buns. Eighth plate - Rack of Lamb. Two rare cuts of spicy bbq lamb with ginger quinoa and pickled cucumber and cabbage. I loved the lamb, which was very gamey and the quinoa. Boyfriend found the smell of the cabbage a little overwhelming. Ninth plate - Stir Fried Rice with Scallops. A nummy soy glazed scallop resting on a bowl full of rice with mango, edamame, ginger, and egg. Great taste! Tenth plate - Aji Mushrooms with a pastry puff top. The taste of the mushrooms was a little overwhelming on its own. But the ahi cream sauce would taste perfectly over a white fish. Dessert - Banana Picarones. Pumpkin banana funnel cake with honey anise lace, spicy peanut sauce and banana sorbet. The funnel cake was tiny but delicious, however I did not like the sharp flavor of the anise. It detracted a little too strongly from the sweet.
label: POS

text: I have never seen a set up reviews so uniformly correct on Yelp. The only great thing about this place is the wonderful outdoor dining area that is charming on a nice night. Unfortunately, I do not like eating outside, nor did I like the smoke (which you can smell from inside this restaurant since the doors are left open and people come in and out often). Although I personally do not enjoy the outdoor dining, it was the only reason I rounded my star rating up to 2. But it barely made the round up. :p The noise level was very high, and the place was packed (seriously, it baffles my mind to no end). The tables were tiny, it was barely big enough for 2 takeout containers and 4 cups. By the time we had dessert, we had to eat over our takeout containers, which were hanging half off the table. The service was half decent. Our waitress was very attentive and was not impatient with us even though we asked for more time to order 3 times (we had restaurant.com coupons and had to do some serious math). However, the food was terribly slow getting to us and brought by a random other person and not by our waitress. Now to lambast the food. My friend ordered shoestring fries and a jumbo chicken steak (no cheese). I tried his food (I know the rule of no 2nd hand reviews :) ), and the fries were not really "shoestring" thin in my opinion. About as thick as your average Burger King, McD or Wendy's fries. However, they were fried very nicely and crisp. That is where anything really positive about the food ends. The chicken steak was huge, but the chicken was rather dry and completely not seasoned. I ordered their chef's special of Italian Sweet Sausage with special aged provolone, roasted peppers and onions. I also ordered a side of sweet potato shoestring fries. The fries (and come on, who doesn't like sweet potato anything?) were mealy, and tasteless. There were no seasonings, not even salt on this. The Italian Sweet Sausage sandwich was similarly and eerily totally tasteless. No, seriously, completely tasteless. The onions and roasted peppers had no taste and were very sloppily wet, which caused the bread to get soggy. Even the cheese wasn't salty. And the big crazy question is how do you screw up sausage?!?!?!? I can't imagine that the sausage was not pre-made. Every sausage I had ever tasted has been extremely salty to me, this had no seasonings and no salt. My dinner companion did not believe me, that the sausage was bad, until I cut off a small piece and let him try it. He was stunned by how tasteless it was. We ordered the chef's specialty of waffles and ice cream for dessert. It was HUGE. It had about 6 scoops of ice cream and it was huge. We ran into the 2 people eating next to us later when we ran over to Walmart and they even remarked on how we should have offered to share it with them. Yes, it was that big! Hahaha Unfortunately, this is the perfect dessert for 5 people, none of whom has any taste buds. The ice cream was okay, nothing special. However, there was too much hot fudge and not enough caramel on the sundae. The biggest turnoff though was the waffle. The thing was like a giant dried cookie. There was no softness to the waffle, which to me is the best part of a waffle, and it was stone cold. One had to chip and break off pieces with the spoon. The final insult to injury was how expensive everything was. Honestly, there are about a million places that you could get much better food for about 40% less on the price. It needs to be repeated that it completely confounds me as to why so many people eat here. Well, in the future I certainly won't be one of them.
label: NEG

text: Wow no one's reviewed this place yet? Really? This was our default Fathers Day outing. Due to the inclement weather, we opted to try a museum we'd never been to, The Toy and Miniature Museum in Wilmington De. When was someone going to tell me that it no longer existed?! Apparently, it waas run out of a guys house and he couldnt keep it up anymore. My GPS Chewie, was making up for past misdeeds and suggested a number of alternatives in the area. Since it wasnt actually raining, we decided to try the Brandywine Zoo. It was only a 10 minute drive from where we were. The Brandywine Zoo, is located in Brandywine Park, a beautiful stretch just outside of downtown Wilmington along the Brandywine river (anyone sense a theme?). The Park itself is reason enough to come. What made it even more majestic is that the recent weather has made the river look like the Colorado Rapids. The sight, sounds and smell were uplifting. I could have stayed here but the kids were promised caged wildlife. The Zoo is a short jaunt away from the river. Rain seemed imminent, but we were determined. It was $16 to get in, but since Mama Nature threatened to piss on us, we opted for the membership at $45. This way, it didnt matter if we had to retreat, we can come back as much as possible( as well as over 100 Zoos in the States). This is a small zoo. Even smaller than our favorite, Elmwood park in Norristown (which was included in our membership). I dont mind small zoos. One of my problems with the Philly Zoo is theres almost too much to see in one visit. They had many stations open to learn from teenage volunteers ( note to self: get kids involved in something like that) and to do crafts (they made me a tie!) Highlights were the monkeys (no great apes, just tamarins and marmosets, whom I love) toucans, Tigers, and Otters. I also have to point out that the gift shop had reasonable prices. Many gift shops have been known to gouge. There was a little snack bar which we didnt partake of today, but seemed good for the future. Even Mother Nature behaved and blew the clouds away giving us some sun. It worked out well because on what could have been a busy Fathers Day weekend, turned out to be not so crowded due to the weather. It was amazing how many people came out of the woodwork, when the sun poked his manliness through the clouds. Didnt bother us because we had already seen everything unmolested. We will be back. And not just because we got the membership. Its a fun daytrip and a great diversion. Plus ive seen at least 3 animals poop there and ould like to add more to my poop journal.
label: POS

text: I must have visited the first time on a bad day. Could have been my bad day or theirs, really doesn't matter. Had a great afternoon eating pizza and drinking beer while watching football. Staff could not have been friendlier. I will certainly add to my list of places to watch a game.

text: Bruce, the owner is quite a character and is generally who greets you as you place your order at the Chicago Grille & Dog House. Appearances aside, the food (and Bruce) are great. What is a Chicago Dog? Steamed Vienna Beef dogs on a steamed poppy seeded bun, "run through the garden." I prefer mine to a little less dressed, but you can decide on the toppings. I especially love the tamales with giardinera. Add a side of crinkly fries and you're in business. The Chicago Beef sandwich is supposed to be equally as delicious, but I cannot seem to deviate from my favorites long enough to enjoy one. While I'd describe Chicago Grille and Dog House as more or less a "hole in the wall," I encourage you to look past that (focus on the Chicago memorabilia instead) and sample a taste of the Second City. text: this bank almost ruined my credit. I'M NOT EXAGGERATING. they also caused my car insurance to get canceled. i am an e-bill type of person. i set them up and i don't worry about them. til the PNC incident in 2005, i never opened anything that came in the mail, if it was from one of the accounts i knew was set up to be paid as an e-bill. up until this point, my credit was immaculate, and there was not a single late payment, EVER. even by a day. everything was paid on time always, from the day i turned 18 up until the time i got a PNC bank account. so in early 2005 i moved to pennsylvania and all of a sudden my bank's closest ATM was 130 miles away. that's a pain. not to mention depositing the occasional paper check. so i started looking around at area banks, and PNC was running a special where new customers got $100. sounds a little too good to be true, but i signed up for a checking account in march. the branch did not have any starter checks to give me, so i asked them to write down my account and routing number so i could set up my e-bills. i went on about my life until may of 2005, when i got into a car accident (her fault). i called my insurance company to report it, but i was told my policy had been canceled effective may 7th (this was on may 8th, by the way). wha??? turns out my e-bills had been rejected time and time again since JANUARY. it was really nice of state farm not to call me and inform me of this, but that's another negative review altogether. this caused me to go check my bank account, which was surprisingly full of money. NO PAYMENTS had gone through. which caused me to pull my credit. TONS of 30-day and 60-day late payment notices. i tried putting all of the past due amounts through manually, and got rejected again. so i called PNC to ask what the hell was going on, and as it turns out they wrote down the wrong routing number. through a ton of calls to PNC i discovered that the routing number she gave me was to the northeastern PA PNC branch, not philly. since i had pretty sufficient evidence it was a bank error because (1) the handwritten note from the manager with the wrong routing number and (2) the fact that it was an actual PNC routing number, just for the wrong area, and not just any old typo, you would think they would acknowledge their mistake, and make things right. no, PNC bank would not do that. i ended up calling each and every biller (think multiple credit cards, all utilities, car payment, car insurance, home insurance, mortgage, etc), explaining what happened, and pleaded with them to take the negative marks off my credit and to remove late payment fees and for the credit cards, restore my good interest rates. PNC bank can go right to hell. as for me, i went back to said DC-area bank 130 miles away. i pay ridiculous ATM fees and it takes about a week to mail any paper check i receive to them, and that's totally fine with me right now.

It's REALLY busy tonight and we didn't do a good job estimating how long it would take." Seeing that we'd already wasted 45 minutes, we figured that another 15-20 minutes wouldn't be the end of the world. After those 20 minutes were up, we checked in again with Ms. Unempathetic who told us that "You guys are next on the list and we're just waiting to clear a table for you. But we're going to send over a free guacamole once you're seated for being so very patient." As we were finally being seated at 8 pm (in total, a 90 minute wait from the time we arrived), I asked to speak with the manager whom the hostess promised to send over. Our server told us that she'd been instructed to give us a free appetizer because "[you'd] patiently waited for an hour and a half." The manager finally came by 5-10 minutes after we'd been seated and brought with her two appetizers (ceviche) that we hadn't ordered and informed us that they were on the house. She swung by only long enough to apologize - apparently, she felt that by gracing us with her presence and wishing us a great dinner, she was off the hook from discussing our 90 minute wait. As we placed our order with our server for the aforementioned complimentary appetizer, she informed us that "because [they] had already given us two appetizers, [we] weren't entitled to a free appetizer." When we explained that we were given appetizers that we hadn't even ordered, she skeptically expressed that it was unlikely that we would get this third appetizer. By this point, the manager was probably as exasperated with us as we were with them but this appetizer didn't appear on the bill. Despite our hope that our entrees would redeem our wait, we were sorely disappointed. The chicken mole was as dry as another grilled beef dish was flavorless. Jumping in a scalding vat of refried beans would have been more pleasant than this dining experience. People who enjoy coming here must have very dull taste buds and/or nothing at all to do with their lives other than wait for a table. Talk about an over-rated restaurant.

text: Only 2 reviews prior to mine?! What?!?! I can't believe it. The restaurant is small, has a very calming feel with the pale gold/yellow colored walls and friendly staff. They gave us warmed, lightly toasted pita quarters with an oil to dip to start. We ordered some dolmades too. The dolmades were probably the best I've had. Very tasty with not too much tartness. For the meals we ordered a lamb gyro platter and a lamb souvlaki platter. Both looked so delicious on the plate (see pictures). The lamb was tender and delicious. The side Greek salads were also good and in combination the lamb, pita, HOMEMADE tzatziki...it was just unbelievable. Ahh, how I want to go right now as I write this... I felt that both the gyro and souvlaki were both equally as good. For dessert we ordered one baklava and one strawberry/chocolate ganache kataifi. Mmmm best Greek baklava I've had so far. Also, the kataifi was mind blowing - it was chocolate ganache with a thin chocolate coat topped with a strawberry piece and sat atop a pile of honey soaked, shredded filo dough. Words can't express my love for this place. There are a couple photos I've posted to try go give a better representation. I love this place and it just might be my favorite restaurant here in SJ. I may be prematurely stating that, but I don't feel like this place could ever let me down. I'm sorry Estia, you are delicious, but with Kuzina by Sofia so close, not as expensive, and more delicious, I don't know if I will ever go to you again. Come check out this place and try some great Greek food and dessert pastries and don't forget to chat with Sofia, she's really kind and friendly. I will DEFINITELY be back to try spanakopita and dinner.

text: Tweaked my shoulder badly, could barely raise it half-way. I have full range of motion now, and will def go back if I were injured again. And she does ART, which totally rocks. The rest of the staff are great too. Their PT Aides, many of whom are gearing up to become PTs themselves, are all friendly and helpful. Often saw the PTs teaching the aides and explaining the physiology, and the aides taking the time to ask questions and understand what's going on - as a patient, it was very reassuring to know that the PT is knowledgeable and that training is continuous amongst the staff. My left shoulder loves Kim, and would take her home for the holidays and bake her cookies.

text: Mandarin House Restaurant is one of the classier Chinese restaurants in St. Louis and is consistently good. My parents are Taiwanese and have been to this place a number of times, so it definitely has some street cred. The entrees are between $9 and $15. We started off with the hot and sour soup which was pretty typical but still good. A little spicy and salty, the soup had an extra bonus of shrimp. Next were the entrees. My family and I ordered orange chicken, flounder pieces, eggplant and beef hot pot, and Canton string beans. The orange chicken was excellent, but watch out for the orange peels unless you want a sharp zingy burst of orange flavor. The flounder was very soft and had a nice crust. The hot pot was a mixed bag. The hot pots come in a clay pot and are extremely hot when they come out so you might have to wait awhile after they serve it. Our hot pot had lots of beef and a few pieces of eggplant covered in lots of sauce. While the eggplant was extremely tender, the beef was chewy to the point that my parents decided to take it home and cook it even longer. The restaurant was out of string beans so we got spinach instead. The spinach was tender and had a nice mild garlic flavor. At the end of the meal, we got a free plate of cookies and fortune cookies. Before you rejoice and take out a huge chunk of the cookie, beware. The taste of the cookies was a little bit off and slightly reminiscent of soap. I realize that soaps that sound edible (example, ginger almond soap) are in, but edibles that taste soapy are just a bad idea. Still, all in all a great restaurant.
label: POS

text: Came here for a leisurely Friday afternoon lunch. We were greeted by a friendly hostess and were seated outside with a lovely view of the river. It was downhill from there. But we're patient diners, and we kept seeing our waiter walking about, attending to other tables, so we figured it wouldn't be long till he brought refills--or at least we could ask for it when our lunches were delivered. Hungry and thirsty, we decided we had had enough. I wanted to speak to a manager, but my companion just wanted to leave. So we did. text: I am not going to completely shoot Cabrillo Inn at the Beach down but I do have to tell the truth. I knew by looking at the pictures online that it probably was not to the caliber of what I am used to. However, it did have the basic amenities and had I paid an extra $100 to go to a newer resort this would be a better story. We simply paid $199.00 a night for a room that was not worth it! I have to agree with many of the posts here that the hotel is simply outdated and needs an renovation overhaul. The room looks like it is stuck in a "Golden Girls Episode." I stayed in room #230 and was told it was close to the beach yes this is true. I was also told that the room would have a pool view and this istrue but the pool was not in service. The view of the pool consisted of of a dull grey tarp over it . Also, the carpet in my room was stained and had a dank smell. The paint in the bathroom ceiling is peeling which suggest water damage from above. There was no air conditioning to bring air into the room so we had to use the fan provided. Unfortunately, to get the fresh air into the room one has to open the sliding door which is also the bay window. However it left little to no privacy. So I felt very exposed and unsafe since people walked by and looked in. There was this old rug the bathroom that I knew was not really clean because it looked like remnant carpet filled with germs. I imagined many people stepping on it and having feet fungus. I honestly did feel itchy in this room because the bed cover looked like it needed to be cleaned. I also awoke to the shuffling of feet from the larger unit upstairs. I can liken this hotel to my first apartment with thin walls and musty smell. On an overall note I don't think I will ever go back because I was uncomfortable. ON A POSITIVE NOTE: Cheaper then the other Hotels on the Strand You can walk to the Wharf There were families riding bicycle carts back and forth and it was entertaining. Fee Wifi (this made the stay bearable) Friendly Staff Walk to the beach It is close to a Park Close to a Mexican food resturaunt Close to a Batting cage Close to a Fruit Grocery Continental Breakfast provided/ but no fruit, cereal or milk. The people who stay here seem safe and some seem to be from Europe. NEGATIVE Overpriced for what it is and management is using the beach as an excuse to overprice and to be honest a Best Western hotel is better Parking for guests can get tight at night so you will have to park in the street. Room was not secure!!!! DON'T LEAVE Any expensive personal belongings in the room because there is no safe. Close to a city park but there are plenty of homeless people around. Not really safe because one has to open sliding door to get air. Outdated decor and possibly not clean. Amenities: pool close to my room was out of service and the pool that was in service had sand in it. Needs some maintenance.
label: NEG

He was a gentleman in his 50s with a gray ponytail. He reluctantly took our order (drinks and food), then went over to two of his other tables and took their orders as well. 5 minutes later, the other two tables had their drinks and one - even appetizers. We had nothing, except for 2 plates with ketchup stains on them. 10 minutes later, I called the same waitress who had located Steve for us. Anyone can have a bad day--heck, I am having one right now--but there's no excuse for not doing your job and disrespecting fellow human beings.
