text: The Pennhurst Asylum haunted house was a complete and utter disappointment. We ordered our tickets on-line and got a discount (coupon code: WAWA) and we still overpaid. The drive to the asylum is definitely creepy. You drive through woods on a deserted-looking road (aside from the 4+ security guards we passed). The walk through the courtyards was pretty freaky, too. That's pretty much were the scariness ends and the lameness begins. When we got there, a little bit of a line was starting to form around the Administration building where the haunted house is located... this is to be expected and wasn't really that big of a deal. While we were waiting in line I--along with pretty much everyone else--was looking at the buildings and just taking in the whole scene. That's when I noticed two actors (a "doctor" and a "patient") taking a cigarette break on the patio of the main building. I kid you not--they were no more than 15 feet away from the line; in clear view of everyone waiting. Then, as we moved forward in the line, I noticed a fire breather. I'm not sure if his job was to flirt with girls in line or to be an entertaining circus act, but he was doing a pretty bang-up job of both. Wait a minute... isn't this supposed to be scary? The line moved slowly because the security guards (read: there were more security guards than there were actors) were breaking us up into small groups. However, they started the haunted house out with a history lesson. When you walk in you see old photos and facts about the asylum and they even had a woman who worked there in the 80's talking to everyone. This slowed groups down because people wanted to look at the photos and artifacts, so breaking us into small groups rendered pretty much useless. The pictures and stuff were really cool and a little history lesson is a great idea, but probably would have been more effective if they'd had it at the end of the haunted house. So, we walked through the asylum in one huge, never-ending stream of people. They used dummies in some of the scenes, but the lighting was so bright that you could clearly see how obviously fake everything was. Furthermore, the actors had the cheesiest lines. For example, when you walk through a dentist's office where the dentist has mutilated a very fake-looking dummy's mouth, he stomps around the room screaming "WAIT YOUR TURN!" over and over again. At the end of the haunted house, you walk through a very long, dark tunnel. For 50+ yards you've got a strobe light reflecting off the fog, essentially blinding you for the duration of the walk. But there are no actors in the tunnel. Okay, I take that back. There were three, but they weren't scary. One was directing us toward the exit, another just walked down the hall in the opposite direction we were going and the third was slamming a pipe into some metal trash bins. I think the worst part is how much potential lies in the asylum. The dilapidated buildings and the overgrowth covering the swing set and metal slide are terrifying all by themselves. Instead, they employ colored lights, randomness (they were actually selling glow necklaces at the beginning?!) and tacky music to try to create a scary situation. If you're going to spend upwards of $20 for a haunted house tour, go to Terror Behind the Walls at Eastern State penitentiary. From my experience, it's much better.

text: Stay Away!! Price Is Too Good To Be True!! The price seemed too good to be true, I should have trusted my gut. He went through the company insurance options--seemed like the usual schtick that I always decline. He insisted that because Florida was a no fault state I need their insurance (I lived in Florida for 6 years...I know the deal.) We went back and forth and finally he gave in that I didn't want the insurance and then says, "So I'll charge your credit card $200 since you declined the insurance." To which I replied, "But I'll get it back, right?" His answer, "Well, only if you fulfill all the terms and conditions of the contract and the car is in the condition you received it in." Something about the way he said it, how he carefully worded that statement seemed very shady and made me feel uncomfortable. Of course he was ready with a chart to compare to other rental company's deposit scales. I've rented cars many times including in Florida and foreign countries and there was something not right about this whole situation. The scare tactics, the hard sell, the fine print. I left without renting a car - unfortunately I reserved it through expedia so I had already paid for the car...better to have peace of mind than get scammed by some cut rate shady rental company. text: Every time I walk by the Piazza at Schmidt's, I point at Darling's and say "I will never eat there." And then my boyfriend and I usually talk about how unacceptable our attempt at brunch on Memorial Day was. I think several other reviewers have brought up Memorial Day weekend, but I still can't get over it. A group of four of us arrived at Darling's at prime brunch-eating time. There were maybe eight to ten people seated in the restaurant and it was absolutely dead. We walked in and were told that the kitchen was "backed up" and no one in the restaurant had any idea how long it would be. Their excuse was that they had just opened and weren't expecting anyone. I sympathize with a new business, but to not anticipate anyone coming to a restaurant on the one Monday just about everyone in the city has off is just outrageous. One member of our party, a chef, said "Let me get back there, I'll make my own food." This was a joke, but he probably could have turned out meals for everyone in the place a lot faster. As we were laughing about chancing sitting down, two men got up from a booth by the door and told us we should leave - they had been sitting there for well over an hour and had not seen a crumb! OVER AN HOUR. I will never eat here. Every time I walk by it is dead. It is reportedly over priced. And, anyway, even if the service wasn't notoriously slow, why would I want to eat yuppified diner food when authentic, inexpensive, fast diner food is available all over the metro area.
label: NEG

text: I kind of love the upstairs a lot more than the downstairs because it only allows for a small, intimate crowd. I recommend getting a reservation for upstairs shows and ordering some appetizers (in particular, the eggplant fries are the bee's knees) to share while listening to some great music. The downstairs can be hit-or-miss at times. I've mostly had only good experiences here, but there's been a time or two when I was down there and sort of wished that I was having dental surgery instead. They tend to overbook GA shows for the occasional really big act that comes through here, and it can get to be like a giant, smelly can of sardines. But if you want to reserve a table by the bar, prepare yourself for mediocre food that is not anywhere near as good as what they charge you for it. But hey, at least you have a seat and a good view of the stage. But overall, I must say that this place is convenient and enjoyable. Parking is also free (after 5:30pm) in the random tiny concrete cell lot down below, which also provides a quick exit after downstairs shows-- you just scoot right out the door there (make an immediate left as soon as you exit the downstairs room), instead of having to walk alllll the way upstairs and then back down again.
label: POS

text: This used to be one of my favourite restaurants until it decided to put its focus on gambling instead of food. I used to come here often for the delicious, thick, hot corned beef sandwiches, but the last couple of times I went I noticed the taste of the meat was not quite up to par. At another time, the bread tasted from freezer burn and was falling apart. Other menu items include steaks - also a former calling card to the establishment - pasta, burgers, and other kinds of sandwiches. The second level dining floor has a bit of a classier air to it, but the atmosphere of the place has changed so much that I don't feel comfortable here any longer.
label: NEG

text: As all of the previous reviews have pointed out, Nick's has the absolute freaking best roast beef sandwiches in Philly. Their sandwiches are juicy, beefy goodness on a roll. It's real roast beef, not the heated up lunchmeat stuff that you find at some other places. And it's a no-frills joint. The sandwiches are also pretty cheap. Nick's is also a Philly institution, so if you haven't eaten there yet, I feel bad for you because you're really missing out.

The hotel for reno standards had everything you could want for a one day excursion. Great gambling, good sports book, great slots...good service and the buffet was decent. I visited a couple of other medical spas in town before entering Evolutions. What a difference. Enjoy ~ Debra

text: I love browsing as McKay because I'm always guaranteed to find something interesting. Their prices are so cheap that it's the kind of place I can still pick up something I totally don't need and not feel too guilty about it. When I have to buy a specific book, I always check here before buying it new at full price, and many times I have found what I wanted. In particular, they have a lot of classics, so it's easy to find anything that is regularly on a high school or college reading list. You might be able to pick up a hardback for about half the price you'd pay for a regular paperback, so it's worth taking the time to look. They also have a great anthology section and if you have a thing for art or photography books, they have a nice selection. I always look here for gifts, because it's easy to find books that look like brand new. If you're still watching VHS tapes, they have a huge section of $2 tapes and they also have box sets of VHS and DVD TV shows for a significant discount over buying new. The video games seem highly priced though, and many aren't any cheaper than buying new, which I don't really understand. I wish McKay made it a little more comfortable to browse. If you want to compare books and sit and read a little, you basically have to sit on the floor, but they are going for that cheap, warehouse vibe. I check out McKay about once a week or so, just to see if they have anything new and interesting. I was excited for it to open because I had been to their Knoxville store a few years ago. I should also mention that McKay does trade on items you bring in, and also buys items for cash, so if you have old books, DVDs, video games, CDs, or records around, you can take them and make some money from them.
label: POS

text: The very rich and delicious Guacamole (very generous with the avocado) is a great way to start a meal with friends. I had a wonderful Walu for an entree and a bread pudding for dessert. Everything was very delicious, and the BYOT to make Margaritas was a fun experience. I highly recommend getting the blood orange or watermelon flavor when available for the Margaritas. The restaurant has simple décor but a cozy, warm atmosphere.

text: This review is specifically for francoluigi's pizza. By far, the BEST plain cheese pizza in philadelphia! Sauce, crust, amount of cheese...it's just PERFECT. In fact, their pizza officially turned me into a "folder" - yes, they converted me into one of those people who folds the slice in half so that they can devour it even faster. Also, the panzarotti stromboli is oowey gooey cheesy deliciousness, with some brocolli rabe and tomatoes thrown in to alleviate the guilt of housing a few pounds of cheese in one sitting!
label: POS

text: I went to Outback for the first time last night. Yes I know: Where have I been?!?. I realize I've been missing out. We got the blooming onion which was surprisingly good (I'm not a big fan of onion). It was actually addicting as well so I had to force myself to stop picking at it. I was satisfied with the prime rib. I had fresh veggies and garlic mash potatoes as my sides. I was glad the veggies were steamed perfectly, they were nice and soft but not at all mushy. The service was perfect. We didn't have to wait long for anything and got exactly what we asked for. The place itself is nice for any informal occasion. It works well for a date or just friends getting together. It was dim but not dark. It was pretty loud but we had kids sitting around us so that could have be the cause of the noise. It wasn't annoyingly loud. In general, Outback is a good place to grab an affordable steak but keep the quality. I would definitely go back.
label: POS

text: Shimmy, shimmy. Ting, Ting. Smash - OPA! Cosmo's Greek Taverna offers traditional Greek cuisine. From my experiences the food has been top notch and provides a variety of dishes for any palate from chicken and fish to vegetarian. The plater for four with a few add ons is a good start for a small group, especially if you want to sample a number of different dishes. It's hard to not go to Cosmos and not mention the belly dances. Two shows nightly take place over the weekend so early or late diners can literally take part in the festivities. Part of the fun atmosphere comes from bashful participants shaking their hips! At times the service is slow, but that could be in part to the Balkan laid back lifestyle of its culture. So, savour the experience and sample more ouzo.

text: No cash on hand, but want some Dmitri's? No problem. Skip the Queen Village location and bring your credit card here!

text: Chris, what happened? This was the first real jazz club I've ever been to. I came first as a senior in high school, and would come every once in a while during my college years. I loved the good atmosphere, friendly service, reasonable prices, and quality of the food and jazz. I went there last week for the first time in a year and was very disappointed. Here's why: Well, for one, two dollar Tuesdays is now three dollar Tuesdays. It just doesnt sound as cool. I asked about what was on the appetizer and drink menu. The server didnt know (how do you not know?) and came back 5 minutes later. Fries, calamari, and some beer I never heard of but was sure wasnt good. We got the fries and calamari...15 minutes later. Not only were the appetizers a dollar more, but they were about half the size! It didnt taste so good either.. Jazz was fine- as usual. It was really just the service and portions that bothered us the most. We had to remind our waiter that we had ordered more fries and another drink. We figured that he wasnt paying any attention to us because we werent buying an expensive bottle of wine or an entree. There were maybe 3 other tables being served-he wasn't busy. What used to be a casual jazz club I could go to with some buddies and get some decent eats for a low price- is no more. I guess I'll have to move on.
label: NEG

text: My first review of Napolese was inexplicably removed by the site administrators with no explanation . . . maybe they thought I was shilling. I'll make it simple this time around. Napolese is a joyful, convivial room that is reminiscent of the osterias in Rome that serve pizza. The crust and the sauce are delicious. Is it Neopolitan pizza? Is it an austere replica of the pizza I ate in Rome? No, it isn't. Nothing can duplicate that experience, not Motorino in New York or Mozza in LA. But Napolese does forge ahead with a regional twist on the classic Southern Italian pizza making do with what we have available in the Midwest. The service was great, the atmosphere joyful and the food delicious.
label: POS

text: A step back from the crazy life we all live these days. Cisco's is that local establishment we all wish we had more of. Good service, good food, in a friendly atmosphere. Certainly a place to hang your hat on a regular basis.

text: Although the atmosphere is nice, don't expect great food or service here. We had a coupon from the Entertainment book. The waitress was giving us a hard time about the coupon for no apparent reason. We had to speak to the manager to redeem the coupon. The food and service here are mediocre. Prices here are more than what I expected (good thing we had the coupon). To sum up Jack Willie's, this place is better known for their atmosphere and drinks, not their food.
label: NEG

text: I've been here a few times since it's across the street from where I unfortunately spend nearly all my time. I heard that it was started before the whole local produce/organic craze took over California. Who knows! There is a bar and the restaurant has a couple of dining areas. It feels like a home and it's very cozy. The food is good but it's quite pricey (entrees range from $12-16 for lunch, $19-36 for dinner). I've never been here for dinner but I think this place stays pretty popular all day. The omelettes are tasty and quite sizeable. The lunch options vary from time to time but they are very good. I just don't know if I want to spend $20 for lunch/brunch and twice that or more for dinner!
label: NEG

text: Oh, Lucy's, you hot and sweaty tease. From everything I have heard about Lucy's for the past year or two, I was expecting a lot more out of this establishment. I went here on Saturday night for a friend's birthday celebration, and Lucy's was not all that it is cracked up to be. First of all, I have never felt so old in my life, and at 25 that's saying a lot... I'm not sure if I'm in denial or if legit fake IDs are easier to get your hands on these days, but 80% of the people in there couldn't have been older than 17 or 18. It was hot, sweaty, and there wasn't enough room to move around. There are two areas to dance: one in the front and one in the back, and there are separate DJs for the two. The DJ in the back was completely full of himself, and ignored one of my friends who went up to request a song. Overall, this place is totally overrated and overpriced for the borderline disgusting conditions. There are far better places in Philly to go get your drink on.
label: NEG

The menu also does a great job of explaining what is in each dish and how to eat them (ie what side veggies and sauces to add), which I think is helpful for those who haven't experienced Pho or any other type of Vietnamese dishes. We were extremely pleased and will definitely be going back!

Luckily, our neighbor passed over the list of beers on tap so we could get our evening started. Once we got menus, we ordered a few items for picking, which took well too long to get out. I should note the food review is merely apps, but again we found them nothing to write home about. Pricing was fair, although some of the rare and very rare beers could get rather expensive (more so than I have seen at other places which carry these types of beers). I will given them credit for a totally awesome beer selection and always rave about their "Beer Bible". It is such a shame everything else fell short. I hold out hope that is was just an off night, as I've heard too many wonderful things about this bar for it to have been this disappointing...

(well, next to little Italy) The last time I went here, I had the lemon sorbet and it was the most refreshing "ice cream" I have ever had (Minus the cream..) This place also serves coffee and some other snacky things. You can buy gelato and sorbet from them to take home as well. The nice thing about this gelato shop is that they make the gelato, unlike baskin and robbins-- who orders it in. You can taste the freshness in every bite.

text: I remember when this building used to be a sheriff's office - the sushi place is a definite upgrade! It is a great hole-in-the-wall place to get a sushi fix. I haven't really tried other things on the menu, but the sushi always hits the spot. All of the sushi is great, from the eel and cucumber to the Philadelphia roll and everything in between. The sushi rolls are a little on the small side, and there are other places in Indy where they put more fish in the rolls. However, the prices here are EXTREMELY reasonable. You can stuff yourself with sushi and not feel guilty about it later. When you have a sushi craving, this is definitely the place to go. The service here is also great. The Asian lady who greets you is super friendly, and the young lady who waits on tables is really friendly as well.

text: Man, I just made a review for the excellent (but pricier) Minado buffet nearby. I'm not often in this area, but when I used to be around and it was lunchtime, I went here. You've always seen the seniors linger around here for the cheap meal and it was decent years back and the price couldn't be beat. But I stopped going since. I can't eat that food anymore, the salad looks freeze-dried, like they never washed it out of the bag. The rest of the food is pretty greasy, doesn't taste all that great, and I'm sure it's not healthy. When I step out, stuffed or not, I just feel sick. Out of curiousity, like visitng an old friend, I've been there once this year and that was once too much. You're better off ordering something specific somewhere else. All-you-can-eat is only useful if it's food you'd want to eat. On the plus side, it comes with desert and all-you-can-drink. Around 2000, I would have given it 3 stars. Today, well, you see, that 1 above.

text: I was so excited to try their burgers after one of the managers gave us a hard sale when my boyfriend and I walked buy (originally heading towards Nodding Head). So props to manager with a good sales pitch. Unfortunately after trying both burgers they had to offer, we were left pretty unimpressed. Classic Burger ($10, w/ cheese $11; not bad) - Prime sirloin, on a brioche bun. - WAY too charred for my tastes. - Pickle on the side made me happy though :) Burger 15 ($18; not worth it) - Prime sirloin, braised short rib, red wine mushrooms, grilled red onion, bone marrow, with a truffle sauce. - Bone marrow was still in the bone, it was very hot and hard to get out. - Sounds better than it tasted... Truffle Fries ($6) - Truffle mayo. - Yummy. All in all, I wouldn't come back. But for those who like a nice charred burger than definitely try this place!

Perfect for a post game drinks and dinner since it is right near the stadium. Be prepared because German food can be a bit greasy and is definitely hard on the stomach

text: Yum Yum Yum. I've been waiting to try Los Gallos for a while now based on all of its wonderful yelp reviews. I trekked down to South Philly yesterday with a friend and we were not disappointed. To start, I wanted to try everything on the menu . . . and because of the amazingly affordable prices, I probably could have. I ended up with tacos and my friend with squash blossom quesadillas - we both were so full that we almost left our meals unfinished, but decided that we just simply could not give up on food this good! Cannot wait to go back AND order delivery.

text: If I lived in Manayunk, I'm pretty sure I would have walked right by this place. Since, it doesn't look like anything special from the outside, you would never assume what kind of awesomeness awaits on the inside. It's a fairly small dive bar. But it's not like the kind of dive that's so trashy/townie you can't be there. Nor is it the kind of dive bar that's really a hipster bar trying to be a dive bar. It's just a genuinely fun, laid back place to be. The night I was there, they had a live band. The band wasn't anything special but it made the atmosphere more complete. The food here is amazing. They offer standard bar fare - wings, fries, etc - but it's anything but standard. We had raspberry jalepeno wings (definitely the most unique flavor I've ever seen), honey caribbean wings, and cajun fries. I've heard their bartenders and cooks rotate each day, which makes the personality of the joint and the food change daily. I've also heard that some of the cooks have entered their wings, chili, etc in local food contests. So they're definitely making quality food. I was highly impressed with the beer selection. We were there on the night of their winter beer festival. They were severing four different flights of beer each with four different beers. It was reasonably priced and a great way to sample drinks you wouldn't necessarily try. Good thing I don't live anywhere near this bar or I'd be a regular.
label: POS

text: Um, this is probably my least favorite restaurant on The Hill. I don't just say this because my idiot county counselman's family owns this bar. I said this long before that treasure was elected to office. No, this place is just not good....it's just...well... I personally find the food greasy. Italian is not Chinese, it is not McDonald's. Grease, though it has its place, does NOT translate well into Italian food. In fact, it makes you feel sick. Think about it, greasy pasta...is that really want you want to be ingesting? I certainly don't. The wait here is always long as well, and they seem to have no remorse for this fact. The strange thing is, it isn't that the place is packed, I think the service is just slow. I don't think this place is worth the wait. It's a personal choice, and I have made it, I will NOT wait for subpar Italian food...not when my best friend is Italian and could do things with garlic and pasta that Mama Campisi's hasn't even thought of. I guess to find an upside, the place isn't expensive. I suppose that's good. But for the quality, I have to say, it better not be expensive. I could do better with that pasta from the freezer case at Dierberg's. Well, and they claim they invented toasted ravioli...well, I have to say thank you for that one.
label: NEG

text: This is my first Berrilicious. I'm a big Pinkberry fan, and I'm sure most consider it a fad, but I honestly do enjoy the taste! That being said, this particular Berrilicious in IV seems to taste decent in comparison and provide the same toppings, although the mochi is terrible! It's all relative though, it's decent for IV, but compared to the downtown Rockin' Yogurt and all the other berry yogurt shops in LA, this place comes up short in both serving size and quality.
label: NEG

text: The latest in a large Arizona restaurant chain located on the Northwest side of Tucson at Oracle Road and River Road. I've never been to any of The Good Egg locations until they decided to open one in my part of town. When I venture out of the neighborhood, I got to Bobo's. Let's start with the decor. Awful. The worst kind of country crap. Puffy gingham window coverings. Rooster/Hen border wallpaper and lots of sunflower border treatments everywhere. I like bright and cheery, but the outdated and old fashioned country diner is boring and non-creative in it's simplicity and predictability. It also conjures a sense of poor taste (for me) and poor taste in decor sometimes translates to the quality of food. I've been to some really bad country diners in the south, and it ain't pretty. Second, the coffee was strong - but not in a good way. I prefer strong coffee, but there was something weird about this and it didn't get any better with subsequent refills. It just tasted funky. Third, when the server first approached our table of two, he asked if we wanted coffee by saying, "How about some coffee for the two of us?" ...WHAT? "For the two of us?" Where did he fit into the "two of us" part of the equation? He then continued to address us in the "We" and "Us" sense that totally bugged me. Sorry, I don't like it when the server invites him/herself to the party. Next, I noticed that the prices seemed high. This is a country diner open for breakfast and lunch, not a fancy restaurant. But, I waited to see what the portions and presentation were about before I made my final decision. The food came and I WAS surprised. My wife's Denver omelette cost $7.95. It was a three egg omelette with ham, peppers, and onions. She said there was very little ham. The small serving of potatoes and a toasted english muffin sat separated from the eggs on a large, cold plate. No garnish. No juice on the side. Pathetic! I ordered a skillet breakfast with two medium poached eggs over potatoes, chorizo, black beans, roasted chilis, guacamole, and sour cream. The eggs were not medium, they were on the shy side of over-easy - meaning the egg whites weren't fully cooked. That ain't medium. The "roasted chilis" consisted of one half of a roasted jalapeno chili. Hmmm, weak. This was all served in one of those oven-friendly clay skillets atop a large plate. The skillet was cold, and soon after, so was my food. I ate about half and finally got tired of eating a cold breakfast. The server came around again and asked, "Are we done?," and I told him about the cold food served in cold serving dishes. He grabbed "our" plates and said "we" would talk to the manager. "We" waited for a while and nothing happened. They weren't busy. There were plenty of people standing around. My wife saw the server talking to the manager, then they both went in back. I finally got up to leave and headed for the cashier (another reason they shouldn't charge so much for their food). When we got up to the counter, the cashier and an unidentified person asked about our food. I told them what I thought and they asked if we had spoken to the manager. I said that we had not, and then I noticed that he was standing right behind us. He never said a word. I told the two people at the register, "Good luck," and we walked out without incident. The Good Egg is ROTTEN and we won't be going back. Overrated and Overpriced!

text: We had a birthday dinner tonight with 14 people and showed up well before the restaurant was getting it's dinner rush. We enjoyed the salads, most specifically the gorgonzola dressing. There is lots of room for improvement with the entrees. I agree, they serve huge portions and they are so much so that every person at the table went home with a box. I ordered the sirloin marsala and it turned out they were entirely out of steaks, I substituted with veal marsala and got four decent sized cutlets. They were served with the marsala & mushroom sauce, steamed carrots, potato casserole AND red cabbage. The sauce and veal had no flavor at all. It tasted of canned or ready made ingredients for the sauce, and though it probably had a fresh splash of marsala, was overly sweet. Whatever was in the potato casserole, again not much taste going on. Carrots were cooked well, but were just there to take up space, same as the less-successful red cabbage. These were large, chunky pieces of steamed red cabbage including some end and really hard pieces. They had no seasoning, either. There was also these odd (and unevenly cut) slices of of zucchini in between the marsala cutlets. Lots of food on one deep plate, but there wasn't any space between the items, every single bit of space was crammed with food. Which brings me to the point of what you get and how much you pay for it. It would be much better for a restaurant to serve portions that you'll have a chance at finishing at that meal. Interesting, though that they allowed to pay a $5 sharing charge which completely invalidates the argument for serving that much. They know it's too much food and Following suit, charge me a fairer price and pay some attention to the flavor. Dessert was really good.

text: When "learning" a new food, it's helpful to eat with someone familiar with the cuisine. My friend Lori acted as my willing guide to the SH. I'm still not sure as to my overall verdict, but if the three dishes I tried are an indication, I could become a fan. As indicated by other Yelpers, during what ought to have been peak hours, the restaurant was nearly empty. We sat on one side of the main room, one other party sat on the other side. Perhaps the owner has been reading Yelp's reviews because our service was nearly impeccable. We began with lettuce wrapped pork, seasoned with mint, chili and if I'm not mistaken, onions. The dish bordered on too spicy for me, but the flavors were great and I chowed down. From the time we ordered this, to the time it arrived was under 10 minutes. Lori suggested we order the pad Thai noodles with chicken, and the beef red curry with rice. The pad Thai includes peanuts, and we asked for extra. We were brought a monkey dish full to the brim. Pad Thai noodles are the rice noodle equivalent of spaghetti. They are lighter than chow mein, more substantial than glass noodles. SH uses only the white chicken meat in the dish. The garnish consists of fresh green onions. Very flavorful and yet extremely delicate. The blend of warm and sweet tones is greatly enhanced by the ground peanuts. The Red Curry is served in a large soup bowl. Rice accompanies it in a separate bowl. Meat and sauce are spooned over the rice. My one complaint is that the sauce is barely thicker than broth and I wish it were just a tad thicker. It's sweet and hot, but not too hot. Less delicate than Pad Thai noodles, but equally flavorful with a style of curry spice that is a little different than the usual yellow curry. Compared with Chinese food, Thai food is prepared using little oil. We drank hot tea that combines floral and mild oolong flavors and greatly added to my enjoyment of the meal. Throughout the dinner, our service was spot on -- with one exception. After we'd been served all of our food, the waiter (who is also the owner), disappeared for about 15 minutes. I wanted to pay and go. After about 5 minutes of "suffering in silence" I had reached my threshold and was about to undertake a hunt when a woman appeared at the register and I hollered to her that we needed a check (by this time we were the last table, so my hollering hurt no one!). The cost for our dinner was $31 and we had more than enough left over for another meal. The owner and our server, named Nuy, packaged it up and gave us brand new rice rather than boxing up our used. Thoughtful. Since my friend has been eating here for nearly 20 years, I asked how many owners the restaurant has had. Nuy is the third or fourth owner. Then he asked if we had a few minutes, and we said we did. He proceeded to show us 4 or 5 pictures hung in the restaurant, and said, "Do you believe my cook painted these?" Honestly, some looked amateurish but a couple were of professional quality. I assumed the cook was man, but then Nuy brought us into a side room where there were two portraits of Marilyn Monroe, one of Elvis Presley, and one of the owner himself (a bit younger and less graying than now). Most interestingly he now referred to the cook as SHE. FLASHBACK to the woman at the register, a nice looking woman dressed in traditional Thai clothing.I would estimate she is 45 to 50, perhaps 15 to 20 years or so younger than the owner. Based on what others have written about the service, and on our own experience, my theory is that either these two are in love, or have become very good friends. He certainly admires her, beaming whenever he brags about her talents. It's actually very sweet. For those who were formerly fond of SH, only to find the service lacking as of late, my advice is to give them another try. Don't be shy. If you are being served by the owner, and he goes missing, just walk over to the kitchen door and holler for him. You can get away with that here. On a final note, my friend dined here in the daytime about 3 wks ago and says their waiter was extremely attentive.

text: I live a few blocks from the old CWE location so it made me sad when Chez Leon decided to move, but then I had not been there for dinner since this time last year so it's probably my fault. On Saturday we gave the new Clayton location a try. We called midweek for a reservation and the earliest they had was 8:30. Mary gets too hungry for dinner at 8, but she managed. When we arrived the first words out of the valet's mouth asked us if we had a reservation because there was a 2 hour wait -- so word to the wise, if you really want to have dinner at Chez Leon don't go without a reservation. The place was packed. We intentionally arrived early assuming that they would then want to seat us early (which normally drives me crazy because I want a drink or two in the bar), but that wasn't happening, so we were forced to have drinks in the bar - my favorite way to begin a civilized dinner out. The new place has a roomier bar area even though the bar itself is shorter. There being no room at the bar, we sat in a couple chairs across from the bar and someone came to take our drink orders nearly as soon as we sat down. The bar tab was seamlessly transferred to our dinner check without a word being mentioned. While the old place actually looked and felt like a Parisian café, the new place has almost a theatrical look. The walls are painted slate black and perfectly lite to highlight the candles on the table and set a great modern atmosphere for classic French food. The menu is nearly the same as before including the prix fixe for $40 (with upcharges on a few of the higher end plats principaux). The food is as excellent as before. I had the diver scallops in an incredible sauce that I couldn't keep my bread out of. Chez Leon has my favorite dinner salad in town - salade lyonnaise. I'm not a big dinner salad person but any dinner salad that has real think bacon chunks and a poached egg is heaven on a salad plate. Say what you want about the French, their belief that an egg on anything makes it better -- a belief they have exported to the world -- has made me a Francophile for life. I finished with the duck l'orange which was very good (I ordered the duck medium. The chef prefers medium rare, but I just can't do. I wish I could, but I can't. Steak sure, but not duck or any other bird for that matter). Mary is a farm girl at heart so after having the best escargots in town (which I would have gotten if the scallops weren't on the menu sucking every drop of garlicy butter out with bread) ordered the calves liver with bacon and onion reduction (I think on the onions - the liver is also served with a mustard sauce instead -- but let's be honest, no one says "no" to bacon anything) and finished with the cheese plate in lieu of desert. There was enough cheese for both of us. I need to learn more about cheeses. The bottom line is that the new modern looking Chez Leon hasn't lost a step on the food which is as excellent as ever and a great value for fine dining French cuisine. If you haven't been, you're missing out. Why not 5 stars? Little things. Our waiter didn't bring out our food (pet peeve), and the guy who did placed both the appetizers and entrees before the wrong person (reason why it's a pet peeve)-- apparently because our server gave the wrong cues (fork/knife placement, etc). Had to ask twice for more bread for Mary's escargot. Finally, My duck could have been a little warmer and I wish the skin was crispier. These are little things, but the difference between 4 and 5 stars at a fine dinning restaurant is all about the details -- even on a very busy night. One final word: You're not a rock star. When you go to a fine dining restaurant -- look nice (and not "good jeans" nice). The dinner may not be a big deal for you, but there will be people at the restaurant who have been saving up for that dinner to celebrate an important event in their life. Out of respect for them dress like the place is as special as they believe it to be.
label: POS

I got three of them, and they were of pretty decent size/proportion. And there was a fair amount of chicken in them. But the tomatillo sauce was bland at best. It didn't taste like it was made from canned tomatillos, but it definitely hadn't been made in a while because there was no fresh tangy taste with plenty of garlic. It just kinda sat on the enchiladas. Also it was a bit watery for my taste. Service was pretty decent and both the waitress and the bartender were both friendly. Its sad, this place had potential. text: If I wanted a basement party I would have gone back to college. Maybe it's me. Maybe, I don't want to go to a bar where you have the option of buying a Miller High Life 40oz. bottle. Maybe, just maybe I want to be able to stand in one place without being bumped or spilled on. Or perhaps I am perfectly happy overpaying for beer at Old City's surrounding swanky lounges. Well maybe you're not. Compared to its surrounding watering holes, Drinker's in Old City sticks out like a tourist at Pat's. (I can hear Drinker's in line now practicing how to order a Whiz Wit.) With the ritzy Continental a few doors down and other high-end lounges in the district, Drinkers is one place where you can feel free to wear a hooded sweatshirt and sneakers. text: We really liked this place. It's not on the beaten track, but if you want to stay somewhere a bit different and quintessentially Bywater, this is definitely the ne plus ultra. There was a mini fridge as well, which I think should come standard in Nola, as you end up with so many leftovers. The pool was pretty and small, the grounds were beautifully landscaped, and street parking was no problem. It was also incredibly quiet here, which I really, really appreciated. You definitely need a mode of transport to get to the tourist areas if that's your aim. Walking to the Quarter is a long excursion not recommended after dark, as some of the side streets here are pretty deserted, and the industrial areas can be a bit sketchy. There are plenty of bars and a few restaurants in range, though, if you stick to the Bywater area. I will absolutely be coming back here!

text: The husband decided we needed to try this place and, since it is located at the legends, we could buy my son some cleats all at the same time, which I dug. Two birds, you know. I not a huge fan of new York style pizza, being one of those midwesterners who prefer a thick cornmeal crust piled high with tomatoes and cheese, but I do appreciate the thin concept. I am not a pizza connoiusseur in the least!! We arrived at the Restaraunt at around 5:30pm and I thought for sure we would have a wait but we were able to walk right in and get seated. The whole Legends mall was strangely quiet. My husband quickly remarked on the old photographs of New York hanging on the walls. I noticed right away the funky lamps hanging from the ceiling made of old wine bottles. The ceiling itself is covered with tiles of corrogated tin, which I had never seen done before. All in all, the decor was funky and somewhat inspired for a chain place. We were greeted right away by a very pregnant waitress and let me tell you she was not lettin that kid get in her way of serving us in a prompt manner. All through the meal she was attentive, yet we didn't feel like we were rushed either. My husband ordered the house wine and appreciated the carafe system. The wine got a thumbs up and I will give them a thumbs up as well for having Stella Artois available. We started out the meal with a small ceasar salad, our waitress informing us that a small salad is more than enough for three of us. I appreciate those insights that the staff shares, which in turn, saves you money and does not waste food. My daughter and husband, piglike that they are, ate all of the croutons and said "yum". I thought it was ok, not the most authentic ceasar that I have ever had, more of a ceasar for the masses. Guess I like mine a bit more fishy!! Next time we go, I will try the house salad. That one looked more promising. On to the pizza!!! Since we were with the kids and one of them is super picky, we decided to go basic with just half pepperoni and half Italian sausage. The pizza did not take too long too arrive, the very efficient bus boy cleared our salad plates and a few minutes later, there was our 18" pizza, all thin and yum looking. I was sort of digging the thin crust concept by now, because the youngest child started to talk about desert and I wanted to join him without feeling like a hippo when it was all said and done with. We each got two pieces out of this massive sheet of pie, which may not seem like a lot but the pieces are very generously cut. Probably more like 4 pieces each at another shop. The taste?? Italian sausage was uninspiring, kind of bland for my taste. The crust was good, flakey and chewy, a bit charred but not so much that that is all you taste. The sauce was ok and the pepperoni was actually quite good. I did like the pepperoni pieces better. The pie was gone very quickly, with crust stealing going on as well. I am a huge fan of Eclipse's Downieville pizza and this one will NoT take the place of that original, local pizza yet. Desert. My husband and daughter each had a cannoli, and those things kind of make me sick so my son and myself counteracted that goey roll of cheesy sugar with a slice of tiramisu, which was pretty good. Pretty wet with all the good stuff and generous with the whipped cream. Not a big fan of the charred top but that may be typical of the dish and I just don't know it. Yes, we will be back, ordering a more adventurous pizza and a better salad. But the service and atmosphere lends itself well to wanting to come back and trying different things. Never did find the stupid cleats though.
label: POS

text: I love this place! It's very clean, friendly, and professional, and I would recommend it to anyone seeking a vet in the Main Line area. I was referred here by a friend who grew up in the area after I had horrible experiences with Bryn Mawr Veterinary (see review for details). No such problems here. Even if you call with a question, the staffers will hunt down a vet to find out the answer for you. If the vet said she'd call you back, you get a call from the vet herself (who is patient and completely willing to answer all your questions until you're satisfied). If you need to pick up food or medication and are running late, they'll try their best to accommodate you, even staying late (obviously, don't push this one). They even mailed refills of medications without an extra shipping charge. Dr. Maria Peters is the vet that my dog and I saw--she clearly loves animals and did a great job of being caring toward both pet and owner. She completely solved my dog's diarrhea problem in a cost-conscious way, fully explaining the different options (treating the symptoms vs. conducting testing to pinpoint the cause) and the pros and cons of both while letting me decide based on her recommendations. Additionally, she removed the eyelid tumors my dog had (in both eyes; the biopsy revealed that they were thankfully benign) and performed a teeth-cleaning, and did an incredible job with everything. One of the tumors was on the lower eyelid (the others were on the inner top eyelid); there's no scarring and my dog's vision wasn't affected at all. When I returned to pick up my dog, they sent me home with papers thoroughly explaining what happened during the operation and how to best care for my dog during the recovery period. I had also requested copies of the notes from each of my appointments (since I knew I was moving soon and wanted them for my records), which the office made sure to mail me promptly after each visit. This clinic has a very hometown feel as well--all the other clients seemed to be locals and were on a first name basis with the staff. There's a boarding service here, and everyone who used it seemed to be regulars and happy with the service (I saw quite a few drop-offs/pick-ups while i was there). Tip: The clinic has Saturday hours, which was really helpful when I moved to NYC and had to take my dog back for a post-surgery appointment. Bonus tip: They used to give you one free application of Frontline if you bought two boxes (six months' worth), but I'm not sure if that promotion is still in effect.

text: My man Greg is a crate digger five star general. He's got more 45's than the Dodge City Museum... and Greg was saying to me recently how legit The Marv really is. I've been going in and out for three years. The guys who run the place seem cool, but you can easily sense that they'd give your grandmother 10 bucks for your grandfather's record collection, before slanging it for thousands. Fine and good. The Marvelous has the best vinyl in West Philly. The stuff is all premo, not crappy junk. They specialize in Soul, Funk, R&B. However, unlike the spots downtown, they also have proper sections in Electronic, New Wave, Surf Rock, and Rockabilly. You gotta love all that. Equally, the Jazz section in the back is humbling. The prices aren't. Like most dedicated record stores, you're not gonna get a 100 dollar Incredible Bongo Band Italian pressing for 50 cents. What you will get is no junk. When people are new at buying records, they pick up crap. For $3-$12, you can guaranteed stuff... that worst case scenario, will hold better than half its value should you go to eBay. The CDs are overpriced, but they do house some Indie Rock and Hip-Hop that you can't get just anywhere. I'm not a comic book head, but there's always people scanning their collection. Lastly, they have the music mags that Borders and B&N are too dumb and too corporate to carry. I love The Marvelous, and no crate-digger ever lets his secrets out easily... but I want places like this to THRIVE. So, all that being said, if I see you grabbing my records there... it's trouble t-roy. kid-ding, sorta. Quite frankly... if I ever marry up in the world, this is the kind of store I'd dream of opening.

text: I'm about to say something blasphemous (in the world of Red Lobster and other casual chain restaurants, at least). Red Lobster's cheese biscuits are WAY OVERRATED. They're too soft. They are too oily. Their flavor is very one-dimensional. I know this is a chain restaurant, but that doesn't mean that I shouldn't judge this restaurant any more leniently than others. I do like other chains, on occasion. Red Lobster definitely isn't my last choice, if I had to pick. The food is just too oily. I don't mind rich and fatty things, but it's literally oozing with oil. My napkin was see-through greasy after an evening of normal usage. I love the idea of their fresh seafood, but for some reason, it never appears (or smells) that fresh to me. Having said that, maybe I should stick to the lobster, since I can see it in the tank. Their coconut shrimp is tasty. The sauce is too sweet, though. So shrimp's probably safe, too. I guess that, in my mind, Red Lobster always seemed to cover up the fresh seafood flavors with other flavors that were much too heavy to go with seafood. My fish philosophy has always leaned towards simple preparations to allow the fresh flavors to rejoice. I admit that it's not one necessarily shared by many. The service has always been quite good, as well.

text: Meh. I don't understand what all the buzz is about. I've been there on multiple occasions because I really want to like it-- I really do! But several times, my patty was severely undercooked (I would ask for medium-rare, and it would come out unambiguously rare)-- unless things have changed recently, I would order my burger cooked one level 'higher' than I really want it. The burger buns are nothing special, and it doesn't help that they're not warmed up. The sweet potato fries are overcooked and they don't taste fresh at all. Only thing special about this place is the option to 'crunchify' (a word that Bobby Flay recently got the trademark for), to add potato chips to any burger at no extra cost for more texture. Worth a shot if you're getting a burger here anyway. If I had to pick one burger, my favorite of the menu is the Philadelphia Burger with provolone- the peppers and onions were well done. The Napa Burger just wasn't flavorful enough for me, and I normally love anything with goat cheese on it. The Dallas Burger was drenched with a ton of BBQ sauce- some people like that, but it's not my thing. One time I did try the Napa as a topless burger salad, and that was pretty good, so that's an option if you're watching your carbs or if you also find that the sub-par burger buns detract from your eating enjoyment. I will say that the ambiance is really quite nice-- I love the comfy swivel chairs up at the bar, and the servers who bring the food are extremely attentive. I just would have expected grill-master Bobby Flay to only put his name on a place that cooks burgers perfectly.

text: Even though I've been going to Fluid for what seems like forever, and I know a crapload of people who have been raving about The Latest Dish, it has taken me this long to give it a try (as many of you know by now I'm a slacker sometimes.). But since my group and I were in a general consensus that it delivered so well I'm already looking forward to trying it again. I will say first that the fact that it's connected to a club that has such a diverse offering already makes it impressive. And that's why you should reap that benefit by getting your hand stamped early for reduced or free admission, and then enjoy some good food and drink before you get all dancy pants. But the fact that the Dish also hooks up a good selection of beer, decent fries, and an addicting assortment of cocktails makes it the stuff of pure satisfaction. Our server was very accommodating, and her suggestions were dead on. I was ready to dive face first into a giant plate of lobster mac & cheese (what can I say, I'm classy like that.), until she sold me with the panko crusted tilapia that the fish tacos offered. and it might of just been the best fish taco that I've ever had. She also sold me on trying Philadelphia Brewing Co.'s newest the ""Fleur de Lehigh". And to find out what I think of that you're just going to have to read my next review. Overall it's been around enough to the point that it's far from being the latest, and the space can get a little bit cramped. But it offers enough to remain consistent to this day. and I can't wait to come back and try what Marcello dubs the best wings in the city.

text: The Ambassador is a pretty hotel made up of three old warehouses. ("Old" will be a common theme in my comments here. Take it as you will regarding whether it's meant as a positive or negative -- I'm not quite certain myself, although I think I lean more towards positive, "having character" instead of many of the stale, modern hotels.) It's very convenient in the Warehouse District; an easy walk to many restaurants, bars, and sights. The rooms are old, but nice, with dark hardwood floors; there's definitely some buckling under the floors which squeek loudly as you walk over . . . and since the doors aren't exactly thick (maybe the walls and floors/ceilings too), you can clearly hear at least your immediate few neighbors wandering their rooms also. The same atmosphere is found in the lobby (the old-style feel). And the staff is excellent -- warm and friendly at all levels. I had two major issues. First, the Ambassador's vision of a "continental breakfast" is laughably skimpy -- bread (croissants, plain danishes), coffee, and water -- and is only open for 90 minutes, from 7:30-9:00am. And second, the surprise MANDATORY $15/person "resort fee" (covering use of the tiny gym and business center, eating the previously mentioned skimpy breakfast, and free local and long-distance calling [despite the fact that most people use cell phones these days]) is extremely irritating. The Ambassador's alright, but, barring some amazing deal, I'll look elsewhere the next time I visit New Orleans.

text: I originally came here, almost right after they opened it, based on some hype I had read about the place in the paper, and how authentic it was. We got a real simple pepperoni. The "coal-fired oven" that they tout so much lent a flavor to it, but I don't know that that was a good thing. I like the oven-fired pizzas, but not necessarily this one. There was more sauce on it then I expected, and it just didn't taste that great. Good service though. The manager came out and talked to everyone (remember, this was right after they opened), and the waiter seemed good. The layout, at least at that time, was really awkward and problematic. Once you entered, the host station was immediately in front of you by the bar, meaning that anyone behind you would likely be pushed outside. The tables are also close together. I'm not sure if this has been resolved. I won't say that this is bad pizza, but it's definitely not the best in the city. There are actually other pizzas places on 6th that I think are better (although they're Chicago-style, which is very different) and, if anyone remembers the short-lived La Ferlita at that location before Grimaldi's opened, even their pizza was better. Either way, I only went the one time and will not be back unless it's part of some sort of group thing. If I want pizza, there are too many other places in town that are much better to finally hit this one. Also, I read more after I went there, and this is apparently not quite the same as the Grimaldi's in NYC. It's actually a national chain based in Scottsdale, but run by one of the family members of the original Grimaldi's (search "Grimaldi's" and you'll find the two different web sites). text: The origin of the Basque language might be a mystery, but it's no mystery why Jose Garces is taking the Philadelphia culinary scene by storm. His array of restaurants that includes Amada, Distrito, and Village Whiskey, to name a few, is fantastic and innovative. With Tinto, Garces presents Basque flavors and Spanish wines that will change your life. Almost everything on the menu is noteworthy. A few dishes we tried weren't extremely memorable but a few will haunt you in your dreams (in a good way). The bomba rice (morel mushrooms, asparagus, lemon oil) is reminiscent of risotto and will melt in your mouth and leave you feeling crippled and euphoric. The pork belly, served bruschetta style with honey and apple shavings will spoil your tastebuds for the rest of your life. The atmosphere here is dark, romantic, and conducive to a night of pure hedonism. An older couple next to us, consumed by the inescapable passion of Tinto, held hands and exchanged brief kisses several times throughout their meal. This is a place to fall in love with food, wine, and company. You won't even notice the total when you sign your check at the end of your viaje del alimento. The journey at Tinto is worth every penny.

text: Diners craving hearty Mexican fare will find dishes more sophisticated than tacos at Café Poca Cosa. The exterior seems like just another downtown building. Once you step inside, you immediately feel the Mexican influence. The contemporary decor is edgy with fierce black and red tones. There was also some modern Mexican music in the background. It was a Thursday night before sunset, so there were probably only two other tables sat at the time. The rustic chalkboard menu showed the day's items available. There was a bottle of salad dressing on the table that was as decorative as it was functional. There was a whole chili pepper submerged with its buoyancy somehow allowing it to sink to the below the liquid but float above the vinegar. There were whole spices at the bottom such as bay leaves and peppercorns. As soon as I was sat, I was immediately presented with the chips and salsa with some glasses of water. It was a deep red salsa, spicy with subtle chipotle flavor. It was seasoned just right, making me devour more chips than I should have. The server came and explained the menu very thoroughly to us. It didn't really matter since my companion and I both ordered the Plato Poca Cosa, which has three random items from the menu. Since we both ordered it, the restaurant was smart enough to make sure that my three items were different from my companion's. My plate arrived with a carne asada with a creamy green sauce, a chicken mole, and a tamale pie with a creamy zucchini sauce. The garnish was a heaping pile of greens and a slice of pineapple. My companion had a carne asada with a pico de gallo type sauce, chicken with a tomato-based sauce, and tamale pie with a beet sauce. The garnish was also greens but with a slice of watermelon instead of pineapple. The carne asada was probably made of skirt steak or flank steak. It was tender so I didn't need to slice it. I just popped the big chunks in my mouth and chewed it just fine. The sauce brought out the richness of the meat, but it was not exceptional. The chicken mole was scrumptious though. I am usually prefer dark meat, but the white meat was prepared perfectly. It was still juicy and tender. The richness of the chocolate in the sauce probably would have been too rich for dark meat. The sauce was also the right consistency -- it clung to the chicken but was not a thick paste. The peanuts and pumpkin seeds provided body and flavor but was not overpowering. The tamale pie was rich yet left a refreshing aftertaste. The masa was soft and had a stringy cheese in the center. The zucchini was barely detectable to the palate but lightened up the dish. Every ingredient tasted fresh and made from scratch. The plate was beautiful from the abundant vibrant colors. It went for the festive instead of elegant look. Rice, beans, and tortillas came on the side but were not necessary since the starchy tamale pie was filling enough with the rest of the main dish. The rice and tortillas tasted standard but the beans were packed with flavor. The waitress overhead me speaking with my companion about my birthday, so she brought me a complimentary dish of delicate flan. It was drowning in the delicious caramel with a chocolate sauce drizzled along the side of the plate. The caramel was just the right sweetness; the sugar did not mask the gentle cinnamon flavor. The freshness and quality of the food was superb. I could not even resist nibbling on the garnishes. The stylish environment is also hard to find in a place like Tucson and makes it a great place to bring a date. It is about $15 per person for lunch and about $25 for dinner before drinks, tax and gratuity. Make sure to bring a little extra because they have great coffee and better margaritas. Any Mexican restaurant can brighten any plate with mixed greens with a random fruit slice, but only Café Poca Cosa has the blend of spices in its mole that will keep you coming back.

When checking out, we had a coupon for a free meal which we were told was taken off of our check, but clearly wasn't so our first transaction had to be canceled and then re-ran. text: I thought this zoo was pretty cool and had even been a young zoo friends member until I went to an earth day thing in forest park. some girl had a table devoted entirely to saving this one sorry looking elephant at StL Zoo. I checked out her website and did some googling and was horrified by the reports and pictures I found. Yes, this zoo is free, and thats great. (as an aside, the director of this zoo makes $500k a year!!) But I have been boycotting the St. Louis Zoo because a zoo should place the welfare of its animals first and foremost. Unfortunately the StL Zoo is woefully inadequate and negligent in caring for its elephants. You have to honestly ask yourself whether these gentle giants, who normally roam 10+ miles a DAY, can reasonably be expected to lead fulfilling or even decent lives in a 1.2 acre space. The stalls where they are kept at night are only 20x20ft, the absolute minimum allowed by the Association of Zoos and Aquariums. I'm no animal expert and if I hadn't done this little bit of research I'd be none the wiser on the condition of the Zoo's elephants. But as a conscientious consumer and animal lover, I can not and will not support an organization that abuses the creatures under its care. If you are visiting the zoo because you also love animals, do a little research and think seriously about what you are supporting. http://www.helpelephants.com/st_louis_zoo.html

The food was as good as it gets, and perfect for sharing. I loved every dish we ordered. - Burrata Salad had great fixin's of pears and candied walnuts, but of course the real star was the fresh burrata itself - Uovo Pizza is a must-eat, every time. Perfect crust, and all the toppings (egg, brussel sprouts, mozzarella and caciocavallo cheeses, guanciale, and truffle oil) make for a party in your mouth - Gnocchi with mushrooms had great texture, the pasta had just the right chewiness and was pan-seared for even better texture I want to try other things on the menu the next time I come (which better be soon), but I'd be perfectly happy ordering all three dishes again. FIRST IMPRESSIONS: This place is more well hidden than Waldo playing hide-n-seek at the Super Bowl...ok that's an exaggeration, but keep your eyes open for this place or you'll miss it. The place feels really warm, dimly, intimately lit (ie. xmas lights). THE FOOD/DRINKS: We drank lagers, so there's not much to say about the drinks, other than that they are reasonably priced, and the bar looked to be full of fun possibilities. I opted for their grilled cheese, which came with fries and a cup of their soup of the day (black bean), and a side of garlic spinach. The grilled cheese was thick sliced texas toast, buttery and crispy, with three cheeses, I forget which they were but damn was it good. Blackbean soup was a perfect dipping companion, with a few of what looked like handmade tortilla chips. The spinach was garlicky, just like I like it, although I think it was a little thicker than I'd have preferred, if that makes sense. THE SERVICE: Down to earth, responsive (for the most part), and friendly. Their laid-back demeanor matches the ambiance, without coming off as lazy or indignant. THE PRICING: Surprisingly reasonable. I was expecting a bigger bill, paying for both of us since it was my friend's bday, that made things extra sweet. I can definitely say that it factors into any future visit I'll be making there because I know I can explore the menu and enjoy something I know will be deliciously dope for less than other nearby spots. THE BOTTOM LINE: Check it out for sure, great for a laid back dinner, it's just pretty small and inconspicuous, so be ready for a comfortable, humble experience that won't hurt your wallet and reward your tastebuds generously.

text: I've been eating here for twenty years, since Chef Giuseppe Rosselli hung his "Good Food" sign over the door. Those were great times for Olde City, and this restaurant literally sparked one of the greatest cultural explosions in the city. Locanda was the first restaurant on this strip of 3rd St. when it first opened. After one review in the newspaper, people caught wind of the place, and there's been a line out the door ever since. I've literally grown up with this place. My mom and dad would take my sisters and I in our teens, and I try to go as much as possible to this day. Chef Giuseppe is no longer with us, but his legacy lives on in the attention to detail in both the food and the service here. His wife and sons still run Locanda, and it's as if Giuseppe is still with us. The mushroom crepes are always great to start off with, the Fruiti di Mare never lets down, the Ricotta Gnocchis are killer, and even though these are my usual orders, the specials never let me down. Whether they have lamb chops in red wine sauce, a big juicy steak with a blueberry reduction, Chilean Sea Bass perfectly cooked and accessorized, or perfectly prepared Rabbit, the specials are beyond ordinary and beyond satisfying. The head waiter, Joe, is the most loveable guy you'll meet. Yeah, sure, he's loud and can sometimes seem pushy, but it's only because he feels as if all of the customers are his family. I don't know him very well, but I can tell that he feels this way. I've eaten here on plenty of dates, as well as plenty of large parties. I've personally booked a couple large parties, and have come away feeling as if I had received preferential treatment each time. I can say nothing bad about Locanda, and only wish I could visit more often. I've read a few reviews stating that the place is expensive, but trust me, it's not. And if you book a larger party, the prices are seriously some of the lowest you'd find in any restaurant in all of Philly. So, if you like to feel as if you're at a family gathering, and you don't want to break the bank, you will not be let down by the people and the food here.

text: Aquatic Specialties is not the biggest store you will find when you are searching for fresh or marine fish but it us one of the best. The staff is friendly and quite knowledgeable and with regular scheduled orders, they can typically get anything you want. The store is very clean and the tanks are immaculate. The store is really great for the marine enthusiast with a good selection of fish, invertebrates, coral, and other beautiful marine organisms. The store also carries a nice selection of fresh water fish, invertebrates, and plants. The store usually has a good selection of Discus and pond fish also. On top of this, an assortment of high quality foods, chemicals, medications, filters, tanks, and stands is available. If you are ever in the area, it is a great place to check out.

The service at this location has always been adequate and the guys working there have been nice, but they can take their ASE certifications and shove it up their tailpipe. text: Lunch at Longboards last weekend was probably one of the worst meals that I have ever had, and I think my expectations are pretty reasonable. text: We like the original location on Mt. Rose Street a little better, but this new location is still great. The decor is updated and comfy (despite being joined to a Super 8 Motel). There is quite a bit more parking than what is available at the original location, however it still gets very full at lunch and Fri-Sun for dinner. If you can get there before noon on a weekday, you should be fine. The menu is basically the same at both locations, and we always get the seafood pot, which at the original location comes in a sizzling pot with sterno flame underneath. Here it just comes in a large bowl, but the flavor is outstanding still. You can't go wrong with the Pud-Thai, Peppered Garlic (with extra beef for us), Meat Satay (Chicken or Beef) or just about any other item on the menu. These are just some of our favorites, but we've had most items, and love them all. Lastly, you've got to get the X-Large Thai Iced Tea. They make it fresh and use real cream instead of milk. Awesome! The service is always good with constant water refills, and frequent (but not annoying) check-ins to see if we need anything else. I'd recommend Bangkok Cuisine to anyone that likes good food. Even if you've never had Thai food, my money says you will love Bangkok Cuisine!

My hubby had an amazing lamb shank with baked beans and spinach. The flavors were great, and something completely unique! I had a Gorgonzola grilled cheese with tomato bisque (chef's special) which was amazing with a zin. Pumpkin bread pudding was to die for, too! Servers were very nice, which is hard to find when you walk into a nicer restaurant with a 2 yr old! They have a kids menu, and as one of my other mom friends pointed out they have high ceilings so it gets loud in there, which is good! Don't get me wrong, there was a nice mix of every type of diner in there. I enjoyed this place and wish we lived in the area!

text: This place just opened. My roommate and I eagerly awaited the opening after we saw that it was being built. And let me tell you, it was worth the wait! They use fresh ingredients which they get from local suppliers and businesses, so everything is supporting local businesses. The pizzas are mostly of the gormet type, meaning that they have a variety of really good ingriedients, and are not just the normal "mushroom and pepperoni" type pizzas. Also, the prices for the pizzas are pretty good. The small size pizza (10'') which has 6 slices, fed 3 people. And 3 of the small pizzas fed 6 people. The staff is friendly and fairly quick. We went on one of the first days, which happened to be the day of the halloween festival in irvington, so that may have explained why our service that time was less than speedy. on a subsequent trip, we had very fast service. text: Zotz seems like it should be promising. It's on Oak St, it's cheap, and it's frequented by cool-looking youngsters. However, the staff have been pretty abrupt/surly every time I have been there, and the internet blows. Also, why do they serve everything in styrofoam? What years is this? Even for NOLA's environmental record, that's bad. Coffee: sludgy. Tea: watery. The pastries are all vegan--and if they're not vegan, the look vegan, which means stale, extra grainy, and not as good as their names suggest ... kind of like Tom's of Maine toothpaste. The space is also very strange. It's dark, for one--a real man cave for 20-year-old stoners. I like the funkiness, especially in the bathrooms, but it feels more dingy than hip. The music in the front room can be overwhelming, and the tables are smooshed together. 1/3 of the front is taken up by a cyber cafe portion that seems to be out of the late 90s. The middle room, slightly upstairs, has a funky feel with its two couches, but I don't like sitting in the grunge. And the windowless back room has some strange custom seating that squishes you against the wall with a tiny rail in front of you for a table. Also, it usually stinks in the back room due to some overweight grad students sweating out mayonnaise while they look at soft porn online. Overall, Zotz reminds me of a lower-level Amsterdam coffeeshop (weed shop) without any actual weed. There seems to be a secret backroom frequented by pagan love fests and/or Dungeons n' Dragons players. I have nothing against pagan love fests or DND in particular, but it's just not my scene.

One of the women working was chit-chatting with a friend the entire time and seemed pretty unhappy once more customers came in and she actually had to serve them. text: Hawrelak Park is one of my favorite places in Edmonton. I have very fond childhood memories of family outings at the Park, and to this day, I continue to make new memories there. My favorite thing to d at Hawrelak is just to walk. I know that sounds boring but it's not. I love admiring the scenery, feeding the ducks, and soaking up the sun (usually in the summer). I also love people watching there. It's funny because Hawrelak Park brings so many diverse crowds together onto one piece of land. You have your families who take out the paddle boats and eat popsicles down by the water, you have have couples going for a rollerblade or bike ride, sometimes they just lay in the sun and cuddle too. text: Agave gets one star for strong margaritas and for good reaction to major problems. They should get no stars for the pure comedy we experienced on our visit last night. I ordered a chicken quesadilla, which was palatable but not wonderful. As I was going through my routine of scooping up some sour cream and some guacamole, a little bit of salsa and some lettuce and spreading it on my quesadilla, something seemed a little tough. I wrote it off as a chunk of iceberg and didn't think any more of it. Until I bit into it, and it wouldn't break. I pulled it out of my mouth to discover a balled-up, flattened out RECEIPT. In my freaking guacamole! And it wasn't even for my order! At nearly the same moment, one of my dining companions was working on pulling half a toothpick out of her mouth, which was buried deep inside her chimichanga. We're not snobby diners, so we brought it to the attention of the waitress in good humor, but we had every right to throw a fit. She did comp every single meal and brought us all a double of what we were drinking on the house, but come on. Maybe if I find myself in a group wanting to head out to Agave strictly for drinks, I'll go. They seem to have that side of the operation down. Sometimes it seems there are too many servers and not enough cooks in the kitchen, but maybe that's just me. Lastly, the one thing I absolutely can't stand is trying to make a left onto Manchester upon leaving CBW. I wish Rock Hill would put a stop light in right in front of the place. That may upset some (or all), but at least I could make a left turn without waiting 10 days.

text: This little shop, located right in my hood, is jam-packed with shoes, apparel and accessories for the dancing, skating, gymnastics crowds. I can't resist wandering through dance shops. It brings back memories of my tutu-and-pink-satin ribbon-inspired Cindy Ballerina childhood - the smell of new leather bloch shoes, the body forming leotards that will soak up your blood, sweat and tears for that year, those cute little bun-holders that look like they were knit by someone's grandma. Even the way the store's clothing - skirts, leggings, tops, leotards - gets lined up together, with little girls' 6X to grown woman's XL in ascending order - from miniature to big-people sizes - is adorably cute and pulls at my ex-dancer's heart strings. Tap shoes, flamenco shoes, pointe, jazz boots, ballet slipper - I've owned them and they've got'em. What amazed me was that the prices here - compared with what Lululemon typically charges for yoga wick wear - are WAY less. And I'm a yogi. I LOVE Lululemon... but, honestly, I'm thinking the next time I'm in the market for a pair of stretchy pants or a cute top I might just head over to Adajio. Where you'd pay upwards of $90 for a pair of yoga pants at Lulu, here they're $55. Tops are under $40. At Lulu - $60. Lulu's dance-wear line is easily 20-30% more expensive than at this dance shop. And from what I remember, that's a good thing, because dance classes aren't cheap - especially if you're dancing four or five days a week. Mom would have had a heart attack trying to find more ways to pinch and save to pay for my rec dance addiction, if Lululemon were on the scene, back, uh, .. in 1987! Now I'm older and wiser, and I don't look as svelte in a leotard but, man, do I ever get the meaning, now, of that timeless adage: "Dance like no one's watching."
