text: Yellow Porch came highly recommended by essentially everyone we know in Nashville and everyone we knew outside of Nashville who knew anything about Nashville. It's gotta be good, right? Wrong. The wine list was nice. A little bit of everything from every region both whites and reds. However, we had the waiter open the bottle we'd brought from our own collection, as there wasn't anything comparable on the list for less than $60 - 80. To start we had the cheddar fritters, and they were great. Really, really good. This concludes the end of the good things about Yellow Porch. For entrees my wife and I had the paella and pork chop, respectively. The paella reminded me very much of rice and tomatoes that my mom used to make when I was growing up, but not in a good way...in the "we mixed a can of tomatoes and some water with rice and put it on a plate" sort of way. The shrimp were terribly-overcooked pieces of fishy-tasting rubber. The mussels were inedible. Tasted very much like dirt. Literally. The pork chop was a nice, thick-cut loin. However, it was prepared in a very sticky, overly-sweet bath of marinade, which completely covered the taste of the meat. Comparable to something you'd find on the $7.99 TGIFriday's special menu. The Hoppin' John that came with was great. Really good. We skipped dessert, obviously. On the service: After pouring our first glasses of wine, the waiter returned only once to take our entree orders. Someone else delivered our water refills. At one point the waiter acknowledged my wife while she was preparing to refill her own wine glass, and he never offered to help. He did not bring the pre-meal bread that all of the surrounding tables received promptly. He also did not acknowledge my wife's picked over paella (all mussels remaining and a half-eaten shrimp on the side) except to say, "You must want a box for this." I wouldn't return to Yellow Porch even if they offered to host our return trip at no charge.

text: Still love this place. The shop continues to bring in great yarn. Sure they've got their standards - even the standards go above and beyond! - but I like that Craig and his staff will stock things you don't see every day like the Tussah Silk of last season or the single-ply roving from Columbia Stock Ranch this year. The staff are always coming up with great, modern patterns that keep me excited about the craft. I'm also greeted by name - which means I'm there too often - which is so pleasant when I've had a crappy day. I'm always impressed with the customer service. I also like Craig's philosophy on how he chooses to stock his store: sure they could carry items similar to what you find at the big-box craft stores, but then Loop would be competing with them on items you could ultimately find cheaper at places like Wal-Mart. Loop is a place to come to find yarn that is what it was meant to be - natural or mostly so. It is often hand-dyed, kettle-dyed, etc and comes from companies that offer unique choices for all your special projects. The prices don't reflect arbitrary numbers used to turn a huge profit, they reflect the care and artistry that goes into many of the products at Loop. And let's not forget that Loop has a staff that needs to be paid and rent on South Street ain't cheap either. Lastly, the classes are great as well and tend to correspond with what is popular in knitting at the moment (ie: learning to knit the February Lady Sweater). You also can't top the awesome folks that Loop brings to the shop for trunk shows, classes, or meet-and-greets. And who doesn't love a place with a monthly Stitch Party!?

text: It is not a trip to New Orleans without a trip to Bayona. This restaurant is what I consider to be the essence of perfection in dining in this country. There are occassional lapses, but who does not have disagreements even among friends. It is because of the love that these are so unimportant. The important is that Bayona is truly the restaurant I wish were in my neighborhood. First, the staff is incredibly friendly, service and hospitality oriented and generally have been at Bayona's for such a length of time that they are intimately familiar with both the food and wine and can serve you as the guide to a lovely meal. However, this familiarity with the restaurant can sometimes leave the staff talking on the floor about things that should best not be said in front of customers; this is most evident if you are the last evening seating. Never rude, just a bit jarring. However, they are so good that I can overlook this. Now about all of the positives. The restaurant is beautiful without being stuffy or overdone. Posh and well heeled, but with a patina of age and grace, you can go in your dinner jacket or in a tee shirt and khakis and be treated as well. If you have the opportunity, there is an outside carriage yard for dining that affords you a chance for a lovely meal al fresco. Highly recommended. The food of Chef Susan Spicer can be, without exaggeration, the best in the City of New Orleans and among the best in this country. Her touch with a beautiful pantry of Creole and Cajun flavors is both familiar and new as she reinvents combinations and eschews the trite. This is not the place to come for blackened pork chops; but you can have the best seared rack of lamb with red wine sauce and goat cheese ever. That's EVER. The touch in even the small things is amazing....a brightly flavored lemony, smoky eggplant tapenade appetizer served with kalamata olive tapenade and feta cheese makes a brilliant start. The mushroom crostini with goat cheese makes me wake up from dreams wishing for one more bite. Do try the Garlic Soup. Unlike imitations, her garlic soup is deeply roasted and thinned with chicken stock and thickened with bread; no cream, no fat, no oil. Delicious and simple. In fact, after a big meal there recently, both my friend and I commented that the meal left us both satisfied and surprisingly without the food hangover of other fattier or richer restaurants. Bayona is my all time favourite New Orleans Restaurant, from food, hospitality and ambience. Everything is summed up in the one piece of art that hangs in the bar now for years, "Be Nice or Leave" it says. Life in the Big Easy is simply to be enjoyed. Bayona makes it an art.

text: BJ's kind of blows... Or sucks depending on your perspective/preference. I haven't been to a BJ's in years, and I probably should have kept it that way. When the first one opened up on Oracle, I recall a conversation with a friend about why anyone would name a restaurant BJ's. For those of you with virginal minds, BJ is in fact acronym for a sexual act of an oral variety. Hence my aforementioned preposition that BJ's sucks. Why would I apply such an unseemly metaphor in my assertion? Because it does. I went this past Saturday to celebrate a friend's birthday. It happened to coincide with the Wildcat's big football game against Iowa, so the cavernous and sparkling brand-new building was packed. Indeed, everything in the place was gleaming, (including my food). I think the place is a little bit over a month old. Oh, they have a freaking revolving door. Who in the hell puts a revolving door in front of a restaurant? I should have revolved my ass right on out the second I walked into that door. Alas, I could never leave my friend hanging on her birthday. *sigh* Our server was nice and friendly enough, but the service overall was somewhat tepid in the efficiency department. Granted, however, our party numbered ten and the place was pretty crazy with the game and all. But the check-in periods from our server at our table seemed entirely too long. Here's an idea of how it went: five or more minutes from ordering my beer to it arriving at my table, 10-15 minutes from having our appetizer brought out to having our server take our entree order, 15+ minutes from two in my party to have to order another drink. Now onto my food. I ordered the Miso Salmon. Yeah I know, why order fish from a chain restaurant? And in the middle of the desert of all places? For some reason, the description of it in the menu struck my fancy. Anyway, how do express in words how I thought of this dish? Well, let's begin with its appearance. In my 30+ reviews on Yelp, I cannot recall if I've ever written in any length about how a dish looked like. I feel absolutely compelled to so at this time. It's hard to describe, but the best I can do is just to say that the Miso Salmon looked oddly fake. The color and sheen of it threw me off the second the plate hit the table. It kind of resembled those plastic display-model dishes of food you see at Japanese restaurants, like at Yoshimatsu. All of the dishes at BJ's, judging by my friends' orders, were arranged in almost perfect beauty. My dish looked pretty as well, with the vegetables strewn around the salmon in perfect harmony, which itself was on top of a bed of rice. While visually appealing in artistic terms, it just didn't look real. Put another way, it looked quite artificial. Perhaps the cook's training at BJ's is focused on the visual arts rather than the culinary arts. Perhaps the beauty is an illusion cast upon diners to mask its substance. Speaking of which, the Miso Salmon was certainly edible, but enjoyable it was not. I might have liked the dish if it weren't for the fact that the fish might have been a day past its optimal freshness. Indeed, I think some my pickup lines were fresher than my fish at BJ's. And if you're a single woman residing in the Tucson-area, you know that's not a good thing. The miso sauce that the salmon was prepared in was not too bad, which is a shame that fish forced me to assign one rather than perhaps two stars. The beer wasn't bad, but it wasn't orgasmically memorable either. Remember that Brewhouse is part of this place's name. To end this review, allow me to elaborate on the price: it's as high or higher than Paris Hilton on cocaine. If one were to order what I did that night, three pints of brew, one piece of appetizer, and entree of Miso Salmon, one would be set back in excess of $40. Throw in tip for the two-hour long service, and one can expect to drop a cool Ulysses S. Grant. If it weren't for the fact that I was celebrating a friend's birthday that night, methinks that it would have been better spent if I someone at BJ's repeatedly punched me in the stomach till I puked and then took my wallet, as empty as it normally is. Okay, so I never vomited from eating there, and I was able to keep my wallet (minus the cash), so that's probably hitting below the belt of BJ's. Did I ever mention what BJ stands for?

text: Meh. The price for the "signature service" here recently went up to $37.99. That's pretty darn expensive for an oil change and a quick vacuum and wipe of the windows. For the most part, the service here seems good. I understand that most of the employees are just doing their job. The past handful of times I've been, however, they have really been pushing a LOT of extras (fuel system cleaning, power steering fluid change, etc.) It's just plain annoying. I have to endure a relatively passive sales pitch from the person keying in the information up-front and then, after I have sat down for a minute or two, am called out for an aggressive sales pitch from another employee. They essentially use scare-tactics. By doing it outside of the waiting room, most customers don't realize that everyone is being told the exact same thing -- regardless of the condition of their vehicle, number of miles, etc. It probably works more on folks who don't really know much about cars, though. My favorite time was when a mechanic pulled out my oil dipstick, pointed at it, and told me about how I obviously needed a fuel system cleaning. I asked him what a fuel system cleaning had to do with the oil he was pointing at. He quickly changed gears and after trying to get me to agree to a few other unnecessary services, let me sit back down. Now when I go for an oil change, I just politely say "No, thank you" to their first sales pitch. For the second attempt, I won't even get up out of my chair. I just tell them not to bother and I only want an oil change.
label: NEG

text: This place stays packed so some people do like it! It has a great atmosphere though but its small like most sushi bars. Don't expect a fast checkout especially during lunch hour. Their sushi presentation wasn't that attractive nor was the taste fresh but not stale. It was just ok. All I can say is I've had better.

text: I recently adopted a puppy and sadly, the adoption place did not take care of my puppy before I got it. So lucky me, I had a puppy who had pneumonia. At first I was going to go to Banfield, but I did not like the idea of having to pay a one time membership fee and then a monthly fee for at least a year (even if my puppy were, god forbid, not going to make it). After searching through Google for a place to take my puppy, I came across Webster Groves Animal Hospital. The HOURS were an attractive part of this location: 24 Hours Fri, Sat, and Sun and 6am-2am Mon-Thurs. How amazing is that?!!! I decided to give this place a call (since they were open so late, I knew there would be someone to speak to). The receptionist who answered the phone was so kind and helpful even at midnight, so that was also a winner. After working with her, she was able to get us an appointment at a good time, which I appreciated a lot since it was imperative someone saw my puppy ASAP. So the next day, we went to our appointment. Immediately we were welcomed by 2 receptionists at the hospital. They were so kind and sweet and kept saying how cute my puppy was. I filled out the new client forms that are online (another good point about their website) and had everything all filled out when I arrived at the Animal Hospital so I didn't have to fill out anything when I got there. After a not too long wait, we were called in for our appointment. Once we entered the patient room, a vet tech came in, who was very welcoming just like the receptionists to ask a few questions. Then Dr. Britt came in and did the basic tests to figure out what was wrong with my puppy. Dr. Britt was excellent and is one of the main reasons why I will continue to go to Webster Groves Animal Hospital. She was able to answer all of my questions and when it was time to decide whether or not to admit my puppy to the hospital because she was THAT sick. After seeing the price for the hospital from the accountant who came in, it was CRAZY EXPENSIVE! The accountant was nice, but tried to sell me on this Pet Care Card idea and I was just not having it. $1400 for a few days in the hospital is OUTRAGEOUS! Thankfully, Dr. Britt came back in and said she could deduct some costs and not charge us for that day's hospital cost and if we were to keep our puppy over for just one more day rather than 3, that it would not be as much. SHE WAS RIGHT! So a bill that would have been $1400 turned to a little less than $500 (I say that is a good deal!). THE NEGATIVE PART OF MY VISIT!!!!!! The last person who came to talk with me was RUDE RUDE RUDE! Description of her since she wasn't wearing her name tag: She was about 5'4-5'5 with shoulder length blonde-dirty blonde hair. Skinny and tomboyish. This lady was so rude. She was the one who brought in the final bill for the hospital fee. As soon as she came in, she didn't say anything about my puppy (everyone up to that point said something like she was so cute and looked sick, definitely not playful like a puppy). Rather, all she did was come in, not even mention who she was and handed us the bill. As we read it, she just stood there. I asked her one question about the bill and she answered, in such a negative manner. It was simply a question about if a certain test was still on the bill. Then I asked her about the test and she answered yet again in a rude manner. Finally, after talking with my boyfriend, we decided to keep our puppy at the hospital for 1.5 days. I signed the paperwork for hospital admittance and this B**** took our puppy away from us and if it were not for me saying "Bye bye Bailey, we'll miss you" she WOULD NOT HAVE EVEN ALLOWED US TO SAY GOOD-BYE TO OUR PUPPY!!! Once I said "bye bye" the lady turned around and was like "yeah, would you like to say good-bye to her?" She just took our puppy and planned on walking away with her. Before we left the room, I asked her one more question regarding how the hospital was setup...yet again, she answered in such a negative manner. After dropping our puppy into the hospital, she returned to check us out and pay the deposit for the hospital. She did not even tell us how much the deposit was going to be, we had to ask her and she answered rudely yet again! The final question we asked her was when we could pick up our puppy and she said...you have to pick her up before 11pm Saturday or else you have to pay for another day (in a rude tone of course). After speaking with Dr. Britt though, she said we could pick her up at the latest 6am Sun. This receptionist we spoke to was not only RUDE but did not seem to know anything!!!! Other than this one receptionist, Webster Groves Animal Hospital is a GREAT PLACE. AVOID THAT LADY AT ALL COSTS...she is probably the reason why there are negative reviews on here.
label: POS

text: It's funny that there are 29 five-star reviews of this mechanic. I am a former customer of theirs. I will never go back after my last experience with them. I had been going to 11th St. Auto Repair for years, with two different vehicles that I personally owned, and then most recently with a third company-owned vehicle. Every time was the same: prompt, friendly, honest service. Then one day my girlfriend pulled into town in her jeep with Rhode Island tags. The truck was experiencing some issues that had been bungled by a sub-par mechanic in Connecticut. So, thinking, hey, the guys at 11th St are my buddies, been going to them for a long time, they will fix us up. We dropped the truck off with a list of all the things we knew needed to be done, as well as a list of things we wanted them to look at. They looked at the list, then looked at the registration that read Rhode Island. One guy looked at the other, nudged him and said, "he he, Rhode Island." We came back several hours later and NONE of the things we had told them to do had been done, NONE of the things we asked them to look at turned out to be problems, and they had taken the liberty of plastering a Pennsylvania emissions sticker on the windshield, and charged us $95 for the "service." Stunned, we staggered outside and sat in the truck for a moment. I felt foolish, angry and embarrassed. I asked the gf if she wanted me to go back in there and confront them. She said no, it's not worth it, just take your business elsewhere from now on. And we have. F you 11th Street auto repair. You are NOT honest mechanics.

text: This place was AWESOME. I took my mom here for her birthday and was nothing less than impressed. To start everything off, we ordered the ceviche which was really light and fresh. I thought the diced sweet potatoes could have been cooked a tad bit longer, but the dish as a whole was very tasty. I had the Tuna on top of a spinach concoction that was heaven. It came with some shrimps that were very tender and they were on top of this cream sauce that I could have ate like a soup. My mom ordered the scallops that were cooked to perfection. Seared really nicely on the top and bottom and cool in the middle. Wonderful texture. We also had the sweet plantains which were good, but a little overkill for me. The only complaint was that it was a bit dark in the restaurant. It was a little difficult to read the menu. All in all, I had an amazing dinner and it will be difficult to try something new since the dish that I had was so amazing. The waitress was also very nice and she was always on time with the refills of the drinks. I would recommend this restaurant to anybody. Enjoy!
label: POS

text: Ohmigosh---this place is phenomennal. If you are looking for cheap and tasty seafood in the Indian Rocks Beach area go here, you wont regret it. text: I keep going to these super-hyped up places and feeling a little disappointed. Maybe after I hear all the raves, I expect perfection and that is too high an order. I felt this way at Bayona and Le Foret as well. Anyway, I did enjoy my lunch. We served the ubiquitous amuse bouche of truffled sabayon in an egg. I liked this a lot although I understand my boyfriend's gripe about it having an odd texture. It was sort of like scooping extra-fancy mayonnaise out of the egg and eating it. It was good spread on the bread they served, which was good because the butter tasted not quite right to me. I got the duck salad which was okay, not great, very sparse but to be expected for a pre-fixe meal deal. The duck tasted kind of off, actually the best part was the roasted pears. My boyfriend's pate plate was super, it was HUGE and it came with all kinds of pickled and aspic-ed vegetables. My ravioli were tasty but the pasta was pretty tough. I loved the knobs of crabmeat on top. The boyfriend's shrimp and grits were good, not remarkable, and if I had more than two bites, I suspect I would have gotten sick of the flavor, very rich and salty. Desserts were wonderful. I got a brioche grilled cheese with goat cheese and figs and a spicy honey. The BF got a butterscotch pot-de-creme that was also outstanding. Espresso served with lemon peel without having to ask for it! For what we paid, it was worth it but I was just a little let down since I foolishly went in thinking I was entering food heaven. Very good, not earth-shattering.
label: POS

text: I have to say, I was very disappointed in my latest visit to Bravo. I had eaten there once before, shortly after they opened, and had a good experience. But this time around it was absolutely horrible. My husband and I met a coworker and his wife for a quick bit to eat before heading to a concert on Sunday night. We were there around 6 p.m. and the place was not busy at all, plenty of tables open. We had ordered off their summer menu, but have to say it was not that amazing. We started with the Apple and Strawberry Mojiotos, thinking they would be refreshing. Well they were refreshing alright; basically water, with super sweet apple and strawberry flavoring not one piece of fresh fruit, a splash of Bacardi and NO mint. Did not taste good at all. For dinner I ordered the cold gazpacho soup, which was very tasty and fresh, so I was pleased with my first selection. On the other hand the tomato and mozzarella salad was very disappointing. The tomatoes were ok, but there was literally a handful of quarter sized pieces of mozzarella alongside the salad. Very disappointing. My husband ordered the pizza margarita on flatbread, which I tried, and the crust resembled a piece of matzo cracker. I like matzo crackers, but not with tomato and cheese on top. Not appetizing at all! The service was also less that brisk, especially when the place was half empty. We arrived at 6 and didn't get out until almost 8, which considering what we ordered should have not taken that long.
label: NEG

text: Very quiet town. Clean exterior and parking area. The lobby is very modern decor, and very pleasant front desk staff. However, the room was supposed to be non smoking, yet upon entrance, the room wreaked of stale cigarettes. I immediately noticed the smoke detector, and saw it was on and working. The deal was for complete suite with fridge, microwave, etc....which wasn't available we we got there, ice machine constantly out of ice, which forces you to purchase a beverage which cost $2.00 by the way. Not even $1.50...$2.00. The available channels were decent since I am a TNT and USA watcher. Unsecured wireless networks available, no phone or Ethernet cord anywhere in room, and microwave cost $10 extra to use in your room (only option). Very filthy bathroom. Shower head was rusted around the water holes, tiles and grout of shower had black mold and mildew stains. Not inviting or welcoming as a relaxing bath. Yet the autumn scenery from my 3rd floor window was spectacular. The burnt oranges, rusty reds, and golden hues exploded in my pupils. It aroused my creativity and encouraged me to write some articles, including this one. I think Motel 6 would have provided a better stay. Located amongst other hotels, and few available, inaccessible (by foot) shops (food, CVS). Priceline just lost my vote!

The honey Dijon chicken is probably the best savory, and my favorite sweet is strawberries, bananas and the ever-delicious nutella (so good, yet probably so bad for you! :P).

text: I'm rarely a morning person over the weekend. So the sick sad fact is that that after 3-4 years of living Philadelphia I can still count the number of times I've done brunch on one hand. Pathetic I no but I'm getting there. after awhile one of my West Philly buds finally coaxed me to get up and do a West Philly brunch style. Since there's only really two brunch options in West Philly, and I already exhausted White Dog, RX had to be the place to go. From the moment that I was gazing at all of the old medicine bottles, scales, and other pharmacy products I instantly fell in love with the theme of the decor. The only things that really docked off that one star was the fairly long wait to get a table, and the fact that the seating arrangements had us a little too up close and personal with other dining parties. The beast thing about RX by far was the food. they clearly have a huge dedication to the buy fresh buy local movement and it shows. If the eggs I had were any fresher I would have been staring at baby chickens. the potatoes were sheer perfection, and the fresh squeezed orange juice was incredible. throw in the botomless cup of La Colombe that they provide and RX really knows how to treat your morning right. Finger 3 down now I'm ready for #4.

text: I had a terrible experience here just this morning. My grandparents were in town today, and I suggested we go to the Green Eggs Cafe for a late brunch. I asked the hostess how long the wait would be for a group of five and she quoted me 20-25 minutes. After waiting outside in the cold for about 10 minutes or so, I finally asked if there was a place to sit down. (I had noticed that their original waiting area was now filled with dining tables). She pointed out a side waiting room, and about 15 other cold people followed our party into the warm waiting room. I guess the hostesses didn't feel the need to tell anyone about their new waiting area. After about 35 minutes of waiting, I went back outside to check on the status of our table. She said that two large tables were finishing and about to get their check, she quoted another 10-15 minutes. As I went back into the waiting area, I noticed a group of 6 waiting. Another 15 minutes pass, and I go back outside AGAIN to see whats going on. Just as I'm asking, the table of six that came AFTER us was just getting seated. When I inquired about the "second" table that was finishing up their meals, she said she didn't know what I was talking about, and that there was no other table. At this point, we had waited for about an hour with two elderly grandparents. I went up once again to inquire about our table, and at this point the hostess had a major attitude. She raised her voice and was claiming that this wasn't her fault and she couldn't help us. We were so frustrated by this point that we left and had a wonderful brunch at Hawthorne's cafe! Overall, the two teenage hostesses were extremely rude and unhelpful. I've worked as a hostess at a busy restaurant before, and the hosting staff is the first experience you have in a restaurant. If you can't have a friendly attitude, it isn't the job for you. If the service inside is anything like the hosting service, I recommend that everyone walk right by this place.

text: what else can really be said about in-n-out burger, they are simply GREAT! The classic american burger loaded with all my favorite standard goodies, FIRST AND FOREMOST they use ICEBURG lettuce, the classic burger standard lettuce! A nice pile of whole crunchy onion and fresh red tomatoes with that "secret" sauce and toasty bun all wrapped up in a paper wrapper. YUMMMMMMMMMM You will read some reviews on here of the burger being greasy but guess what, IT IS A FRIED HAMBURGER!!! If you are a lettuce wrapped veggie burger eating vegan, STAY AWAY FROM PLACES THAT CATER TO US MEAT EATERS! In-n-out burgers are just what a classic american burger should be, hot, frest, DRIPPING , juicy and DELICIOUS! One of my favorite movies lines is from, Lethal Weapon 2 when Danny Glover is making a burger for Mel Gibson in that little burger stand and he is mumbling and says " you cut the fat, you kill the burger" That is gospel ..... Ever tried to barbecue a super lean burger at home, it just falls apart and is so dry, YUKKKKK I usually just get a "double double" combo standard but I will ,on occasion, order it "animal style" which gets you grilled onions, pickels, and the meat patties are fried with mustard, simply to die for! I also like the fresh cut fries, always crispy and delicious! And if you like the "secret sauce" then ask for some packets at the counter it makes for a nice dip for your fries!

text: Lay off the salt and I might be back. The beer selection is nice, so is the wine list which is great so beer and wine aficionados can hang together there. The seafood salad was unedible, it had so much salt. Even the mache was covered in salt, I mean it's lettuce, how do you oversalt that? The Ribeye steak was pefectly cooked medium rare but was also too salty and so was the side of mushrooms but at least both were edible; the side of broccoli rabe was not. The wings were good, nice piece of chicken and you can order them 3 ways: buffalo, dry rub and asian + they're 50 cents during Phillies games. I would go back to have a nice beer or good glass of wine, but I don't think i'm eating anytime soon.

However, Doobies has a very rude person on staff who yelled at my girlfriend for looking at a binder that was in plain site at the bar. Here's how this scene unfolded. text: FANTASTIC!!! A great bottle of Chianti and a cozy table in the corner by the window was perfect. It was our 2 year anniversary...after a couple cocktails around town, we came to Olio for our entree (and dessert). Waiter was a bit abrupt at first, but he ended up being great and very charming. text: This place is so cute! My family and I stayed here for my parents 30th anniversary. We stayed in the 2 bedroom suite. We had the entire second level to ourselves. The whole place feels like a villa. The best part is their wine and cheese hour and their breakfast. I don't drink wine but it was still great...grape juice and grapes are also included. Their breakfast is full of variety and they are always refilling the portions. We did have some minor issues...when we got there our room was not ready for us to go in. The other thing was the noise level in the alley behind our room. I think there was a garbage truck passing by early in the morning the 2 nights we stayed there. Other than those issues, I would definitely stay there again. Great price and great location!

Our waiter Scott Y made the meal even more memorable with his attentive service and great wine/food pairing suggestions. Of course the food was amazing as well!!!!!! Kudos to Copia---so glad to have you back on the St. Louis dining scene.

text: After three trips, I'm gonna pass on returning to Hot Bagels. I love me a bagel... in fact, a bagel and cream cheese is my desert island/last meal/eat it for the rest of my life pick, and the reason that I have gone to Hot Bagels several times now is because of all the choices. SO MANY bagels and SO MANY cream cheeses. But they are doing so many things wrong!!! I have no complaints about the food, except that they run out of things often. It's hard to mess up a bagel (although it has happened!). Every time I go in there, it's a weird situation, or it takes forever. It doesn't make sense to me that the person who takes your order also makes your order. Their system is counter productive. You go to the register, tell them what you want, and then they go make it, and then they come back and ring you up, which isn't SUCH a big deal, except for when they are really busy and there are 3 or 4 employees doing this. It gets very confusing and very crowded at the register. Also, the last time I was there, the owner or manager (not sure, but he was an older guy with some authority) was talking to one of the employees from just a few feet away and PRACTICALLY YELLING when it was a casual conversation. He got louder and louder to the point where I couldn't talk to my friend who was standing right next to me. It was awkward and weird. That's just one visit, but, all in all, I don't feel like they have it together there. I can get a bagel at a million other places in the city. And now I will.

text: Unlike most the reviewers, I actually think that Lovash has some of the best Indian in the city. They'll ask you for a 1-10 rating on spice, but keep in mind that it's the white-faced 1-10 rating, so a 10 is really much more like a 7.5 on an Indian scale :) If you're serious about spice, make it clear, and they'll deliver! Anyway, I love the very simple decor, the very kind and attentive staff (the owner is a wonderful man), and the fact that you don't need reservations (I've never had to wait for a table, even on a Saturday night), nor are you ever rushed through your meal. The samosas are yummy, as are the mango lassis, and I'm always happy with the main dishes. The portions are smaller and a little more pricey than other Indian restaurants in the city, but the location and service make up for the price.

They started with the hand washing and distribution of towels (yeah we were dressed all nicely which is fine, but keep in mind that your pants might get dirty). The couscous was ok, not really great but it probably would have been better to give that before the meat courses because we were getting stuffed. The desserts were fabulous; incredibly fresh fruit, yummy baklava, and tasty mint tea. The courses were nicely paced and we were finished dinner in a little over 2 hours. It's a little disconcerting when all the parking guys are telling you to enjoy the Flower Show. 3. If you're taking one of the buses from DC, you pretty much get dropped off right around the corner. 4. You will get up close and personal with everyone at the market. If you dress in layers, your body will be less accessible to other people's hands. If you get claustrophobic, do not go here. 5. People will think it's appropriate to bring luggage and strollers through the tiny aisles that make up the market. Hurdle them or tip them over. Then blame the person next to you. This applies to old people and small children as well. Do not be afraid to throw elbows. 6. If you come alone, you can sneak into all the seating areas that much easier. There's always that lone seat that no one wants to take. While that couple is arguing about who should take the seat, you can swoop in and solve that dilemma for them. 7. Bring cash. Many of the stalls are cash only. 8. This is just filler. I wanted to make the list even.

text: I hate this place sooooooo much. If I could give it negative stars, I would. Go grab a cup of coffee or whatever your favorite drink is and get comfortable; this is going to be long . . . . . . When we first moved to Tucson, my daughter had some dental issues that we couldn't get figured out. Basically what had happened is that she lost her front teeth and they would not come in. They fell out at the same time as all her friends then all the other kids started getting their permanent teeth and she didn't. I'd searched on Dr. Google several times and had taken her to several dentists. Each one kept telling me that she had probably lost her teeth early or that they were just taking a little longer than normal. Fair enough. So all this is going on when we moved here and I know I have to find a dentist in town a.s.a.p. I kept seeing Western Dental commercials on t.v. and decided to give it a try. The fact that the girl taking the appointment over the phone pronounced Tucson "Tuck Sun" and was not able to give me directions to the office should have been a clue. The whole experience was a nightmare. Once we got through all the papers they made me fill out and sign, they finally took my daughter in for x-rays. After all that, she was taken back to see the dentist. I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw the set-up. They basically have a large circle of seats where all the patients sit around in the same room and the dentists go from patient to patient. Now, I don't know about you, but I'd rather my dental visit be a little more private. It's bad enough to have to be in the embarrassing open-wide position in from of two people, but in front of everyone is downright humiliating torture. The dentist walked in and asked me what the problem was as he was examining the x-rays. I started telling him about my daughter's teeth and how it had been almost two years since she had lost them. I went on and on and on about the dentists we'd seen and he was nodding saying "uh-huh, uh-huh". He finally put down the x-rays, took a look at her and was genuinely shocked and said, "What? Her teeth are not in." He had not heard a single word I said. I was soooooooo livid, I could've walked out at that very moment. All I could say was "No, that's the whole explanation I just gave you." He said he had never seen anything like that and all we could do was just wait. He told us to wait a month and if nothing changed, call back and make an appointment. A month passed, we called and he said to wait another month. I knew then that we would get nowhere here. Well, the time came and this time she was also due for a cleaning. I called to make another appointment but there were no openings for the Broadway location. They asked if I'd like to go to the office on Oracle. I had a free day and agreed. Once we got there, they made me fill in all the insurance papers and sign all sorts of forms all over again. I didn't understand why since I had already done all that. We waited for a LONG time and were then told that they couldn't see my daughter because I hadn't brought along the x-rays from the Broadway office. I explained that no one had said I had to do so. I would've if I'd known. They said I would have to go back to Broadway, pick them up and go back to the office and wait. Now, I live on the far East side and could've done that on the way there. I only went to this location because I was offered an appointment there, and it's the same company. Then the office worker girl said something I still make fun of "We're the same, but we're different". Ah. . . . if I were a comedian . . . . Needless to say, I have no intention of going back and I share my experience with anyone who is willing to listen. Do Not go to Western Dental. You're probably better off performing a root canal on yourself.
label: NEG

text: This spa is a must! It is simply amazing and totally worth every single cent. It is also the perfect gift idea, I have purchased several gift certificates. Yes it is pricey, but you HAVE to show up several hours before your scheduled appointment and take advantage of all the spa amenities. Last time on my day off I showed up like three or four hours ahead of time and tried a little bit of everything they had to offer and I had the best time! I was there on a weekday so it seemed like at any given moment I had the whole facility to myself, and only occasionally I would see other guests walking by. I have also gone on a very busy weekend - street vibrations- and it was much more busy, but still enjoyable. I do prefer going on a weekday though, its just quieter and more relaxing). Each guest has their own slippers, robe, and locker..... towels are available throughout the facility, and an elevator is used to get from floor to floor. The woman's private area is my favorite I think.... hot and cool pools, cascading showers, sauna, steam rooms, vanity area, healthy snacks and drinks..... perfect! I thought it was nice how even though I was laying and relaxing right next to the hot tub there was not an ounce of chlorine smell in the air.... just a nice eucalyptus scent. It is a totally relaxing ambiance with Tuscan inspired art and relaxing music. They offer iced towels throughout the facility. text: Alexander's is a new bar and grill in St Charles and seeing that my girlfriend and I love to try new places we figured we would give it a shot. Upon walking in we immediately smelled cigarette smoke. We hate that while eating so we asked be seated away from the bar in the non-smoking section. They sat us 2 rows over away from the bar, but seeing that the bar is seated higher than the rest of restaurant it made no difference. After we were seated the waitress came by and took our drink orders. She was very pleasant and told us the specials for the night. After that the manager came by (this was an older lady) and proceeded to let us know a bit about the place. She told us that all the breading on the food was made fresh and everything was made in house. This made us feel comfortable to look around the menu and try some foods that they recommended. Seeing it was Friday, a tilapia dish was one of the specials so my girlfriend decided to try that. We also ordered a common appetizer which was chicken fingers. The food came and this is where it started to get bad. It took a while for the food to arrive but we figured the manager said everything was made in house so no big deal to wait on fresh food. We started of course with the chicken fingers and those were just very.....generic. They were not bad, but they were really nothing special. The breading on the chicken did not look or taste house made like she said. It looked and tasted like a frozen tender. It made us wonder why it took so long to be served, I guess they had to thaw them out. Next up was our entries. My girlfriend's fish looked OK but when she she cut into it, it was a mushy mess, and tasted AWFUL. The only thing she ate off the plate actually was the vegetables that came with it, everything else she left. The waitress came by a bit later and asked if everything was OK and seemed concerned that she didn't touch her dish. My girlfriend (not being one to normally complain) whispered to her that it was not very good at all and was very mushy. The waitress said that she would talk to the manager and see what she could do. My dish by the was (some pork dish) was again very generic and I could just not see any of this being house made. It all tasted like mass produced food. During our wait for the waitress to come back there was a table 2 down from us that had complained about the fish as well. After hearing this we were glad it was not just us complaining about the fish. After a minute the manager (again an older lady) came to our table and said I heard you did not like the fish, what was wrong. Again we explained what was wrong and then she did something that kind of blew us away. She leaned over, put both hands on the edge of our table and told us "well I don't know what to tell you, no one else has complained...well, except them over there" . WOW, we were stunned. No apology, no can I get you another dish, nothing. We didn't ask for anything, just our bill. After seeing us obviously stunned she said, "how about I get you a piece of cake?" At first we said no and the manager just walked away, but we reconsidered after the waitress (still being very nice and obviously embarrassed) asked us again if we would like that cake to go. We got the cake to go, paid the bill (left a normal tip) and left. We got home later that night and tried the cake. Again...very generic. Nothing great about it at all. In fact we didn't even finish it. For a place that made such an effort to tell us that everything was house made, nothing tasted that way at all. If in fact it was all house made, the cooks need to be let go or retrained. Needless to say we will not be back to Alexander's in St Charles. Save your money and try something else.

text: My bf and I adopted two adorable kittens through ACCT/PSPCA over Labor Day weekend, and while we went to the ACCT headquarters for the paperwork, I have now been to the PSPCA headquarters multiple times due to one of our kittens. We decided to adopt a brother and sister who were being fostered by an amazing foster mom, and we wanted to pick them up ASAP after their surgery. I got a call the evening of their scheduled visit from the foster mom telling me that the boy was unable to get his surgery due to an undescended testicle. And so the epic saga began. I was able to 'adopt' him temporarily as a foster myself (since PSPCA doesn't allow you to adopt animals that aren't fixed), and told I had to reschedule his surgery for when he's big enough to handle the surgery. Over a week ago I brought him in at the ungodly hour of 7am to be neutered, and when I arrived that evening to pick him up they told me they COULDN'T FIND the undescended testicle. FML. They explained what they did, that its possible he doesn't have another one but we won't know until I bring him BACK in a month to check if he's developing sexually. They gave me some painkillers for him since he had two major incisions on his belly and he had a plastic collar on so he couldn't reach his incisions (one held together with stitches, the other with glue). The collar ended up being too small and we realized a few days into his recovery that he COULD reach his incisions and was licking them, possibly causing some minor bleeding and maybe beginning to infect himself. We called Jessie, who had left her number in case we had any questions, and made an appointment with her the next morning. She saw me immediately, took a look at his belly herself, then showed it to a surgeon who had operated on him and also one of their primary doctors who had also operated on him. They all agreed it didn't look bad (and that the collar was WAY too small for him), but while the glued incision was healing well the stitched one looked a little infected. They put a larger collar on him, gave me both oral and topical antibiotics, and told me to bring him back in a week to remove the stitches. The best part of all of this treatment is that not only was it all free as part of his neutering surgery (since its technically not done - YET), but both Jessie and Dr. Howard talked to me about him and what they saw and what I could do, answered all my questions, and handled him like he was their pet. These people are wonderful and they do not get enough credit for all the hard work they do, and the GOOD they do on a daily basis. They are an extremely organized place, and CLEAN and MODERN facilities from what I saw. Go and adopt one of the many wonderful animals in need of good homes, and help support the PSPCA's efforts!

If I am in desperate need of a trim again, I shall ask my 5 year old Granddaughter to do it with her paper scissors. I have more faith in her abilities.

text: There are a lot of cheesy salons out there- this is not one of them. Cozy, convenient, clean, personable. text: I love Cuban food and was very excited when I learned that a Cuban restaurant was opening in Chestnut Hill, near where I live in Mt. Airy. Cuba! is very pleasant-- good music, nicely decorated, decent art on the walls. The service was friendly. The food was somewhere between mediocre and terrible-- under seasoned, oversalted. text: I'm updating my review after hosting an obligatory Philly cheesesteak tour. Here are some necessary upgrades: cheese wiz, peppers, fried chili peppers, and salt and pepper (at table). text: I love high end cosmetics as much as anyone and regularly spend thousands. We decided to skip dessert - why give this place more of our money? - but two of our party got the frozen peanut butter pie to share. text: "Living it up while you're going down" If I were gonna shop at any store based on name alone it'd have to be here. My initial thoughts were that a place with a moniker with connotations like the one this conjures can't really be all that bad. Can it? Color me surprised again. I always equate that with the crayola color of "burnt sienna" for some unknown reason. This place does exactly what you would expect from a name like that. Sucks. I think this is someone in corporate America's idea of a lewd joke. Like most anachronistic warehouse stores this one in particular promotes the 3 carnal D's. Dark, dreary and dusty, my shoes depreciated 30% in value by just stepping in the doors. Nothing in the store was even worth looking at! But I went through the motions anyway in order to not seem overly cynical about the whole ordeal. The fresh produce was abysmal and picked over. The butcher was unenthusiastic. The food samples were decent, but they're free so don't they naturally taste better? Barely anything was name brand and the sale prices were laughable. Whole foods has cheaper prices on organic stuff and they're nowhere close to being the type of place this is. It was like a grocery swap meet on crack. By the time I left I realized I'd come in looking to drop at least $200 alone on grocery items, not to mention an untold amount on miscellaneous items that I desperately need for the house. (Anything to avoid the 6th lvl of hell that is Wal-Mart) What I ended up spending was considerably less (22.50 on a shirt and some Prosciutto wrapped Mozzarella) and then had 15% tacked on at the register because I was "just visiting". If this is the way you treat guests I'd hate to see the deals "members" get. In the end this place was a big freaking disappointment. Ugly face, no swallowing, no deep throat, just a bit of teasing around the tip and an ominous feeling of needing to be tested for disease after wards. Worst date in Tampa ever!
label: NEG

text: This place embodies everything I don't want in a bar, EXCEPT a spectacle(hence the second star). text: I don't frequent the Manayunk area too often anymore, and when I did it was more to catch a band at Grape and do a little drinking than for eating. Luckily during an early evening a while back, some friends and I headed over to Le Bus. I remembered it being a pretty decent dining experience, even on a crowded night. Last night I returned to Le Bus for only the second time and I couldn't be happier with the place. It was pretty dead on a Tuesday, so our service was more prompt than I recalled previously. I had a fresh pot of decaf all to myself, which was nice and delicious. My friend and I both ordered the turkey burger, but instead of my usual toppings extravaganza, I decided to just take it as it comes. I have to say, I was more than impressed! The turkey burger itself is ground turkey mixed with celery, spanish onions, shallots, garlic, scallions and peppers. It makes for an extremely tasty burger, even without cheese. (And I love cheese!) And all the extras inside probably are what kept the burger from tasting dried out as so many turkey burgers have the tendency to do. My only regret is that I wasn't more hungry so I could have finished my entire burger and side of sweet potato fries. Some people may think the portions are a bit on the small side, but I actually appreciated the small side of sweet potato fries. It's more in line with what a REAL serving size should be anyway. Overall our experience last night was excellent and I'm glad we happened to be back in the Manayunk area last night so I could have an excuse to enjoy a delicous meal.
label: POS

text: Zeitgenössische Kunst an den Mann und die Frau zu bringen, ist nicht immer einfach. Erleichtert wird der Zugang, wenn die Kunstwerke nicht in einem leblosen Museum ausgestellt werden, sondern sie gut arrangiert in einem wunderschönen Landschaftspark zu bestaunen sind. Grounds for Sculpture bietet aber noch viel mehr als einfaches Betrachten von Kunstobjekten in hübscher (Kunst-) Landschaft: Manch verstecktes Objekt will im Gebüsch entdeckt werden, in den Gebäuden auf dem Gelände finden regelmäßig musikalische Veranstaltungen statt, und ein Restaurant und ein Cafe laden zur Erholung der müden Füße ein. Es fällt mir schwer einzelne Ausstellungsstücke besonders zu würdigen. Im Gedächtnis bleiben aber besonders die Bronzeguss-Kopien J. Seward Johnson's von Manets Déjeuner Sur l'Herbe und Renoirs Luncheon of the Boating Party (siehe Photos). Da kann man tatsächlich in einem Bild herumlaufen Es gibt aber viele viele richtige Schätze zu entdecken. Man kann problemlos einen ganzen Tag auf dem Gelände zubringen. Zwischen den einzelnen Kunstwerken erholt sich das Auge beim Betrachten der Landschaft. Die Website bietet umfassende Informationen über die Sammlung, Sonderausstellungen und das aktuelle Programm.
label: POS

text: Antoine's is a place to which you come solely for the experience. However, the food is not worth the price. In addition, I worked fine-dining in New Orleans and there is a big difference between service that digs at you to feel privileged to be there, and a restaurant that feels privileged to have YOU there. Antoine's is definitely the former. I gotta give an extra star just for the old fashioned experience.

text: Took the summer off from Yelping but I am back! I have been travelling most of the summer and I have lots of good, bad and ugly stuff to Yelp about! First the UGLY! text: This is the place to go if you're completely broke and want to get drunk. All you have to do is get buck naked and sit at the bar: all your drinks will be free. Yes, I'm serious. And yes, people actually do it. Have never witnessed it myself, but know people who have. In case you were wondering: it's almost always guys. So if you're hoping for hot naked Tulane freshmen, I'd wait to find Girls Gone Wild when they're in town, and just follow those dudes around for a while. (You'd be amazed what people will do for a free tshirt. Especially your very conservative freshman year roommate who left that night swearing up and down that she'd never, ever do something like that, yet comes home wearing a GGW tshirt. Or hat. Something along those lines. It's better than beads, I suppose.) So I think I've solved a mystery about Snake 'n Jakes that has been plaguing me for over a year now. At one point, I vividly remember being at Snake 'n Jakes and overheard a conversation between--gasp!--TOURISTS. Now, how the f-ck did a couple of TOURISTS manage to find Snake 'n Jakes? Did it end up in a tour guide or something? It was a mystery to me... Until yesterday, when it hit me: Yelpers. I'd be willing to bet money that Yelp is responsible for revealing Snake 'n Jakes to the world, and the fact that there are reviews dating back to 2007 pretty much proves my theory. Oh well. We're glad you're around, Yelpers. A belated welcome to Snake 'n Jakes. Nice work, Patrick G. of San Francisco. An impressive find, for sure. Whatever made you think it was a good idea to enter that sketchy, magical shack on Oak Street is beyond me. Perhaps you were lost? Or you had local friends? In any event, props to you. My favorite part about Snake 'n Jakes on Yelp: the majority reviews say things like "this is one of the nastiest bars I've ever been in" and "nothing good ever happens [here]" and "Sketchy. Really, that's all." And, of course, these are all 5-star reviews. Classic.
label: POS

text: i know, i know, i'm giving this restaurant my highest possible rating. after a snafu with dinner reservations for new year's eve 2009, my party of four ended up at this brand new, little known, two-week-old restaurant at 13th and sansom (in the heart of the gayborhood). we had a fantastic evening, and i look forward to returning soon! you cannot beat the location of this place! there are a number of restaurants and bars in the area, and it's just blocks away from the EL stop at 13th and market (not to mention market east train station). the staff was EXTREMELY friendly and competent. our waitress checked several times to make sure our food was arriving, our glasses were filled, and we were satisfied. she was present without being overbearing. she was assisted by another server who was energetic and friendly. they even gave us party hats and noise makers to bring in the new year!! the house cocktails were not boring at all...and they were well mixed. i had a mango cardamom sour (made with whiskey). it was amazingly refreshing. not too sweet at all! it was garnished with these incredible macerated tart cherries that added just the right burst of flavor. other people in the party had beer or the blood orange martinis (made with gin). the four of us sampled at least 8 or 9 items from the menu (the entire menu is small plate style for sharing), shared 2 desserts, a bottle of sparkling wine, and each had a cocktail. the bill, including tip, was $60. not bad for new year's eve! i won't detail each item we ate (though i could), but for seafood lovers, i HIGHLY recommend the lobster gyoza (we ordered it twice!). for vegetarians the edamame dumpling is not to be missed. for beef lovers, you MUST get the braised beef short rib satay!! i don't eat beef, but everyone else at the table RAVED over it. it was so tender that it fell off the satay sticks. the chicken satay was just 'ok'. i'm not a fan of gristle in my chicken. some people are..and those people would love the chicken satay. as well, my dessert (chocolate cups filled with a peanut butter mixture) was delightful, but i would have appreciated a tiny dash of sea salt for sweet/salty contrast. these criticisms pale in comparison to how wonderful my experience was. i was mad i didn't have enough room to keep ordering things off the menu!! before leaving, you MUST use one of the individual bathrooms. there is an endless loop of some of the most famous movie quotes of all time. everyone i was with admitted they stayed in the bathroom a few seconds longer than necessary just to hear what came next...
label: POS

text: I'd love nothing more than to heap praise upon this newcomer, after all, I'm a nut for asian, pan-asian, food...in particular thai, and I can literally walk to the restaurant. But my three trips have each ended with one disappointment or another. But predominantly, it's the inconsistency. The first visit was literally their soft opening, so I chalked it up to a learning curve in the kitchen. The second was a week later. And the third was last week. Seems ample opportunity to "get it right". You have to order the ubiquitous pad thai initially right? After all, if they can't do that right you might as well get up and leave then and there. The positive is that it's a pleasing rendition, the negative is that the heat is inconsistent, and in general if you ask for it 'hot' the sauce itself appears the same, instead a heap of hot chilis is simply placed on top. Regardless, the flavor profile itself isn't bad and is recommendable. Another dish worth recommending is their "drunken noodles". In fact, I'd simply say to stick to the noodle dishes and you'll be ok. Protein dishes on the other hand.... the kitchen apparently has inexperienced hands, or inattentive hands, when it comes to gauging doneness. Obliterated meat in the spicy beef salad is one thing, but underdone chicken on *two* visits is quite another, and frankly a serious liability for the owner if it's not corrected. Again though, we found most of the flavors and spices to be generally good, so if the kitchen can get its act together there is some promise. We tend to not be complainers, with the philosophy that we'll simply stop frequented a place if there is something to complain about often enough. On each visit however, without prompting, the owner (mgr?) noticed an uneaten plate of food and inquired as to why that was. Without fail a request was made as to whether or not we'd like to try something else instead. So at least the notion of customer service is alive and well and that tends to go a long way to helping a new restaurant along to success. I hold out hope.
label: NEG

text: Funky Pickle has always felt like a piece of home. In a bar district that's desperate for late-night post-bar munchies venues, Funky Pickle at least partially fills a hole. In Toronto, you can stumble out of a bar and find any number of late-night snack-shacks, pizza-by-the-slice parlors or hot dog vendors ready to fix you up. In Edmonton, it's very difficult to find a pizza joint that sells by the pie piece. In Toronto, it's a given. I miss that. Funky Pickle isn't the best pizza in the world. The closest I've gotten to that is the Wicked Wedge in Calgary and Famoso's Naples-style pizza, which is amazing. But Funky Pickle is very good. The ingredients are fresh, there are lots of great toppings and it's the closest you can get to gourmet pizza at a fast-food establishment. They could take a few tips from Wicked Wedge with their crust. Crust has so much wasted potential. But Wicked Wedge gives sweet E-town just a little more cosmopolitan edge.
label: POS

text: Dear Varga Bar, You are not as cool as you think you are. We were shocked at the lack of happy hour prices, even though your board promises half price for beers during happy hour. (That's a great deal!) We spoke with the "service manager", who could do nothing for us even though her staff did not warn his patrons that Stone's Beers were not included with the happy hour deal. Moreover, Varga Bar, if you can't chill kegs of specialty beer within a three hour span of time, then you shouldn't try to keep a demanding beer week schedule. Also, if the best your service manager can do is exhibited in the Silly Bandz collection on her wrist, then she shouldn't be in charge of speaking with disappointed customers. We don't want her name so we can drop it and get some kind of deal during our next visit. We will not return to this place, even if it is very close to our place of employment. Thanks, but no thanks. text: I'm not going to get hoity-toity on you. None of this "I've visited/lived in/sniffed New York, so I know what 'real pizza' is!" crap. I don't care. DO NOT CARE. What I do care about is that Racanelli's is damn tasty. This, to me, is what pizza is -- a triangle-shaped slice that's light on sauce, heavy on melted cheese, and juuuuust greasy enough. Cheese is where it's at; awesome toppings are a bonus. In my opinion, Racanelli's is the only pizza in the area that delivers on what I want. Now I'm not talking about those pizzas that have dainty asparagus pieces or cheese that's from Uncle Franco's favorite goat or whatever. Those pizzas have their place in the food world, but I eat those too. But when I want just a freaking piece of nummy, straight-up pizza, I head to Racanelli's. The crust is thin and chewy. The sauce has a good balance of sweet with slight tang. The cheese is abundant and MOZZERELLA. Yes, actual cheese. Not provel. And the grease is lovely to look at and have running down your chin. Yes, I know I'm weird -- shut up. Spring is a-coming, and that means I'll be walking the Loop more and more. So when I make my weekly treks to Vintage Vinyl and Star Clipper, I'll be walking with a slice -- or three -- of Racanelli's in hand. (By the way, the pizza still is delicious when it's delivered. I miss living in Skinker-DeBaliviere for this very reason.)

text: Definitely my favorite place in the Santa Barbara Area. I lived in SB for about a year and this is one of my favorite places. Their food is really good and their portions are absolutely huge! Oh and its not cheap guac either, its fresh and chunky and has tomatoes, its very very good. If you go on weekend nights too after 7PM they have live music which is such a refreshing change. They have both inside and outside seating, both of which allow you to enjoy the excellent weather in the Santa Barbara area. I would advise that you make reservations before hand, as this place does get pretty packed, pretty fast. Oh and make sure to arrive early, because unless your willing to walk, their private parking area is part of a strip mall and is very small. Plus the service here is very good too. The first time i went, our waiter was very rude and very unhelpful but since the first time i haven't seen him working there...i hope he doesn't anymore. Everyone i have had since then though, has been more then friendly and helpful. They also have a good selection of wine and alcohol that include margaritas and mojitos. Both of which are very good and worth the price. I will say that the prices in this place could be a little bit lower for my taste, but for the large portions and good service, it is definitely well worth it! Whenever i go back to SB i always make sure to eat here. You definitely cannot miss this place in SB!

text: During a recent road trip, my boyfriend and I stopped here at 11:30am on a Sunday, after some friends in NorCal told us it was not to be missed. True to all other reviews, there was a 15 minute wait - but being huge Yelp fans, we were happy to chill in line since the reviews were so positive. Boy were we disappointed. After all the hype, the food was just so-so. My bf's tri-tip taco was pretty bland, and my pork suizo had an unexpected sweetness to it, and lacked much flavor. I also ordered the alhambre pechuga, which was diced chicken with green peppers, onions, mushrooms on a corn tortilla. Again, nothing very exciting, about as plain as the menu description itself. The lone bright spots were the horchata (mexican rice milk - cold and sweet, served in paper cups with ice), fresh corn tortillas (chewy and soft), and the chorizo. That said, though, given the line and lack-luster cuisine, we won't be coming back here to get our Mexican food fix. Final note, this is my first Yelp review ever - this place was such a far cry from Yelp's usually consistent reviews, I had to speak up! Take it from a true foodie, Super-Rica Taqueria just isn't worth your time.

I honestly never have room for dessert so I have no idea what that tastes like. It CAN be expensive, so just be prepared for that, but food/service is worth it, esp. if you're with good company. text: So many people seem to like this place. Yes, it is all vegan and yes, it is kosher. Which means for people with some religious, dietary, or moral restrictions on diet, they can just about order anything on the menu for once. Don't get me wrong, it's rare that I can do that, too. The prices are reasonable and the dish sizes are generous. Yet I also have to say that just because it's vegan doesn't by any means make it automatically healthy. Most of the dishes I've tried here have been quite oily and very strongly seasoned. Most of the appetizers are deep fried. The one dish that I really do like here is the ginseng soup, which I believe was a special. Be sure to check your take out before you leave. Last time I got take out here, it was a TOTALLY wrong order, nothing in it was anything I had ordered AT ALL. The bottom line is that the food here is really just okay. It's not spectacular and I've definitely had better. That being said, I'm not sure many people have really had gourmet Chinese cooking, the pleasure of which I've been able to experience in my travels around the world. So if you come here expecting the regular Chinese food, but vegetarian, that's what you're going to get here. As for an epicurean adventure, this is definitely not the place to go.

text: All pizza suffers when forced to spend time in a cardboard box, but that mainly effects the crust, and the crust was fine. It was the toppings that didn't please. Three were delivered to a friend's party: a White pizza, a No Cheese, and a Pepperoni/Spinach/Jalapeño. The White lacked seasoning and the texture was mushy and lumpy. A guest commented that it was like eating cottage cheese piled on a pizza crust. The No Cheese was *loaded* with great veggies (a plus), but the seasoning -- although pronounced -- was bland. It was as if, equipped with only a limited palette of seasoning, more was added to compensate for the missing meat and cheese. This happens often with veggie alternatives created and executed by non-vegetarians. The Pepperoni/Spinach/Jalapeño was the best of the lot and the jalapeños packed a whallop. It was quite greasy, a problem I overcame by topping the meaty slice with a slice of the veggie-loaded No Cheese pizza -- creating a kind of Calzone-marriage between vegan and carnivore pizza. The solution tasted great, but need I call upon my ingenuity to eat pizza? Pizza is eaten precisely to avoid having to be clever about meal preparation! Normally I'd offer to give this place another chance, but as of this Sunday morning, I just don't feel like it.
label: NEG

That's a must, because you would be shocked how many waxers disobey that all important rule. Not Lynette though, she is a true professional. She is so nice and friendly, there is no awkwardness whatsoever. Today I got a facial from her for the first time, and I can't tell if I actually slept or was so relaxed I was in a dream-like stupor. Of course, not during the part where she gets out the blackheads, but she did that more gently than other facialists (is that a word?) I've had before. She is just so gentle but thorough, I don't know how she does it. The facial felt catered to my skin's needs, and she discussed my skin so I could understand how to take care of it better. This also included a shoulder massage, hence my dozing off into euphoria... You have to be sure you know where you're going to find her, she's behind Local Honey, a little clothing shop on Linden Ave near Mafiozo's and Rumour's in the trendy 12th South area. Lynette's prices are extremely reasonable, and she'll give you the top treatment in town, no doubt. I haven't tried the masseusse yet who is in the same space, but I want to. text: Terrible service and decent food! Skip this place and head to El Charro! We went to Cafe Poca Cosa for lunch on a Sunday. OUr first impression was the extremely rude hostess who greeted us with a shrug and told us that all of the tables were full (we were well dressed and well-mannered and in a small group of four). When we asked how long the wait would be, she merely replied "I don't know" and offered us a table outside. We accepted, since we were hungry and still willing to overlook her behavior. She then led us through the restaurant, to the second-class seating area where we were cold and alone. As a vegetarian and frequent special orderer, I was appalled. I have been to many restaurants where chefs care deeply, but are more than willing to prepare a special request or merely accomodate dietary preferences. When our food finally arrived, the presentation was fantastic, however, the plates were lacking. The salsa tasted too tomato-y and canned. The vegetarian dish was a basic corn tamale and was over-poweringly sweet. My husband had the fish that day and said it was good. My friend had the chef's platter and was not impressed--the flavors were not complimentary. To top it all, during our meal we were solicited for money THREE times by bums on the street! Needless to say we departed quickly and will not be back again. One can have a MUCH better experiance at El Charro!

text: I came to this location not expecting much. Everything is overpriced except the pizza and the pasta. Our waitress also stressed the point that if you do not like something that they will bring you another entrée with no questions asked and with no hesitation. And, we did not even provoke such a statement, but it is nice to know. The Cherry Limeade ($2.99, no refill) is badass! The best I have ever had. I attempted to avoid all of the cheese covered items, so I ordered the Lettuce Wraps (about $10.00) which were surprisingly good. It would have been better with a better lettuce, instead of cheap snappy iceberg, and if it was $4.00 cheaper. But, live and learn. I also ordered a half salad of the Miso Salad ($11.49 half), which is a glorified coleslaw with 3 diced shrimp and some crab meat on top. The dressing was even sweet like cole slaw and I did not taste any miso at all. I would have been so pissed if this was the only thing that I ordered and actually ordered a full size for $15.00. What a rip-off. My check for just me was $28.00 w/ tip. This experience is very much like eating at Cheesecake Factory, same prices and quality but without the four hour wait. My co-workers ordered a White Pizza and a Mushroom Pizza. Both were exceptional and around $12.00 for a 10 inch. I don't think that I will ever be coming back here, because I do not drive all the way to Tampa to eat pizza. If you do happen to eat here, just order the damn pizza.

text: let's be clear about something: i don't like the 50s. when i think about the vestiges of that chrome cut, lassie-loving, segregated, dolled-up, suburban, blackandwhiteleaveittobeaver, toothpaste hugging, fake-smile-toting fucked up shtick, it generally makes me cringe. yes, this is a generalization. and yes, it's not exactly fair. but hell, like nearly all things bad (stalin, hitler, dave matthews band, tv shoppping channels, malls, orlando, and the like excluded), there is a silver lining. for me, that's a pretty short list, and three of them are actually, literally silver: toasters, airstream, and diners. yes, silk city certainly has a bit of this silver shtick going. but it's a good shtick. and it's shtick with at least a play way from true shtick. and it's also pretty tasty shtick....and there's beer. embracing the best of the 50s shtick, silk city celebrates the diner, the airstream form, and has toasters, meanwhile accessorizing these staples with the following wonderful elements: beautiful waitstaff, a side-bar lounge done up sleek and dark, great bathrooms, great tunes bouncing from motown to beebop to rock, booth seating, and, most importantly, liquor and beer. good beer. like southhampton and troeggs and more on the ol' tap (done up sweet goldchrome style), and the duvel and such standards in the bottle. unexpected and delicious. the food is also pretty kick ass for the price. meeting some friends here for dinner on a swing into town, and trying not to gawk at the service staff too much, we happily devoured some spot-on spice-battered calamari, heaps of fries, unanimously satisfying sandwiches (my beersoaked pulled pork sandwich with mustard and kraut was pretty goddamn huge and amazing), and some of the best wings i've ever had, done up in a cilantro-lemongrass-chile sauce that had me dipping my fries in to soak up the afterburn. for 15 bucks, that's pretty sweet. so sweet in fact, that we came back the next morning for some wake-up coffee, breakfast, and a drink or two. and, of course, to stare and talk shit. sure enough the place was bumping again, but no wait for the counter. so it was easy enough to saunter on up and take down a salmon/goatcheese/arugula omelette, some hash, some pancakes, and some sweet broke yolk before hitting the road. all that was missing was a bit of salt. oh. and that really cute bartender from the night before. anyway, i hope to come back here soon sometime not so far away when i can check in on the biergarten in the works. and make proposals with my eyes....
