text: I went to Tom's last night with a group of friends and family. Most of the people in our party are physicians at Barnes, so we've frequented Tom's for happy hour; but after last night, we will probably NEVER go back. We were drinking at another bar in the CWE when a member of our party called Tom's to ask how long they were taking Karaoke song requests. They said until 1am. We left our bar and arrived at Tom's at 12:45. When we arrived, the staff was far from happy about it. In fact, most of them were blatantly rude. The bartender called "last call" as soon as we walked in. We all ordered one drink. A couple members in our party went to the DJ to put in song requests, but he told them he would not take them. Finally, he let one member in our party sing a song. Another member of our party asked the bar tender for an ashtray, and she rolled her eyes and slid one over. After Karaoke ended, the staff hurried people out of the bar. We finished our drinks (quite quickly) and when we were leaving, one staff member told us to have a good night. The bartender told her coworker, loud enough for us to hear, "DON'T BE NICE TO THEM!" I understand that the staff wants to go home at the end of their shift and are generally annoyed with late-shift customers. I have had waitressing jobs in the past. However, if we call ahead, and someone tells us they are taking song requests until 1am, they should honor that. We would not have made the trip there, if we thought they were CLOSING at 1am. And honestly, I wouldn't be writing this review if it were just a matter of not getting to sing Karaoke (although I think there should be better communication among staff about last song request time); I'm writing this because I have never before been treated so poorly by workers in a restaurant establishment.

text: Yea, I don't exactly get how people could think that the Factory has good sound. It doesn't. And, look, maybe it's just that I haven't been to a lot of other mid-sized rock venue's in other cities -- hell, maybe the Factory is actually one of the better ones for its size. I don't know. But in with my humble rock concert-going experience (most of it acquired right here, in Philly), I can say: I'd rather hear a show at the TLA; I'd rather hear a show at the Troc; I'd rather hear a show at the Khyber; and I'd rather hear a show at the Grape Street Pub. Not that I'm ever blown away by the sound at those places, either. The crowd, of course, always depends on the artist -- it's not like the same crew will role up two nights in a row for Slayer and then Sara McLaughlin (not that I'm judging you, if you're a Slayer/McLaughlin fan.) But when I used to come in from the burbs to go to shows there, I used to find the neighborhood unsettling. And with good reason, I think. No, it's not one of the city's reputedly tough districts, but everything is so dim on the surrounding streets, where tons of concert-going kids are parked, many of them unfamiliar with the city. It has just always seemed to me like their walking targets from muggers. Plus, a lot of the shows bring sketchy peddlers of hash and other goodies. I wouldn't trust those guys, man. You get the feeling that they don't actually have anything to sell but want to drag you off to some alley ("to make the deal") and then mug your unknowing suburban ass off. Be careful.

text: Coney Island is in my mind a quintessential St. Petersburg institution chock full of character and dishing out nostalgia and yummy hot dogs for 80+ years. The ambiance is mid century diner with plenty of stainless steel+white tile, brown and red vinyl stools/booths, a long formica counter, and a plain white menu board that has hardly changed in all those years. Of course the main draw are the hot dogs (always sold in twos) probably followed by the milk-shakes. The dogs maintain a perfect balance between the frank, yellow mustard, raw chopped onions, and chili. However if one thing stands out more than all the rest of the ingredients, and is probably the secret to their success, it is the chili. At first glance it looks like nothing more than just seasoned ground beef, but let me tell you there is something special happening in their big pots of chili. I have many great childhood memories eating here, it always seemed extra special treat when my dad would bring home a brown paper bag of chili dogs after a day of work. It is definitely worth a trip if you are a hot dog aficionado or just want a great trip down memory lane to a simpler time.

They have an incredible selection of sandwiches. Their "regular" hoagies are damn good, but they really excel with the specialty sandwiches. Normally I'm not big on the vegetarian options, but the veggie hoagie, with eggplant, rabe, roasted peppers and share provo is simpy awesome. I'm also a big fan of the Johnny Marz, with tuna and prosciutto, which sounds like a weird combination at first, but is great. The Chicken parm is good, but try the Chicken Fantasia, which adds roast eggplant, and prosciutto. The Chickies special is a perfect combo of Capicolla, Sopressata, and Prosciutto, with roasted peppers and sharp provo. They have some tasty antipasto options, and the obligatory rack of tastykakes and frito lay products. A big plus is they have Hank's sodas in addition to pepsi varieties, so I can satisfy my periodic Wishniak cravings. My only real negatives are that they only stay open until about 3 PM, and are closed on sundays. Even though I live very close, sometimes I don't get there for weeks at a time.

text: It was a dark night - like most nights typically are. Me and my girl were on the prowl for a decent meal with no fuss. Earlier that day I had spotted a little italian spot on Gulf Blvd. We decided to take our chances and try it out - Stefano's Italian Cuisine. At first glance, the place looks small and questionable. Please be advised, you will love this place. The restaurant is small and quaint with your choice of outdoor or indoor seating. Upon entering you will find a small bar, being tended by what I assume is the owner. Hang a right - theres the dining area. The room is decorated in a very unique style, but it all comes together and presents itself as an Italian theme in a wierd way. There are classic movie star framed photographs on the wall, small paintings and other random beach style art you would find in a beach-bum's home. The room is dimmed perfectly for a nice little date, if youre into that kind of thing. The ambient music is a mix of carribean, and italian opera & classical. I utilized my priceless Sound Hound app to capture the sound of Guateque All Stars -- SuperWhirly. My girlfriend thought she knew the artist. I knew she didnt. We sat down in a cozy little private nook towards the back of the dining area and were soon greeted by Brian, our waiter. Nice dude, clean cut. Our drink orders - she had a diet coke; our beer selection were the standard bud light, miller light, bud, etc.... I opted for Peroni, partly because I love that beer, partly to support the recently weakening Euro. We were soon served fresh bread with olive oil with condiments mixed in. The bread was warm, I also remember pointing out that it had nice texture for some reason. The oil dip lacked some taste, but it was nothing that upset me. While we waited for our food I took a closer look at the dining room. Every table has its own unique little style. They each have their own table cloths, table style, and a little lamp. Those tables in the middle were decorated with candles -- all except for one unlucky table. Maybe they ran out. Who knows. Our entrees were served with our choice of soup or salad. The soup choice was beef noodle. We both opted for the salad with house dressing. No disappointment here. The dressing was a creamy italian citrus blend. Very good. Soon after, Brian brought our entrees. She had chicken gorgonzola with broccoli served with penne pasta. We had earlier made a deal to share our food. The chicken gorgonzola had a very good taste. You could taste the freshness in the vegetables. However, the chicken felt chewy as if it was defrosted, then cooked. Regardless, a tasty dish. I went with the spinach ravioli special. This was an excellent dish. It was obvious the pasta was made on-site and the spinach was freshly grown. The pasta was light and did not over-power the dish. This is not the crap they serve at Olive Garden. I highly recommend this dish. After dinner, the gentleman who I assume is the owner came by and asked how everything was. It was a nice finish to the experience. I could see he was genuinely interested and cared about his customers. My one complaint of the night was that they had replaced the restaurant thermostat and failed to re-paint around the old one. FYI - the last coat of paint was an off-white... maybe eggshell. Oh - they charged for a refill on the coke too. Come on... build that into your cost. All in all, Steffano's gets an A++. The extra + is for their catering capabilities for your next corporate event. Why are you still reading this? Go eat at Steffano's.

text: Two parts to this review, the station and Amtrak itself. Station: 1.5 stars. Amtrak Train travel in general: 3.5 stars. I really enjoy taking the train now. It is a new thing for me. Flying for years visiting relatives, although fun when I get there, is almost always torture. Squished together, the lines, check in, re-check in, security check, and now pat down/shoes off/power up laptop, take off jewelery etc.. ad nauseam... Amtrak has none of that nonsense. Advice: I always recommend the business class as it is only 20 bucks more, with the same lousy food naturally (hehe) but the seating is more spacious and comfortable with a lower noise volume which makes the comfort level goes up the scale to 100% in comparing to just regular fare. I have tried coach (LOUD and sometimes Greyhound-sque) & I have tried the lowest level of 2 person suite for travel (less leg room,) and I still prefer the business class. Perks: Business class you have 2 foot rests... one in front of you that you can rest your feet on and a leg/foot rest that props up like a lazyboy chair. You can lean back in your chair without disturbing who is behind you. There are 120V electrical plugs (for coach also) for every seat pairing. Pros/Cons: It is a longer way to travel, by train, but not that much longer if you are going to Chicago or Michigan. Sleeping our way to Michigan, rather then driving through the ice and snow is a blessing. Your luggage does not get searched, you can pack liquids and breakables as you choose, you don't have to take off your shoes, in business class you sit in a different (A LOT less crowded) waiting room. For $20 it is beyond worth the cost. Pros: Your luggage is always with you. You don't have to pack like someone might go through your stuff and you don't have to worry about your lip gloss causing an international incident etc.. If you pack something your big suitcase that is your favorite item, you don't have to worry about a luggage handler/sorter/etc.. lifting it off your hands. Carry that hair gel and in your carry on with no worries. This part is a big deal for me. Through many years of flying and the last few years of having to pack everything trying to keep in mind where to pack valuables (on me,) liquids of any sort (sealed in something and pray it doesn't burst in the suitcase.. oh the horrible memory of ruining a beautiful dress from Hair conditioner. :( etc....) .. THANK GOODNESS all I have to do is pack it up and go to take the train! Cons: Your luggage is always with you. Make sure ALL your luggage rolls or your shoulder bag is VERY light. Trust me. Your shoulders/back will NOT like you if you lug your heavy (or soon to feel that way) luggage around everywhere (thinking of Union Station and trading off to go to another hub.) The station itself: I like the location, as it seems a bit removed from the immediate area's traffic. The people who are working the ticket counter have 10 shades of attitude but they get 10 flavors of crazy going through there and not just mine. ;) (Good crazy is ok :p :D ) The fastfood joint is dirty and I couldn't bring myself to eat there. The chairs are horrible and there are no good places to put your luggage nor yourself for that matter. All sorts of characters walking in and out of there. I feel safe enough but I wouldn't have anyone I care about stay there too long waiting for me to pick them up. Always room for improvement. What's up: Take luggage that has wheels. Your shoulders/back/neck will scream at you if you try to carry bags everywhere. Pay the extra 20 bucks for business class for a much better experience. I love trains now. So stress free compared to driving/flying. Don't tarry at the station. Time your rides to be close to pick up time. I have heard many stories of VERY long waits for taxicabs, be warned. As you can call while you are on the train there is no reason to make people wait at the station for you or vise versa. Have fun! :)

text: I've hit the Red Lion now for drinks once and a separate visit for a whole meal. Overall, this is a pretty solid place. Decor is nice with a red pressed tin ceiling ( I am sucker for these aesthetically), dark wood, a good sized bar, booths and a seating area with tall tables and chairs in front of a projection screen. There are also 2 large screen TVs flanking the bar and if you are lucky like we were and get the right booth, both you and your companion can see each screen to watch the game while conversing; they also pipe in the game audio so it's not just visual and is loud enough to hear but still converse---Awesome. Draft beer is a small but well chosen collection---Thelonius Monk, O'Fallon 5 day and a Hefeweizen, 4 bucks a draft. Domestic bottles are $3.50 and imports $4.50, so reasonable pricing. We started with some wings which were good, fried with a classic butter/Frank's hot sauce sauce. They also have 2 other varieties. For our meal, my companion got the soft cheddar burger with a beef, pork, lamb patty which was very tasty and cooked to a true medium rare. I got the lamb burger medium which was well cooked and mighty tasty; it is extraordinarily rare for me to eat a burger without ketchup (I am addicted, I blame public school lunches in the 80's--hey it's a veggie!) but I did not put a drop on this. Sweet potato fries were crisp and flavorful and not dried out. Yum. We went crazy (hey, the Rams were winning!) and got dessert too---ordered the deep fried twinkie and ice cream. They were out of plain ice cream and subbed another dessert which is ice cream rolled in crushed oreos and fudge. The twinkie was extremely overly breaded (served with a nice berry sauce) but the ice cream balls were nice. Service was good overall and we were not rushed (my peeve), impressive given our waiter was the bartender who was negotiating a full bar and about 3-4 booths on top of that. I would not go here to enjoy super fancy drinks or groundbreaking mixology, but they make a competent Manhattan. If you are into it, they prominently display a lot of flavored vodkas. Wish they had more draft selections. We will be back, awesome game day destination.

text: The Arch is quite an experience. It just looks kinda cool from afar, but when you get up close it's really impressive. You just don't see the magnitude until you're at the base. A warning: the tram you ride up in is very small and a bit rickety. Once you get to the top, though, the ride is worth it. The St. Louis skyline itself itsn't all that exciting to look at (unless you've lived there & know what all the buildings are) nor is East St. Louis, but it's just cool to be 630 feet up in the air looking down at everything. One time I went up in the Arch, it had snowed outside so everything was covered in white - it was quite pretty. The most recent time I went up, it was a very clear day with blue skies and we had a great aerial view of the brand-new Busch Stadium. The museum underneath the Arch is kind of neat, and it's free, so check it out while you're there. You can also get tickets to a movie about the Arch construction and for a riverboat ride down the Mississippi, but I haven't experienced either of those attractions yet. If you're visiting St. Louis, the Arch should be on your agenda. You won't forget it.

text: This place was intriguing. It fits about 8-10 people depending on the size of the groups. All it really consists of is a sushi bar with about 10 stools. I went in thinking that was actually kind of cool so for me that was a plus not really a minus. When we got there the bar was full but it really only took like 15-20 minutes to get a couple of seats. This is no longer than a wait (without a reservation) at like a normal sushi restaurant on a Saturday night right around prime-time would probably be anyway, so that was fine. Let me get starting by talking about the only thing that stopped me from giving this place a 5/5. The ordering process. Yes the place is small, and yes I guess if I had too big of a problem with it I don't have to go, but the place is so good that I would go again even because of this. I don't find it very appealing that you have to order like right in front of the entire bar, and almost scream it over the bar for the lady to hear you. It's kind of a privacy breach and it makes you feel a little awkward when you want to order a lot to (which at this please is very easy to do.) That having been said, everything else was fantastic. The sushi came out super quick and everything was super fresh. It would be nice if they could give you cold glasses of water for free instead of having to get a couple water bottles out of the fridge, but they do provide free hot green tea, which I guess is good enough. The sushi was probably the best sushi I have ever had in my life for the price. For an appetizer we got the spicy tuna tar-tar. It was really good. Not the best thing I have ever eaten but it was really tasty. We each got a 3-roll special. 3 rolls for $10.95. Any 3 non-special rolls from the menu are allowed. All together we got the eel roll, yellow tail-scallion, spicy tuna, shrimp tempura, Alaska, and I believe spicy salmon but I could be wrong. Every roll was incredible. The fish was unbelievably fresh and tasty, presented well, neat, and quickly. For that price you definitely cannot beat it. They give you kind of small amounts of wasabi and ginger and they charge you $.50 for extra, but we didn't need any (although I can see some people getting a little upset over this.) Overall you can see the little things I have mentioned that have kept this place from getting a perfect score, but it's real close to perfection. Little subtraction on the environment, non-free water, and the condiments, but other than that top notch sushi for a very affordable price. Our entire dinner (appetizer, 6 rolls, two drinks), was under $40 including tip. Can't beat that. By the way it's BYOB! I would definitely go back anytime.

text: Ok, I know it sounds more than a bit strident and maybe I sound more than a bit mental, but I'm extremely accurate and have been eating at places like this for over 40 years. Here's a copy of what I just sent to Potbelly corporate: This was my first visit to a Potbelly...and, unless there are drastic changes, my last. Just reading the "Our story" and "Our food" sections of the web site tells me all I need to know. In the past, there may have been an original store that was famous for great sandwiches. Then during the franchise process, a board room meeting where accolades are heaped upon the company about "how wonderful we are" and "how amazing our food is". No one has the nerve to ask if it';s true. It isn't. As soon as I opened my turkey and Swiss sandwich, I could see in an instant and before discovering that they not-at-all-busy sandwich maker was too busy talking to actually include any Swiss cheese, that the turkey was "jelly turkey", which is the lowest quality formed turkey breast available. It's translucent, watery texture is visible from across a room. This has absolutely nothing to do with whatever quality sandwiches began the franchise and everything to do with placing price above quality by someone who has zero connection to the food. If you don't think that food quality plays a big part in the restaurant business, then doom is waiting for you. For another $.50, the company could use at least passable turkey. Also, I was deeply surprised by the dearth of choices on the menu. I thought that a store specializing in sandwiches would have...special sandwiches. The options on the menu are so basic, it's a joke. Mayo or mustard? What is this, 1952? Where are different flavored sauces, edgy mustards, horseradish or barbecue sauce, wasabi mayonnaise. Where are sweet peppers, bacon, grilled onions and mushrooms...nothing! Is that them, hidden in the "extras" banner? This is Philadelphia, where we know sandwiches. Jelly turkey is a tip off that nothing on the menu is prepared with pride, but only an unblinking eye on costs. Well, that attitude just cost you a customer.

text: My high school aged son had warned me that the word in school was Paoli Diner was no good. But I had visited it once with an out of town friend for a Sunday breakfast a couple months after it had first opened, and found a busy diner with the service faultless and the food ( an omlet with toast and pancakes) acceptable. So I differed with him But my second visit today fulfilled my son's warning. I guess a nearly empty parking lot and the fact that only a handful of the tables were busy at 10AM on a Sunday morning was a hint of what to expect. And although most of the tables by the bright, cheery windows were available, the hostess seated us next to the biggest party in the room and a table waiting to be bussed, buried in the dark middle of the restaurant. She gave us our menus, and said our waitress will be with us shortly. We waited. And we waited. The dirty table next to us was cleared. The hostess took our fully examined menus. Finally, our waitress arrived, and was confused that we didn't have menus. We placed our simple orders, and she was gone in 20 seconds. Eggs Benedict and OJ, omlet and toast with coffee. Home fries with both. No questions from the waitress regarding the type of toast (whole wheat, white, rye?), or the type of coffee (decaf?). The drinks arrive, and in a timely manner, the food does too. It looks fine. As I touched my plate with a fork to grab a bite of home fries, one of my poached eggs for the Benedict break - other than a thin layer of cooked white skin on the outside, it's raw. It oozed all over the plate. I take a bite of my potato, and that's what I taste - potato. No onion, Not even salt or papper. Just mushy lumps of potato, with a bit of a griddle-browned crust. I taste my eggs. The english muffin is toasted well, the canadian bacon is warm, but the eggs are beyond soft, (I like soft eggs) and the hollandaise is gooey, thick and flavorless. My companion's potato's were the same as mine, her omlet hard and uninviting. and the toast - well, she didn't touch the white toast. In five minutes, my plate was clear, my companion's was still half full, but she was done. Our waitress arrived, and offered to bring the check. Never asked how our meal was, or if we needed a drink refill... Fine. We were ready to leave. We take our check to the front counter, and I hand my 20 over to a silent hostess. Not a word. The only words were muttered by me. I play both roles... "How was everything today?" "Just OK, actually..." "Well thanks for coming - have a nice day..." "You too." There are many other dining options in the area - use them. If this is your only option, just eat at home.

text: Walking into the Jerk Hut it looks like you'd expect, a faux hut with some wooden tables, fake plants and reggae music on the speakers. The drink specials were great on the wallet, $6 pitchers and $3 shots of tequila. There was one bartender waiting tables and slinging drinks though, so the more this place filled up, the longer you had to wait for your beverage. The food was sub par at best. I've been to Jamaica so that probably hurt it's standings right out the gate, but even if I hadn't had the real thing it would still be getting the "meh" rating. We had the beef pattys, curry chicken, roti, rice and Jamaican bread. The beef pattys had decent flavor with a little back heat but didn't taste much different than a frozen patty you'd get from a freezer section of a grocery store. The rice was alright. The roti tasted like a quesadilla and is an Indian dish, so I'm not sure why it was on the menu to begin with. Now it takes a lot for me to not eat something on my plate, but the curry chicken was AWFUL! It tasted like I was eating fat covered in a lazily made, flavorless curry. Thumbs down, waaaay down. The Jamaican bread was good, thick and sweet, but no one goes to a restaurant just for bread... that's what a bakery is for. Let me sum up by saying, my meal was free because I was there for a meeting and there is no way I would eat here a second time unless it was again, free.

All the food is fresh, tasty, and served piping hot. For such a cramped place with huge crowds, especially weekends and most the college kids from University City, who will have a difficult time now that the South St. bridge will be closed for years to come for a new bridge. So they will have to detour across Walnut to get to the Ants Pants but it's worth the hike. Even just the simple eggs and toast has a kick that really is the ants in the pants. The only Aussie-based foods that you'll find here are two items. 1. Vegemite- a peanut butter-like spread that is used on mainly toast along with butter. Sometimes you'll find vegemite mixed with butter but a true Aussie puts puts butter first followed by the vegemite. 2. Iced Coa Coa Milk- Basically it's a glass of chocolate milk but with ice and a scoop of sweet vanilla ice cream, close to a milk shake but presented differently and just as delicious, if not even better. Well there you have it! You won't leave with ants in your pants but you will leave with a satisfied grin.

text: ... and here, I'm guessing, is how enemies are made. Pat's- I really wanted to like your steaks- no- I wanted to LOVE your steaks. As someone who grew up in the Philadelphia metro area eating delicious gooey cheesesteaks from the likes of Real Pizza in Wayne, etc., I've been traveling the world for the last 13 years proselytizing our city's primary culinary export, bitching about airport restaurants that claim to offer "Philadelphia Cheesesteaks," and spreading the word about Amoroso's rolls to all who would listen. I had never been to Pat's Steaks and, honestly, I thought I was just saving the best for last. In San Francisco, I got my wife hooked on the Cheese Steak Shop on Divisidero, so when we got to Philly, we were both primed and ready to dive into Pat's (Geno's is not and will not be an option for us given their English-speaking only stance for their customers. Call it racism or xenophobia, I call it just plain sad and mean-spirited, especially since they're adjacent to a Mexican food restaurant. Aren't business owners supposed to be inclusive as a profit-maximizing strategy? Anyway, back to the review). So we fight our way down the sidewalk past the neon abomination known as Geno's and see Pat's looking as Philly as Philly can be. We order at the steak window (no chicken cheesesteaks for the wife, it would seem), then head over to the soda and fries window (annoying rigmarole) to get birch beer (why hasn't this PA treat made it out of the state???). I was so hungry I horked my steak down, but completely without relish. In my mind, one of the things that makes a great cheesesteak is that all of the ingredients are jumbled up together because the chef has taken the time to chop it all together on the grill. At Pat's, they take the roll, layer on the cheese (provolone, in my case), then put on the meat and finally top it off with grilled onions. Separate but equal? I think not. The roll was huge, the steak ended up being pretty dry (since it wasn't slathered in gooey cheese), and the whole concoction just sort of slid, slowly, down my gullet like a fat, dry-meat watermelon. Where was the flavor? Sad. Pat's. We could have been so good together, but you're just not for me. I'm leaving you for Jim's on South Street who, if I remember correctly, knows how to do gooey cheesesteaky goodness. Disappointing.
label: NEG

text: If I were cool I would wear my sunglasses inside at night, in a crowded bar while listening to bad house jams. No really, thats what I would do . . . Psych Honestly, I'm pretty surprised to see how many gave the g spot a relatively solid review. Well to each his own, and if you are one of the members of the elite class of boozehounds who loves this spot, far be it for me to judge. Here are the highlights as I see 'em. Philly has a lot to offer in the realm of dive bars and shadowy gin joints. Some are cool, some are not. What this city's night life scene seems to lack is a great lounge and G tries to fill that gap. Albeit I'm new here, I call it like I see it. Lets be honest, sometimes we all like to go out and spend it like we got it . . . or at least I do, maybe that makes me weird, but hey, thats what I'm into. The problem with G lounge is that it has all the pretentiousness of a SOHO banger with none of the class. There is VIP bottle service. Its overpriced. There is a dress code. It makes the crowd seem somewhat contrived, as if just crammed into their latest swag simply to fit the part. Frankly, you shouldn't have to force people to look slick. Your spot should do that for you. I also got a good chuckle out of the fact that just throwing on a untucked collared shirt counts a classing-it-up for the evening. I will say the girls, many of whom spent some quality time dancing on top of one table or another, were consistently smoking. Dimes, top of the line, cute face, little waist and a big behind. However, I'm a sucker for skin tight dresses and high heel shoes. Who isn't right? But I digress . . . There is a DJ. I've been there a handful of times now and the MC has never put the place on its feet, there are far better places in this City for a party. The decor is fine. The doormen are quite content to make let you stand outside for a while, only to arrive indoors to find the club relatively empty - I suspect this is just a trick to make passer-bys see the line and go "Whoa, that place must be cool." Bottom line, go for the ladies, but not the scene. I'll be elsewhere.

text: If my car was an human being and these people were doctors, then I would no other person taking care of my car at this point. Let me tell ya as a gal with an old old car, it's hard to find good/honest/affordable mechanic. I've gone to a few places in philly. One (starts with a B..ends with a T...and they sell tires) tend to give the glamour treatment and charge $$$$ for their glamour service. They seem to be in the money making business.PLUS I've been there several times and the manager looks at me like he's never seen me before each time!!! Another place was recommend which is mom and pop (11th street is the location) and the are pretty reliable and honest people but just too far for me to get to...being there once and had good times there also. I was referred to Monte's by a friend after my car overheated this summer. So I went to monte's. First of all, just my calling them on the phone dude already asked for my first name...really friendly down to earth. I trusted this guy already. I got the impression he cared about "me" and "my car". I don't care what he was selling, I'm buying twice! The shop is not expansive. Again, really friend warm staff. I explained the situation. We talked about the possibilities before I left the keys so they can do their diagnostic thang. they gave me a ride back home. I paid the price for the parts and the labor was not expensive at all and job was done pretty quickly. They knew my car was OLD, still had some juice left in it, and that I depended on it. I get sentimental about my baby...he has served me well. So i appreciate a mechanic that understands that tho it's an old car..it's all I have. And they actually know what they are talking about (car wise). After they fixed it, I was encouraged to bring it back for weekly checks (at no additional cost) for a month just to make sure there was no hidden internal damage from the overheating episode. Then my gas door broke off (I tell ya my car is olddd). Well I took it Monte's and I appreciate that FIRST he tried to get used parts. I mean, some mechanics don't even attempt to get used parts. I'm not saying used parts are the way to go all the time but if it's not the engine (and with a car as old as mine) there is no point in getting fancy new parts. If it's an engine issue then by all means call the manufacturer, but for random parts and pipes...just get used or generic parts and keep it moving. The labor was cheap esp considered that he did some minor fixups to the car that I didn't even ask for. PLUS encouraged me to bring it in monthly & he'll help me check it up emphasizing that I rely on this car (which I SERIOUSLY DOOO) and so i need to make sure certain things are up to snuff. This shop has a very mom and pop feel. It's a family owned business. Again, they know your first name. They speak to you like you are someone they actually care about. it's a business but they such great personality. Again, if you were to have a doctor for your car, then I'd recommend this shop. Some dude with a US Airways badge takes our passports away. Feel a bit uneasy. 2. Dude returns, mentions something called an ESTA form. Tells us we might not be allowed into America when we arrive. Go online in a panic and fill in the ESTA form (more later for those of you now worried). Feel a bit better. 5. Get on 'plane. One screen per cabin. Feel a bit annoyed. Should we have taken the upgrade? 6. Girl comes round and thanks to her IQ of 60 it takes 10 minutes to work out that I want a vegan meal. It's not difficult! 7. 'Plane takes off. No drink for two hours. 8. Girl comes round with headphones for the ONE MOVIE on the 7 hour flight. Oh, and they are $5. And the screen's crap so the picture flickers every two minutes. Really? 9. Food comes round. Still want to give me chicken. No! Might as well have been. Lukewarm rice and tomato tastes rubbish. 10. Get to Philly. Circle for an hour. Come on! 11. Land. Wait for half an hour in the rain. Are you kidding me? 12. Get off a US Airways 'plane for the penultimate time. Now I'm hoping no-one from said airline reads this before my last flight with them, my journey home next week. So.. this ESTA nonsense: It's basically a good idea that the US have introduced. It's a form which acts as a visa waiver and you fill it in online. It came in in January 2009 so if you've been to the States since than and haven't filled in an ESTA, you're on dodgy ground - fill one in asap. text: Flowing Well is an 18-acre oasis that sits on the north side of 116th Street, midway between the center of Carmel and the center of Fishers. This park is something of a well-kept secret (not as much so if you live in the immediate vicinity), which is unfortunate because it is so peaceful and shady here. One thing I like about this park is that it has retained much of the mature tree growth rather than having been cleared to make playgrounds, prairies and the like. On a hot day, this is still a nice place to be outside. The park offers fishing, picnic shelters and walking trails - some of the trail path is even paved, making it accessible to just about anybody. However, the thing that makes this park truly unique among the Carmel-Clay Parks & Recreation family is the flowing well for which it is named. A flowing artesian well is the highlight here and people come from miles around to fill jugs and bottles with the cool, refreshing water that bubbles up from an aquifer below the park grounds. The well was actually discovered by accident during a natural gas drilling expedition in the early 1900s. Rather than gas, the crew found the underground aquifer, which apparently created a small geyser when it was tapped into. The result all these years later: Carmel's very own public flowing well. One of the best ways to enjoy this park is to take your empty water bottle with you, fill it up at the well - which is conveniently situated at the park's entrance - and then take a hike on the trails. You'll enjoy beautiful foliage, flowers and Cool Creek along the way, as well as, that delicious FREE spring water! BTW: while dogs are welcome at the park - on a leash of course - they may not drink directly from the flowing well spigots so be sure to bring a small tupperware or other water dish for your four-legged companion :-)

text: We visit White Dog Cafe only about once a year, but have been a fan for more than two decades. But our recent visit will be the last unless I hear that significant changes have been made. First, I was surprised by a couple of items on the menu. Knowing Ms. Wicks' commitment to healthy and sustainable food, wild striped bass appears to be an inappropriate contradiction. The DEP warns that consumption of this fish should be limited to a maximum of 4 servings per year for most people while pregnant women and other high risk individuals should avoid eating this fish altogether. Wild striper is heavily contaminated with cancer-causing dioxin and PCBs. Considering the ready supply of healthy and sustainable farm-raised striped bass as a suitable alternative, why would any knowledgeable diner want to pay for the wild toxin-laden fish? Food that comes with a safety warning is simply not something I would expect at White Dog Café. The same comments apply to the tuna appetizer. Environmentally conscious diners simply do not eat tuna anymore, especially the ahi type, because it is an unsustainable food under severe environmental pressure. Health concerns about mercury levels in tuna are also well documented. (I suggest the book Bottomfeeder and the NJ DEP Web site for more information on seafood safety. One bad mussel in the appetizer undetected by the kitchen gave the entire dish an unpleasant smell and unfortunately I did not detect the bad one until I bit into it and had to spit it out. (Anyone who has eaten a bad mussel knows what I mean). The sauce was the most bland I have ever had on this dish. A restaurant serving mussels, especially in the summer when more shellfish die in transit, needs to be more careful about inspecting each mussel before cooking. My wife's broiled scallops were delicious, but the vegetables on the dish were completely bland. It doesn't take much effort to make vegetables taste great, but these just didn't make the grade. Most disappointing was the $7 bacon & cheese risotto. The bacon and cheese completely overpowered the dish so that I couldn't even finish. Again, it is not difficult to create a great taste with these basic ingredients, so it is surprising that the kitchen managed to find a way to make it almost inedible. The best dish this night was the beet salad. The beets were well prepared with a great dressing and the portion was generous. We opted for glasses of wine because the bottles were a bit over our budget. Given the $120 price for dinner for two, I expected more.

I got the medium (2nd level) and yes it did have enough kick. So go easy on the spice level. Lunch was served on porcelain plates with stainless steel utensils, with drinks in a glass tumbler. Food quality was 5-star. Ambience, cleanliness, service, value are 4 star, and worthy of toney Castleton. Lunch prices are reasonable for the quality. Their dinner (supper) prices are a little on the high side. Even so, the food quality seems to justify it. Staff is from Thailand. The menus on their web site are exact replicas (PDF) of their actual menu so you can check that out before you go. This is a nice place to impress the boss/gf/wife/inlaws. They are located on the South side of East 82nd street, corner of Bash. That's 2 stop lights West of I-69. Turn at the Speedway gas station. Their sign is pretty big, so you can see it from 82nd street. This place is larger, more elegant, and less homey than Thai Taste at the other end of Castleton. The waitresses are cute here. The food is about the same, or perhaps just a tad better. Both are worthy of patronage.

text: I was taken aback when going into Maggianos last weekend. Much fancier than I expected and felt totally underdressed. I would have preferred normal portions for a cheaper price but I like taking home leftovers so whatever. The food was tasty, but if you want the real Italian experience I would recommend the Hill. One of my favorite things when going for Italian is dipping bread in Olive Oil with Parmesan cheese. The bread came out crispy on the edges and warm and soft in the inside. Dipped in the olive oil, it was a delicious combo. We also ordered an appetizer mussels, diablo style, which came in a garlic tomato sauce. The mussels were good but nothing extraordinary. I would pass next time. Stopped early on the appetizers and bread to save room for my massive entree, the mushroom and veal ravioli. They came 5 large raviolis to half order and were covered in a white creamy sauce with sundried tomatoes. The ravioli was ok, I was looking for more flavor in the filling, kind of bland overall and so I made sure to include the sauce in every bite. My friend ordered the chicken tortellini special which he claimed was really good. We split an order of the side spinach. Just the right texture and seasoned wonderfully, I liked the spinach better than my entree. I know I need to try more on the menu, but I'm not sure I would bother to come back. So many other places to try. The desserts I saw made my mouth water so if anything coming back for coffee and dessert might be an option!

text: Why is this place in business? An overpriced abortion of what might have been a unique local business. Grotesque food and with operating hours which leave many of what few customers they have scratching their heads at the locked doors. Some of the most unpleasant, un-fresh food I have ever tasted in my life, and this is after two tries. Nothing about this place is remotely Cajun; I say that as a bonafide Cajun myself, born and raised in the Acadiana region of (south) Louisiana. An example of two of their menu items are things called "Jack Daniels Chicken" and "Tortellini de la Casa". HUH? Come again? Their "Chicken & Shrimp Creole" is some confused mishmosh slop with stale, dried chicken bits and what appear to be Chinese shrimp with one or two whole crawfish which appear to have been laying out on the counter for hours; the food equivalent of multiple personality disorder. Reading their website, the owner decided on the name of the place from an old 1980s movie. Well, might as well since judging from the food and the business model, he has never worked in, lived near nor had the pleasure of enjoying the food of Louisiana or any restaurant with normal business hours and good food. What's most annoying about this place are the hours. The website will tell you they're open from about noon through 1a.m.. However, it took us THREE attempts to eat at this place before we could ever discover it opened. A truly horrible experience not for the serious or casual diner or even those dieing from starvation. Poor focus on maintaining customer trust. The owner needs to shutter the place or sell it off before he embarrasses himself or his family even more. You're better off eating rock undergrowth down by the river.

text: I can't believe no one has reviewed this awesome sandwich place. It's been open almost a year. City Market is a side project of the woman who owns Cafe Galleria on S Main. Their tag line is "Where the dedicated vegan and unapologetic carnivore can eat together in harmony" or something like that. In other words, they are very vegan friendly but I still love them. Aside from fresh deli sandwiches, hot breakfast items, panninis, quiches, salads and soups they sell a few specialty grocery items like dry pasta, sauces, a few stir fry supplies, basic milk, eggs, cheese, fruit AND Pirate's Booty, my favorite snack ever. They're also very reasonably priced, deliver on weekdays, make a decent cappuccino and have fabulous pastries in the am- I mean the best croissants I've had since I was in Paris, baked on premises an hour ago. Go EARLY- they sell out quick. Best Part: The Super Italian: Prosciutto, sopressatta, cappy ham, provolone and whatever else you like. Or for the vegans, The 'Lil Debbie: a bunch of green stuff I don't like and hummus on a pita. My vegan friend says it's good. Also, lots of nice semi-locally bottled drinks- MASH and Boylan's Pure Cane Sodas, in addition to the usual Coke and OJ. Other Best Part: I LOVE that they slice the meat/cheese to order for each sandwich, not ahead of time. I hate going to Subway and imagining how long that slice of swiss has been sitting around. Worst Part: Lunchtime on weekends is pretty crazy. I recommend sitting at the counter with a friend or a book in case your order takes a few minutes. The seats are rarely full, most people take out. Service is very friendly, but occasionally a bit slow. There are only a few people there who have any experience. The place is still pretty new, so they're working out the kinks. The sandwiches are worth the wait.

text: The last time we went to Sammy's was a HUGE disappointment. A couple of us recommended it to our group as it was amazing the last time we'd been there, but I am sorry we went. Heading over to Sammy's after deciding that was where we were going to go, the usual friendly and eager face outside their door with menus was beckoning us in. "Don't worry, we're already headed your way," I said. Our group seated, we all order. The food came out fairly quickly, and the meal itself lasted about that long, too. I felt like just as soon as we were seated and given our meals, they were being taken away before we were even done. Why bother beckoning with a smile if you know you're going to kick us out soon after? Trying to make that last dollar before closing-time is understandable. Especially since businesses were still hurting after Katrina (it really was taking a while for some to get back on their feet), but whisking us away the way they did lost them business. They just didn't care. The food wasn't as great as I remembered either, but I'm not sure if it was because it was rushed in the making, or if the experience was making the food seem worse than it was. Either way, I know none of us were really happy with that meal. Sorry, Sammy's. There are just too many other spectacular places in New Orleans to even contemplate giving you another try.

text: I usually don't give a negative review without trying a location twice which I did at Luke. I ordered the pressed couchon sandwich which was warmish in the outside with cold guts. My mates had the rib-eye which was not appropriately charred which led to a big pile of mushy fat left on his plate. A Luke burger and the couchon special rounded out the foursome. Yawn. text: Really good Halloween dinner here. With advance reservations, we were able to secure a lovely dinner for 10. This means I got to try LOTS AND LOTS of things. It started off with a cajun martini, which was such a unique and spicy drink. They have jalapeño infused house-made vodka, garnished with pepper slices and other treats. It really made me cough a lil,because Ive never had a spicy alcohol drink, but this was great. Next were the buffalo style frog legs, accompanied by HUGE house made onion rings. The legs were great, though they are not for the squeamish, esp if you like frogs. They look very leg like, as opposed to chicken wings, for example, and you can easily make out the little webbed feet. You've been warned vegetarians. For the main event, I had the blackened drum. Apparently the chef won the Iron Chef with this dish and I can see why. The drum fish (white, flaky, fluffy, great cut) is pressed with a delicious mix of cajun spices and is really infused with the flavors. The result is an outstandingly tender filet, with a perfect mix of spice and flavors, served under cajun butter. there's a roasted vegetable rataouille on the side, which is nothing out of this world, but a great accompaniment. The final step is a creamy mashed potatoes which soaks up the spicy butter perfectly. TRY THIS DISH. Dessert was a panoply; the chocolate molten cake was a halloween special, so you will not find it, but try is cousin if you can. The best was the bread pudding, YOU MUST have this, it's absolutely amazing.

text: Before telling Thai Lotus' "story," let me first say that the food is excellent and the service is great. My wife and I have spent time in Thailand and we can say that this is authentic Thai food. I've eaten most items on the menu and they've ranged from quite good to exceptionally excellent. Also, unlike some Thai restaurants, they always ask how spicy you want it - we advise "2" or "3" on a 1-5 scale unless you're a very experienced Thai food gourmet... and have a very strong digestive system. I've been going to Thai Lotus since 2004 - during that time it's gone through three ownerships. Earlier, the food was good, but the ambiance was "tacky fast food" in nature. When the current owners, Jen and Sitt (young wife and husband) moved here from Thailand and bought it in 2007, things started changing immediately. The food, always good, has improved to "excellent." It is now very attractive inside and the staffing has improved significantly - you usually get your water within seconds and your order is taken promptly... which is quite impressive, as the restaurant has gone from mostly empty during lunch to usually full. The lunch "specials" menu has more than tripled and many additional dinner items have been added. All the lunch specials are very good. There used to be about six or so reasonably-priced lunch specials. Now the list approaches 20 or so. The regular menu is very large. A real dinner favorite of mine is the Green Papaya Salad, which is a large and delicious meal and a bargain at about $10. The Seafood Salad, just two or three dollars more, is loaded with squid, octopus, fish chunks, scallops, clams, and more - mixed with vegetables and Asian "sweet vinegar" for extra taste. All the soups are fantastic. The noodle dishes are great. There are pages more of other dishes. I used to eat at Thai Lotus occasionally before Jen & Oat bought it... it was just plain ugly. Now it's a small "bistro" feeling and very elegant place with excellent food and quick, friendly service. Now I eat there at least once a week... once, I ate there five times in one week! My wife and I just ate there again tonight and had one of the "sizzling" Chef Specials along with a Larb Gai salad - what a treat!

text: The best food I ate last time I was in town although, admittedly, I otherwise ate mainly crap to soak up the booze. This was my one excellent meal though! I recommend the rabbit and sausage jambalaya. The best ever! Damn! Also, the creole fried chicken -- I think this is what Popeye's was supposed to be like. You should never really get gumbo or red beans at a restaurant, but Coop's does 'em both right...pleasantly surprised. Good drinks to booze up the soak too. Highly recommended. I forgot to mention -- they also have a cat and picture of Professor Longhair on the wall so ambience is thumbs up.
label: POS

text: Worst airport food concessions in America. Dried out hot dogs and a pot of Perpetual Nacho Cheese. Mmmmm! Disgusting bathrooms. Walls covered with strip club ads. White people who've turned gray from chain-smoking. If ever an airport was in need of a makeover, this is the one.

text: Old Red Room: PBR in a can, punk palace, Nintendo in the back, total dive. New Red Room: What? It's all clean and weird in there. What happened?

text: For all the hype that this place (and Geno's across the street) gets, the experience is exactly the opposite. In fact, I wish yelp allowed zero stars, because this place sucks so bad, I threw away my cheesesteak after 3 bites. And I suffered through all of them . . . I should have heeded the bad reviews I read on Yelp . . . especially the one that said that Pat's can suck a dick. I really can't sum it up any better than that. The sandwich was cold, the meat was dry, there was no cheese, and the stupid ordering system is, well . . . . stupid. Save yourself the trip and go elsewhere. I don't know where in Philly to get a really good cheesesteak, but this is not the place.
label: NEG

text: Finally got to try this place tonight...I really liked it! Very cozy, laid back atmosphere. A few small groups chatting, people reading, etc. Friendly bartenders. TV's in the corners, which seemed a bit out of place actually. There was a jukebox that didn't seem to have power...I'd much rather make music the focus here than a hockey game. Thats my main issue but it doesn't kill the place by any means. Beer was of course unique and the one I had (Royal Amber I believe?) was delicious. Definitely want to check out their other offerings (around 6-7 or so in all. Maybe more). They also had several wines but I didn't look into that at all. I wanted something basic and quick to eat so I got a chicken salad wrap. It was decent, but I've certainly had better (and cheaper) elsewhere. Nothing wrong with it, so maybe its just not their thing. I'll try something else next time I go. This is a nice little place tucked into the area...I will make it a stop before shows at the Keswick from now on.
label: POS

text: My roommate described our love/hate relationship with SEPTA better than I ever could... "If I saw the 38 bus being gang-raped and left for dead on the side of the Benjamin Franklin Parkway, I would just laugh..." SEPTA never ceases to disappoint me. Just when I think it couldn't get any worse, the bus that is scheduled to come every 40 minutes just doesn't show up, leaving me standing in some of the not so nice neighborhoods in West Philly at night for an hour and a half, just waiting to be mugged.... Because you just never know; the bus could be late, it could be early, or it could not come at all... Although I'm being overly generous, one star goes for having a direct train line from the airport to the city that actually manages to run reasonably well. I award the other star for SEPTA's self awareness. They may not care that they are a sh*tty public transportation service, but they do acknowledge it, which is more than I can say for other public works in this city...
label: NEG

text: If I could have rated this place a 2.5, I would have. This place was definitely disappointing. The service was mediocre and the food was not worth the price. We were promptly seated upon arrival. Service was slow in the beginning as we sat for awhile between our drink order and our meal ordering. My boyfriend requested to have pasta in replace of his potatoes, in which they couldn't accommodate. Nice restaurants should always please the customer. The most disappointing part of the meal, however, was the mediocre (at best) food for the outrageous price. My scallops were extremely chewy and others commented on the bland seasoning of their dishes. Had the bill come to $120 for an appetizer, four meals, and a bottle of wine, I would have been pleased. However, for double the price coupled with the service and food quality, I would have rather dined elsewhere.
label: NEG

text: Mmmmmmmm yummy! I love how you can order a mini-carafe of wine (oh I know, it has a fancier name than 'carafe'). The house salad was absolutely scrumptious, the perfect amount of dressing. My boyfriend ordered the chopped salad, and I kept stealing the tiny fresh mozzarellas off his plate. Num-num-nums! We ordered the chicken pesto pizza. The pizza crust was outstanding - it reminded me of Dewey's, which has some of the best crust in the St. Louis land. Crisp and lightly doughy. I wasn't terribly impressed with the pesto sauce - it wasn't very flavorful. All in all, they may have a few kinks to get over - but if you want quality pizza in South City, this is a true hidden gem. My guess is that they will only continue to improve over time. I can't wait to try the strombolis and calzones. I have a distinct feeling that the more traditional italian-style fare will knock my socks off. Our waitress seemed a little bit... what's the word? Oh, stoned. But that didn't really bother me. She wasn't the greatest but she wasn't terrible - and I was eating pizza and drinking wine, so I really didn't care. The interior is cute x 1,000, and I'm looking forward to trying their take-home products (pasta sauces, etc.) I love the bigger-city feel of this joint. I'd love to see them put a few tables outside! Quick, casual bite to eat near home. Good times.
label: POS

text: I just tried Yats for the first time yesterday. I didn't know what to expect, never had creole before, and was having trouble deciding. The guy at the counter was super nice and actually spent time explaining to my friends and I what the dishes were and about some of his favs. It was great. Then we got our food, which was scrumptious. The serving sizes are large and I had enough for a leftover lunch today. Awesome! At $6.25 for two meals, this place can't be beat!
label: POS

text: I moved to the Kolb and I-10 area about 6 months ago and I've been lamenting the lack of anything commercial in the vicinity. Taking a cue from Yelp, I jumped on the freeway and made the 5 minute trip to the Triple T. I am so glad I did. First impression of Omar's: the establishment is exceptionally well-run. It is clean, comfortable, attractive, and every member of the staff was friendly, attentive, and personable. I felt very much at home in this place as soon as I came in. The menu is huge and while I was looking it over my waitress gave me some cards with specials and featured dishes. I chose a grilled chicken breast special with chicken noodle soup, fries and green beans. Supposedly this dish was a "smaller portions" special, but the waitress warned me not to dawdle with my soup because I had a lot of food coming. She wasn't kidding. The food was solid and quite good. I'm not going to make it out to be something it's not. It's all diner food. But it's really good, well-executed diner food, and it's a bargain. I got the deep-dish apple pie for dessert and as earlier reviewers had warned it came with a massive topping of vanilla soft-serve which eventually started melting and incorporating itself into the bowl to create a warm vanilla-apple soup (Mmmmmmm). I was back again the other night and saw another server bring one out and the mound of soft-serve was easily twice as big as the one I got. I don't think I would want that much, but consider yourself warned. Finally - they are open 24 hours. That is awesome!
label: POS

text: Went to chima twice. Once when it first opened then tried it again about 2 weeks ago. For the price of the food it was very so-so. My wife is brasilian and I have experianced hundreds of brazilian steakhouses here and abroad. If you want a dolled down non authentic brazilian steakhouse that taste nothing like a brazilian steakhouse then this is the place. Its kinda like saying man I love mexican food and touting taco bell as your fav. It may be good for the general population but for a real authentic brazilian steakhouse FOGO DE CHAO is better. I just wish they would add rice and beans to the saled bar. Chima does have great rice and beans. Im not hatting on chima; the one in ft lauderdale is GREAT.
label: NEG

text: The pizza better be good here. I didn't have any but will be back to try it due to the positive reviews. But this place is gross. And the wait staff was curt and rude. text: If i were Carmen Sandiego, I would fly my helocopter and steal you away to San Francisco. Even better, I'd put you in my pocket so I can take you everywhere. This place is great, and definitely comparable to Monks without the ridiculous wait. It also has a less "stuffy" feel to it - very local pub feeling, which i love!

text: First, let me explain that I used to eat here once a week and it was very impressive. Over the past year, however, the service and quality of food has diminished quite a bit. *Note - my review is for the sushi half of the restaurant. I have never tried the hibachi as I visit for the sushi. I used to rave about this restaurant to friends, but have stopped giving it my recommendation. I still go back once in a while to give it another go - each time promising myself that will be the last. I suppose it's one of those love affairs I just don't want to let go. Consistent lack of quality includes: * not as fresh as it used to be * servers are quite rude - standing over me as I sign my cc slip like I'm not going to tip. Not very cool. * Nori is stale or has been subject to a lot of moisture. Used to be crisp, but as of late, just stays in your mouth and you're chewing it forever - gross. Same thing with anything that has tempura in it - not crisp. Overall, as an old fan of this restaurant, I'm just sad to see how it's changed. Change is good, but not when quality and service lack. Maybe I'll give them another go - eh, on second thought.

I once tried another Vet in the Rittenhouse area simply due to convenience (they would be closer following a move) and immediately went back to Radbill. They are the best!

text: I knowI said I'd be back for cocktails, but this time I got takeout. #31, Bun Thit Nuong (Pork Vermicelli) It was absolutely delicious. I'd been craving it all day. Obviously I'm not a Vietnamese cuisine connoisseur, but I know what tastes good to me. This is only my second time at Vietnam Cafe and both times everything I've tried has been flavorful, fresh, and filling, plus the meat is always high quality, tender, and cooked just right. . This is the type restaurant I'd recommend to everyone, even if that means traveling from the other side of the city. Add it to the list of West Philly's greats.

text: ..as I keep returning to this place I find myself in bliss simply for the fact that it not only maintains the momentum but improves with age. My dinner last night was a delight. After the Craig LaBan glowing review, I decided to finally try the less obvious choice : the Portrichmond Platter. It was soooo good. I started off with a Victory Saison which was very good and as I was waiting for the food, Brendan co-owner and his Wife Leigh, both greeted me separately. They're so friendly and welcoming. Brendon suggested a great beer for my follow up drink, however he excitedly changed his mind when he saw my plate arrive. He suggested the Legacy Pilsner since it was light, crisp and sure to clense my palatte between each bite. WOW , was he dead on! Leigh suggested a great dark mahagony beer with 8.0 Alch. that was great for dessert. I'd remember the name if it hadnt enjoyed the beers so much. My friend had Wahu fish replacing the MahiMahi since they ran out of that. IT was so good, flakey and buttery that I'd kind of rather have the replacement fish next time! Boy,I love this place.

text: Although all Salvation Army thrift stores in town have a wide variety of items to choose from they are one of the most expensive thrift stores in town. I also don't think they are very well organized. I would much rather spend my time and money somewhere else.

text: Before I complain, let me say a few nice things. The tandoori chicken was wonderful, amazing, delicious, and I say that as someone who usually doesn't like chicken. The decor is fun - the lighting is really dramatic and beautiful. I think the sunken area in the middle is a bit too kitschy, but that's just me. All the other tapas we had there were, well, not bad, but nothing better than the sort of thing I typically cook at home. And certainly not worth $10 each. All in all, I might recommend this restaurant if the food cost a fifth or less of what it does, but there's no justifying this quality at this price. As a side note, I ordered a Guinness, and it might be my fault for not looking closely enough at the beer menu, but what I got was a Guinness Draught, which looks like a Guinness but tastes like a mixture of mayonnaise and wet gravel.
label: NEG

text: I've had their Pho and their Spring rolls and both are excellent! The owners (husband and wife) are very friendly and they offer excellent service and hospitality. I've had Pho at a number of locales and Little Saigon is really top notch!
label: POS

text: Look at that. I actually went under three stars. This place merits the changing of my standards, and I'll tell you why. I went here for my roommate's birthday with 10 others (two are fellow Yelpers- let's call them Kevin W. and George R -note, names have not been changed to protect the guilty). This is how the night went. 7:00- We get seated, our server introduces herself, takes drink orders. (I would like to add that she forgot the one order for a drink, which was a soda, until after the food came out, two hours later). 7:45- George R. turns to me and says, "So, I guess there are going to be a lot of new reviews for this place, tomorrow. I know what I'm going to write." 8:15- Kevin W. shouts down the table to me (he hadn't heard what George R. said), "I know what I'm going to write. How 'bout you?" We all had something bad on our minds. For several reasons. The service was terrible. The prices are uncalled for. And the service was terrible. Granted, we were a large party and two people were 30 minutes late, but it took the server over an hour to show up to take our orders (after the initial introduction and poor drink order). That means we spent over 30 minutes actively craning our necks looking for her to no avail. Besides disappearing and making us wait forever, our server forgot my soup and charged us for an appetizer that she wasn't supposed to bring out and said she wouldn't charge us for. Also, they ran out of several of the foods that were ordered but didn't tell us until 30 minutes after we ordered them. Twice. That's right. I ordered something, 30 minutes later had to order something new, and then 30 minutes later was forced to order something new. Besides the poor service, the atmosphere could really use a revamping. It's one thing to joke about "Jamaican service" while you're eating at a Jamaican restaurant. It's another thing entirely when that slow service gets in the way of enjoying a nice meal.
label: NEG

text: When it comes down to it, it is the people who run the restaurant, not only the food, which makes a difference. I have eaten in EVERY Japanese restaurant within 30 miles of Camden and Oh Yoko is #1. The husband/wife team really care about making your experience memorable. Every detail, down to the shape and color of the plates is attended to. [Many will claim that Sagami is #1. I believe it has been cruising on empty for a long time. I was once scalded by an entire bowl of hot miso soup by a harried waitress (they are ALWAYS harried at Sagami) and received not so much as an apology. Maybe it was a cultural thing, huh?] Oh Yoko is not to be missed.
label: POS

text: I don't understand why this place gets such great reviews. If I were to review the smell alone as you walk by I would have to give it five stars. After moving to Philly and walking by it on several occasions I really looked forward to eating there. Unfortunately that is where the good things i have to say about it end. I ordered a jerk chicken plate and a fanta which I figured had to be safe. It came to just under $20!!! for chicken. On top of that it was awful. So over-cooked and dry it was almost inedible.
label: NEG

text: I dun luv me sum Sundubu This was my first time visiting Miga and I definitely will be back. Immediately when you walk in, you can't help but notice how nicely designed/decorated the place is. It gives you the impression that you are in a much more expensive place than you actually are. The tables have these really cool infrared/charcoal grills in them which serve as eye-candy and a nice conversation starter. I came here with my asian food club. Seven of us stepped lightly through the menu with the help of a few Korean food veterans. Our appetizers were the Ddukbokki and the Pajun. I was more partial to the pajun which was fried very nicely. The sauce of the Ddukbokki was very tasty but I found the dish to be a tad heavy. I ordered the seafood Sundubu and wow was it delicious! It came in a sizzling hot pot and was served with a raw egg. Taking the advice of my food compatriots, I cracked the egg over the hot soup and stirred it in with the chopsticks. The egg added an extra layer of richness and slightly cut the heat of the soup. The soft tofu was delicious and the spice level stayed at a constant level throughout the dish. Just perfect by my standards. I would call the heat of this dish "the edge of pain." I didn't get to use the grills in the table, so I'll be going back. We had an interesting discussion at the table that Korean might be the best cold weather asian food. After this experience, I think it's been settled. Up next: Bulgogi.
label: POS

text: Gullifty's is a solid place to grab a beer and watch a game. The bar area has adequate seating with close views to several flat screens. The beer selection is extensive and the menu has something for everyone. The service is usually prompt and friendly. They have Quizzo on Thursday nights and outdoor seating when the weather cooperates. It's conveniently located next to a Border's which is a nice place to waste time if you have to wait for a table.
label: POS

text: Unabashed awesomeness of the highest caliber. That's if you like Belgian beers, which o Lordy I do. Two floors, 1st it more of a bar and 2nd more a restaurant. Food's a decent Belgian spin on pub grub, but the star here is the beer. I don't even know where to begin. Suffice to say they'll be turning my money into urine every time I am in Philly from here on out.

text: I only go here since it is convenient. I have a golden retriever and this place doesn't seem to cater to larger dogs as much those that can fit in someone's purse. They always seem to be out of inventory whenever I need something. I was looking for an easy walk harness; I stopped in multiple times and they never had the right size or gender appropriate color. Recently, I went in looking for some goodies for my dog's birthday, and they had nothing whatsoever; no hat, no cake or birthday-related dog treat. The only thing that would be somewhat relevant was a small birthday cake furry toy that played music. My dog would have ripped it to shreds in no time. The only thing they always have in stock is poop bags.
label: NEG

text: One of my all-time favorite restaurants. Although there aren't too many exciting kinds of sushi, their sushi is definitely the best around. I haven't tried many other things on the menu, but everything I have tried has been delicious. The mochi ice cream is awesome, I highly recommend that you try it (mango, chocolate, and strawberry are all good). It's a very popular place, so if you're going for dinner on a Friday or Saturday night, it's a good idea to call ahead for reservations.

text: This place has a great menu, beer selection and ambiance. You can't beat their Bacon, Brie & Apple sandwich on Raisin bread, or the deliciously light but tasteful Black Plum & Ricotta salad. The "Frites" are accompanied by a horseradish dip that is to die for and go well with the ever-changing list of beers on tap. The servers are very friendly and the only downside is they put a pool table in the back and don't have enough room for groups above 4, which they used to be able to fit comfortably.

text: Service was good but the wings suck. I'd prefer Buffalo Wild Wings any day.

text: Prohibition is probably the place I have frequented most in the city. I lived in that area for a year and Prohibition is like a golden treasure some leprechaun must have dropped on his way to other parts of the city. I mean, really, that is such a shady street. I know, I lived on it. Thank you Prohibition for being a haven in bumble-fu¢k Philadelphia. The Fried Green Beans are amazing. And the Grilled Cheese specials which change every week. Oh and the amazing burger specials. Did I leave out the macaroni? They have a consistently changing draught list which is where I have found some of my favorite obscure beers. I can't leave out the fact that the wait staff is one of the best I've encountered in the city. They are over-the-top friendly to the point where they get to know people's names. This is 2010; I barely know my aunt's name. Good job, Prohibition.

text: I have fixed my 1997 Chevy Monte Carlo more times than I would like to say, so I am quite familiar with cars. I dropped my car off for a standard state inspection. They called and informed me that the rear lug nuts were "really tight" and they couldn't get them off. They had even sprayed them with "lubrication". This seemed funny to me since I had hand tightened them myself with just a standard tire iron and no excessive force. They then proceeded to say that they had to break the studs off and charge me to REPLACE BOTH REAR HUBS! I told them that was ridiculous, and I would pick up the car. On arrival I inspected the rear nuts. Three nuts (1 driver, 2 passenger) were completely rounded by someone too aggressive with an air ratchet. A simple tire iron would have cleanly broken the nuts free. I don't trust these people. Now I have to deal with these stripped nuts.
label: NEG

text: Great tacos. Loved the abodabo. Def would come back. Very basic menu. Super cheap.

text: I was in town visiting my Mom and we went to have a late lunch here. We had the Tuna Asada, Guava Ribs, Island Quesadilla and Balsamic Grilled Vegetables. The only thing we didn't love was the tuna - not enough flavor. On the other end, my Mom is STILL talking about the Guava Ribs. I have no doubt the next time we're in Tampa, we're headed back there just for the ribs. Holy crap they were good. We ate outside and the service was average. The final bill was very reasonable - but that's because of what we selected. Some items on the menu didn't seem worth the price.

text: As a San Francisco-area resident visiting Santa Barbara, it is fair to say that my bar was set pretty high. Maybe the reviews are right, and this IS the best night-life spot in Santa Barbara...but that still doesn't make it any good.

text: It was so packed that nobody could move around. The waiters even had a hard time. We were rushed and told repeatedly that our table will needed for the next party. The menu on the very back page does have a set of rules that everyone must follow including, being considerate with volume, paying extra if you share, 20% tip will automatically be included, etc. The food was too buttery and the meatballs microwaved. text: Wasabi is one of my lesser favorite sushi restaurants. The decor is cute and cozy, but the tables are a little small. I ordered the Crunchy Roll and the Honey Shrimp. The Roll was not very appetizing, the fish did not taste as fresh as I would like. The shrimp was good but halfway through, the dish became boring with the same flavor. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone but if you are adventurous go for it.
label: NEG

text: So the only reason why this place even has 1 star is for its view. I admit, the view is fantastic - from the 14th floor of the Grand Hyatt, you can sip on some wine and watch the sunset over the bay, cars driving down the Courtney Campbell Causeway Bridge, while listening to a live pianist. Aside from that, I think Armani's should be embarrassed to serve the food they do at the prices they charge. For appetizer, I ordered the tagliatelle. Pasta - the test of a true Italian restaurant. Tagliatelle was slightly over-cooked but veal ragout was okay. Some friends ordered the lobster bisque. From what I heard, there was a weird bitter wine taste. Maybe the wine wasn't reduced down? For dinner, I ordered the sea bass with a side of risotto. Sea bass was also overcooked and a little bland. Risotto was by far the worst I've ever had. Very undercooked center - the result of trying to cook risotto too fast. When we returned it to the server, his reaction was "oh". He took it and walked away. No "I'm so sorry" or "Is there something else we can get for you". Maybe they're just hotel staff and really don't care about the restaurant. I hope Armani's gets their food on track. Otherwise, it's a spectacular location and view gone to waste. PS - Armani's, I have a great risotto recipe from Epicurious. If you want it, I can send you a link.
label: NEG

text: If you can't make risotto in a (pretend) Italian restaurant you may as well go back to flipping burgers. This writer nearly broke his teeth on the undercooked rice they served as risotto and sent it back. It was replaced with polenta at the suggestion of the waitress because she clearly had no faith in the kitchen getting it right the second time. The polenta was lukewarm and slightly dry when it arrived. Has no one been to Italy here? Polenta is just grits with butter and cheese. What's the problem? Wine service - hold carafe at arm's length and shoulder hight and turn upside down. A room with a view - someone else has also mentioned this. The outside dinning area has a splended view of the parking lot and it's fun to count the number of Stupid Ugly Vehicles four-wheel driving by your table while waiting for anyone to pay attention to you.

text: went for valentine's dinner, which fell two days before fat tuesday. the inside of the restaurant was a nice calm getaway from the ruckus of bourbon street outside the window. text: First of all, the service here is amazing. The hosts are happy to see you. There is a lot of attention paid to your table. We started off with the exotic wild mushroom saute. text: I desperately wish I could give this place more stars. I *love* Ethiopian food, and as far as I know, this is the only Ethiopian place in the St Louis area, so I had really high hopes. It's right smack in the middle of a really vibrant area, I would have expected more than white walls and plastic tablecloths. Oddly enough, the plant next to our table was wearing an Arby's name tag. That really didn't help with the ambiance. On to the food... It wasn't bad. I know people joke about how Ethiopian food is a grain of rice on a plate, but really, Ethiopian cuisine is really vibrant and tasty. (It reminds me a little of Indian food, what with the heavy reliance on stews and lentils, but the seasonings and flavors are completely different) The entrees came out in those oval-shaped dishes, just like in cheap Indian restaurants. The injera was pretty good. Not really noteworthy, but since it effectively a combination side dish and utensil, it doesn't really need to be. The real stand-out parts of the meal though were the couple of lentil-based side dishes. Holy crap, they were delicious. I don't remember much about our entrees, but I remember those. The red lentil one especially. Unrelated to the restaurant itself, I also want to mention that our waitress had a beautiful accent, and was drop-dead gorgeous. Models would kill for her cheekbones. I will probably go again, since I regularly get cravings for Ethiopian food, but I so wish that the restaurant itself were nicer. If it could really be a cultural experience as well as food, I would drive into the city for it all the time!
