text: A must when in Philly. Here is a little history from the website: "Opened in 1829 as part of a controversial movement to change the behavior of inmates through 'confinement in solitude with labor,' Eastern State Penitentiary quickly became one of the most expensive and most copied buildings in the young United States. It is estimated that more than 300 prisons worldwide are based on the Penitentiary's wagon-wheel, or 'radial' floor plan. Some of America's most notorious criminals were held in the Penitentiary's vaulted, sky-lit cells, including bank robber Willie Sutton and Al Capone. After 142 years of consecutive use, Eastern State Penitentiary was completely abandoned in 1971, and now stands, a lost world of crumbling cellblocks and empty guard towers." The narrated tour is informative, engaging, and entertaining. It's narrated by Steve Buscemi---how could that be bad? Located in one of my favorite northern Philly neighborhoods--Fairmount. text: One of the best bars anywhere, period. The building dates from before 1772 and may be the oldest continuously operating bar in America. If you don't know the story, here goes: Jean Lafitte was New Orleans' original bad-ass pirate. He operated this blacksmith shop as a front for his pirating operations around the Caribbean. In the War of 1812, when the British were about to attack and overrun New Orleans, president Andrew Jackson asked Lafitte for help. US forces were badly outnumbered 3 to 1 by the well outfitted British and faced almost certain defeat. Lafitte subsequently called together his ragtag band of 1000 pirates - with an intimate knowledge of the swamps, smuggler's routes and rivers they harassed the British unrelentingly and helped to save the day. Lafitte claimed to have never pirated an American vessel so he was really more of a privateer or corsair than a true pirate. He was really a legendary figure in New Orleans and there is all kinds of folklore surrounding him - my favorite is that he was caught in a hurricane off the coast of Texas and saved his ship by literally riding the storm surge *over* the island of Galveston into its harbor. No one knows whatever happened to him - he sailed off into the sunset with a huge treasure that has never been recovered. Anyway the guy was a true bad ass, and sitting at the bar you will feel a little bit of the pirate inside of you come to life. One more thing - I sat at the bar talking to the cute punky bartender and had her show me how to make a Sazerac, which is kind of like the national drink of New Orleans: In a shaker filled with ice combine: 1 jigger Cognac (or Rye Whiskey) 1 tablespoon simple syrup 3 dashes of Peynaud's bitters 2 dashes Angostura bitters At the same time, pour a dash of Absinthe or Herbisant into a Aperitif glass. Rotate the glass so the walls are well coated. Shake the hell out of the shaker and then strain into the glass (i like this drink cold so I always shake it hard enough that ice crystals form on the top of the drink after it's been poured!). Twist half of a thin lemon slice into the drink and enjoy - tasty and lethal. PS Was it was just my foggy post-sazerac memory or are there no doors on this bar (since they never close)? Now that is a SERIOUS bar.

It has the texture of stale bread, but this ended up being great. the burger held in place wonderfully and it did not fall apart like the softer potato rolls for example. My burger was cooked great but was extremely salty on one side. The cheddar was rubbery and flavorless, and the onions were very overcooked, mushy and flavorless. The side of pickles was unexpected and a bonus (I love pickles!). Good size in my opinion, but my food mate thought it was too small for the price (almost looked like a slider, 5.5oz uncooked patty). Overall it was a good burger, but not great. Out of 5 I would give it 3. If the cheese and onions were better, it would gain +1 because the meat was tasty and juicy (the heart if you will). The truffle fries were a gigantic portion for $2... we should have shared a single order. They were awesome and the smell of truffles was fantastic. The flavor was not overpowering, almost subtle addition to the fries. The fries were not at all greasy which I really, really appreciate and the way they were cut was great. Some were nice and crunchy and some were soft so there was alot to like here. Fries get 5 out of 5! The spicy fries were on par with these. Milkshake: god I wish I ordered one after seeing them make it : ) but I am sure my wallet (5 bucks!) and my stomach thank my brain for saving them. From the looks of it though, it would have raised the rating 1 star alone! haha. Value: was the burger worth $5.50? in my ideal world... no. but comparatively in the market it wasn't outrageous. Total meal cost without drink was $9 after tax and I think that is slightly too much considering what you get, but we could have also split the $2 fries for how many you get. I couldn't make this a 'regular' place to eat as I don't see the value. Summary: The wait times were prohibitive of a lunch time meal, and the value is right on the border of being overpriced (the jury is still out) but I enjoyed the meal enough that I would go back. 2 stars is not mean to be a put down, and I think it is accurate of the food and experience. I hope the lines get more manageable at lunch time though. *Me and my friend made an over/under bet on if this place would last. Goodburger didn't survive a year for the same issues I brought up with 500d (value, wait time). However, I expect it to last so took the over side. I hope I don't lose!

Brad (the owner) let me know upfront what the maximum price would be, and then added that they would only charge for the amount of refrigerant (R134a) that they added to the system. Sure enough, it came out less than the max. It was also comforting that I did not receive a laundry list of potential repairs when I picked up my car. The job took a total of two hours, I got my car back the same day, and it was a pleasant experience. What more can you ask for. Just so you know, this shop has a long history of working with Volvos, although they are perfectly capable of working on other makes as well. They are also actively becoming Mini Cooper specialists, so I would recommend giving them a try for Mini service as well. Lastly, although I'm not an expert on prices, the price of the AC recharge was not the cheapest on the block, but also not particularly expensive. The rabbit was by far superior, though I am a big fan of the lamb, as well. By the time the kebabs came out, we were too full to dig in, so I'm eating them along with the cous cous for lunch today (mmm!). Fruit then baklava and mint tea rounded out the very filling, very tasty meal. The fruit was clearly very fresh and I happily partook of the juicy, seedless watermelon. Also the pineapple and red grapes. The baklava was perfect: dry and crunchy up top and gooey on the bottom. The mint tea was sweetened with honey and very tasty. The belly dancer was a lot of fun- she pulled me up to show me how to move my hips. Despite my lack of coordination, it was a lot of fun. Definitely into going back, next time with a large group.

There are too many open spaces with nothing happening. We were trying to set up our blanket on the grass and I fell in a hole and twisted my ankle. Unless you want to go down a HUGE slide or play in the kid area your only choice is the wave pool. Well, I can go swimming in a huge pool for 1 to 3 bucks. I just dont see this as being a good value for the money. I can see that they have to make some money to pay for the things they provide.. but come on! How can they not be busier than they are? text: I've been pretty impressed with this place. First things out of the way, I really don't care where a place is located or what it looks like unless it is clean and has delicious food. This place does have delicious food and got a 95 on their health inspection rating. So both criteria are met there. Now to the good stuff, the chicken. It is juicy and very flavorful. It is clear that they either put it in a spicy brine or marinade prior to cooking, and it makes all the difference. As for the style of the fried chicken, it comes out crisp with a spicy wet finish on the outside. I got the 400 degrees level and it was hot, but not enough to make me sweat. As a matter of fact, I didn't take the first sip of my soda until I was done. Given that I am spicy freak, this should be plenty hot enough for mortals (for reference, I can eat the spiciest thing Prince's has without batting an eye, I frequently consider using pepper spray as a condiment). But all in all, damn good fried chicken. For sides, they have spicy crinkle fries (hit the spot), baked beans (the way they are supposed to be made), cole slaw and potato salad. As well, they have a couple of random things like a burger(?) and they have fresh cookies for dessert. Another nice perk about this joint is the people that run it are friendly - great customer service. So there is another way they have Prince's beat. Their hours are a little wonky,. 11AM-3PM M-F and 11AM-1AM Saturday. As well, they only take cash, so make sure you come prepared or you'll be washing dishes. My wait time was very reasonable, a little less than 20 minutes, and they recommend you call in your order in advance.

text: I spend the weekend in Philly with my boyfriend and some of our good friends. Josh H and I decided to go off by ourselves for a romantic dinner. I hit up the trusty ole Yelp app on his I-Phone for a recommendation. We were both craving Italian, and Modo Mio showed up as the first 4.5 star rec. Conveniently, it was also in the same hood that my friend was having her bday party. Finally, as an added bonus, I found out this place was BYOB, which means that Josh and I could splurge a little more on food instead of spending 50 bucks on a bottle of booze that really cost 15 dollars at the distributor. We arrive at like 7:30, sans reservation. All the tables inside were booked, but we were able to sit outside right away. It was a touch too hot to eat outside, but by that point, we were starving. The waitress explained that a lot of people try the 'tourista' menu. For 32 dollars, one can get: an app, pasta, an entree, and dessert. For Josh, who can eat a lot, this seemed like a good value. Knowing myself, I stuck to an entree. I could have ordered pasta if I wanted, however, because they have GLUTEN FREE OPTIONS! Yay!!!! They can do any spaghetti and gnocchi dish gluten free, which ROCKS. However, the lamb shank and wilted dandelion greens combo looked pretty outstanding, so I chose that. Josh went with: snails and capers over toasted bread, shrimp and arribata gnocchi, breaded pork loin with gorgonzola over corn, and vanilla panna cotta with biscotti for dessert. We were both super pumped. What we loved: Josh loved his snails and the cheesey bread that accompanied it. He also liked the gnocchi. He said that it had a small spicy kick, but that even someone as spice sensitive as me could have handled it. He loved the pork, especially because it was covered in gorgonzola. I was kinda meh about my lamb. The lamb itself was cooked perfectly, but the accompanying tomato and plumb puree was a bit cloying. Josh's pork dish looked way better. If only the breading were gluten free. Otherwise I would have gone halfsies with him. All in all, this place was super cute. You could tell that they care a lot about food. If my lamb were not covered in that saccharine sauce, I would have easily given Modo Mio 5 stars.
label: POS

text: People come to the Colonnade for many reasons. People who grew up in South Tampa will tell stories how it once was a tiny hang-out for the local teenagers. He liked the seafood and the view of Davis Islands, and the huge selection of food for everyone. I guess as I get older, I like the Colonnade because it is reliable and has a large menu with something for everyone, a well-trained staff, and decent prices. I too head for the seafood. As for people who complain about the old people - well, too bad, you're looking at the USA in 30 years. Who do you think are living in most of those condos along the Bayshore - 20 year olds? The beds were surprisingly comfortable and we had a nice view of the pool. My favorite part of this hotel was how friendly the staff members were! Peter, one of the maintenance guys, was a very helpful person and a very hard worker. All of the guys who worked there are very accommodating and full of cheer. My only complaint is that the female concierge only had one suggestion as far as places to eat. New Orleans is full of restaurants and for a person who lives here to give the same suggestion three times was a bit annoying. If you're looking to stay at an uber fancy hotel, this is not the place for you. If you're trying to find a reasonably priced place to pass out after drinking all night and day with wonderful employees and that is in the perfect location, you can't beat the Chateau Lemoyne. I would definitely stay here again.

text: Yes, there will be a line. Yes, you'll sit at mix-and-match tables. And yes, you'll have to deal with the vagaries of a parking lot shared with a Rite Aid. But the lines move quickly, the seating is comfortable, and parking is always a problem in Drexel Hill, so why should your visit to Ming's be any different? There's no better place for breakfast, anywhere. Ming's pancakes are remarkable -- moist, buttery, and flavorful beyond imagining. Ming uses only the freshest of ingredients and keeps a watchful eye over her small but prodigious galley-style kitchen (which runs like clockwork) and table servers who are young, but skilled. Everyone works together to keep things moving. Ming's coffee is the best French Roast I've ever tasted -- and I'm not a fan of dark roasted coffees, especially in the morning. It's hard to know if all of her coffees are the product of a hand-press, but that's how every cup tastes. Never had a single cup delivered to our table which tasted stale, overbrewed or bitter. My wife loves Ming's teas, which are prepared to perfection. So, take a ride to Drexel Hill and enjoy breakfast at Ming's. You'll be delighted.

This on the other hand was not done well. You weren't kidding about the atmosphere, this place is dismal. But whatever, it's a takeout joint, I get it. The food however was inexcusable. I got the General Tso's tofu because it's an unusual tofu option. The tofu is tough and chewy and the sauce is way too sweet. Plus, doesn't this style usually include sesame seeds? text: What a difference a year makes. *** (see response after the review) I sent the following letter to the owner of Yalda because our recent experience was so bad. It's been a month, and I have yet to receive a reply, so I'm posting it. ***************** I want to tell you how disappointed we were with our dinner at Yalda last night. Because we have had great experiences here in the past, my daughter specifically requested that we take her here on her birthday. Coming with her, were her mother and father-in-law, and her husband's grandparents; neither of those couples had been to Yalda and were anxious to try your restaurant, based on our recommendation. We ended up being embarrassed hosts. I called for a reservation the day before, and therefore thought you would be prepared for a party of 8. It didn't seem that you were. The bread/chutney came out quickly, but after that, service just disappeared. The appetizers were wonderful, but took forever to come out. The salads, torn lettuce on a plate with dressing, also took forever. What takes so long to plate up lettuce and dressing? And the entrees? We had to ask several times where they were. Then only 6 of the 8 were served. The other two took an additional 20 minutes, and multiple inquiries to our server. The guest of honor had to sit at the table, watching everyone else eat, while she waited for hers. By the time she finally got her entrée, everyone else was finished their meal, and she didn't have much of an appetite to eat while everyone else watched her. She just packed her dinner up to take home. Inexcusable. I had called earlier that day to ask about doing a special dessert for the birthday. I spoke to you again when we arrived at the restaurant. It was surprising, then, when it took so long for our server to even ask if we wanted dessert - we foolishly thought that the delay was his waiting for "something special" to be plated in the kitchen. Not so. We skipped dessert and left, fearing that the additional course would not get us out of your restaurant until after 10 pm. I don't know if you were understaffed, if the fact that we were using a Restaurant.com certificate made a difference, or what the problem was, but it was certainly not the celebration we anticipated. Not once during the entire meal did anyone - either the server or you - apologize or even acknowledge that the service was terrible or that there was a delay. Not once. Even though my husband had to get up out of his seat numerous times to ask where out food was. Was the food good? Yes it was, but the terrible service overshadowed everything else. Well, we probably won't be back. Neither will any of the people who were with us. We had gotten them all excited about a great place, with wonderful food, and all left with a bad taste in their mouths. No, I'm not going to write a bad review on those sites where I originally posted glowing ones, unless of course you choose not to acknowledge my letter. I just won't be able to continue recommending Yalda to others. Or if I do, I will let them know up front that they will have to put up with some real service issues. Probably the most upsetting thing to us was that we, as the hosts, expected to be part of a special experience, and to show those who hadn't been to Yalda what we had been raving about. Instead we looked like fools with very poor taste in restaurants. I came in the door being a very vocal fan of your restaurant. I didn't leave that way. ********************************************* I received a very nice letter of apoplogy from Laila, who is the daughter of the owner. She had seen my updated review on Yelp & apologized profusely for the poor service we received and and said that she never received my original letter of complaint (it was sent to the email address posted on their website). She even offered to reimburse half of our bill. I sent her a reply, thanking her for her response, and declining her offer of the rebate on our bill. My intent was never to solicit a comp, but rather to let people know that a place I had vociferously raved about in the past had fallen way short. I was hoping that the complaint would reach the owners and that it might cause a change in their service so others wouldn't go through the same thing we did. It looks as though the posting had it effect. Am I ready to go back to Yalda? I really really love their food. Yeah, I WILL go back, just not right away. And I probably won't go with a group. I commeneded Laila for replying to my posting on Yelp. It shows she cares about her customers and her restaurant's reputation. Just based on that, Yalda is worth another shot.

We started with cocktails - my friends had Pom margaritas, I ordered a Pom martini. I guess I should of had the margarita, what I got was a beer glass with grapefruit and Pom over ice - a twisted Vodka "sunrise". The waitress said that the bartender was using a different "form" for the Pom martini.......utter nonsense. Next - Appetizers. These were good! My friends had the Tortilla Soup - good flavor with some non-traditional veggies in a tasty broth. I had the Columbian Arepas - sweet masa pancakes with a cabbage cole slaw and spicy sauce. The entrees were not so good. I had the Chimichurri steak, prepared medium rare with a beautiful char on the outside - but really on the tough side. My friends had all ordered the Latin combo specials with different meats - Pulled pork, Carne Asada, chicken, etc. Overall, no one was pleased with their choice. Our waitress was very good, service was friendly and quick. Sur Real is probably good for happy hour, the appetizers were really good. But when it comes time for Dinner, it's just not a good choice for the money.

text: What's not to like about Trader Joe's? Fresh produce, seasonal specials, dependable samples, friendly employees-- you can't go wrong here. TJ's is the place to go if you need a feisty alternative to your neighborhood Schnuck's. Everyone I know has a TJ's favorite. I really love the frozen gnocchi -- 7 minutes with a tablespoon of water in a skillet and you've got a dish your Italian grandma would have been proud of. The toffee's great come the holiday season, and the sparkling pomegranate juice is the most sexual beverage I've ever encountered. The biggest pain in the ass about this place? Getting there. Every time I make it to the parking lot and get out of my car I need to choke my heart back down my throat. That entire shopping center needs to be nuked and rebuilt. So until I have a kid and have a reasonable chance that my DNA will be propagated into an iPhone-filled future, I prefer to stay safe and boring and shop at Schnucks. When iPhones give way to personal teleportation devices, though, maybe I'll be a Trader Joe's regular.

And you don't have to go through aisle over aisle of ridiculous Halloween goods in the middle of March to get to them! This is one of the first places I stop when shopping for any kind of party goods. I mainly buy solid color paper plates, napkins, cups and gift bags here, because they have a great selection and they are cheap. If you need theme stuff though, they have plenty of that too! They have most of what a larger "big box" retailer would have, as well as some more unique items too. The sales people are nice and helpful and quick to get you what you need, and the store isn't huge so everything is easy to find. Stop by next time you need 15 sombreros or a pirate sword or Hannah Montana napkins. They've got it all.

text: This place is spectacular! BMB's menu includes udon and ramen noodles (with toppings at an additional cost) some great appetizers and crepes. Their drink menu is a long list of fruit juices, coffees, and teas that can be combined with tapioca balls, better known as boba. I wish someone would start serving flavored boba. That would be cool... and definitely besides the point. I ordered a Thai Milk Tea, which was super refreshing and delicious. I wanted to order another. But then my beef crepe was served to go. It had grilled beef that was actually tender, mozza, spinach, garlic and some sauce... Unfortunately my crepe included a leaf of iceberg lettuce. Warm lettuce.... so gross. However, I decided to pick it out and enjoyed the tasty (and surprisingly plentiful) meal in Forest Park. Quite enjoyable. text: Am I the only one left that thinks a $400 bill for two people should be accompanied by an outstanding meal? I admit that I expect a lot for that kind of money but that is why we chose delmonico in the first place. We arrived 10min early and were sent to the bar for a drink. 3min later, without getting so much as a hello from the bartender, we got shown to our table. We ordered martinis, since it was a special occasion, mine arrived lukewarm. We felt rushed during the ordering process, but intentionally took our time. My wife ordered the appetizer special, it was sold out at 7pm. Waiter 1 brought me a second martini that I didn't order. Waiter 2 didn't bring the glass of wine my wife did order. The apps were tasty enough. Our $153 bottle of wine was delicious, but for $153 it should be. That was a low to middle of the road bottle on the extensive wine list that topped out at $5500. Our entrees were good, but nothing memorable. My $39 8oz filet was not the best I ever ate and it was a la carte. The best part of the meal was the $7 dirty rice side order. We joked that we could have gotten 6 orders and a few beers and it would have been fantastic. The final disappointment was the $12 after dinner drink "the 7 elixers" if you don't like jager or green chartruse you will not like it, oh but you'll pay for it whether you like it or not. All I'm saying is that, for the money, it should be outstanding and it is merely good. If you have eaten at fancy restaurants with great service you will probably be a bit disappointed.
label: NEG

text: An excellent place to get pizza. Sal is a really cool guy too. He'll come up and strike up a conversation with you. HUGE slices of pizza (NY style). For the style of pizza it is, very very good. Try the pepperoni bread sticks here. When I lived in Hendrick's County, I loved getting the bread sticks here.

text: This place is great! I have been there multiple times now and everything I have ordered there has been wonderful. Portion size is good to generous, I almost always have to take part of my meal home. The soft shell crab dish is amazing. Everyone is very friendly and the chef almost always comes out personally to ask how the meal was. I have been there both during the week and on weekends and have not had to wait long for my food at all. Go early or make reservations on the weekend as others are catching on. BYOB is always a plus.

text: This place was pretty sweet. I got a great deal on a room ($80 or something of the sort) for a really nice room. They have a pool, and a computer room, and a breakfast buffet ($12 in the morning), and free wi-fi. :) We actually had a fire alarm go off in the middle of the night the time we stayed there but they compensated the lack of sleep with a delicious FREE breakfast. I won't be visiting St. Louis again (it's a pretty dead city) but if you are, this Hilton Garden Inn is a good affordable option.

text: How do you review the Po-Boy Preservation Festival? It's difficult because everyone's experience is so personal and based on their own likes and dislikes. I liked the live music that included a stage with a band and a marching band playing 'oh when the saints'...and doing a little who dat chanting. I loved being with all those people who love New Orleans, it's just such a good feeling. I loved that you could get smaller versions (half) poboy's so you could try more than one. I loved that it is outside in November because the weather was great. But, the things I did not love really outweigh the loves: It was super-de-duper crowded. At times it was impossible to walk at all and you were crammed into the crowd. The lines were pretty long. I waited 25 minutes to get a drink. I only found one vegetarian poboy- the french fry poboy Le Citron Bistro. The fries weren't really done but I was so hungry that almost anything would've tasted good. I found out later that there was a fried mashed potato poboy at Ninja! (go ninja!!). I thought the prices were steep. Oh, and i had a black bean taco that tasted so fresh and homemade- that was good. I got some great photos, check 'em out.

text: Mama Pho is located on South Grand at Chippewa, in the former home of McDonald's. As Dustin said, the decor isn't a big reach from McDonald's. Very sterile, same floor, drop ceilings, etc. We shared spring rolls with the standard fish sauce and peanut dips. They were fresh and yummy. I ordered the pork chop combo. The sunny-side up egg wasn't just sunny side up, it had gooey raw egg-white, as well. Far too undercooked for me. The pork & egg cake that usually comes with a Vietnamese pork chop seemed as though it was microwaved and it had an incredibly foul taste. I usually like the egg cake in other Vietnamese restaurants, but this was terrible. The pork chop itself was delicious and cooked to perfection. The waiter was INCREDIBLY friendly and apologetic for the mishaps with the food and said they are working to improve the food and menu. Because there is plenty of parking, the pork chop was great and the waiter was excellent, I'll be back to give Mama Pho another try. They will have to do better on the food to get me back a third time. My lunch companions liked their food.

text: Recently some friends and I traveled to historic Franklin, TN for a fun weekend. While there we decided to try the local cupcakes. We ate beautiful cupcakes from Iveycakes, Naticakes (we were told they were previously called Curious Gourmet), and Gigi's. Although the Gigi cupcakes were pretty, we were seriously disappointed with the taste. The cupcake itself tasted like it was from a mix, not a fresh made from scratch cake. I almost went into diabetic shock from the frosting. Way too sweet! Did not taste any different from your local chain grocery store. All three of us really enjoyed Naticakes. Totally cute upscale shop. Friendly service. Not only were the cupcakes beautiful to look at, but they were absolutely delicious!!! The frosting has very creamy texture, and is not overly sweet. One of the cupcakes had a pastry cream filling, another one had a caramel center, and the other one was a peanut butter and chocolate cupcake. It was so nice to get out of the cold, and enjoy our cupcakes with a nice latte. The cupcakes were so good we each took home a half dozen home.

text: The Hooters Restaurant in Fairview Heights has set a new low, and after reaching rock bottom, has begun to dig. How hard is it to cook an unbreaded, well done chicken wing? Apparently for the kitchen staff at the Fairview Heights Hooters, it's an insurmountable task. For the third time in as many visits, they have failed to cook my requested dish of chicken wings the way I requested them to be cooked. One would think that Hooters could manage to cook an order of their SIGNATURE DISH properly, but that would not be the case. Each time I have visited Hooters, I have ordered the same thing--unbreaded well-done wings. Each time the same thing has happened--the first order of wings (after a 20 minute wait) comes out with breading, and then the second time (after sending the first order back because I ordered them naked since I don't like greasy fried breading) after I make the identical order, I receive unbreaded and UNDERCOOKED wings. Each time I waited FORTY MINUTES and left without getting anything to eat. I cannot put into words how incompetent the waitstaff or the kitchen or both has to be in order to screw up the IDENTICAL order TWICE IN A ROW on the same visit and have this happen on THREE SEPARATE VISITS IN A ROW. I have never seen such incompetence at any restaurant IN MY LIFE and for this to happen REPEATEDLY on THREE SEPARATE VISITS is simply beyond the pale. Chicken wings are Hooter's SIGNATURE DISH. If they can do nothing else, they SHOULD be able to manage to cook a batch of unbreaded well-done wings yet they have failed to do this SIX CONSECUTIVE TIMES. It's not a complicated thing and if they can't master something this simple, then they should really close the restaurant and try something they could succeed at doing--such as playing with their lower lips or walking and chewing gum at the same time. I will NEVER go back to Hooters again--I don't know if their wings are good or bad because I've never gotten to eat any of them. So, to the siliconed and nubile waitstaff I offer this advice: Write down the order and to the imbecile in the do-rag I advise him to READ the order. This could possibly result in my actually getting something to eat although I'm not holding my breath.
label: NEG

text: DON'T make the mistake of limiting your South Philly taco intake to La Veracruzana and La Lupe. Los Taquitos de Puebla is too good to miss, and just as the cuisines of Puebla and Veracruz (neighboring states in Mexico) have marked differences, not least of which are the differences in local agricultural products, no two South Philly tacos are exactly alike. I had an order of tacos al pastor, cooked on a kabob-like rod and containing a unique blend of seasoned beef and pork. They were served up with delicious nopales (a popular cactus dish) and two fabulous salsas. Go for the roja! Go for the fire. An order of cebollitas preparadas (little grilled onions, seasoned) can really round out a meal, especially if you can share them with a few friends. And for your drink, grab an agua de horchata: a milky, rice based drink made with cinnamon and lime. Sooooo good. It's pretty rare to find "real" homemade horchata these days. I didn't ask if theirs was the "real deal" at Los Taquitos de Puebla, but I certainly found it convincing enough.

text: We decided to try Wang Gang because of a group coupon special. When we entered the mildly crowded establishment, we weren't exactly sure what to expect. The cash registers and large flat panel TV made us think this was more of a fast food type of establishment, and we were right. After a slightly longer than average acknowledgement from waiting in the "Please wait to be seated" zone, we were sat down and introduced to our friendly waitress. She took our drink orders as well as our appetizer orders; Tom Kha Kai soup and Spring Rolls. After the waitress came back a few minutes later to take our main course order, she had remembered that she'd forgotten our drinks, no big deal, but she did mention that she was a novice and just began working as a waitress. Hmmm...Friday night, busy with lots of people...waitress on her 2nd expedition into the restaurant world. :/ We received the appetizers after 10 minutes. The spring rolls were very large although awkwardly prepared and unusually shaped. The taste was bland because the roll was mostly lettuce and had little sprout and carrot. The dipping sauce was overly tart and had a sharp after taste to it. The soup was served acceptingly hot, but not steaming. It had a rich mushroom creaminess but lacked some other ingredients one would expect from a spicy thai soup. My partner wasn't too hungry and simply ordered a fried rice for an entree, but since the expediter didn't bring it out even though we mentioned it was missing, she never got it. The waitress was very busy with other tables (full of other relatively not too happy customers) so by the time she came around, it was too late to re-order it. One thing I'd like to encourage the mgmt. there is to teach the staff to never say "the Mexicans in the back don't speak any English and that's why your fried rice did not make it to the table". :/ The other entree that did make it (called #88, $10) was described as a "classic black pepper dish with vegetables and a 3 pepper soy sauce." Since I am a huge fan of the Thai style pepper dishes, I was looking forward to a zesty chicken dish, but was served something that reminded me of take-out Chinese bucket food. The meat was sub-par and had the rubbery consistency of a take out dinner meat. To top things off and what ultimately went down from a two star review to a one star was the music. I do not want to hear country music, and pop rock music while trying to enjoy Asian fusion.
label: NEG

text: It was just after 9am, and the place had just opened. After being promptly seated and menu'd, It took a while for us to decide what to get to drink. Hot or cold chocolate? Granita or soft drink? Or, in the face of overwhelming chocolate overload, milk or water? A chocolate Granita, a yellow granita, and iced coffee were ordered. I had originally intended to get the Heuvos Rancheros as it's a personal favorite of mine, but didn't realize it came as a burrito, so I passed and went with the Max'ican Omelet. My son, who I thought surely would go for the illegal chocolate pancakes, stepping in and ordered the burrito for himself, so I'd have a chance to try it anyway. His uncle ordered the Max'ican as well, but with fresh tomatoes versus the fire roasted salsa. Those two ordered sides of bacon, but I felt I was doing enough damage with what I had so I held there. We also ordered the Mediterranean trio to share. The yellow granita was actually green, and pronounced very good. My son had the chocolate granita, and pretty much anything here that has chocolate in the description is going to be excellent. I had the iced coffee, which was thoughtfully served with simple syrup for sweetening purposes. A night thoughtful touch that foreshadowed the meal as a whole. There's no picture of the Mediterranean plate. Three nice sized portions of hummus, spanish eggplant, and babaganoosh served with chili dusted tortilla chips. We were hungry and it was good, so Yelp photos be damned we dug right in. It was pretty much three empty bowls when I realized I should have snapped a pic. We'll leave it with my assurance that it's very pretty. The hummus was nice and light, lemony, with some chopped tomato on top. The spanish eggplant, roasted, slightly sweet, and chunky, was my personal favorite and deep and complex. The babaganoosh was very nice as well, but not a personal thrill of mine so I tasted it and deferred to the other two offerings. Let me say that throughout the meal, our host was very attentive, as was Kathy, either the Chef owner or Head Chef. It was a pleasure to see people who enjoyed their job that much, and a change from the usual sad sacks we see in Philly. Of course, you do work in a place that smells like chocolate, and it's hard not to walk out with a smile when food is this good. We can tell this place hasn't been open long yet, as the literal dozen of wait staff were still all rail thin. With food this good, that will change shortly. The black and tan beer battered onion rings, half a stack of which remains in the photo I posted, were served with a cocoa ranch dipping sauce. The black and tan adds a huge flavor to the batter, so much so that the flavor tips to almost a wine infused batter versus the mild and calm flavor we're used to. The chocolate ranch sauce they can keep, we used their omnipresent chocolate ganache instead, which was strong enough to hold up to the intense taste of the batter and fresh onion slices. Truly delish. My max'ican omelet arrived and was accompanied by a light as air fluffy biscuit and finely chopped hash browns. The omelet was prepared with swiss cheese, avocado, onions, and topped with fire roasted salsa. It was delicious, and I noted specifically how perfectly ripe the avocados were. The hash brown bits were exceptionally flavorful, crispy outside and tender within. Yum. The two sauces you see in the picture are butter and 'the omnipresent chocolate sauce' mentioned above. The chocolate sauce is, as you would expect, incredibly good. The mixed the bacon into my son's burrito, which worked out fine. Miscommunication in ordering on our part I assure you. He ate half of it and called it a day to save room for dessert. Yes, at 10am we were having dessert, because not to would be a crime indeed. My son and I split the 'sharing fondue' an $25 tasting of all their iconic dishes. His uncle ordered the churros fondue, which Chef Kathy assured us was being made fresh to order as we chatted. And Chef Kathy does not lie. The Churros came out still hot, accompanied by a trio of dipping sauces (toffee, chocolate, and raspberry). text: Just visited this while some friends were in town for the Fourth of July. I was perfectly content to just poke around the lobby and gift shop, but the out-of-towners insisted on seeing the tour. $12 later, I was seated in the small high-tech theater. The speaker/actress did her voiceover work very well, and the presentation was mildly captivating (the presentation format was rather impressive and engaging to me as an audience member). After the brief history of America's creation and the constitution, I followed my friends up to the second floor, where there's a more-or-less self guided tour of various facts and histories revolving around the constitution. Much of it was decent material. My only real complaint is that while watching a humorous video of Ben Stein explaining the various interpretations that could be made of articles and amendments and other facts about the constitution, the video was cut off (in the middle of a segment), and replaced with a PowerPoint presentation entitled "Political Cartoons 101". The only people sitting in the area watching the video were my three friends and I, and soon an employee walked into the area and asked us if we liked cartoons, and proceeded to delve into a 15 minute long presentation on the History of Political Cartoons in America. First off, we were enjoying the Ben Stein video, which was why we were sititng there in the first place, and I was annoyed that she assumed we would rather learn about political cartoons. Secondly, her presentation was dreadfully boring. The four of us just made awkward eye contact with each other debating whether we could leave without insulting her and just mumbled whenever she tried to engage us. Though we were all in our mid-twenties, she posed us questions appropriate to very young gradeschoolers ("Now, what do we all think the shark symbolizes? Anyone? That's right, it's supposed to be something we're afraid of!"), and while I would be fine with this if it were a presentation I chose to go to, she chose to come present this to us (against our will!), and could have at least tailored the presentation to the audience. The final room of the constitution experience was actually very cool. It was just a meeting hall styled room with bronze statues (I'm led to believe they are all accurate life-size casts) of signers of the constitution. They have a guest-signature book out, and it is a very nice photo opportunity kind of room. I regret that my experience here was largely tainted by a sub-par (albeit dedicated) employee, but overall the museum was just 'decent'. If you're a history buff, or just need to say you've been there, I suppose the $12 is worth one trip. I don't think I'll ever go a second time, and I won't likely recommend it to my less-than-110%-patriotic friends. Still, the building is very nice, and that's something too, I suppose.

text: I periodically go to the Marlton Diner, and I usually have a decent experience, as some of the dishes are tasty, especially for a diner. I went there this evening, though, for dinner to-go and was taken aback by the hostess when she asked me if I wanted to place a tip on the bill. I normally tip between 20 and 25%, even at lunch--or more money if I stay longer than usual or if I rack a tiny bill, but I do not think that the hostess should ask people if they plan to leave a tip for take-out food! It's a tasteless thing to do. The purpose of leaving a tip is to show appreciation for service, and I did not stay to sit because I was trying to save money, yet this woman put me on the spot. I said, "Is that standard with take-out food," and she replied that the waitress had to package the food, which is more work than if she had brought it to me at the table. Is she kidding? When I buy clothing, the cashier puts it in a bag, and I don't tip her. At Victoria's Secret, they even wrap the items first in tissue paper, and I don't tip them either. I understand that waitresses make very little money by the hour, and I sympathize because I have been a waitress in the past, but it should be my choice to leave a tip for TAKE-OUT food, and I should not be asked. The question creates pressure. Obviously, I would look like a jerk if I didn't leave any money after that, so I was suckered into leaving 20%, and it was only after I did so that she said, "Most people leave about 10%. If that is even true, she should have told me that BEFORE she punched in my 20% tip. The situation was uncouth, and it lacked good form. Somehow, it just really turned me off, so I will never go there again. In the end, it's about principle--not money. For me, the staff at a restaurant really make or break the restaurant's appeal, so they should exercise tact.

It came with rice, beans, lettuce and sour cream. Also, it was covered in a yellow cheese sauce. My only qualm was no guacamole. I actually didn't have any here at all, which I regret. Oh well, just another reason to go back. My friend ordered the tacos, to which she said "they have better meat than Las Palmas. Put that on Yelp." Lastly, the bathrooms were SUPER clean. I was extremely impressed. Again, gotta say it, I loved the waitstaff. They acted almost like they were on a tip share. And, when we finished our meal and realized we had 15 minutes left in our lunch break, they didn't have a problem with giving us more chips and salsa to munch on while we sat there and chatted. text: Well I have to confess that I was not that big of a cupcake fan, as there have been many a evil cupcakes that have marred my dessert experience. This place is like willy wonka meets a chic LA boutique. the backroom houses the machinery that churns out these deliciously looking treats, and the front has swanky closets that house their latest batches of cupcakes. As soon as u enter u r greeted by one of staff who hands out a flier of the days offerings. The good news is that it it tastes as good as it looks, the cake was fluffed to perfection, the carrot gives it a dense texture and the Nuts and Resins enhance the flavor. the Cheesecake was also smooth and pretty much melts into the cake with each bite, making for a dynamic duo. The ratios of icing to cake was spot on too. They do have a website, http://www.phillycupcake.com/, though I wish they added some more info on that. They only accept cash and offer takeouts. In summary, i am happy to see a cupcake shop in my hood that along with great cupcakes have a charming staff, a great setup that one would like to visit often. text: I'll admit that I really like going to the Bishop's Collar, which is my favorite bar within walking distance of my second home (the Fairmount neighborhood). While there can sometimes be a wait for a table and while it can get REALLY PACKED on the weekend nights, they do move through pretty quickly and it's not a huge deal to hang out at the bar until something opens up. The double gin and tonics are strong, and always made consistently: you know exactly how many to drink to straddle the line between pleasantly drunk and unpleasantly plastered. This summer they've also had the Arnold Palmer, which has become my favorite summer beverage and discovery: sweet tea infused vodka (oh. my. god.) and lemonade. They are fabulous, especially if you can manage to snag an outdoor table, enjoying the summer air and sipping on one of these. And although I'm not really a beer person, they have enough available that I can find something I like if I have to, and my more beer snobby friends never have problems either. However, secretly, I like the Bishop's Collar because they have perfect, cheap, unhealthy, fantastic, filling bar food. The plate of nachos is intimidating when sober, but after a night of drinking, sharing it with a friend hits the spot. Their wings are not gristly in the least, and the hot sauce, while not quite the same as a buffalo wing, is tangy and tasty. My favorite thing MAY be the chicken chipotle sandwich, with Old Bay fries, which is an absolute steal for $6, but it's hard to choose. Usually we just end up splitting nachos and wings, because it's hard to mess with a classic combination like that. But back to the Bishop's Collar: hits-the-spot food, great drinks, and a nice, low key evening to hang out with friends in the neighborhood.

text: Cute Italian BYOB at a convenient location in Medford with plenty of parking. I'd say the other reviews have done a pretty good job painting the picture in terms of the atmosphere, so I'll limit mine to my opinion of the food. If you order the right thing, there aren't many better values in local dining, especially since you can bring your own bottle of wine. Yes, this does imply that the menu can be hit or miss here. But the hits are great enough to garner a 4-star review from me. Favorites: - The Garlic Knots: love those, sometimes ask for extra - Involtini Di Melenzane (Stuffed Eggplant): this appetizer you could make a meal of. They also offer it as an entree with pasta - but to me all that spaghetti in red sauce just gets in the way of my delicious stuffed eggplant. - Spaghetti Carbonara: If you REALLY want to try and kill yourself with a super heavy dish, try ordering the Carbonara with Gnocchi instead of spaghetti. I did it once and barely survived the experience, but it was so good. Proceed at your own risk. - Gnocchi w/ Vodka Sauce - Linguini w/ White Clam Sauce Not So Much: - Calamari Fritti: The fried calamari appetizer is the most disappointing thing on the menu for me. It's average at best; not good for an Italian spot like this. To qualify my opinion, it's one of my stupid little missions in life to find the best fried calamari out there. Whenever we go out to eat at a new restaurant and they have fried calamari, I order it. Had it from Italy to throughout New England to Arizona (where I had a very good Buffalo Calamari). It's average here. At best. - Vongole Casino: The Clams Casino were terrible, especially for the $8.99 price tag. - Crab Cakes: I'd ballpark these at below average. They're huge, I'll give them that, but if you are craving them you are much better off at a good seafood restaurant. They have a lot of dessert options, but with the portion sizes (one order of the Gnocchi w/ Vodka Sauce is enough for me to get 3 meals out of - and be full for all 3), you'll probably never dream of it unless you go in with the gameplan to eat conservatively and take home a massive doggy bag. Bonus - they do catering trays for parties at very reasonable prices. We did that for our Super Bowl party this year and it was SO worth it. Cut down on our work immensely. Again though - heed the portion sizes here. Yes, a tray of Pasta Tarantella for 5 will feed 5 adults ... if those 5 adults are intent on eating the entire tray and then passing out at the table. All in all, good place, good food, great value!

text: I just got back from selling clothes at Kid To Kid... it was AWFUL! They weren't particularly helpful or friendly which didn't bother me that much. I got the clothes back and gave them the $12... I figured I could sell them at a garage sale or on craigslist for more than that! I understand consignment stores, I have sold my clothes to them before. I just think 75 cents for a shirt that is new (bought within the last year), with tags, NEVER been worn, from GAP is outrageous!!! Not to mention, I know damn well they will turn around and sell it for much more than that! text: This is easily the best of the three bus company (other two-greyhound and new century bus) options for my fortnightly trip down to Baltimore. Before I get into the review, I want to give you some advice for riding the Apex bus to DC (Baltimore). - Buy your ticket online and print it out before arriving at the station. - Be sure to check in at the office 30 min. before your departure (FYI this is 45 min. for greyhound). - Leave at least a 2 hr. buffer between your ETA and your next scheduled event. - Avoid using the mobile bathroom on the bus. I love this company for three reasons: 1) I can bring my bike on the bus without hassle. 2) Planning ahead by buying a ticket online guarantees that you will make it to your destination at a reasonable time. 3) Some of the buses have free wireless internet. ---------------------- 1) Greyhound and AMTRAK both require that you break your bicycle down and put it into a box. They will charge you for the box if you don't have one and they lack tools to help you do this (no surprise really). The Apex and other "chinatown" bus drivers are very cool about bikes. Often they take me around to the other side or open up extra compartments under the bus to help me find space. However, the first come, first serve system puts those with large luggage items (like bikes) at a severe disadvantage (see 2). 2) Apex is especially good because they give priority to those who planned ahead and bought online tix. This means that those with e-tickets board the bus before those who purchased their tix at the station; however, e-tickets are only good for a specific bus where the purple tix sold at the station are good anytime. Bear in mind that they do not regulate the online ticket purchases, so during holiday weekends, when they get overloaded, they cope by scheduling multiple buses instead of limiting ticket sales. Not all of the buses arrive at the same time (some are up to an hour later), but they get you where you need to go. 3) Apex recently purchased some new buses that are equipped with wireless internet. I imagine the facilities are nicer as well, but come on people. Remember when your parents told you to use the bathroom before long trips. That was meant to be a life-long lesson.

Fried dumplings are one of my absolute favorite things to eat. If I could eat them once a week, it wouldn't be enough for me (although it might be too much for my arteries). Since people know I love fried dumplings so much, David's has been recommended to me on more than one occasion. So, the other night in Chinatown I decided to try dinner at David's, partly in an attempt to get out of my rut and partly because I just saw "No Country For Old Men" and was making all of my decisions based on a coin toss. I'm torn about my dining experience. The service was fine. The restaurant is small, but it doesn't take away from anything. And the food was good. So what could I possibly be upset about? The dumplings! Oh the dumplings! They just weren't all they cracked up to be. First of all, the filling is straight pork that tastes like it's 50% hotdog. Very generic. The wrappers were ok, but they were PAN FRIED. If a menu says "Fried" I expect my dumplings to be fried! Say they are pan fried on the menu and I won't bother ordering them! That said, it is neat that they are served with a ginger relish sort of thing. However, it was cold, and I thought that was jarring with the hot temperature of the dumplings. Despite my lack of enthusiasm for the dumplings, the entrees we chose (via coin toss) were pretty good. The sauces weren't too thick or gluey and the flavors of the proteins really shone through. If I go back, it won't be for the dumplings, that's for sure. But, I'd be wiling to stop in for a small meal or a quick beer to go.

They have increased their prices slightly, but not as much as I feared when I first heard about the move. Our meal consisted of naked gyoza with spicy tuna, sleeping volcano and rolling fire rolls, and a few pieces of nigiri and sashimi. The food was all excellent. I am impressed when a sushi place not only offers brown rice as an option, but gets the texture right to work perfectly in sushi. I am surprised to read complaints about the service. I have always found them to be friendly and efficient. Sometimes the food takes a little while, but when it arrives, the complexity of the preparation and presentation makes it obvious why. This is not a restaurant for hurrying. The decor is a complete turnaround from the humble dark wood that I so loved at Shinju. The new space is much more sleek and fancy, typical of what you would expect from a high-end sushi restaurant. This, combined with the liquor license application in the window, makes me believe that high-end sushi restaurant is where they are headed. This is not a bad thing in itself, but the city already has a couple of those. text: Sometimes I think there a rule among Philly sandwich shops. The better they are, the less frequently they are allowed to be open. The 24 hour tourist traps are pretty bad, and at the other end of the spectrum, you have John's You pretty much have to live or work in South Philly to get a chance to go to John's, because they keep bankers hours. And when they say they close at 3, they mean 3 is when the bread is usually gone, so don't think you can sneak in a 2:40, I've been there late as they started surveying the line to figure out who would get the last roll. Despite a lot of praise from all corners, John's remains largely off the beaten path, with much longer lines at the other cheesesteak institutions. That being said, if you ever have a weekday off, you need to get here. Both the cheesesteaks and the roast pork sandwiches vie for the title of best in the city. The rolls are fantastic, lightly seeded with a good thick crust and a light but not spongy breadiness. The pork is perfectly seasoned and nicely juicy. As a bonus, most of the people in line are waiting for a cheesesteak, so you can jump to the front for a roast pork and other non grilled items. Definitely get the pork with sharp provolone and spinach, its really is a marriage made in heaven. The cheesesteaks are cooked to order on a big griddle. Unlike the assembly lines of Passyunk avenue, cheese whiz is verboten here, provolone is the cheese of choice, and they expertly melt it into the meat. Their menu has a good variety of cheesesteak offerings, including chicken cheesesteaks, but I prefer to keep to the classic. They also make cold hoagies, but the point is the hot sandwiches. Like any great steak shop, they have no indoor seating and limited outdoor seating. The building itself is on an island between some railroad tracks, the strip malls on Snyder ave, and an imposing factory. It makes a great place to grab lunch while shopping along Delaware ave, as it is right between the Target and the Ikea down there.

My friends and I were finally able to get back to North Bowl in mid-August and any memories of our last evening were washed away completely. Our waitress was sweet and attentive. The party sitting across from us ordered drinks and food about as often as we did and everything came out of the kitchen (hot and delicious) or the bar (cold and strong) quickly. After we finished bowling we went upstairs to the lounge and just hung out for awhile; overall we had a great time. My main call-out of the night would be the DJ; he went from Kanye West to Frank Sinatra in 2 moves. Spectacular! He played great tracks all night, mixed it up and made the evenings soundtrack pretty on-point.

text: From the overall customer experience to the finished product, (the 'product' being your hair cut/style) Robert Cris Salon is about the best it gets in the Delaware Valley, and I state this from experience. It's taken me two years to find a place I'm happy with in New York, where I typically get my hair cut; but being in Delaware for a few months, I began a search of the area's salons to hopefully find my zen. I'm really not a fussy guy over my hair, I just like a good cut that makes me look and feel better. After trying a few of the large, expensive salons, I found Robert Cris and decided to give this one a try as well. After calling-in & asking for an appointment, I was recommended by Robert to see his business partner Cris. The environment of the salon is beautiful, custom designed by the two owners but without the thick pretense one might expect. This is a SALON, nothing on the door says 'spa' which seems to be the trend with so many hair salons lately. Staff was attentive, warm, friendly. Located in the trendy Wilmington area of Greenville, I was even more surprised considering my experience with the locals has been negative for the most part, this experience being the exception. Chris was helpful, suggesting we look through Google at some basic mens' styles and cuts I might want to consider. And even though I was the last client of the day, coming in at 7:30 on a Thursday evening, I was treated with smiling staff, offered wine, soda, water; made comfortable and right at home with no visible signs of fatigue by any of the staff. I was completely at home and felt welcome and appreciated. Great salon, friendly people, competitive price and overall excellent experience.

text: First, this review is based on an experience three years ago when my mom got married here. I know that they must have chosen this venue based on price alone as they were on a tight budget (and shouldn't have been getting married in the first place--different story for another day). The day before their wedding (June 30th, 2006) was a wet one in Tucson. Everyone in the wedding party went here to rehearse and it was an okay place. It wasn't like the fancy wedding places I would have chosen, but it was my mom's taste as she was having a hill billy -- er, I mean, "cowboy" themed -- wedding. It was Southwestern-y feeling, for sure. Her minister didn't even rehearse as the ground was too wet to practice on. No one working there insisted that we go ahead with a rehearsal to make the wedding went off without a hitch (ha! Irony). Instead, they kept to themselves until the "rehearsal" was over with. The next day, the storms came even harder just before the ceremony. No one working there offered to dry off the seats for the guests; we had the ushers do it. No indoor options were arranged or even avaliable for that matter. My mom had her joke of a wedding, cowboy hats on all the men and all. We all went inside where the reception was to be held. It was pretty basic. If they had done something to the chairs, it would have made a spectacular change and even looked a little classier. Instead, we were all seated on plain metal folding chairs -- fitting, I suppose, for the Cowboy wedding. The people who catered the wedding (Golden Corral, of all places!) weren't worth making note of, but I'm going to. They served up the food, but for the bridal party, well my sister the other bridesmaid, they said she only had the option of ____ instead of the white meat chicken she was pointing to. Had I known this took place, I would have reminded them that my mom was the one paying them to stand there and be rude (and everything else as her husband is a cheap bastard), so they could at least be nice enough to the bride's daughters. People enjoyed the open bar and a lot of drunks took it upon themselves to act stupid. The entire time I was wondering where the hell the people running this place were to put a limit on the number of drinks people could get, or to at least lasso the drunks still parading about the dancefloor picking up the flower girl and tossing her around. She giggled the whole time, but I'm sure she'll have strange flashbacks later in life. Anyways, this place is okay if you don't have the funds to have a big fancy wedding (or don't want one, for that matter). However, it's not somewhere I would choose to marry.
label: NEG

text: Mema's is one of those Tampa establishments that makes me feel like I'm in Austin, TX, minus the reconstructed 1950s cars and greased-back pompadours. The grungy vibe and grubby food are a PERFECT compliment to a night in Ybor. And I mean "grubby" in the most glorious way possible. Think: crisp, gooey, mouth-wateringly seasond, fresh, and filling. Add a hoppy beer for a transcendent experience. For one, the vegan selection is supernaturally amazing; whether you like straight veggies or tofu, an entire Mexican fiesta is available to you. I mean, the receipt even has a line on it that says "MAKE IT VEGAN"...no more having to tell people, that "no" you don't think a dead cow is in cheese, but that you don't want animal products in your food at all. And I'm not even a full-time vegan, so I can imagine the relief of vegans everywhere when they actually see the word on the menu. And the taste is great for something so cheap. I don't know if it's because I'm always drunk when I eat there or on my way to buzz-town, but the food tastes insanely savory and satisfying, without nasty MSG or additives. The service is deadpan (think the adlibbing supporting actors in a John Waters movie), yet winkingly friendly if you're the least bit nice and cordial. If you are a douchebag, you'll never know you're being mocked, but you wouldn't get it anyways. You could bring your kids here, but I'd do it during the day. You don't need a bunch of hipsters talking about anal sex and Cat Power in front of your toddler, do you? Or better yet: have a beer and relax and get your kids ready for the inevitable future.
label: POS

text: Stella Mare's 50 Los Patos Way Santa Barbara, Ca. 93101 805-969-6705 12/26/10 Dining out is our thing. We budget 2,500.00 per month to dine at different restaurants. This restaurant is our number one pick for the year of 2010. We have been to Stella Mare's a few times and it just gets better and better. You can't beat the style and atmosphere. It's hard to find a classic French restaurant. There just don't seem to be that many around. Classic French with a country flair. No nouvelle cuisine small portions served here. Classic French with country portions. You get your monies worth. Martinis all around which was my only complaint for the evening as it wasn't cold enough. But I kept my mouth shut. Oak grilled Frogs legs in thyme butter melted in your mouth. Foie Gras and lobster with apples and sauce Grand Mariner on brioche. Of course we had to try the classic escargot with garlic butter and parsley. The filet béarnaise with accented flavors produced olfactory orgasms. But that's not what I want to talk about. The duck confit brought back memories of the south of France. Not one but two legs and thighs on salad frisee with lentils. Not to salty as some confit turn out. This was perfect...Falling off the bone. Finished off with the cheese platter. No soufflés????We washed it all down with a nice Bordeaux. What I did find interesting is that the French wine selection pricing went from wines around 30 to 50 then the pricing jumped from 50 to 125.00 with nothing in-between. Not much of a selection in the French category from 50.00 to 100.00. I would have liked to see more wines in that price category. I am sorry but I didn't get our servers name perhaps Carol (sorry) OUTSTANDING service, knowledge of menu. Our empty glasses were carted away and not left lingering. She never skipped a beat. We will be back to this spot.

text: Full review in the blog. Served in a large bowl and easily big enough for 2 (and as it turned out a 3rd,) Lamb Tripe and cabbage stew with parsley, olive oil, basil plus grilled Tellagio bread was my first experience with Lamb Tripe, but ideally not my last. Flawlessly cooked the offal was minimally gamey and mildly pork-like in flavor. Cut into thin strips the preparation was raw and rustic with the flavors reminding me of my Grandmother's Hungarian Style Stuffed Cabbage. With my companion appropriately impressed but already starting to feel full we offered a sample of the dish to our neighbors and they graciously accepted. When the biggest complaint about a dish is that it is "too much good food" and "now I have to come up with a different antipasti to try" that is saying something. The cheesemonger's first course would've been my choice had he not ordered it. Entitled "Crocante" with prosciutto wrapped chicken livers, cherries, gorgonzola, and sweet red wine reduction this dish was perhaps my favorite of the evening. Lightly fried pancetta encompassing mild chicken liver was served over warm artichokes and chopped cherries tossed with a creamy gorgonzola. Topping the whole amalgam with a thick and aromatic red wine reduction and spices lent an almost haute-Marsala flavor to the whole dish - it was beautiful. Faring well amongst the second courses would be "Lingue" with braised calf's tongue, pizziola, portabello, plum tomato, and capers. Inspired by the Italy trip our server stated that the concept here was to "introduce" diners to tongue by creating a pizza-esque flavor without the dough. Delicate and thinly shaved the protein was surprisingly light while it was actually the mushrooms that lent heft to the dish. With ample notes of basil, tomato, olive, caper, and cheese I can say their attempt to replicate a pizza flavor was spot on and I enjoyed the dish much more than I had expected. My secondi selection (trumping the duck on our server's suggestion) would be "Animelle" with veal sweetbreads, artichoke, pancetta, lemon, and thyme. Bearing in mind the fact that I'd already eaten substantially during the day and was now eating for two I was lucky this was so good - it was worth being "stuffed" for. Ample in portion, crispy on the surface and creamy within the offal was paired inspiringly with crispy artichokes - similar in texture yet vegetal in composition. Topped with chopped pancetta and a lightly lemon accented olive oil the entire plate came together nicely and ranks amongst my favorite dishes in Philadelphia - an assessment that Phillymag also seems to agree with. Our third dessert and the last taste of the evening would be Gorgonzola Panna Cotta, White Figs, Honey - it would also be (by far) the best dessert of the night. Like a composed cheese plate arranged into a stunning cheesecake the panna cotta would prove to be impossibly light despite its hefty cheese notes while the pungency and bite of the aged cheese was tempered beautifully by the lavender accented honey and sweet poached figs. Bordering on a genuine food coma at this point we were asked if there is anything else we'd like and while I'm sure I would have liked to try almost everything on the menu we decided to take a rain check. Settling the tab - a mere $45/pp with a hefty tip Looking back on my visit to (and receipts from) Philadelphia Modo Mio would invariably be my cheapest lunch or dinner - less than 1/2 the price of Le Bec Fin and less than 1/3 the price of Vetri...it was also cheaper than recent Italian jaunts in New York, Las Angeles, and Columbus. While not every plate was spot on, the dishes that did excel did so to an incredible degree and not a single flavor fell short of at least being good. Speaking with fellow diners (and waiters) at Zahav, Vetri, Supper, and Le Bec Fin I can't say I was surprised by the fondness with which people speak of Modo Mio - it truly is a special place that I was lucky to enjoy with a fantastic fellow gourmand.

text: Ok here's what I love about Aveda salons: natural products, well thought out products, sustainable from a long time ago before it was hip. As well when you go to the concept stores, they always draw you in with the scents and a cup of hot tea. And even though it's a bit more expensive, sometimes you splurge and get something. You feel good coming away with a shopping bag of products. You know you're on to something good that goes w/ your beliefs. You know that you can have it everyday, until the last drop in the bottle etc. But here's my thing: A few years ago when the St. Pete institute first opened up I went there, because "Oh my god, there's an AVEDA here now!!!" Having come from another state and gone to them a lot for products etc, over about a 10 year period of time. But usually I never went for services. So one day like I said some years ago when they first opened in St. Pete, I thought that since it was a school I might be able to get "exclusive-like" services for cheaper than going to an upscale salon. As an intro tester to see how they'd be, I made an appointment for a back facial which included some massage. I couldn't wait for the day. When the day came I was so excited!! Nevertheless, I was not disappointed. It was my first time being in a spa like atmosphere. It was awesome. The student who worked on me was awesome. She quietly explained everything she was going to do and prepped me for how I would feel. Example is like if they tell you they're going to put something on your back and say this may feel a little cold/cool. I made another appointment. What happened to my girl? I found out she graduated and who knows where she went. This next experience was not great at all. I had decided to have the same type of treatment, plus add a regular facial. This girl just went ahead doing everything, her timing was not good, she didn't prepare you for anything and would just glob some cold, startling amount of goop on your back!! That's one lesson. Don't get attached to any of them, they are students and they will eventually graduate and possibly move to Vegas. So again don't get attached... But here is my biggest problem with the Aveda Institute in St. Pete. For all the times I had gone there for services or to drop in to pick up products, there was a time I finally decided to graduate myself to making a hair appointment. When I decided to make a hair appointment, I was told to hold on a minute while they went to get someone who specialized in my kind of hair. The person came and sat down with me out front. She most politely as she could told me that they really aren't able to do my "kind of hair"... African American hair... You can't imagine how that made me feel. You just don't know. Oh, I thought I was on to something. I just knew they would be my one stop shop for everything for my "spa" experience for however often I could afford it. I was willing to pay. Hey wait a minute, I had paid!! I had paid all those times I had other services. I had paid everytime I dropped in for more product (understanding the reputation of how great the it is )from over 10 years ago of using it. I had paid everytime I had gotten a service and was escorted back out to the front by the student to peruse and be persuaded to buy the products used on me that day. I think that I had well deserved to have services for my "kind of hair"!! Why, with Aveda's universal appeal is that one area that seems unable to be cared for? The person who sat me down informed me that they really didn't have anyone there at that point (I guess in the slew of students) who understood nor was able to do "Afro hair" as she called it. I slunk out of the salon feeling pretty dejected. I really don't think she meant anything personal by it. I could tell she was just being honestly sincere which is why I did not pursue it on a legal level. But I really agree with her and observed that she must be right, due to the fact that in walking through the salon, you generally do not see diversity of people nor hair textures, (despite advertisement.) Again why is that? It shouldn't matter what ethnicity the students are who are attending, the institute is losing out, because they will have trouble drawing a certain clientele. As well and more importantly they are giving their students a disservice to not be well versed or trained in the diverse world that they live in. Many of their students may be kicking and screaming later after graduation when the salon they dream of getting into is already inundated with those who handle a set number of hair types. They should live up to their progressive credo and teach their students to dream bigger and maybe even have their own salon because there is another clientele out there who are just as progressive. There is more to a strand of hair than meets the eye. As from the musical Hair "Hair, hair, hair...Long, straight, curly, fuzzy,Snaggy, shaggy, ratty, matty!!
label: NEG

text: I usually review a place right away or the next night, but Farmicia left a bitter taste in my mouth. I was highly disappointed at such a beautiful restaurant serving sub-par food. For starters, this place is gorgeously decorated. Beautiful wooden floors with deeper stained furniture lined the entire room. There were many plants and classic farm/rural motifs around; I think I saw a barnyard door. Then adding oil paintings and dimly lit lights makes the restaurant complete. Did I mention it just feels natural and organic being there? True story, I almost took the place down in flames when the flimsy paper menu caught fire from the candle. After that fiasco, we ordered our food. For an appetizer we tried the Trio of Cheeses, which included fruit chutney and toast. I had no problems with this dish. Cheeses were fresh and tasted great, some better than others. The cow milk was formed into a rich cheddar, while the sheep and goat milks found their way into the feta form. The latter cheeses were creamy and had deep flavor. The fruit chutney was sweet and complimented the feta cheeses well, sweet and smelly. As entrees, my lady got the London Broil with cheddar potatoes au gratin and green beans. The meat was cut pretty thickly, thicker than what I am used to. It was also cooked uneven with some areas more medium and some areas more rare, when she ordered medium rare. Also a bit on the chewy side, what happened? The meat did not set really and left a wet messy plate. As for me, I got the Pan Roasted Lamb Tenderloins with a mint-shallot dressing over white bean salad and asparagus. I figured since it was pan roasted, I'd have nice coloration on the outside, but it was grey, the white bean salad was pretty plain tasting. It was either the dressing or the beans that was super wet. It soaked my lamb in all this juice, that wasn't the most tasty liquid. No thanks, I didn't even finish it and I almost always finish my plates! I was not that happy of a customer, but they tried. The veggies ere fresh and brightly colored. If they could treat their protein as well as their vegetables, they would have a returning customer.
label: NEG

text: I had been wanting to try Royal Tavern for weeks. Heard and read great things about their burger and grilled cheese. I went here on a Saturday night with my parents and boyfriend. It ha a small bar and dining room, but is cozy and not as "divey" as I thought. At around 7pm on a Saturday night, we had a bit of a wait, but it wasn't too bad. My boyfriend loves popcorn, so we started with the truffle butter and Parmesan popcorn, which was addicting. I had a bite of the burger, which lived up to it's reputation. It was juicy and had a great flavor combination with bacon, caramelized onions, gouda, and chile mayonnaise. The Grilled Chicken Sandwich was both sweet and savory with proscuitto, sliced pear, arugula, blue cheese and a lavender-honey mustard. And the french fries were killer. They came with a malt vinegar mayo, reminding me of my childhood in Maryland, where the combo of fries, vinegar, and old bay are a staple. The menu had a myriad of mouth-watering options, I have a feeling we'll be back soon for Round 2.

text: Let me begin by saying...wow I can't believe I haven't reviewed this place yet. Driving down Ewing you'll see the red roofed house that is known as Hot Diggity Dogs. For those who don't know...taken from Wikipedia: "A Chicago-style hot dog is a steamed or boiled, never broiled all-beef hot dog on a poppy seed bun, which originated in the city of Chicago, Illinois. The hot dog is topped with mustard, onion, sweet pickle relish (usually a dyed neon green variety called "Nuclear Relish"), a dill pickle spear, tomato slices or wedges, pickled sport peppers, and a dash of celery salt; sometimes, but not always, cucumber slices." The cornucopia of flavors and textures will win you over. Cool, crisp, hot...all having a get down. The fine ladies at Hot Diggity Dogs do Chicago justice. You really can't find a better dog in Nashville.
