text: Like a previous post, I thought the Treehouse Restaurant, next to a Best Western would be decent. MAN was I wrong... There are only two cute things about this place. One is the name, "Treehouse"... ooohhh, so artsy... so safe... so inviting... so wrong (shaking my head no like a two year old)... The other was the old fashion cash register. I haven't seen something like that in years. I'm thinking like something from the "Gunsmoke" tv show... Old West... 1920's... that type of cash register. That should have been a warning to me, but I was stuck in the Twilight Zone (cue the music) because I missed all the clues. Clue number one. The inside of this place is stuck in a timewarp from the 1950's - and that's not by design like Johnny Rockets. The primary difference is Johnny Rockets is clean. You see where I'm going here? The interior looks like the owners haven't put one single dime into redecorating the inside. Basically the interior looks like a restaurant in one of those horror movies where you know you shouldn't stop, but you stop anyway. Well, keep driving. You'll thank me - and yourself later. Clue number two. I don't drink coffee, so I ask if you should be able to "see" thru it - should you? I've never seen coffee that was so watered down, you could almost see the bottom of the cup. But to have the nerve to pour and serve it like it was completely normal - something is frighteningly wrong with that. Gives me the chills. Try sending it back and getting another one. Whew, do so at your own risk. Clue number three. Our waitress never smiled. Not once. Not even when I thanked her for politely telling me - although I didn't ask - what the difference was between one thing on the menu and another. That scared me. Clue number four. When you order your food, shouldn't it look appealing to eat? I mean really. As a kid, even when my mother was mad at me and made my breakfast, she still made it look appealing. The breakfast served was absent any personality - or appeal - and I'm talking about simple sausage and eggs. By the way, my hash browns were cold, but they looked like they were cooked. How does that happen? Nevertheless, I'm sure you get the picture. Needless to say, I'm not a fan. I believe the only way they survive is on unsuspecting tourists from Eastern Europe staying at the BW and on locals who don't know any better. Do yourself a favor, no matter how warm and inviting BW looks from the outside, the Treehouse out front is a horror movie. There are too many other places to eat, that are "one million times better" in Santa Barbara than eating here. Do yourself a favor, save yourself and go elsewhere.
label: NEG

text: Decent Yet Distracting Salon. I had my hair cut at Saturn Club for about 2 and a half years. I generally went with whatever stylist was around, but most often had Sabrina. The atmosphere of the Saturn Club is really funky, but sometimes it seems equally distracting to the stylists and patrons. Be prepared to walk up and down stairs as the salon is on all three levels of the row house. The coffeehouse is on the main level and most stylists are more than happy to grab you a treat from their selection (which will be added to your bill). I would recommend picking an off-time (not after 5pm or on weekends) for a cut if you can, otherwise it can be VERY busy in here. Be prepared to walk a bit as it's on the busiest section of Sansom Street. Overall, I always felt just okay about the final results of my haircut (I think I only ended up crying my way up the hill of Sansom once). However, no matter what I asked for, I always seemed to come out with the same cut. As with any salon, be sure to speak up and be very specific about what kind of cut you want and/or bring pictures. The prices of cuts are average for a female's hair in the city, ranging from $35-$50. At the end of the day, Saturn Club is worth a try or if you are in need of a haircut and can't schedule at your normal place.
label: NEG

text: i don't generally like live music or rock bands, but exit/in also has electronic shows, so in my months in nashville, i've been here probably six or seven times to see acts like infected mushroom and pretty lights. it's my kind of place. parking isn't bad, i've never had to park more than a block away. the line can get crazy with a sold out show, since there is no line management at all, just a crush to get to the door, where an imposing but easygoing guy will quickly check your i.d. and mark you off for your presale, and you're in. the bar is reasonably priced, and the bartenders are pros, so i've never had that will-i-ever-get-served feeling there. as some have mentioned, the bathrooms are weird. the women's room is up some stairs on the side, very funky, but hey, i don't go out for the bathroom, i go out for the music. someone mentioned having attendants in the bathroom... i have never seen that, and can't imagine where one would stand in that shrinky-dink toilet. the main room is big, black, plain and simple, just like i like it. there is some seating in the back, and apparently upstairs, where i've never bothered to venture. the stage is big enough for the special effects of a show like pretty lights, or the 20-foot-tall inflatable psycho mushroom the infected mushroom guys use for their shows. along the wall, just like on the front of the building, is a huge list of all of the incredibly famous and diverse people who have played there. awesome. basically, it's just what you need -- a big dark plain box of a room with good sound and good vibes, so you get get down and dance. like i said, it's my kind of place.

text: My number one favorite place to go!!!! BYOB. The atmosphere is really nice. Exposed brick wall, copper table tops simple and elegant. text: i had the pleasure of eating at baja burrito a few months ago for the first time and have been hooked ever since, even though i've been back only a handful of times... if you are having a craving for a huge burrito that is delicious but on the healthier side, baja is one of your best bets in town... i am a vegetarian who loves mexican food and for fast mexican food this is the best place by far in town.. i have never been a huge fan of chains like baja fresh or qudoba... so this was a refreshing find for me i had been hearing about this place all year and am so glad i finally checked it out and wish i had sooner they have yummy queso and chips and equally good guacamole... you can get burritos in a 10" or 12" size and they are so big you could eat half of one and save half for another day and be satisfied... they also have some delicious fruit tea to drink.... (and i've had fruit tea all over nashville)... you get a chance to interact with the employees as you build your burrito, tacos or taco salad... picking out your ingredients as you move down the line... it's fun! the seating is limited so if you can't find any you can always take your food to go overall a wonderful experience to say the least... love love love it!
